strong.kjv: among, X before them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
58 μέσος, -η, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for תָּוֶךְ;]
middle, in the middle or midst;
1. prop., as an adj.: Lk 23:45, Jo 19:18, Ac 1:18; c. gen. pl., Lk 22:55, Jo 1:26; gen. temp. (Bl., § 36, 13), μέσης νυκτός, Mt 25:6; μ. ἡμέρας, Ac 26:13.
2. In adverbial phrases, neut., μέσον, τὸ μ., as subst.: ἀνὰ μέσον, c. gen., between (cl.; in LXX: Ge 1:4, al.), elliptically (but v. M, Pr., 99), I Co 6:5; = ἐν μ., among, in the midst of (Bl., § 39, 2; 40, 8; cf. in LXX: Jos 19:1, Si 27:2), Mt 13:25, Mk 7:31, Re 7:17; διὰ μέσου, c. gen., Lk 4:30; διὰ μέσον (Rec. -ου, v. Bl., § 42, 1), between, Lk 17:11 (ICC, in l.); εἰς τὸ μ. (v.s. εἰς), Mk 3:3, Lk 4:35 5:19 6:8, Jo 20:19, 26; εἰς μ., Mk 14:60; ἐν τῷ μ., Mt 14:6; ἐν μ., Jos 8:[3, 9], Ac 4:7; c, gen. loc., Mk 6:47, Lk 21:21 22:55, Ac 17:22, He 2:12(LXX), Re 4:6 5:6 22:2. c. gen. pl., Mt 10:16 18:2, 20, Mk 9:36, Lk 2:46 8:7 10:3 22:27 24:36, Ac 1:15 2:22 27:21, I Th 2:7, Re 1:13 2:1 5:6 6:6; κατὰ μέσον τ. νυκτός, Ac 27:27 (Bl., § 47, 6); ἐκ τοῦ μ. (Lft., in l.; Deiss., BS, 252 f.), Col 2:14; ἐκ μ., II Th 2:7; ἐκ τοῦ μ., c. gen., Mt 13:49, Ac 17:33 23:10, I Co 5:2, II Co 6:17.
3. Neut., μέσον, adverbially, c. gen., in the midst of, Mt 14:24 (WH, txt., R, mg., aliter), Phl 2:15 (διὰ μέσου—v. supr.—also Jo 8:50, R, mg.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θραύω, [in LXX for רצץ (De 28:33, Is 42:4 58:6), etc.;]
to break in pieces, shatter; metaph., to break down: Lk 4:18(LXX).†

strong.derivation: from (the neuter of) G3588 (ὁ) and G3753 (ὅτε);
strong.def: the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
160 τότε, demonstr. adv. of time, correlat. of ὅτε,
then, at that time;
(a). of concurrent events: Mt 2:17 3:5 and freq., Ro 6:21; seq. ptcp., Mt 2:16, Ga 4:8; opp. to νῦν, Ga 4:29, He 12:26; ὁ τ. κόσμος, II Pe 3:6;
(b). of consequent events, then, thereupon: Mt 2:7 3:5 4:1 and freq., Lk 11:26; τ. οὖν, Jo 11:14 19:1, 16 20:8; εὐθέως τ., Ac 17:14; ὅτε . . . τ., Mt 13:26 21:1, Jo 12:16; ἀπὸ τ., Mt 4:17 16:21 26:16, Lk 16:16;
(c). of things future: Mt 24:23, 40 25:1, 31ff.; opp. to ἄρτι, I Co 13:12; καὶ τ., Mt 7:23, Mk 13:21, Lk 21:27, I Co 4:5, al.; ὅταν . . . τ., Mt 9:15, Mk 2:20, Lk 5:35, I Th 5:3, al. (more freq. in Mt than in the rest of the NT).

strong.def: a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 Σαδδουκαῖος, -ου, ὁ (< Heb. צָדוֹק, II Ki 15:24, al.),
a Sadducee (cf. Swete, Mk., 277): Mt 3:7 16:1, 6, 11, 12 22:23, 34, Mk 12:18, Lk 20:27, Ac 4:1 5:17 23:6-8.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2508 (καθαίρω) (meaning cleansed);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
32 ἀκάθαρτος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., καθαίρω), [in LXX chiefly for טָמֵא;]
unclean, impure;
(a). physically (LS, MM, VGT, s.v.);
(b). ceremonially: Ac 10:14, 28 11:8, I Co 7:14, II Co 6:17, Re 18:2;
(c). morally: Eph 5:5, Re 17:4; c. πνεῦμα, as always in Gosp., Mt 10:1 12:43, Mk 1:23, 26, 27 3:11, 30 5:2, 8, 13 6:7 7:25 9:25, Lk 4:33, 36 6:18 8:29 9:42 11:24, Ac 5:16 8:7, Re 16:13 (cf. Cremer, 320).†

strong.def: to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient
strong.kjv: bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 † μακροθυμέω, -ῶ (< μακρό-θυμος, long-tempered; v.s. -ία), [in LXX: Ec 8:12 א2, Pr 19:11 (ארךְ, אַף הֶאֱרִיךְ), Jb 7:16, Si 2:4, al.;] SYN.: ὑπομένω, q.v.
1. actively = καρτερέω, to persevere (Plut., 2, 593 F).
2. Passively, to be patient, long-suffering: absol., I Co 13:4, He 6:15, Ja 5:8; seq. ἕως, c. gen., Ja 5:7; ἐπί, c. dat., Ja 5:7. (Si 2:4); πρός, c. acc., I Th 5:14; ἐπί, c. dat., Mt 18:26, 29, Lk 18:7; εἰς, II Pe 3:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 μακρός, -ά, -όν, [in LXX for אָרֶךְ, רָחוֹק and cognate forms, etc.;]
of space and time, long: μακρὰ προσεύχεσθαι, Mk 12:40, Lk 20:47.
of distance, far, far distant: χώρα, Lk 15:13 19:12.†

strong.def: to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φορτίζω (< φόρτος), [in LXX: Ez 16:33 (שָׁחַד) * ;]
to load: c. dupl. acc., Lk 11:46; pass., to be laden: metaph. (EV, heavy laden), Mt 11:28.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4570 (σβέννυμι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἄ-σβεστος, -ον (< σβέννυμι), [in LXX for נפח לֹא, Jb 20:26 א3 A (ἄκαυστον, א2 B)*;]
unquenched, unquenchable: πῦρ, Mt 3:12, Mk 9:43, Lk 3:17.†

strong.def: used only in certain tenses, the rest being supplied by G5315 (φάγω); to eat (usually literal)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
163 ἐσθίω, and (poet, and late prose) ἔσθω, [in LXX chiefly for אכל ;]
to eat;
(a). absol.: Mt 14:20, 21 Mk 6:31, Jo 4:31, al.; ἐν τ. φαγεῖν (on this aor. form, v. M, Pr., 111), I Co 11:21; διδόναι φαγεῖν, c. dat. pers., Mk 5:43, al.; ἐ. καὶ πίνειν, Mt 6:25, 31 Lk 10:7, al.; of ordinary use of food and drink, I Co 9:4 11:22; of partaking of food at table, Mk 2:16, Lk 5:30, al.; opp. to fasting, Mt 11:18, Lk 5:33, al.; of revelling, Mt 24:49, Lk 12:45 .
(b). c. acc. rei: Mt 6:25, Mk 1:6, Jo 6:31, Ro 14:2, al.; ἄρτον (Heb. אָכַל לֶחֶם), Mt 15:2, Mk 3:20, al.; τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ἄ., II Th 3:12; ἄ. seq. παρά, gen. pers., II Th 3:8; τά seq. id., Lk 10:7; τ. πάσχα, Mt 26:17, Mk 14:12 al; τ. κυριακὸν δεῖπνον, I Co 11:20; τ. θυσίας, I Co 10:18; seq. ἐκ (= cl. part. gen.), Jo 6:26, 50, 51, I Co 11:28; ἀπό (cf. Heb. אָכַל מִן), Mt 15:27, Mk 7:28; metaph., to devour, consume: He 10:27, Ja 5:3, Re 17:16 (cf. κατ-, συν-εσθίω) .

strong.def: to think well of in common, i.e. assent to, feel gratified with
strong.kjv: allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** συν-ευ-δοκέω, -ῶ [in LXX: I Mac 1:57, 4:28 א1, II Mac 11:24, 35 * ;]
to join in approving, consent, agree to or with: absol., Ac 22:20; c. dat. pers., Ro 1:32; c. dat. rei, Lk 11:48, Ac 8:1; c. inf., I Co 7:12, 13 (chiefly in late writers).†

strong.kjv: any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
90 μηδείς, -δεμία, -δέν (and -θέν, Ac 27:33, a Hellenistic form; v. Bl., § 6, 7; Thackeray, Gr., 58), related to οὐδείς as μή to οὐ,
no, none, no one; neut., nothing: Mt 16:20, Mk 5:43 6:8, Lk 3:14, Ac 8:24, Ro 13:8, al.; c. gen., Ac 4:17 24:23; neut. acc., μηδέν, adverbially, in no respect, Ac 10:20 11:12; as acc. obj. after verb, βλάπτειν, Lk 4:35; ὠφελεῖσθαι, Mk 5:26; ὑστερεῖν, II Co 11:5; μεριμνᾶν, Phl 4:6; in double negation, strengthening the denial, μηκέτι μ., Mk 11:14, Ac 4:17; μὴ . . . μηδέν (μηδένα, μηδεμίαν), II Co 13:7, II Th 2:3, I Pe 3:6.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 σποδός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for אֵפֶר ;]
ashes: He 9:13; ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σ. (Is 58:5, Jo 3:6, Da LXX 9:3, al.), Mt 11:21, Lk 10:13.†

strong.derivation: feminine of the same as G4074 (Πέτρος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 πέτρα, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for סֶלַע, צוּר;]
a rock, i.e. a mass of live rock as distinct from πέτρος, a detached stone or boulder: Mt 7:24, 25 27:51, 60, Mk 15:46, Lk 6:48 8:6, 13; of a hollow rock, a cave, Re 6:15, 16 (cf. Is 2:10, al.). Metaph., Mt 16:18 (on the meaning, v. Hort, Eccl., 16 ff., but cf. also ICC, in l.), I Co 10:4; = πέτρος, Ro 9:33, I Pe 2:8(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
67 πιστός, -ή, -όν (< πείθω), [in LXX chiefly for נֶאֱמָן;]
I. Pass., to be trusted or believed;
1. of persons, trusty, faithful: Mt 24:45 25:21, 23, Lk 12:42, Ac 16:15, I Co 4:2, 17 7:25, Eph 1:1 6:21, Col 1:2, 7 4:7, 9, I Ti 1:12, II Ti 2:2, He 2:17 3:2, 5, I Pe 5:12, Re 2:13 19:11; of God, I Co 1:9 10:13, II Co 1:18, I Th 5:24, II Th 3:3, He 10:23 11:11, II Ti 2:13, I Jn 1:9, I Pe 4:19; seq. ἐν, Lk 16:10-12 19:17, I Ti 3:11; ἐπί, c. acc., Mt 25:23; ἄχρι θανάτου, Re 2:10; ὁ μάρτυς ὁ π., Re 1:5; id. καὶ ἀληθινός, Re 3:14.
2. Of things, trustworthy, reliable, sure: Ac 13:34, I Ti 1:15 3:1 4:9, II Ti 2:11, Tit 1:9 3:8, Re 21:5 22:6.
II. Act., believing, trusting, relying: Ac 16:1, II Co 6:15, Ga 3:9, I Ti 4:10 5:16 6:2, Tit 1:6, Re 17:14; pl., Ac 10:45, I Ti 4:3, 12; opp. to ἄπιστος, Jo 20:27; π. εἰς θεόν, I Pe 1:21; π. ποιεῖν, III Jn 5. (On the difficulty of choosing in some cases between the active and the passive meaning, v. Lft., Gal., 157.)†

strong.def: Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Ἀριμαθεία (WH, Ἁρ.), -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Ἁριμαθάιμ, I Ki 1:1, al. (רָמָתַיִם);]
Arimathæa: Mt 27:57, Mk 15:43, Lk 23:51, Jo 19:38.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 θυμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< θύω), [in LXX most freq. for אַף, also for חֵמָה, חָרוֹן, etc., 30 words in all;] SYN.: ὀργή, παροργισμός.
passion, hot anger, wrath: He 11:27; ὀργὴ καὶ θ., Ro 2:8, cf. Col 3:8; πικρία κ. θ., Eph 4:31; πλησθῆναι, πλήρης θυμοῦ, Lk 4:28, Ac 19:28; θ. ἔχειν, Re 12:12; οἶνος τ. θυμοῦ τ. πορνείας (cf. Je 28 (51):7), Re 14:8 18:3 (cf. Re 17:2); οἶνος τ. θ. τ. θεοῦ, Re 14:10; id., τ. ὀργῆς τ. θεοῦ, Re 16:19 19:15; ὁ θ. τ. θεοῦ, Re 14:19 15:1, 7 16:1; pl., impulses or outbursts of anger: ἔρις, ζῆλος, θυμοὶ, ἐριθίαι, II Co 12:20, Ga 5:20 (Cremer, 287, 733).†

strong.def: the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest
strong.kjv: chief (high) priest, chief of the priests

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
122 ἀρχ-ιερεύς, -έως, ὁ, [in LXX for כֹּהֵן, הַגָּדוֹל כּ״, הָרֹאשׁ כּ״;]
1. high-priest: Mk 2:26 14:47, al.; of Christ: He 2:17 3:1, al.
2. In pl., chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families: Mt 2:4, Mk 8:31, al. (Cremer, 294; DCG, i, 297 f.; MM, s.v.).

strong.def: to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
26 ἥκω [in LXX chiefly for בּוא;]
pf. with pres. meaning (hence impf. = plpf.), to have come, be present: Mt 24:50, Mk 8:3 (late pf., ἧκα, v. Swete, in l.; WH, App., 169), Lk 12:46 15:27, Jo 8:42, He 10:7, 9, 37, I Jn 5:20, Re 2:25 3:3, 9 15:4; seq. ἀπό, c. gen. loc., Mt 8:11, Lk 13:29; ἐκ, Ro 11:26; id. seq. εἰς, Jo 4:47; μακρόθεν, Mk 8:3; ἐπί, c. acc., Re 3:3. Metaph., of discipleship: Jo 6:37; of time and events: absol., Mt 24:14, Jo 2:4, II Pe 3:10, Re 18:8; seq. ἐπί c acc. pers., Mt 23:36, Lk 19:43 (cf. ἀν-, καθ-ήκω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 δῶρον, -ου, τό (< δίδωμι), [in LXX chiefly for קׇרְבָּן, also for מִנְחָה, etc. ;] SYN.: s.v. δόμα.
a gift, present: Mt 2:11, Re 11:10; of gifts and sacrifices to God, Mt 5:23, 24 8:4 15:5 23:18, 19, Mk 7:11, Lk 21:1, 4, He 5:1 8:3, 4 9:9 11:4; δ. θεοῦ, Eph 2:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
22 τεσσεράκοντα (Rec. τεσσαρ-, v, WH, App., 150; M, Pr., 45 f.; Thackeray, Gr., 62 f., 73 f.), οἱ, αἱ, τά, indecl.,
forty: Mt 4:2, Mk 1:13, Lk 4:2, Jo 2:20, Ac 1:3, al

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 βασανίζω (< βάσανος), [in LXX: I Ki 5:3, Si 4:17, and freq. in Wi, II, IV Mac;]
1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test.
2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mt 8:6, 29 14:24, Mk 5:7 6:48, Lk 8:28, II Pe 2:8, Re 9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10.†

strong.derivation: from G4253 (πρό) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 προ-τρέχω, [in LXX: I Ki 8:11 (לִפְנֵי רוּץ), Jb 41:13 (14) A (דּוּץ), To 11:3 (seq. ἔμπροσθεν), I Mac 16:21*;]
1. to run forward.
2. to run on, run in advance: Jo 20:4; seq. εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν, Lk 19:4.†

strong.def: an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† ὠτάριον, -ου, τό
= ὠτίον (q.v.),
the ear: Mk 14:47, Jo 18:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
22 ἐκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν (< ἐκλέγω), [in LXX for בָּחַר (so prob. in Is 28:16, Pr 17:3, for MT בָּחַן), בָּרִיא, etc. ;]
1. choice, select (cl., rarely; Thuc., Plat., al.), hence, eminent: Ro 16:13 (cf. Ez 27:24).
2. As in Inscr. (MM, Exp., xii), chosen; esp. as in LXX, of Israel, elect, chosen of God (Is 65:9, Ps 105:43, al.); so in NT;
(a). of Christ: Lk 23:35 (cf. Is 42:1); fig., λίθος, I Pe 2:4, 6 (LXX);
(b). of holy angels: I Ti 5:21;
(c). of Christians: Mt 24:22, 24, Mk 13:20, 22, 27, II Ti 2:10, I Pe 1:1; τ. θεοῦ, Lk 18:7, Ro 8:33, Col 3:12, Tit 1:1; τ. Χριστοῦ, Mt 24:31; ἐ. κυρία, II Jn 1; ἀδελφή, II Jn 13; γένος, I Pe 2:9 (LXX); κλητοὶ καὶ ἐ. κ. πιστοί, Re 17:14; opp. to κλητός (not so in Epp.; v. Lft. on Col 3:12), Mt 20:16 (T, WH, txt., R, omit) Mt 22:14 (Cremer, 405, 775).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3551 (νόμος);
strong.def: lawless, i.e. (negatively) not subject to (the Jewish) law; (by implication, a Gentile), or (positively) wicked
strong.kjv: without law, lawless, transgressor, unlawful, wicked

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἄ-νομος, -ον (ἀ. neg., νόμος), [in LXX for עָוֺן, פֶּשַׁע, רֶשַׁע, etc.;] SYN.: v.s. ἄθεσμος.
1. lawless, wicked: Mk 15:28, Lk 22:37, Ac 2:23, I Ti 1:9, II Pe 2:8; ὁ ἄ., II Th 2:8 (= ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας, II Th 2:3).
2. without law (= οἱ μὴ ὑπὸ νόμον, Ro 2:14): I Co 9:21 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of G3778 (οὗτος);
strong.def: of (from or concerning) these (persons or things)
strong.kjv: such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1387 οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, gen., τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, [in LXX chiefly for זֶה, זֹאת;] demonstr. pron. (related to ἐκεῖνος as hic to ille),
this;
1. as subst., this one, he;
(a). absol.: Mt 3:17, Mk 9:7, Lk 7:44, 45, Jo 1:15, Ac 2:15, al.; expressing contempt (cl.), Mt 13:55, 56, Mk 6:2, 3, Jo 6:42, al.; εἰς τοῦτο, Mk 1:38, Ro 14:9; μετὰ τοῦτο (ταῦτα; V. Westc. on Jo 5:1), Jo 2:12 11:7, al.;
(b). epanaleptic (referring to what precedes): Mt 5:19, Mk 3:35, Lk 9:48, Jo 6:46, Ro 7:10, al.;
(c). proleptic (referring to what follows): seq. ἵνα (Bl., § 69, 6), Lk 1:43, Jo 3:19 (and freq.) 15:8, Ro 14:9, al.; seq. ὅτι, Lk 10:11, Jo 9:30, Ac 24:14, Ro 2:3, al.; ὅπως, Ro 9:17; ἐάν, Jo 13:35;
(d). special idioms: τοῦτο μὲν . . . τ. δέ (cl), partly . . . partly, He 10:33; καὶ τοῦτο (τοῦτον, ταῦτα), and that (him) too, Ro 13:11, I Co 2:2, He 11:12; τοῦτ’ ἐστιν, that is to say, Mt 27:46.
2. As adj., c. subst.;
(a). c. art.
(α). before the art.: Mt 12:32, Mk 9:29, Lk 7:44, Jo 4:15, Ro 11:24, Re 19:9, al.;
(β). after the noun: Mt 3:9, Mk 12:16, Lk 11:31, Jo 4:13, Ac 6:13, Ro 15:28, I Co 1:20, Re 2:24, al.;
(b). c. subst. anarth. (with predicative force; Bl., § 49, 4): Lk 1:36 2:2 24:21, Jo 2:11 4:54 21:14, II Co 13:1.

strong.derivation: from a primary (to be put in fear);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
47 φόβος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for יִרְאָה, also for פַּחַד, אֵימָה, etc. ;] SYN.: v.s. δειλία (and of. DCG, i, 381)
1. in Hom., flight.
2. That which causes flight, fear, dread, terror: Lk 1:12, Ac 5:5, I Ti 5:20. I Jn 4:18, al.; cogn. acc., φοβεῖσθαι φ., Mk 4:41, Lk 2:9; c. gen. obj., Jo 7:13 19:33 20:19, He 2:5, I Pe 3:14 (but cf. ICC, in l.);ἀπὸ (τοῦ) φ., Mt 14:26, Lk 21:26; εἰς φ., Ro 8:15; μετὰ φόβου, Mt 28:8; φ. καὶ τρόμος (Lft., Notes, 172), I Co 2:3, II Co 7:15, Eph 6:5, Phl 2:12; by meton., of that which causes fear, Ro 13:3; of reverential fear, Ro 13:7, I Pe 1:17 2:18 3:2, 15; τ. κυρίου, Ac 9:31, II Co 5:11 (v. Field, Notes, 183); Χριστοῦ, Eph 5:21; θεοῦ, Ro 3:18, II Co 7:1

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πάντοθεν, adv. (< πᾶς), [in LXX: Je 31 (48):31 (כֻּלֹּה), al.;]
from all sides: Mk 1:45, Lk 19:43, He 9:4.†

strong.def: Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Ἡρῳδιάς (Rec. Ἡρω-), -άδος, ἡ,
Herodias, granddaughter of Herod the Great: Mt 14:3, 6, Mk 6:17, 19, 22, Lk 3:19.†

strong.def: to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel
strong.kjv: declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
54 εὐαγγελίζω [in LXX for בָּשַׂר pi., hith.; for good news in general: I Ki 31:9, al.; of God's loving kindness, Ps 39 (40):10 95 (96):2, and esp. of Messianic blessings, Is 40:9 60:6, al. ;]
to bring or announce glad tidings;
1. act. (only in late writers): c. acc pers., Re 10:7; seq. ἐπί, c. acc pers., Re 14:6; pass., of things, to be proclaimed as glad tidings: Lk 16:16, Ga 1:11, I Pe 1:25; impers., I Pe 4:6; of persons, to have glad tidings proclaimed to one: Mt 11:5, Lk 7:22, He 4:2, 6
2. Depon. mid. (cl.), to proclaim glad tidings, in NT esp. of the Christian message of salvation: absol., Lk 9:6, Ro 15:20, al.; c. dat. pers., Lk 4:18 (LXX), Ro 1:15, al.; in same sense c. acc pers. (not cl.), Lk 3:18, Ac 16:10, Ga 1:9, I Pe 1:12; c. acc rei, εἰρήνην, Ac 10:36, Ro 10:15 (LXX); τ, βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, Lk 8:1; c. dat. pers., Lk 1:19 4:43, Eph 2:17 3:8; αὐτῷ τ. Ἰησοῦν, Ac 8:35 17:18; c. dupl. acc, Ac 13:32; c. acc pers. et inf., Ac 14:15; τ. κώμας (πολεῖς), Ac 8:25, 40 14:21 (cf. προ-ευαγγελίζομαι)

strong.def: a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 νόσος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for חֳלִי, etc.;] SYN.: v.s. ἀσθένεια.
disease, sickness: Mt 4:23, 24 8:17(Aq.) 9:35 10:1, Mk 1:34, Lk 4:40 6:17 7:21 9:1, Ac 19:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
34 βιβλίον, -ου, τό (dim. of βίβλος, q.v.), [in LXX also in the alternat. form βυβ-, chiefly for סֶפֶר and the most freq. of the cognate forms;]
1. a paper, letter, written document: β. ἀποστασίου, bill of divorce, Mt 19:7, Mk 10:4.
2. a book, a roll: Lk 4:17, 20 Jo 20:30 21:25, Ga 3:10, II Ti 4:13, He 9:19 10:7, Re 1:11 5:1-9 6:14 10:8 20:12 22:7-19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Re 13:8 17:8 20:12 21:27.†

strong.def: to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
97 ὑπ-άγω [in LXX: Ex 14:21 (הָלַךְ hi.), elsewhere only as v.l., To 8:21, al. ;]
a word of the vulgar language, in Pres. and impf. only (Bl., § 53, 1).
I. Trans.
1. to lead or bring under, subdue (Hom., Hdt., al.; Ex, l.c..
2. to lead on slowly (Hdt., Xen., al.).
II. Intrans., to go slowly away, withdraw oneself, depart (so less freq. in cl.; Thuc., Eur., al.): absol., Mt 8:32 13:44, Mk 6:33, Lk 8:42 17:14, Jo 6:67 8:2 11:44 14:5, 28 18:8; οἱ ἐρχόμενοι κ. οἱ ὑπάγοντες, Mk 6:31; ὑπῆγον κ. ἐπίστευον, Jo 12:11; ἵνα ὑπαγῆτε κ. καρπὸν ψέρητε, Jo 15:16; opp. to ἔρχεσθαι, Jo 3:8 8:14; imperat., ὕπαγε, Mt 4:10 8:13 20:14, Mk 2:9 T, 7:29 10:52; εἰς εἰρήνην (ἐν εἰ.), Mk 5:34, Ja 2:16; id. prefixed to another imperat. (Bl., § 79, 4), Mt 5:34 8:4 18:15 19:21 21:28 27:65 28:10, Mk 1:44 10:21 16:7, Jo 4:16 9:7, Re 10:8; with καί inserted, Re 16:1; euphemistically, of death, Mt 26:24, Mk 14:21; c. adv.: ποῦ (q.v.), Jo 12:35 14:5 16:5, I Jn 2:11; ὅπου (q.v.), Jo 8:21, 22 13:33, 36 14:4, Re 14:4; ἐκεῖ, Jo 11:8; c. prep.: πρός, Jo 7:33 13:3 16:5, 10, 17; εἰς, Mt 9:6 20:4, 7, Mk 2:11 11:2 14:13, Lk 19:30, Jo 6:21 7:3 9:11 11:31, Re 13:10 17:8, 11; εἰς . . . πρός, Mt 26:18, Mk 5:19; ἐπί, Lk 12:58; μετά, Mt 5:41; ὀπίσω, Mt 16:23, Mk 8:33; c. inf., Jo 21:3.†

strong.def: Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νινευΐ, ἡ (Heb. נִינְוֵה),
Nineveh: Lk 11:32, Rec.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and (to stretch);
strong.kjv: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ** ἀτενίζω (< ἀτενής, strained, intent; < τείνω), [in LXX: I Es 6:28, III Mac 2:26*;]
to look fixedly, gaze (MM, s.v.): c. dat. pers., gaze upon: Lk 4:20 22:56, Ac 3:12 10:4 14:9 23:1; seq. εἰς, c. acc. pers., Ac 3:4 6:15 13:9; metaph., Ac 1:10 7:55 11:6, II Co 3:7, 13.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G71 (ἄγω) or G2233 (ἡγέομαι);
strong.def: a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ (< στρατός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר ;] SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Ac 16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217).
1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.).
2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Ac 16:20, 22, 35, 36, 38.
3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Ac 4:1 5:24, 26; pl., Lk 22:4, 52.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) ἀντ-ε͂ιπον (ἀντί, εἶπον), [in LXX for שׁוּב hi., דבר pi., ענה, etc.;]
2 aor., without present in use, to speak against, gainsay: Lk 21:15, Ac 4:14.†

strong.def: to lead up on, i.e. (technical) to put out (to sea); (intransitively) to return

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐπ-αν-άγω [in LXX: Za 4:12 (רוּק hi.), Si 17:26 26:28, II Mac 9:21 12:4 * ;]
to bring up or back (sc. ναῦς); to put out to sea (DB, iii, 63b): Lk 5:3, 4; intrans., to return: Mt 21:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Ἀλφαῖος (WH, Ἀλ-), -ου, ὁ (Aram. חַלְפַּי)
Alphæus.
1. Father of Levi: Mk 2:14.
2. Father of James: Mt 10:3, Mk 3:13, Lk 6:15, Ac 1:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἅρπαξ, -αγος, ὁ, ἡ (< ἁρπάζω), [in LXX: Ge 49:27 (טרף)*;]
rapacious: Mt 7:15, Lk 18:11; as subst., a swindler, an extortioner (MM, s.v.), I Co 5:10, 11 6:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βύσσος, -οῦ, ἡ (cf. Heb. בּוּץ), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ ;]
byssus, a fine species of flax, also the linen made from it: Lk 16:19.†

strong.def: to take an inventory, i.e. estimate (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
40 λογίζομαι (< λόγος), [in LXX chiefly for חשׁב;]
1. prop., of numerical calculation, to count, reckon: c. acc. seq. μετά, Mk 15:23(LXX) (Rec., R, mg.), Lk 22:37.
2. Metaph., without reference to numbers, by a reckoning of characteristics or reasons;
(a). to reckon, take into account: c. acc. rei, I Co 13:5; id. seq. dat. pers., Ro 4:3(LXX), 4, 6, 8(LXX), II Co 5:19, II Ti 4:16; seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. נֶחֱשׁב לְ; Bl., § 33, 3), Ac 19:27, Ro 2:26 4:3, 5, 9-11, 22-24 9:8, Ga 3:6(LXX), Ja 2:23(LXX);
(b). to consider, calculate: c. acc. rei, Phl 4:8; seq. ὅτι, Jo 11:50, He 11:10; τοῦτο, ὅτι, II Co 10:11; c. acc. pers., c. inf., Ro 6:11; seq. ὡς, Ro 8:36(LXX);
(c). to suppose, judge, deem: I Co 13:11; ὡς, I Pe 5:12; οὕτως, I Co 4:1; c. acc. rei, II Co 3:5; id. seq. εἰς, II Co 12:6; ὅτι, Ro 8:18; τοῦτο, ὅτι, Ro 2:3, II Co 10:7; c. inf., II Co 11:5; acc. et inf., Ro 3:28 14:14, Phl 3:13; c. acc. pers. seq. ὡς, II Co 10:2;
(d). to purpose, decide: c. inf. (Eur., Or., 555), II Co 10:2 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, παρα-, συλ-λογίζομαι).†

strong.kjv: abundance, that was left, over and above

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 † περίσσευμα, -τος, τό (< περισσεύω), [in LXX: Ec 2:15*;]
that which is over and above, superfluity, abundance: opp. to ὑστέρημα (q.v.), II Co 8:13, 14; pl., Mk 8:8; metaph., π. τ. καρδίας, Mt 12:34, Lk 6:45 (cf. Ec 2:15; Plut., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 συγγένεια, -ας, ἡ (< συγγενής), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
1. kinship.
2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred: Lk 1:61, Ac 7:3, 14 †

strong.derivation: from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) or G5534 (χρή);
strong.def: employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution
strong.kjv: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
49 χρεία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: II Ch 2:16 (15) (צֹרֶךְ), II Es 7:20 (חַשְׁחוּת) freq. in Si, I-II Mac ;]
1. need, necessity: Ac 28:10, Tit 3:14; πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χ. (RV, txt., for edifying as the need may be; but v. Field, Notes, 192), Eph 4:29; ἕστι χ., Lk 10:42, He 7:11; χ. ἔχειν, c. gen., Mt 6:8 21:3, Mk 11:3, Lk 9:11 15:7 19:31, 34 22:71, Jo 13:29, I Co 12:21, 24, I Th 4:12, He 10:36, Re 21:23 22:5; seq. τοῦ, c. inf. (Bl., § 71, 3), He 5:12; absol. (sc. gen.), Ac 2:45 4:35; c. gen. pers., Mt 9:12 26:65, Mk 2:17 14:63, Lk 5:31; c. inf. (Bl., § 69, 5), Mt 3:14 14:16, Jo 13:10 , I Th 1:8 4:9; seq. ἵνα, Jo 2:25 16:30, I Jo 2:27; absol., Mk 2:25, Eph 4:28, I Jo 3:17; οὐδὲν χ. ἔχειν, Re 3:17; ἡ χ., c. gen. subjc., Phl 2:25 4:16, 19; pl., Ac 20:34, Ro 12:13.
2. matter, business (so esp. in late writers, Polyb., al.; I Mac 12:45, al.): Ac 6:3.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and G5021 (τάσσω);
strong.def: literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce
strong.kjv: bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀπο-τάσσω, [in LXX: Ec 2:20 (יאשׁ pi.), I Es 6:27, Je 20:2, I Mac4*;]
to set apart. Mid., in late Gk. (Bl., § 37, 1; Swete, Mk., 136 f.; MM, s.v.), c. dat.,
(a). to take leave of: Mk 6:46, Lk 9:61, Ac 18:18, 21, II Co 2:13;
(b). to forsake: Lk 14:33.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Ἀαρών (Heb. אַהֲרוֹן), indecl. (in FlJ, -ῶνος),
Aaron (Ex 4:14, al.): Lk 1:5, Ac 7:40, He 5:4, 7:11, 9:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
93 πούς, ποδός, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for רֶגֶל;]
a foot, both of men and beasts: Mt 4:6(LXX), Mk 9:45, Lk 1:79, Jo 11:44, Ac 7:5, al.; ὑπο τοὺς π., Ro 16:20, I Co 15:25, 27, Eph 1:22, He 2:8; ὑποκάτω τῶν π., Mt 22:44(LXX); πρὸς (παρὰ) τοὺς π., Mk 5:22, Lk 8:41, al.; fig., Mt 15:30, Lk 10:39, Ac 5:2, al.; ἔμπροσθεν τῶν π., Re 3:9 19:10, al.; ἐπὶ τοὺς π., Ac 10:25. By meton., of a person in motion (Ps 118 (119):101): Lk 1:79, Ac 5:9, Ro 3:15 10:15, He 12:13.

strong.def: to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-κύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Jb 9:27 (עזב), Si 12:11 19:26 * ;]
1. to bend forwards (Arist., al.).
2. to be bowed down: Lk 13:11.†

strong.def: a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas G5056 (τέλος) is usually a general toll on goods or travel)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 φόρος, -ου, ὁ (< φέρω), [in LXX chiefly for מַס, also for מִדָּה, etc. ;] SYN.: κῆνσος, τέλος (q.v.)
tribute paid by a subject nation (cf. I Mac 10:33): φ. δοῦναι (I Mac 8:4, 7), Lk 20:22 23:2; ἀποδοῦναι, Ro 13:7; τελεῖν, Ro 13:6 (Hdt., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
52 διό
conjunct. for δι᾽ ὅ,
wherefore, on which account: Mt 27:8, Lk 7:7, Ac 15:19, Ro 1:24, al.; δ. καί, Lk 1:35, Ac 10:29 24:26, Ro 4:22 15:22, II Co 1:20 4:13 5:9, Phl 2:9, He 11:12 13:12 (v. Ellic. on Ga 4:31).

strong.derivation: middle voice from the base of G4756 (στρατιά);
strong.def: to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT (< στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יצא, צבא; metaph., IV Mac 9:23 ;]
used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Lk 3:14, I Co 9:7, II Ti 2:4. Metaph. (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: II Co 10:3, I Ti 1:18, Ja 4:1, I Pe 2:11.†

strong.def: properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially) contrariwise (in many relations)
strong.kjv: and, but (even), howbeit, indeed, nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
638 ἀλλά (ἀλλ’ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., Pr., 93 f.; WH, App., 146), adversative particle,
stronger than δέ; prop. neuter pl. of ἄλλος, used adverbially, with changed accent; hence prop. otherwise, on the other hand (cf. Ro 3:31);
1. opposing a previous negation, but: οὐ (μὴ) . . . ἀ., Mt 5:15, 17 Mk 5:39, Jo 7:16, al.; rhetorically subordinating but not entirely negativing what precedes, οὐ . . . ἀ., not so much . . . as, Mk 9:37, Mt 10:20, Jo 12:44, al.; with ellipse of the negation, Mt 11:7-9, Ac 19:2, I Co 3:6 6:11 7:7, II Co 7:1, Ga 2:3, al.; in opposition to a foregoing pos. sentence, ἀ. οὐ, Mt 24:6, I Co 10:23; οὐ μόνον . . . ἀ. καί, Jo 5:18, Ro 1:32, al.; elliptically, after a negation, ἀ. ἵνα, Mk 14:49, Jo 1:8 9:3, al.; = εἰ μή (Bl., §77, 13; M, Pr., 241; but cf. WM, §iii, 10), Mt 20:23, Mk 4:22.
2. Without previous negation, to express opposition, interruption, transition, etc., but: Jo 16:20 12:27, Ga 2:14; before commands or requests, Ac 10:20 26:16, Mt 9:18, Mk 9:22, al.; to introduce an accessory idea, II Co 7:11; in the apodosis after a condition or concession with εἰ, ἐάν, εἴπερ, yet, still, at least, Mk 14:29, I Co 9:2, II Co 4:16, Col 2:5, al.; after μέν, Ac 4:17, Ro 14:20, I Co 14:17; giving emphasis to the following clause, ἀλλ’ ἔρχεται ὥρα, yea, etc., Jo 16:2; so with neg., ἀλλ’ οὐδέ, nay, nor yet, Lk 23:15.
3. Joined with other particles (a practice which increases in late writers; Simcox, LNT, 166), ἀ. γε, yet at least, Lk 24:21, I Co 9:2; ἄ ἤ., save only, except, Lk 12:51, II Co 1:13; ἀ. μὲν οὖν, Phl 3:8 (on this usage, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀνα-σπάω, -ῶ, [in LXX for לקח, עלה hi.;]
to draw up: Lk 14:5, Ac 11:10 (in π. of pulling up barley; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime"))
strong.kjv: avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
27 κρίμα (Bl., § 27, 2), -τος, τό (< κρίνω), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּט;]
the issue of a judicial process, hence,
1. judgment, the decision passed on the faults of others: Mt 7:2; in forensic sense, c. gen. pun., Lk 24:20; esp. of the judgment of God, Ro 2:2 5:16 11:33 (ICC, in l.), II Pe 2:3, Ju 4; κ. λαμβάι εσθαι, Mt 23:13 (Rec., R, mg.), Mk 12:40, Lk 20:47, Ro 13:2, Ja 3:1; ἔχειν, I Ti 5:12; βαστάζειν, Ga 5:10; ἐσθίειν ἑαυτῷ, I Co 11:29; εἰς κ. συνέρχεσθαι, I Co 11:34; εἶναι ἐν τ αὐτῷ κ., Lk 23:40; c. gen. obj., Ro 3:8, I Ti 3:6, Re 17:1; of God's judgment through Christ, Jo 9:39; τὸ κ. ἄρχεται, I Pe 4:17; τ. κ. τ. μέλλον, Ac 24:25; κ. αἰώνιον, He 6:2; ἔκρινεν ὁ Θεὸς τ. κ. ὐμῶν, Re 18:20; of the right of judgment, Re 20:4.
2. a matter for judgment, a law-suit, a case: I Co 6:7.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G5399 (φοβέω);
strong.def: a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φόβητρον (LTr., WH, -θρον), -ου, τό (< φοβέω), [in LXX: Is 19:17 (חָגָא) * ;]
that which causes fright, a terror: pl. (as always, exc. Is, l.c.), Lk 21:11 (Hipp., Plat.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 εἴκοσι (never -ιν in WH, cf. Bl., §5, 3, and note), indecl., οἱ, αἱ, τά,
twenty: Lk 14:31, Jo 6:19, Ac 1:15 27:28, I Co 10:8, Re 4:4, 10 5:8 11:16 19:4.†

strong.def: to stand up (literal or figurative, transitive or intransitive)
strong.kjv: arise, lift up, raise up (again), rise (again), stand up(-right)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
115 ἀν-ίστημι (ἀνά, ἵστημι), [in LXX chiefly for קוּם;] SYN.: ἐγείρω.
1. causal, in fut. and 1 aor. act., c. acc., to raise up: Ac 9:41; from death, Jo 6:39, Ac 2:32; to raise up, cause to be born or appear: Mt 22:24, Ac 3:22, 26.
2. Intrans., in mid. and 2 aor act.;
(a). to rise: from lying, Mk 1:35; from sitting, Lk 4:16; to leave a place, Mt 9:9; pleonastically, as Heb. קוּם, before verbs of going, Mk 10:1, al. (v. Dalman, Words, 23; M, Pr., 14); of the dead, Mt 17:23, Mk 8:31; seq. ἐκ νεκρῶν, Mt 17:9, Mk 9:9;
(b). to arise, appear: Ac 5:36, Ro 15:12 (cf. ἐπ-, ἐξ- ἀνίστημι, and v. Cremer, 306, 738; MM, VGT, s.v.).

strong.def: to stand apart, i.e. (reflexively) to remove, intervene
strong.kjv: go further, be parted, after the space of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δι-ίστημι (Rec. διΐσ-), [in LXX: Ez 5:1 (חלק pi.), Pr 17:9 (פּרד hi.), etc. ;]
to set apart, separate; of time (or space), to make an interval, intervene: διαστάσης ὥρας μιᾶς, Lk 22:59; βραχὺ διαστήσαντες, Ac 27:28. In pass., mid. and 2 aor., pf. and plpf. act., to part, withdraw: Lk 24:51.†

strong.def: to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 δειπνέω, -ῶ (< δεῖπνον, q.v.), [in LXX: Pr 23:1 (לחם), To 7:8 8:1, Da LXX 11:27 * ;]
to take the chief meal of the day, to dine, to sup: Lk 17:8 22:20 (WH, br., R, mg. omits), I Co 11:25; metaph., Re 3:20.†

strong.def: depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition)
strong.kjv: base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ταπεινός, -ή, -όν [in LXX for שָׁפָל, עָנִי, עָנָי, etc. ;]
low-lying; metaph.,
(a). lowly, of low degree, brought low: Ja 1:9, II Co 7:6 (cf. Si 25:23); οἱ τ., opp. to δυνάσται, Lk 1:52; τ. ταπεινοῖς (neut., R, txt.; masc., R, mg.; v. ICC, in l.), Ro 12:16;
(b). lowly in spirit, humble, in cl. usually in a slighting sense (v. Tr., Syn., § xlii; but v. also Abbott, Essays, 81), in NT in an honourable sense: II Co 10:1; seq. τ. καρδίᾳ, Mt 11:29 (cf. Ps 33 (34):19); opp. to ὑπερήφανος, Ja 4:6, I Pe 5:5 (LXX).†

strong.def: to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. incarcerate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-κλείω, [in LXX: Je 39 (32):3 (כּלא), Wi 17:2, 16, II Mac 13:21, III Mac 3:25*;]
to shut up:. c. acc. pers., seq. ἐν φυλακῇ (-αῖς), Lk 3:20, Ac 26:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 ἐκ-πλήσσω (Attic -ττω, Ac 13:12), [in LXX: (pass.) Ec 7:16, (שָׁמֵם hithp.), Wi 13:4, II Mac 7:12, IV Mac 8:4 17:16 * ;] SYN.: " πτωεῖν, to terrify, agitate with fear;
1. prop., to strike out, drive away.
2. to strike with panic or shock, to amaze, astonish: pass., Mt 13:54 19:25, Mk 6:2 7:37 10:26, Lk 2:48; seq. ἐπί, c. dat. rei, Mt 7:28 22:33, Mk 1:22 11:18, Lk 4:32 9:43, Ac 13:12.†
τρεμεῖν, to tremble, predominantly physical;
φοβεῖν, to fear, "the general term," Thayer;
cf. also φρίσσω, to shudder, and v.s. δειλία

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κυκλόω, -ῶ (< κύκλος), [in LXX chiefly for סבב;]
1. to move in a circle, revolve.
2. to surround, encircle: c. acc. pers., Jo 10:24 (WH, txt., cf. -εύω), Ac 14:20; pass., Lk 21:20, He 11:30 (cf. περι-κυκλόω).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3539 (νοιέω);
strong.def: not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination)
strong.kjv: (be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
22 ἀγνοέω, -ῶ (> ἁγνίζω), [in LXX for שׁגה, שׁגג, אשׁם, etc.;]
1. to be ignorant, not to know: absol., I Ti 1:13, He 5:2; c. acc., Ac 13:27 17:23, Ro 10:3, II Co 2:11; ἐν οἷς, II Pe 2:12; seq. ὅτι, Ro 2:4 6:3 7:1, I Co 14:38; οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, a Pauline phrase: c. acc., Ro 11:25; seq. ὑπέρ, II Co 1:8; περί, I Co 12:1, I Th 4:13. ὅτι, Ro 1:13, I Co 10:1 (for similar usage in π., V. MM, VGT, s.v.). Pass.: I Co 14:38, II Co 6:9, Ga 1:22.
2. not to understand: c. acc., Mk 9:32, Lk 9:45.†

strong.derivation: probably from G3007 (λείπω) (through the idea of destitution);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 λιμός, -οῦ, ὁ (so in Att.; in Dor. ἡ, and so sometimes in LXX, v. Th., Gr., 146; in NT: Lk 15:14, Ac 11:28; cf. M, Pr., 60), [in LXX chiefly for רָעָב;]
hunger, famine: Lk 4:25 15:14, 17, Ac 7:11(LXX) 11:28, Ro 8:35, Re 6:8 18:8; λ. καὶ δίψος, II Co 11:27; pl., Mt 24:7, Mk 13:8, Lk 21:11.†

strong.def: to tax upon, i.e. censure or admonish; by implication, forbid

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 ἐπι-τιμάω, -ῶ [in LXX for גָּעַר, Ge 37:10, Ps 9:5, Za 3:3(2); Si 11:7, al. ;] SYN.: ἐλέγχω, q.v
1. to honour.
2. to raise in price
3. to mete out due measure;
(a). to award;
(b). to censure, rebuke, admonish: absol., II Ti 4:2; c. dat., Mt 8:26 17:13 19:13, Mk 4:39 8:32 10:13, Lk 4:39, 41 8:24 9:21, 42, 55 17:3 18:15 19:39, Ju 9; seq. ἵνα, Mt 12:16 16:20 20:31, Mk 3:12 8:30 10:48, Lk 18:39; seq. λέγων, λέγει, etc., Mt 16:22, Mk 1:25 8:33 9:25, Lk 4:35 23:40.†

strong.derivation: from G4253 (πρό) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to go onward, precede (in place or time)
strong.kjv: go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 προ-έρχομαι, [in LXX: Ge 33:3, 14 R (עבר), Jth 2:19, Si 35 (32):10, al;]
1. to go forward, go on, advance: seq. μικρόν, Mt 26:39 and Mk 14:35 (WH, mg., προσελθών): ῥύμην μίαν (cf. Plat., Rep., i, 328e), Ac 12:10.
2. Of relative position, to go before, precede: c. gen. (cl.; Jth 2:19); c. acc. pers. (not cl.), Lk 22:47 (c. gen., Rec.); seq. ἐνώπιον, Lk 1:17 (cf. Ge 33:3).
3. Of time, to go before or in advance: Ac 20:5, 13 (WH, mg., R, mg.), II Co 9:5; c. acc. pers. (= cl. φθάνω), Mk 6:33.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from (a row or ring);
strong.def: to dance (from the ranklike or regular motion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὀρχέομαι, -οῦμαι, [in LXX for רקד, etc.;]
to dance; Mt 11:17 14:6, Mk 6:22, Lk 7:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀνά-λημψις, -εως, ἡ (κοινή form of ἀνάληψις; v. Th., Gr., 108 f.),
a taking up: Lk 9:51 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: neuter of (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone;
strong.def: properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀλάβαστρον, -ου, τό (also -ος, ὁ, ἡ; colloq. and κοινή for ἀλάβαστος), [in LXX: IV Ki 21:13 (צַלַּחַת)*;]
a box of alabaster (ἀλαβαστίτης) for ointment: Mt 26:7, Mk 14:3, Lk 7:37 (v. DCG, i, 41b; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπ-αιτέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Ps 108 (109):10 (H7592) Si 40:28 * ;]
1. to ask besides.
2. to beg (as a mendicant; cf. MM, Exp., xiv): Lk 16:3 18:35 (Cremer, 74).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a reduplicated derivative of the base of G939 (βάσις) (compare G307 (ἀναβιβάζω));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐπι-βιβάζω [in LXX chiefly for רָכַב hi. ;]
to place upon: c. acc pers., Lk 10:34 19:35, Ac 23:24.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as particle of union) and the base of G3045 (λιπαρός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἀλείφω (cf. λίπος, oil), [in LXX: Ge 31:13, Ex 40:15, Nu 3:3 (משׁח), Ez 13:10 ff. (טוח), Ru 3:3, II Ki 12:20 14:2, IV Ki 4:2, II Ch 28:15, Mi 6:15, Da LXX TH 10:3 (סוךְ), Es 2:12, Jth 16:8*;] SYN.: χρίω, μυρίζω (against the distinction made bet. ἀ. and χ. in Tr., Syn., § 38, v. MM, VGT, s.v., ἀ.)
to anoint, festally or in homage: c. acc rei or pers., Mt 6:17, Jo 12:3, Mk 16:1; seq. dat., ἐλαίῳ, Mk 6:13, Ja 5:14; μύρῳ, Lk 7:38, 46, Jo 11:2.†

strong.def: pay for service (literally or figuratively), good or bad

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 μισθός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for שָׂכָר;]
1. prop., wages, hire: Mt 20:8, Lk 10:7, Ro 4:4, I Ti 5:18, Ja 5:4, Ju 11; μ. ἀδικίας, Ac 1:18, II Pe 2:13 (but v. Mayor and ICC, in l.), II Pe 2:15.
2. Generally, reward: Jo 4:36, I Co 9:18; esp. of divine rewards, Mt 5:12 6:1, 2, 5 6:16 10:41, 42, Mk 9:41, Lk 6:23, 35, I Co 3:8, 14, II Jn 8, Re 11:18 22:12; ἔχειν μ., Mt 5:46, I Co 9:17.†

strong.def: to hope out, i.e. fully expect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀπ-ελπίζω, [in LXX: Is 29:19 (אֶבְיוֹן), Jth 9:11, Es 4:17, Si 22:21 27:21, II Mac 9:18*;]
1. to give up in despair, despair of (Polyb., Diod., LXX).
2. to hope to receive from or in return (Field, Notes, 59; Cremer, 712; Soph., Lex., s.v.): c. acc. (M; Pr., 65; MM, s.v.), Lk 6:35.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee origin (by parody on H01176);
strong.def: dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 Βεελζεβούλ (WH, App., 159, Rec., βεελζεβούλ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord, and the Talmudic זִבּוּל, from זֶבֶל, dung (Dalman, Gr., 137n), or perh. זְבֻל, habitation, but, v. DB, iv, 409 f.; DCG, i, 181). The AV, RV, Beelzebub, comes through Vg. from IV Ki 1:2, בַּעַל זִבוּב, lord of flies (LXX, βάαλ μυῖα, Sm., βεελζεβούβ),
Beelzebul, Beelzebub, a name of Satan: Mt 10:25 12:24, 27, Mk 3:22, Lk 11:15, 18, 19.†

strong.def: to dwell near, i.e. reside as a foreigner

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 παρ-οικέω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for גּוּר, also for ישׁב, שׁכן;]
1. in cl., to dwell beside (c. acc.), among (c. dat.) or near by (absol.).
2. In late writers, to dwell in a place as a πάροικος (q.v.) or stranger: Lk 24:18, He 11:9.†

strong.def: a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
40 θύρα, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, also for דַּל, דֶּלֶת, etc.;]
a door: κλείειν (ἀποκ-) τὴν θ., Mt 6:6, Lk 13:25; pass., Mt 25:10, Lk 11:7, Jo 20:19, 26, Ac 21:30; ἀνοίγειν, Ac 5:19; pass., Ac 16:26, 27; κρούειν, Ac 12:13; διὰ τῆς θ., Jo 10:1, 2; πρὸς τὴν θ., Mk 1:33 11:4 (WH om. τήν), Ac 3:2; τὰ πρὸς τὴν θ., the space by the door, Mk 2:2; πρὸς τῇ θ., Jo 18:16; ἐπὶ τῇ θ, Ac 5:9; πρὸ τῆς θ., Ac 12:6; ἐπὶ τῶν θ., Ac 5:23; ἡ θ. τ. μνημείου, Mt 27:60, Mk 15:46 16:3. Metaph., of Christ, ἡ θ. τ. προβάτων, Jo 10:7, 9; of the Kingdom of Heaven, Lk 13:24; of opportunities, θ. πίστεως, Ac 14:27; θ. μεγάλη, I Co 16:9; θ. τ. λόγου, Col 4:3; θ. ἀνεῳγμένη (ἠνεῳγ-), II Co 2:12, Re 3:8 4:1; of Christ, ἑστηκὼς ἐπὶ τὴν θ. καὶ κρούων, Re 3:20; of his second coming, ἐπὶ θύραις εἶναι, Mt 24:33, Mk 13:29; πρὸ θυρῶν ἑστηκέναι, Ja 5:9.†

strong.derivation: from G4413 (πρῶτος) and the alternate of G5088 (τίκτω);
strong.def: first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 πρωτότοκος, -ον (< πρῶτος, τίκτω), [in LXX chiefly for בְּכוֹר;]
first-born: Lk 2:7; pl., He 11:28. Metaph., of the priority of Christ (originally perh. a Messianic title, cf. Ps 88 (89):28, He 1:6; v. ICC on Col 1:15): He 1:6; π. πάσης κτίσεως, Col 1:15; ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, Ro 8:29; π. (ἐκ) τ. νεκρῶν, Col 1:18, Re 1:5; pl., of the elect, ἐκκλησία πρωτοτόκων, He 12:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 βρυγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< βρύχω), [in LXX: Pr 19:12 (נַהַם), Si 51:3 * ;]
a biting, a gnashing of teeth: Mt 8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Lk 13:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † τετρααρχέω (Rec. τετραρχ-; v. WH, App., 145), -ῶ (< τετραάρχης),
to be tetrarch: c. gen., Lk 3:1 (FlJ, BJ, iii, 10, 7).†

strong.def: a man (properly as an individual male)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
216 ἀνήρ, ἀνδρός, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for אִישׁ, freq. אֱנוֹשׁ, also אָדָם, etc.;] SYN.: ἄνθρωπος, q.v. (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).
a man, Lat. vir.
1. As opp. to a woman, Ac 8:12, I Ti 2:12; as a husband, Mt 1:16, Jo 4:16, Ro 7:2, Tit 1:6.
2. As opp. to a boy or infant, I Co 13:11, Eph 4:13, Ja 3:2.
3. In appos. with a noun or adj., as ἀ. ἁμαρτωλός, Lk 5:8; ἀ. προφήτης, 24:19; freq. in terms of address, as ἀ. ἀδελφοί, Ac 1:16; and esp. with gentilic names, as ἀ. Ἰουδαῖος, Ac 22:3; ἀ. Ἐφέσιοι, 19:35.
4. In general, a man, a male person: = τις, Lk 8:41, Ac 6:11.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
21 βασιλεύω, (< βασιλεύς), [in LXX for מלךְ, its parts and derivatives, exc. IV Ki 15:5 (ישׁב);]
to be king, to reign, rule: I Ti 6:15; c. gen. (cl.), Mt 2:22; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. (= Heb. מלךְ על; Bl., § 36, 8), Lk 1:33 19:14, 27, Ro 5:14; ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, on earth, Re 5:10; of God, Re 11:15, 17 19:6; of Christ, Lk 1:33, I Co 15:25, Re 11:15; of Christians, Re 5:10 20:4 (constative aor., M, Pr., 130), Re 20:6 22:5. Metaph., Christians, Ro 5:17, I Co 4:8; θάνατος, Ro 5:14, 17; ἁμαρτία, Ro 5:21 6:12. Ingressive aor. (M, Pr., 109), to begin to reign: I Co 4:8, Re 11:17 19:6 (Cremer, 137).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** φωτεινός (WH, φωτινός), ή, όν (< φῶς), [in LXX: Si 17:31 23:19 * ;]
bright, light: νεφέλη, Mt 17:5; opp. to σκοτεινός, Mt 6:22, Lk 11:34, 36.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
strong.def: to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or violate
strong.kjv: cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought, reject

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 † ἀθετέω, -ῶ (< τίθημι), [in LXX for seventeen different words, פּשׁע, מרד, בּגד, מעל, etc., often meaning, as I Ki 13:3 (Heb., al.), to revolt; properly, to make ἄθετον, or do away with what has been laid down (v. DCG, i, 453 f.)].
1. to set aside, disregard (in Gramm., to reject as spurious): διαθήκην, Ga 3:16; ἐντολήν, Mk 7:9; νόμον, He 10:28; πίστιν, I Ti 5:12.
2. to nullify, make void: Lk 7:30 (v. Field, Notes, 59), I Co 1:19, Ga 2:21.
3. to reject: Mk 6:26 (Field, op. cit., 30), Lk 10:16, Jo 12:48, I Th 4:8, Ju 8 (for exx. in π., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1121 (γράμμα). a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
63 γραμματεύς, -έως (acc. pl., -εῖς, v. Bl., §8, 2), ὁ (< γράμμα), [in LXX always for שׁטר in Hex., elsewhere chiefly for ספר;]
1. a secretary; γ. τ. πόλεως, a state-clerk: Ac 19:35.
2. In π., of a military officer (Deiss., BS, 110f.). So Jg 5:14, IV Ki 25:19 (ספר), al.
3. a scribe, a biblical scholar, teacher of the law (so first in I Es 8:3, II Es 7:6; in Lk 5:17, νομοδιδάσκαλος; in Lk 10:25, νομικός): Mt 7:29, Mk 1:22, and freq. in Gosp. γ. καὶ ἀρχιερεῖς, Mt 2:4, et al.; γ. κ. Φαρισαῖοι, Mt 5:20, et al.; γ. μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τ. οὐρ., Mt 13:52; ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ γ., I Co 1:20 (Cremer, 167; DB, iv, 420, 800).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 Ἀβιληνή v.s. Ἀβειληνή.

strong.def: a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
50 γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (< γράφω), [in LXX chiefly for כְּתָב ;]
1. a drawing, painting.
2.
(a). writing;
(b). that which is written, a writing: πᾶσα γ., II Ti 3:16; γ. ἅγιαι, Ro 1:2; προφητικαί, Ro 16:26; al αἱ γ. τ. προφητῶν, Mt 26:56; ἡ γ., αἱ γ., the sacred writings, the Scriptures (i.e. the OT; v. Milligan, NTD, 205); in pl., when the sacred writings as a whole are meant, e.g. Mt 21:42 26:54, Jo 5:39, Ro 15:4; in sing., when a particular passage is referred to, as in Lk 4:21, Jo 19:24, Ro 4:3 9:17 10:11 11:2, Ja 2:23 (Cremer, 165; DCG, ii, 584).

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G726 (ἁρπάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
66 καρπός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for פְּרִי;]
fruit: of trees, Mt 12:33 21:19, Mk 11:14, Lk 6:44 13:6, 7; of vines, Mt 21:34, Mk 12:2, Lk 20:10, I Co 9:7; of fields, Mk 4:29, Lk 12:17, II Ti 2:6, Ja 5:7; βλαστάνειν, Ja 5:18; ποιεῖν (cf. Heb. עָשָׂה פְּרִי), Mt 3:10 7:17-19 13:26, Lk 3:9 6:43 8:8 13:9, Re 22:2; διδόναι, Mt 13:8, Mk 4:7, 8; φέρειν, Mt 7:18, Jo 12:24 15:2, 4, 5, 8, 16; ἀποδιδόναι, Mt 21:41, Re 22:2; ὁ κ. τ. κοιλίας (פְּרִי בֶּטֶן, De 28:4), Lk 1:42; τ. ὀσφύος (Ge 30:2, al.), Ac 2:30.
Metaph.,
(a). of works, deeds: Mt 3:8 7:16, 20 21:43, Lk 3:8, Jo 15:8, 16; τ. πνεύματος, Ga 5:22; τ. φωτός, Eph 5:9; τ. δικαιοσύνης, Phl 1:11; σφραγίζεσθαι τὸν κ. (Deiss., BS, 238 f.), Ro 15:28; κ. ἀγαθοί, Ja 3:17;
(b). of advantage, profit: Phl 1:22 4:17; ἔχειν, Ro 1:13 6:21, 22; συνάγειν, Jo 4:36; κ. τ. δικαιοσύνης, He 12:11, Ja 3:18; of praise, καρπὸν χειλέων (Ho 14:2, al.; cf. Æsch., Eum., 830): He 13:15.†

strong.def: not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. none, nobody, nothing
strong.kjv: any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
234 οὐδείς, -δεμία, -δέν (also in WH, txt., the Hellenistic forms -θείς, -θέν, Lk 22:35 23:14, Ac 15:9 19:27 26:26, I Co 13:2, II Co 11:8; cf. Bl., § 6, 7; M, Pr., 56n, Thackeray, Gr., 58), related to μηδείς as οὐ to μή,
no, no one, none: with nouns, Lk 4:24, Jo 10:41, Ro 8:1, al.; absol., Mt 6:24, Mk 3:27, Lk 1:61, Jo 1:18, Ac 18:10, Ro 14:7, al. mult.; c. gen. partit., Lk 4:26, Jo 13:28, al.; neut., οὐδέν, Mt 10:26, al.; id. c. gen. partit., Lk 9:36, Ac 18:17, al.; οὐδὲν εἰ μή, Mt 5:13, Mk 9:29, al.; c. neg., strengthening the negation, Mk 15:4, 5, Lk 4:2, Jo 3:27, al.; adverbially, Ac 25:10, Ga 4:12, al.

strong.def: properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἄστρον, -ου, τό, [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב;]
(a). mostly in pl. (as in cl.), the stars: Lk 21:25, Ac 27:20, He 11:12;
(b). in sing. (Xen., al.), only of some noted star; the symbol or image of a star, Ac 7:43 (cf. ἀστήρ, and v. MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 ποτίζω (< πότος), [in LXX chiefly for שׁקה hi.;]
to give to drink: c. acc. pers., Mt 25:35, 37, 42 27:48, Mk 15:36, Lk 13:15, Ro 12:20; c. dupl. acc., Mt 10:42, Mk 9:41; fig., γάλα, I Co 3:2; ἐκ τ. οἴνου, Re 14:8; of plants, to water (Xen., Strab., al.; Ge 13:10), fig., I Co 3:6-8. Metaph. (cf. Is 29:10, Si 15:3), of the Spirit, I Co 12:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πτύον, -ου, τό, [in Sm.: Is 30:24*;]
a winnowing shovel or fan: Mt 3:12, Lk 3:17.†

strong.derivation: from G3361 (μή) and the neuter of G5100 (τὶς);
strong.kjv: not (the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 μή-τι, interrog. particle,
expecting a negative answer: Mt 7:16 26:22, 25, Mk 4:21 14:19, Lk 6:39, Jo 8:22 18:35, Ac 10:47, II Co 12:18, Ja 3:11; in hesitant questions (v. M, Pr., 170n), μ οὗτός ἐστιν, can this be, Mt 12:23, Jo 4:29; μ. ἄρα, II Co 1:17; on εἰ μήτι (Lk 9:13, cf. Bl., § 65, 6), v.s. εἰ.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πλατύς, -εῖα, -ύ, [in LXX for רָחָב;]
broad: Mt 7:13. As subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for רְחֹב;] a street: Mt 6:5 12:19(LXX), Mk 6:56, WH, mg., Lk 10:10 13:26 14:21, Ac 5:15, Re 11:8 21:21 22:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† ἀνα-ζάω, -ῶ, [in Al.: Ge 45:27*;]
to live again, regain life (cf. cl. ἀναβιόω; Cremer, 722; and for other exx., v MM, VGT, s.v.): metaph. of moral revival, Lk 15:24 (WH, mg., ἔζησεν); of sin, Ro 7:9.†

strong.derivation: probably contracted from (compound of G2811 (κλέος) and G3962 (πατήρ));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κλεόπας, -α (v. Bl., § 7, 2), ὁ,
Cleopas: Lk 24:18.†

strong.derivation: probably adverb of comparative from G3739 (ὅς);
strong.def: which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows)
strong.kjv: about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all speed

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
435 ὡς, adverbial form of the relative pron. ὅς, ἥ, ὅ.
I. As relat. adv. of manner, as, like as, just as, even as;
1. with a demonstrative, like οὕτως, expressed or understood: οὕτως . . . ὡς, Mk 4:26, I Co 3:15, Eph 5:28, Ja 2:12, al.; ὡς . . . οὕτως, Ac 8:32, I Co 7:17, al.; elliptically (sc. οὕτως, οὕτω), c. nom., Mt 6:29, al.; c. acc., Mt 19:19, Mk 12:31, al.; c. prep., Mt 26:55, Mk 14:48, Lk 22:52, Jo 7:10, al.; c. verb., Jo 15:6, II Co 3:1, Eph 2:3, I Th 5:6, al.; c. ptcp. (the ptcp. however not having the special force wh. it has in cl.; v. Bl., §73, 5; 74, 6), Mt 7:29, Mk 1:22, He 13:17, al.; freq implying opinion or belief, Ro 9:32; so esp, c. gen. absol., I Co 4:18, II Co 5:20, I Pe 4:12, II Pe 1:3.
2. Before numerals, about, nearly: Mk 5:13, Jo 1:40, Ac 5:7, al.
3. Before adjectives and adverbs, how: Ro 10:15 11:33, I Th 2:10; c. superl., ὡς τάχιστα, as quickly as possible, Ac 17:15.
II. As conjunction;
1. temporal,
(a). as, when, since: Mk 9:21 14:72, Lk 1:23, Jo 2:9, al.;
(b). while, when, as long as: Lk 12:58, Jo 12:36, Ga 6:10 (Field, Notes, 191); ὡς ἄν (M, Pr., 167, and v.s. ἄν), Ro 15:24, I Co 11:34, Phl 2:23.
2. Final, in order that; c. inf., in order to (M, Pr., 204n), Lk 9:52, Ac 20:24, He 7:9.

strong.def: to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
23 χαρίζομαι (< χάρις), [in LXX: Es 8:7 (נתן), Ca 1:4 א, Si 12:3, II-IV Mac 9 * ;]
1. to show favour or kindness: c. dat. pers., Ga 3:18.
2. to give freely, bestow: c. acc et dat., Lk 7:21, Ac 3:14 25:11, 16 27:24, Ro 8:32, I Co 2:12, Phl 1:29 2:9, Phm 22.
3. In late Gk. (= Lat. condonare), to grant forgiveness, forgive freely: of debt, Lk 7:42, 43 (EGT, in l.); of sin, II Co 2:7, 10 12:13, Eph 4:32, Col 2:13 3:13 (cf. DB, ii, 57a).†

strong.def: to journey together; by implication, to assemble

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 συν-πορεύομαι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX chiefly for הלךְ ;]
1. to journey together (Plat., al.): c. dat. pers., Lk 7:11 14:25 24:15.
2. to come together: Mk 10:1 (Plut., al.).†

strong.derivation: apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb;
strong.def: to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 βοάω, -ῶ (< βοή), [in LXX chiefly for זעק, צעק, קרא ;] SYN.: καλέω, to call, invite, summon; κράζω, to cry, harshly or inarticulately, as animals; κραυγάζω, intensive of κράζω. βοάω expresses emotion, whether joy, fear, etc.
1. absol., to cry, call out: Mt 3:3, 27:46, Mk 1:3 15:34, Lk 3:4 9:38 18:38, Jo 1:23, Ac 8:7 17:6 25:24, Ga 4:27.
2. C. dat., to call on for help (Heb. זעק על, Ho 7:14, al.), Lk 18:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἐσλεί (Rec. Ἐσλί, v. WH, Notes, 155), ὁ,
Esli, an ancestor of Jesus: Lk 3:25.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of (a stone) and the base of G3584 (ξηρός) (in its original sense of scraping);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † λαξευτός, -ή, όν (< λαξεύω; < λᾶς, a stone, ξέω, to scrape), [in LXX: De 4:49 (פִּסְגָּה); in Aq.: Nu 21:20; Th.: Jg 7:11*;]
hewn (in stone); Lk 23:53 (elsewhere κοινή writers use λατομητός, IV Ki 12:12, al.; cf. λατομέω).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3982 (πείθω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀπειθής, -ές (< πείθομαι), [in LXX for מרה, מְרִי, סרר;]
disobedient: absol., Lk 1:17, Tit 1:16 3:3; c. dat., Ac 26:19, Ro 1:30, II Ti 3:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἐνκάθετος (Rec. ἐγκ-), -ον (< ἐγκαθίημι), [in LXX: Jb 31:9 (אָרַב), Jb 19:12 * ;]
suborned to lie in wait, lying in wait: as subst., Lk 20:20.†

strong.def: to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 προφητεύω (< προφήτης), [in LXX chiefly for נבא ni., hith.;] SYN.: μαντεύομαι, q.v.
to be a προφήτης (q.v.), to prophesy: in the primary sense of telling forth the Divine counsels, Mt 7:22 26:68, Mk 14:65, Lk 1:67 22:64, Ac 19:6, I Co 11:4, 5 13:9 14:1, 3-5, 24, 31, 39, Re 11:3; with the idea of foretelling future events (an idea merely incidental, not essential; v. Lft., Notes, 83 f.), Mt 11:13, Ac 2:17, 18(LXX) 21:9; seq. περί, Mt 15:7, Mk 7:6, I Pe 1:10; ἐπί, c. dat., Re 10:11; λέγων, Ju 14; ὅτι, Jo 11:51.†

strong.def: Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 Βηθλέεμ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בֵּית לֶחֶם, house of bread),
Bethlehem, a town 6 m. S. of Jerusalem: Mt 2:1, 5, 6, 8, 16, Lk 2:4, 15, Jo 7:42.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5100 αὐτός, -ή, -ό, determinative pron., in late Gk. much more freq. than in cl. (WM, 178 f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., v. infr., iii);
(1). self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Lk 5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jo 2:25; αὐ. ὑμεῖς, Jo 3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Ro 15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jo 2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ, Mk 2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mk 6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mt 3:4, Mk 6:17, Jo 16:27, I Th 3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Lk 10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, s.v.);
(2). emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., § 48, 1, 2, 7), Mt 1:21 12:50, Lk 6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Mt 8:24, Mk 4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (Bl., § 48, 1), Mt 14:2, Mk 14:15, 44, Lk 1:22 2:28, al.
2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd pers., he, she, it, Mt 7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in gen. absol., Mt 9:18, Mk 13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., § 74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לֹו; WM, 184 ff.; Bl., § 50, 4; MM, s.v.), Mk 7:25, Re 3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Mt 4:23, Ac 8:5, II Co 2:13, al.; gen. αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Ro 11:11, I Th 2:19, Tit 3:5, He 2:4.
3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: He 1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mt 5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Ro 12:16 15:5, Phl 2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Ac 15:27, Ro 2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, s.v.), Ac 14:1, Lk 6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, s.v.), Mt 22:34, Ac 1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., I Co 11:5, 12:11; c. dat. (cl.), I Co 11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mk 14:39; μέτρος, Phl 1:30; πνεῦμα, I Co 12:4.

strong.def: properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
30 ἀγοράζω (< ἀγορά), [in LXX chiefly for שׁבר, קנה;]
1. to frequent the ἀγορά (Hdt., al.).
2. to buy in the market, purchase (Xen., al.; LXX; in π. very common in deeds of sale, v. MM, VGT, s.v.): absol., Mt 21:12, Mk 11:15; c. acc. rei, Mt 13:44, 46, al.; seq. παρά, c. gen. pers., Re 3:18 (LXX, Polyb.); ἐκ, Mt 27:7; c. gen. pret., Mk 6:37, al.; metaph., I Co 6:20 7:23, II Pe 2:1, Re 5:9 14:3, 4.

strong.def: to lie all around, i.e. inclose, encircle, hamper (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** περί-κειμαι, [in LXX: Ep. Je 24, 58, IV Mac 12:3*;]
1. to lie round about: μύλος, λίθος (RV, were hanged about), Mk 9:42, Lk 17:2; νεφος μαρτύρων, He 12:1.
2. to have around one, be clothed with: Ac 28:20; fig., ἀσθένειαν, He 5:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * γαλήνη, -ης, ἡ,
a calm: Mt 8:26, Mk 4:39, Lk 8:24.†

strong.def: a park, i.e. (specially), an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 παράδεισος, -ου, ὁ (an Oriental word, first used by Xen. of the parks of Persian kings and nobles), [in LXX chiefly for גַּן, Ge 1:8 ff., al.; also for עֵדֶן, Is 51:3; פַּרְדֵּס, Ne 2:8, Ec 2:5;]
1. a park, pleasure-ground, garden (LXX), an orchard (in π., v. MM, ii, xviii; Deiss., BS, 148).
2. Paradise, the abode of the blessed dead: Lk 23:43, II Co 12:4, Re 2:7.†

strong.def: a current of air, i.e. breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively, a spirit, i.e. (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, demon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy Spirit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
379 πνεῦμα, -τος, τό, (< πνέω), [in LXX chiefly and very freq. for רוּחַ;] SYN.: νοῦς, which in NT is contrasted with π. as "the action of the understanding in man with that of the spiritual or ecstatic impulse" (DB, iv, 612); ψυχή—the usual term in cl. psychology—in NT, "expresses man as apart from God, a separate individual, π. expresses man as drawing his life from God" (DB, 1-vol., 872).
1. of air in motion;
(a). wind: Jo 3:8; pl., He 1:7(LXX);
(b). breath: π. ζωῆς, Re 11:11; π. τοῦ στόματος, fig., II Th 2:8 (cf. Ps 32 (33):6).
2. Of the vital principle, the spirit (Arist., Polyb., al.): Lk 8:55, Jo 19:30, Ac 7:59, al.; opp. to σάρξ, Mt 26:41, Mk 14:38, I Co 5:5, al.; to σῶμα, Ro 8:10, I Co 6:17 7:34, I Pe 4:6; to ψυχή, Phl 1:27, He 4:12; τὸ π. καὶ ἡ ψ. καὶ τ. σῶμα, I Th 5:23 (M, Th., in l.); dat., τῷ π., in spirit, Mk 2:8 8:12, Jo 11:33 13:21, Ac 18:25, Ro 12:11, I Co 7:34, I Pe 3:18, al.; of the human spirit of Christ, Ro 1:4, I Ti 3:16.
3. spirit, i.e. frame of mind, disposition, influence: Lk 1:17, Ro 8:15, I Co 4:21, Gal 6:1, Eph 2:2, II Ti 1:7, I Jo 4:6, al.
4. An incorporeal being, a spirit: Lk 24:37, 39, Ac 23:8; π. ὁ θεός, God is spirit, Jo 4:24; πατὴρ τῶν π., He 12:9; of disembodied human beings, He 12:23, I Pe 3:19 (ICC, in l.; DB, iii, 795); of angels. He 1:14; of demons or evil spirits, Mt 8:16, Mk 9:20, Lk 9:39, al.; π. πύθωνα, Ac 16:16; πνεύματα δαιμονίων, Re 16:14; π. δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, Lk 4:33; π. ἀσθενείας (Bl., § 35, 5), Lk 13:11; π. ἀκάθαρτον, Mt 10:1, Mk 1:23, Lk 4:36, Ac 5:16; π. ἄλαλον (καὶ κωφόν), Mk 9:17, 25; πονηρόν, Lk 7:21, Ac 19:12, al.
5. Of the Holy Spirit, π. ἅγιον, τὸ ἅ. π., τὸ π. τὸ ἅ., τὸ π., π. (the article as a rule being used when the Spirit is regarded as a Person or a Divine Power, and omitted when the reference is to an operation, influence or gift of the Spirit; v. WM, 1515; Bl., § 46, 7): anarth., Mt 1:18 3:11, 16 4:1, Mk 1:8 (Swete, in l.), Mk 1:10, Lk 1:15, Jo 7:39, Ac 19:2, Ro 5:5, I Co 2:4, al.; c. art., Mt 4:1 12:31, 32, Mk 1:10 3:29, Lk 2:26, Jo 7:36 14:26, Ac 4:31 5:3, Ro 8:16, al.; (τὸ) π. (τοῦ) θεοῦ, Mt 3:16, Ro 8:9, Eph 3:16, I Jo 4:2, al.; τὸ π. τ. πατρός, Mt 10:20; π. θεοῦ ζῶντος, II Co 3:3; (τὸ) π. τοῦ κυρίου, Lk 4:18, Ac 5:9 8:39; τὸ π. Ἰησοῦ, Ac 16:7; Χριστοῦ, Ro 8:9; Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, Phl 1:19; τὸ π. τ. ἀληθείας, Jo 15:26 16:13, I Jo 4:6; λείγει (μαρτυρεῖ) τὸ π. (τὸ ἅγιον), Ac 21:11 28:25, I Ti 4:1, He 3:7 10:15, Re 14:13; seq. τ. ἐκκλησίαις, Re 2:7, 11, 17, 29, 3:6, 13, 22; ἐν τ. π., Lk 2:27; κατὰ πνεῦμα, Ro 8:4, 5; ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ π., Jo 3:5; διὰ πνεύματος αἰωνίου, He 9:14; ἐν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος, II Th 2:18, I Pe 1:2; ἓν π., I Co 12:13, Eph 2:18 4:4; ὁ δὲ κύριος τὸ π. ἐστιν, II Co 3:17; of that which is effected or governed by the Spirit, opp. to γράμμα, Ro 2:29 7:6, II Co 3:6.

strong.def: a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 σύνεσις, -εως, ἡ (< συνίημι), [in LXX for בִּינָה and cogn. forms, מַשְׂכִּית, דַּעַת, חׇכְמָה, etc. ;] SYN.: v.s. σοφία
1. a running or flowing together (Hom.).
2. (a) understanding: Lk 2:47, I Co 1:19 (LXX), Eph 3:4, Col 1:9 2:2, II Ti 2:7
(b). the understanding, the mind or intelligence: Mk 12:33.†

strong.def: the dell; Caiaphas (i.e. Cajepha), an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 Καιάφας (T, Καϊ-), -α ὁ,
Caiaphas (on the name, v. Exp. Times, x, 185): Mt 26:3, 57, Lk 3:2, Jo 11:49 18:13, 14, 24, 28, Ac 4:6.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G1349 (δίκη);
strong.def: to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce guilty

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
0 δικάζω ,
to judge: Lk 6:37 (Tr., mg.; v.s. καταδ- ; Cremer, 199).†

strong.def: to stone down, i.e. to death

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατα-λιθάζω (= cl. -θόω; cf. -θοβολέω, Ex 17:4, Nu 14:10),
to cast stones at, to stone: Lk 20:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἀράμ indec. (Heb. רָם),
Aram: Mt 1:3, 4, Lk 3:33 (R, txt., WH, Ἀρνεί).†

(cl.), Lk 1:73; c. acc. (of that by which one swears; cl., v. MM, xviii), Ja 5:12; seq. κατά, c. gen. (LXX; Bl., § 34, 1), He 6:13, 16; seq. ἐν (εἰς), as in Heb. classic.entry: 6 (KJV) Ἰούδα, v.s. Ἰούδας.

strong.derivation: a primary particle of present time;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
147 νῦν, adv., [in LXX chiefly for עַתָּה;]
1. prop., of time, now, i.e. at the present time: as opp. to past, Jo 4:18, Ac 7:52, Ro 13:11, II Co 7:9, Col 1:24, al.; opp. to fut., Jo 12:27, Ro 11:31, al.; c. art., ὁ (ἡ, τὸ) et subst., the present: Ro 3:26, Ga 4:25, I Ti 6:17, Tit 2:12, al.; ἀπὸ τοῦ ν. (LXX for מֵעַתָּה), Lk 1:48, Ac 18:6, al.; ἄχρι τοῦ ν., Ro 8:22, Phl 1:5; ἕως τοῦ ν. (LXX for עַתָּה עַד), Mt 24:21, Mk 13:19; τὰ ν., as regards the present, Ac 5:38; c. pret., just now, but now, Mt 26:65, Jo 11:8 21:10; c. fut., now, presently, Jo 12:31, Ac 20:22; so c. praes., presently, forthwith, Jo 12:31 17:13; καὶ ν., Jo 11:22 17:5, al.; ἀλλὰ ν., Lk 22:36; ἔτι ν., I Co 3:2; τότε (πότε) . . . ν. (δέ), Ro 6:21 11:30; ν. ἤδη, I Jo 4:3; ν. οὖν, Ac 10:33, al.
2. Of logical sequence (often difficult to disting. from the temporal sense; cf. Lft., Notes, 113 f.), now, therefore, now, however, as it is: Lk 11:39; καὶ ν., Ac 3:17, II Th 2:6, I Jo 2:28; id. seq. δεῦρο, Ac 7:34; ν. δέ, Jo 8:40 9:41 15:22, 24 18:36, I Co 5:11 7:14 12:20, al. (cf. WM, 57911).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.entry:

pleasure: II Pe 2:12; pl., Lk 8:14, Tit 3:3, Ja 4:1, 3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

an egg: Lk 11:12.†

substance, property: Lk 15:12, 13.†

to deride, laugh scornfully at: c. gen. pers., Mt 9:24, Mk 5:40, Lk 8:53.†

strong.def: properly, through (all over), i.e. around; figuratively with respect to; used in various applications, of place, cause or time (with the genitive case denoting the subject or occasion or superlative point; with the accusative case the locality, circuit, matter, circumstance or general period)
strong.kjv: (there-)about, above, against, at, on behalf of, X and his company, which concern, (as) concerning, for, X how it will go with, ((there-, where-)) of, on, over, pertaining (to), for sake, X (e-)state, (as) touching, (where-)by (in), with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
333 περί, prep. c. gen., acc. (in cl. also c. dat.; cf. M, Pr., 105f.),
with radical sense round about (as distinct from ἀμφί, on both sides).
I. C. gen.,
1. of place, about (poët.).
2. Causal, about, on account of, concerning, in reference to: Mt 2:8, Mk 1:44, Lk 4:38, Jo 16:26, Ac 28:21, al. mult.; τὰ περί, c. gen., the things concerning one, one's state or case: Mk 5:27, Ac 1:3 28:15, Eph 6:22, al.; at the beginning of a sentence, περί, regarding, as to, I Co 7:1, al.; in the sense on account of (Mt 26:28, I Co 1:13, al.), often with ὑπέρ as variant (cf. M, Pr., 105).
II. C. acc.,
1. of place, about, around: Mt 3:4, Mk 1:6, Lk 13:8, Ac 22:6, al.; οἱ περί, c. acc. pers., of one's associates, friends, etc., Mk 4:10, Lk 22:49, Jo 11:19, Ac 13:13; οἱ περὶ τ. τοιαῦτα ἐργάται, Ac 19:25; metaph., about, as to, concerning: I Ti 1:19 6:4, II Ti 2:18 3:8, Tit 2:7; τὰ περὶ ἐμέ, Phl 2:23; αἱ περὶ τ. λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι, Mk 4:19.
2. Of time, in a loose reckoning, about, near: Mt 20:3, 5, 6, 9 27:46, Mk 6:48, Ac 10:3, 9 22:6.
III. In composition: round about (περιβάλλω, περίκειμαι), beyond, over and above (περιποιέω, περιλείπω), to excess (περιεργάζομαι, περισσεύω).

classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἁλεεύς (Rec. ἁλιεύς, the older form; WH, App., 151, -έως, ὁ (< ἅλς, the sea), [in LXX for דָּג, דַּוָּג;]
a fisherman: Mt 4:18, 19, Mk 1:16, 17, Lk 5:2.

strong.def: to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively) extol

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 μεγαλύνω (< μέγας), [in LXX chiefly for גּדל pi., hi.;]
1. to make great: Mt 23:5, Lk 1:58.
2. to declare great, extol, magnify: Lk 1:46, Ac 5:13 10:46 19:17, II Co 10:15; pass., seq. ἐν, Phl 1:20.†

strong.def: to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-παρα-γίνομαι (Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Ps 82 (83):8 (לוה ni.) * ;]
1. to come up or be present together: seq. ἐπί, Lk 23:48.
2. to come up to assist (Thuc., al.; II Ti 4:16, Rec.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λεῖος, -εία, -εῖον, [in LXX: Ge 27:11, I Ki 17:40 R (חָלָק, חַלּוּק); ὁδὸς λ., Is 40:4 Α (בִּקְעָה); Pr 2:20 12:13 26:23*;]
smooth: opp. to τραχύς, Lk 3:5(LXX).†

strong.def: a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σιδώνιος, -α, -ον (< Σιδών),
of Sidon, Sidonian;
(a). the region: sc. χώρα, Lk 4:26;
(b). the people: Ac 12:20.†

strong.derivation: including the comparative ; a primary word;
strong.def: "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
24 νέος, -α, -ον, [in LXX for נַעַר (Ge 37:2, Ex 33:11, al.), חָדָשׁ (Le 23:16, Nu 28:26, al.), etc.; compar. -ώτερος for קָטֹן, צָעִיר, etc.;] SYN.: καινός, q.v.
1. young, youthful: Tit 2:4.
2. new (prop., in respect of time; v.s. καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, Mt 26:29), Mt 9:17, Mk 2:22, Lk 5:37-[39]; φύραμα (fig.), I Co 5:7; διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., He 9:15), He 12:24; metaph., ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, Eph 2:15), Col 3:10.
3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: Lk 15:12, 13 22:26, Jo 21:18; pl., οἱ ν., Ac 5:6 (Rackham, in l.), I Ti 5:11, Tit 2:6; opp. to πρεσβύτεροι, I Ti 5:1, I Pe 5:5; αἱ ν., I Ti 5:2, 14.
4. Νέα Πόλις, Neapolis: Ac 16:11 (Rec., Νεάπολις, q.v.)

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of a primary (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form pimplemi);
strong.def: to "fill" (literally or figuratively (imbue, influence, supply)); specially, to fulfil (time)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
24 (KJV) πίμπλημι, [in LXX chiefly for מלא, also for שׂבע;] trans. form in pres. and impf. of πλήθω (intrans. in these tenses), which supplies the other tense forms; SYN.: πληροφορέω, πληρόω.
to fill: c. acc., Lk 5:7; c. acc. et gen., Mt 27:48; pass., Mt 22:10, Ac 19:29; of that which fills or takes possession of the mind: pass., c. gen., Lk 1:15, 41, 67 4:28 5:26 6:11, Ac 2:4 3:10 4:8, 31 5:17 9:17 13:9, 45. Metaph. (as in LXX for מלא: Ge 29:27, Jb 15:32), to complete, fulfil: pass., of prophecy, Lk 21:22; of time, Lk 1:23, 57 2:6, 21, 22 (cf. ἐμ-πίμπλημι).†

strong.derivation: accusative case singular masculine of G3778 (οὗτος);
strong.def: this (person, as objective of verb or preposition)
an intensive form of , to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow)
strong.kjv: cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
143 ἀφ-ίημι, [in LXX for נשׂא, נוח hi., נתן, סלח ni., עזב, etc.;]
1. to send forth, send away, let go: of divorce (DB, iii, 274a), τ. γυναῖκα (Hdt.), I Co 7:11-13; of death, τ. πνεῦμα (Ge 35:18, Hdt., al.), Mt 27:50; (φωνήν, to utter a cry, Mk 15:37; of debts, to remit, forgive (cl.), τ. δανεῖον, Mt 18:27; τ. ὀφειλήν, Mt 18:32; esp. of sins (Cremer 296 f.), τ. ἁμαρτίας, ἁμαρτήματα, ἀνομίας, Mt 9:2, Ro 4:7(LXX), I Jo 1:9, al.; punctiliar and iterative pres. (M, Pr., 119), Mk 2:5, Lk 11:4; Ion. pf., ἀφέωνται (M, Pr., 38), Lk 5:23.
2. to leave alone, leave, neglect: Mt 4:11 5:24 15:14, Mk 1:20, 31, Jo 4:3, 28 al.; τ. ἐντολὴν τ. θεοῦ, Mk 7:8; τὸν τ. ἀρχῆς τ. Χριστοῦ λόγον, He 6:1; τ. ὀγάπην τ. πρώτην, Re 2:4; ptcp., ἀφείς, pleonastic (as in Aram.; M, Pr., 14; Dalman, Words, 21 f.), Mt 13:36 22:22, Mk 8:13, al.
3. to let, suffer, permit: Mt 3:15; c. acc., Mt 3:15, 19:14, al.; c. acc. rei et dat. pers., Mt 5:40; c. inf. pres., Mt 23:14, al.; aor., Mk 5:37, al.; in late Gk. (M, Pr., 175 f.), seq. ἵνα, Mk 11:16, Jo 12:7; c. subjunct. (M, Pr., 175 f.; Bl., § 64, 2), Mt 7:4 27:49, Mk 15:36, Lk 6:42 (see further MM, s.v.).

strong.def: to estop, i.e. prevent (by word or act)
strong.kjv: forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
23 κωλύω (< κόλος), [in LXX for כּלא, מנע, etc.;]
to hinder, restrain, forbid, withhold: c. acc. et inf., Mt 19:14, Lk 23:2, Ac 8:36 16:6 24:23, I Th 2:16, He 7:23; inf. om., Mk 9:38, 39 10:14, Lk 9:49, 50 11:52 18:16, Ac 11:17, Ro 1:13, III Jn 10; acc. om., I Ti 4:3; c. acc. pers. et gen. rei, Ac 27:43; c. acc. rei, I Co 14:39, II Pe 2:16; id. seq. τοῦ μή, Ac 10:47; id. seq. ἀπό (like Heb. כָּלָא מִן, Ge 23:6, al.), Lk 6:29 (cf. δια-κωλύω).†

strong.def: byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 σινδών, -όνος, ἡ [in LXX: Jg 14:12, 13A, Pr 31:24 (סָדִין), I Mac 10:64 A * ;]
fine linen cloth;
(a). as used for swathing dead bodies (cf. Hdt., ii, 86): Mt 27:59, Mk 15:46, Lk 23:53;
(b). a garment or wrap of this material (cf. ICC, Jg, l.c.): Mk 14:51, 52.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G1097 (γινώσκω);
strong.def: the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
