classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 νοέω -ῶ (< νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בּין, also for שׂכל hi., etc;]
1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, v. MM, xvii): absol., Mt 16:9, Mk 8:17; c. acc., Eph 3:4, I Ti 1:7; c. dat. instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jo 12:40; pass., Ro 1:20; seq. ὅτι, Mt 15:17 16:11, Mk 7:18; c. acc. et inf., He 11:8.
2. to think, consider: absol., Mt 24:15, Mk 13:14, Eph 3:20; c. acc. rei, II Ti 2:7. (cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†

strong.derivation: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of G3563 (νοῦς) and G2192 (ἔχω);
strong.def: in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * νουνεχῶς, adv. (< νοῦς, ἔχω),
sensibly, discreetly: Mk 12:34.†

strong.def: by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ξέστης, -ου, ὁ (a Sicilian corruption of Lat. sextarius), [in Al.: Le 14:10 (לֹג, LXX κοτύλη)*;]
1. a sextarius (about a pint).
2. In NT, a pitcher of wood or stone: Mk 7:4.†

strong.derivation: feminine (abstract) of a compound of G3624 (οἶκος) and the base of G1430 (δῶμα);
strong.def: architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 † οἰκοδομή, -ῆς, ἡ (< οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), [in LXX: I Ch 29:1 A (בִּירָה), Ez 17:17 40:2 (בּנה, מִבְנֶה), Si 22:16 40:19, al.;] = cl. οἰκοδομία (q.v.), -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.),
1. the act of building; in NT always metaph., building up, edifying: Ro 14:19 15:2, I Co 14:26, II Co 10:8 13:10, Eph 4:29; c. gen. obj., I Co 14:12, II Co 12:19, Eph 4:12, 16; λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ., I Co 14:3.
2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: Mt 24:1, Mk 13:1, 2; metaph., I Co 3:9, II Co 5:1, Eph 2:21.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to G3588 (ὁ), G3739 (ὅς), and G3745 (ὅσος);
strong.def: such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with negative, not so
strong.kjv: so (as), such as, what (manner of), which

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 οἷος, -α, -ον, relat. pron.,
qualitative (related to ὅς as qualis to qui), what sort or manner of, such as, in NT usually without its correl. τοιοῦτος: Mt 24:21, Mk 9:3, II Co 12:20, I Th 1:5, II Ti 3:11, Re 16:18; seq. τοιοῦτος, I Co 15:48, II Co 10:11; id. redundant, Mk 13:19; τ. αὐτὸν . . . σἷον, Phl 1:30; οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι, elliptically, but it is not as though (RV), Ro 9:6.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of a compound of G3650 (ὅλος) and a derivative of G2545 (καίω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ὁλοκαύτωμα, -τος, τό (< ὅλος, καίω), [in LXX chiefly for עֹלָה;]
a whole burnt offering: Mk 12:33, He 10:6, 8(LXX) (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 113 f.).†

strong.def: a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὄμμα, -τος, τό, in cl. chiefly poët.; [in LXX for עַיִן (Pr5, Wi2, IV Mac3)*;]
an eye: pl., Mt 20:34, Mk 8:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὁμοιάζω (< ὅμοιος),
to be like: Mt 23:27 (L, Tr., txt., WH, mg.) Mt 26:73 (WH, mg.) (not found elsewhere. Cf. παρ-ομοιάζω.)†

strong.def: belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a ass)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ὀνικός, -ή, -όν (< ὄνος),
of or for an ass: μύλος ὀ., Mt 18:6, Mk 9:42 (elsewhere only in π.; v. MM, xviii).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary (a bound or limit);
strong.def: a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ὅριον, -ου, τό (< ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX chiefly for גְּבוּל;]
a boundary, bound; chiefly in pl., and so always in NT: Mt 2:16 4:13 8:34 15:22, 39 19:1, Mk 5:17 7:24, 31 10:1, Ac 13:50.†

strong.def: to put on oath, i.e. make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὁρκίζω (< ὅρκος), [in LXX: Ge 24:37, al. (שׁבע hi.);]
1. to make one swear (Xen., Polyb., a1.).
2. to adjure: c. dupl. acc., Mk 5:7, Ac 19:13 (cf. ἐν-, ἐξ-ορκίζω).†

strong.def: to "burrow" in the ground, i.e. dig

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὀρύσσω, [in LXX chiefly for חפר, also for כּרה, etc.;]
to dig: c. acc., ληνόν, Mt 21:33; ὑπολήνιον, Mk 12:1; γῆν, Mt 25:18 (cf. δι-, ἐξ-ορύσσω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† οὐά, interj. of wonder or irony,
ah! ha!: Mk 15:29.†

strong.derivation: from the same as G3694 (ὀπίσω) (through the idea of backwardness);
strong.def: (adverbially) late in the day; by extension, after the close of the day

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὀψέ, adv. of time, [in LXX: Ge 24:11, Ex 30:8 (עֶרֶב, הָעַרְבַּיִם בֵּין), Je 2:23; τὸ ὀ., Is 5:11 (נֶשֶׁף)*;]
1. long after, late.
2. late in the day, at evening (opp. to πρωί); in late writers used almost as an indecl. noun (v. MM, xviii): Mk 11:11, 19 13:35.
3. C. gen., late in or on; and, in late writers also after (M, Pr., 72 f.), a sense which seems to be required in Mt 28:1.†

strong.def: late; feminine (as noun) afternoon (early eve) or nightfall (later eve)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 ** ὄψιος, -α, -ον (< ὀψέ),
late: ἡ ὥρα, Mk 11:11 (Rec., WH, mg.). In late writers, ἡ ὀψία (sc. ὥρα), as subst., evening [in LXX: Jth 13:1*]: Mt 8:16 14:15, 23 16:2 20:8 26:20 27:57, Mk 1:32 4:35 6:47 14:17 15:42, Jo 6:16, 20:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παιδιόθεν (< παιδίον), adv., [in LXX: Ge 47:3*;]
= cl. ἐκ παιδός, παιδίου, from childhood: Mk 9:21.†

strong.def: to lead near, i.e. (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 παρ-άγω, [in LXX chiefly for עבר;]
1. trans., to lead by, lead aside, lead into, lead forward, etc.
2. Intrans.,
(a). to pass by: Mt 9:9, 27 20:30, Mk 2:14 15:21, Jo 8:59 R, txt., 9:1; seq. παρό, c. acc., Mk 1:16;
(b). to go away, depart; metaph., to pass away: I Co 7:31; mid., I Jo 2:8, 17.†

strong.def: to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 παρα-δέχομαι, [in LXX: Ex 23:1 (נשׂא), Pr 3:12 (רצה), II Mac 4:22 R, III Mac 7:12*;]
to receive, admit;
(a). of things: Mk 4:20, Ac 15:4 16:21 22:18, I Ti 5:19;
(b). of persons: He 12:6(LXX).†

strong.def: transmission, i.e. (concretely) a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 παρά-δοσις, -εως, ἡ (< παραδίδωμι), [in LXX: Es 7:26 (אֱסוּר), Je 39 (32):4 (נתן ni.), Je 41 (34):2*;]
1. a handing down or over, transfer, transmission (Arist., Polyb., al., LXX).
2. tradition of doctrine (Plat., Epict., al.); by meton., of the doctrine itself : Mt 15:2, 3, 6, Mk 7:3 ff., I Co 11:2, Ga 1:14, Col 2:8, II Th 2:15 3:9.†

strong.def: to mishear, i.e. (by implication) to disobey

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 παρ-ακούω, [in LXX: Es 3:3, 8 (עבר, עשׂה, c. neg.) 4:14 7:4 (חרשׁ hi.), Is 65:12 (שׁמע, c. neg.), I Es 4:11, To 3:4*;]
1. to overhear.
2. to hear amiss or imperfectly.
3. Later (as in LXX, Polyb., Plut.; also in π., v. MM, xviii), to hear without heeding, take no heed: Mk 5:36; c. gen., Mt 18:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 *† παρα-λυτικός, -ή, -όν (< παραλύω),
paralytic: Mt 4:24 8:6 9:2, 6, Mk 2:3-5, 9, 10, Lk 5:24 (Rec., WH, mg.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 παρα-πορεύομαι, [in LXX chiefly for עבר;]
1. to go beside, accompany.
2. to go past, pass by: Mt 27:39, Mk 11:20 15:29; seq. διά, c. gen., Mk 2:23 9:30 (WH, mg.).†

strong.def: a side-slip (lapse or deviation), i.e. (unintentional) error or (wilful) transgression

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 † παρά-πτωμα, -τος, τό (< παραπίπτω), [in LXX for מַעַל, פֶּשַׁע, etc.;]
1. a false step, a blunder (Polyb.).
2. Ethically, a misdeed, trespass (LXX): Mt 6:14, 15, Mk 11:25, 26, Ro 4:25 5:15 ff. Ro 11:11, 12, II Co 5:19, Ga 6:1, Eph 1:7 2:1, 5, Col 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρ-όμοιος, -ον (also -η (Hdt.), -α (Arist.), -ον),
much like, like: Mk 7:13.†

strong.derivation: from G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G4483 (ῥέω);
strong.def: all out-spokenness, i.e. frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication, assurance
strong.kjv: bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly(-ness)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
31 παρρησία, -ας, ἡ (< πᾶς + ῥῆσις, speech), [in LXX: Le 26:13 (μετὰ π., קוֹמְמִיּוּת), Pr 1:20 10:10, Wi 5:1, al.;]
1. freedom of speech, plainness, openness, freedom in speaking (Eur., Plat., al.): Ac 4:13, II Co 3:12; παρρησίᾳ, adverbially, freely, openly, plainly, Mk 8:32, Jo 7:13, 26 10:24 11:14 16:29 18:20; opp. to ἐν παροιμίαις, Jo 16:25; ἐν π., Eph 6:19; μετὰ π., Ac 2:29 4:29, 31 28:31.
2. In LXX (I Mac 4:18, Wi 5:1, al.), FlJ, and NT, also (from the absence of fear which accompanies freedom of speech), confidence, boldness: II Co 7:4, Phl 1:20, I Ti 3:13; ἔχειν π., Eph 3:12, Phm 8, He 3:6 10:19, 35, I Jo 2:28 3:21 4:17 5:14; μετὰ π., He 4:16; ἐν π., Col 2:15; id. (as בפרהסיא in Rabbinic lit.; v. Westc., Jo., i, 262), in public, Jo 7:4 and (without ἐν) 11:54.†

strong.derivation: dative case feminine of a derivative of G4228 (πούς) (as adverb);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πεζός, -ή, -όν (< πούς), [in LXX for רַגְלִי;]
1. on foot: Mt 14:13 (WH, mg., R, txt.).
2. Opp. to going by sea, by land: Mt 14:13 (WH, mg., R, mg.).
3. As adv., πεζῇ (sc. ὁδῷ), on foot or by land: Mt 14:13 (WH, txt.), Mk 6:33.†

strong.def: to take around (as a companion); reflexively, to walk around

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 περι-άγω, [in LXX: Am 2:10 (הלךְ hi.); Is 28:27, Ez 47:2 (סבב hi., ho.); Ez 37:2 46:21 (עבר hi), II Mac 4:38 6:10*;]
1. to lead about or around: c. acc. pers., I Co 9:5.
2. Intrans., to go about: Ac 13:11; seq. ἐν, Mt 4:23; c. acc. loc. (governed by the περι-, not so in cl., v. Bl., § 34, 1; 53, 1), Mt 9:35 23:15, Mk 6:6.†

strong.derivation: from G4012 (περί) (in the sense of beyond);
strong.def: superabundant (in quantity) or superior (in quality); by implication, excessive; adverbially (with G1537 (ἐκ)) violently; neuter (as noun) preeminence
strong.kjv: exceeding abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, exceedingly, very highly, beyond measure, more, superfluous, vehement(-ly)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 περισσός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX for יֶתֶר and cogn. forms;]
1. more than sufficient, over and above, abundant: Jo 10:10, II Co 9:1; c. gen. (a popular substitute for πλειών, Bl., § 11, 34), Mt 5:37; id. c. ellips. gen., Mt 5:47 (EV, more than others; but v. infr.); ἐκ περισσοῦ, Mk 6:51, Rec., T. (on ὑπὲρ ὲκ π., v.s. ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ). Compar. neut., -ότερον: Lk 12:4, 48; c. gen., Mk 12:33; adverbially (cf. περισσῶς), more abundantly, II Co 10:8, He 6:17 7:15; c. gen., π. πάντων, I Co 15:10; pleonast., μᾶλλον π., Mk 7:36.
2. out of the common, pre-eminent, superior: Mt 5:47 (Thayer, s.v., but v. supr.); τὸ π., as subst., Ro 3:1; compar., -ότερος, c. gen., Mt 11:9, Lk 7:26; c. subst., Mk 12:40, Lk 20:47, I Co 12:23, 24, II Co 2:7.†

strong.kjv: more abundantly, a great deal, far more

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 περισσότερον, -ως, v.s. περισσῶς.

strong.kjv: exceedingly, out of measure, the more

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 περισσῶς, adv. (περισσός), [in LXX: Ps 30 (31):23 (עַל־יֶתֶר), Da TH 7:7, 19 8:9 (יַתִּירָה, יֶתֶר), II Mac 8:27 12:44 A*;]
beyond measure, exceedingly, abundantly: Mt 27:23, Mk 10:26 15:14, Ac 26:11. Compar.
(a). περισσότερον (v.s. περισσός);
(b). περισσοτέρως: II Co 1:12 2:4 7:15 11:23, Ga 1:14, Phl 1:14, I Th 2:17, He 2:1 13:19; π. μᾶλλον, II Co 7:13; opp. to ἧττον, II Co 12:15.†

strong.def: to place around; by implication, to present
strong.kjv: bestow upon, hedge round about, put about (on, upon), set about

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 περι-τίθημι, [in LXX for נתן, שׂוּם, etc.;]
to place or put around: c. acc. et dat., Mt 21:33 27:48, Mk 12:1 15:36, Jo 19:29; of garments, etc., to put on: Mt 27:28 Mk 15:17 (Si 6:31). Metaph., like περιβάλλω, to bestow, confer (Thuc., al., Es 1:20): I Co 12:23.†

strong.derivation: from G4012 (περί) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 περι-τρέχω, [in LXX: Am 8:12, Je 5:1 (שׁוּט pi.)*;]
to run about: c. acc. loc., Mk 6:55.†

strong.def: to convey around, i.e. transport hither and thither

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 περι-φέρω, [in LXX: Ec 7:8 (7) (הלל po.), al.;]
to carry about: Mk 6:55, II Co 4:10. Pass., metaph.: Eph 4:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * πετρώδης, -ες (< πέτρα, εἶδος),
rock-like, rocky, stony: τὸ, τὰ π., of shallow soil with underlying rock, Mt 13:5, 20, Mk 4:5, 16.†

strong.derivation: probably from G4078 (πήγνυμι) (through the idea of gushing plumply);
strong.def: a fount (literally or figuratively), i.e. source or supply (of water, blood, enjoyment) (not necessarily the original spring)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 πηγή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for עַיִן, also for מָקוֹר, etc.;]
a spring, fountain: Ja 3:11, II Pe 2:17; τ. ὑδάτων, Re 8:10 14:7 16:4; of a well fed by a spring, Jo 4:6; π. τοῦ αἵματος, of a flow of blood, Mk 5:29; metaph., Jo 4:14, Re 7:17 21:6.†

strong.def: from the base of G4008 (πέραν)); to traffic (by travelling), i.e. dispose of as merchandise or into slavery (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 πιπράσκω, [in LXX chiefly for מכר ni.;]
to sell: c. acc. rei, Mt 13:46 (on this pf., v. Bl., § 59, 5), Ac 2:45 4:34 5:4; c. gen. (of price), Mt 26:9, Mk 14:5, Jo 12:5; c. acc. pers. (of slavery), Mt 18:25; hence metaph., Ro 7:14 (cf. IV Ki 17:17, I Mac 1:15, al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† πιστικός, -ή, -όν (πίστις),
1. having the gift of persuasion (Plat., Gorg., 455 A).
2.
(a). of persons, faithful, trusty (Plut.);
(b). of things, trustworthy, genuine: νάρδος π., Mk 14:3, Jo 12:3.†

strong.def: the largest number or very large

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 3 πλεῖστος, πλείων, v.s. πολύς.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πλέκω, [in LXX: Ex 28:14 (עֲבֹת), Is 28:5 (צְפִירָה)*;]
to plait, twist, weave: Mt 27:29, Mk 15:17, Jo 19:2.†

strong.def: repletion or completion, i.e. (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period)
strong.kjv: which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 πλήρωμα, -τος, τό (< πληρόω), [in LXX for מְלֹא;]
the result of the action involved in πληρόω (Lft., Col., 255 ff.; AR, Eph., 255 ff.), hence,
1. in passive sense, that which has been completed, complement, plenitude, fullness (in Xen., Luc., Polyb., al., of a ship's crew or cargo, and by meton. of the ship itself): Jo 1:16, Ro 11:12, 25 15:29, I Co 10:26(LXX), Eph 1:23 (AR, 42 ff.) 3:19 (AR. 87 ff.) 4:13, Col 1:19 2:9; of time, Ga 4:4, Eph 1:10; κοφίνων (σφυρίδων) πληρώματα, basketfuls, Mk 6:43 8:20.
2. In active sense (= πλήρωσις, as freq. in words of these formations, cf. κτίσις, and v. MM, xx);
(a). that which fills up (but v. Lft., Col., 255 ff.): Mt 9:16, Mk 2:21;
(b). a filling up, completing, fulfilment: Ro 13:10.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4143 (πλοῖον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 * πλοιάριον, -ου, τό (dimin. of πλοῖον),
a boat: Mk 3:9, Lk 5:2 (πλοῖα, WH, txt., R), Jo 6:22, 23 (πλοῖα, WH) 24 21:8.†

strong.def: to wheeze, i.e. (causative, by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πνίγω, [in LXX: I Ki 16:14, 15 (בּעת pi.)*;]
to choke: c. acc., Mt 13:7 (WH, mg.); impf. (conative), Mt 18:28; of drowning, pass., Mk 5:13 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐπι-, συν-πνίγω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 πολλάκις, adv. (< πολύς),
often: Mt 17:15, al.

strong.kjv: costly, very precious, of great price

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πολυτελής, -ές (< πολύς, τέλος), [in LXX for יָקָר, etc.;]
very costly, very precious, of great value: Mk 14:3, I Ti 2:9; metaph., I Pe 3:4.†

strong.def: harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively, idolatry

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 πορνεία, -ας, ἡ (< πορνεύω), [in LXX for זְנוּנִים, תַּזְנוּת and cogn. forms;]
fornication: Ac 15:20, 29 21:25, I Co 5:1 6:13, 18, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:19, Eph 5:3, Col 3:5, I Th 4:3 (Lft., Notes, 53), Re 9:21; pl. (v. WM, 220; Bl., § 32, 6), I Co 7:2; disting. from μοιχεία, Mt 15:19, Mk 7:21; = μοιχεία (Am 8:17, Si 23:23, al.), Mt 5:32 19:9. Metaph. (of idolatry: De 23:2, Ho 1:2): Jo 8:41 (Westc., in l.), and so perh. (Thayer-Grimm, s.v.; but v. Swete, in ll.), Re 2:21 14:18 17:2, 4 18:3 19:2.†

strong.def: the prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 *† πραιτώριον, -ου, τό, (Lat. prætorium),
1. headquarters in a Roman camp.
2. The palace or official residence of the Governor of a province: Mt 27:27, Mk 15:16 (v. Swete, in l.), Jo 18:28, 33 19:9; τ. π. τ. Ἡρῴδου, Ac 23:35.
3. the Prætorian Guard: Phl 1:13 (v. Lft., in l.; ICC, 51 f.).†

strong.derivation: perhaps from (a leek, and so an onion-patch);
strong.def: a garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πρασιά, -ᾶς, ἡ, [in LXX: Si 24:31*;]
a garden-bed; metaph., of ranks or orderly groups of persons: Mk 6:40.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed compound of G4253 (πρό) and G833 (αὐλή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προ-αύλιον, -ου, τό (< πρό, αὐλή),
a porch, vestibule: Mk 14:68.†

strong.def: forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πρόθυμος, -ον, [in LXX: I Ch 28:21, II Ch 29:31 (נָדִיב), Hb 1:8 (חוּשׁ), al.;]
willing, ready: Mt 26:41, Mk 14:38; neut., τὸ π. = ἡ προθυμία (Thuc., al., III Mac 5:26), οὕτως τὸ κατ’ ἐμὲ (= cl. τὸ ἐμὸν) π., Ro 1:15 (but v. ICC, in l.).†

strong.def: to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** προ-λαμβάνω, [in LXX: Wi 17:11 א2, Wi 17:17 א2B*;]
1. to take beforehand: c. acc., I Co 11:21 (but v. infr.).
2. to be beforehand, anticipate (in cl., c. acc., gen. or dat.): c. inf. (= cl. φθάνω, v. Bl., § 69, 4; Swete, in l.), Mk 14:8.
3. to overtake, surprise: pass., Ga 6:1 (on the virtual disappearance of the temporal force of the preposition in this compound here and perhaps also in I Co 11:21, v. MM, xxi).†

strong.def: to say beforehand, i.e. predict, forewarn

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 προ-λέγω, [in LXX: Is 41:26 (נגד hi.)*;]
1. to tell or say beforehand: II Co 13:2, Ga 5:21, I Th 3:4 (R, txt.; cf. προεῖπον, but v. infr.).
2. to declare, tell plainly: II Co 13:2, Ga 5:21, I Th 3:4 (R, mg.; v. MM, xxi, and cf. Is 41:26).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προ-μεριμνάω, -ῶ,
to be anxious beforehand: Mk 13:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † προ-σάββατον, -ου, τό, [in LXX: Ps 91 (92) tit., א (שַׁבָּת) Ps 92 (93) tit., Jth 8:6*;]
the day before the Sabbath: Mk 15:42 (L, Tr., txt., πρὸς σ.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προσ-αιτέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Jb 27:14*;]
1. to ask besides.
2. to continue asking; hence, to importune, beg, ask alms: Jo 9:8.†

strong.def: for the occasion only, i.e. temporary
strong.kjv: dur-(eth) for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** πρόσ-καιρος, -ον, [in LXX: IV Mac 15:2, 8, 23*;]
1. in season.
2. for a season, temporary, transient: II Co 4:18, He 11:25; of plants, short-lived: Mt 13:21, Mk 4:17.†

strong.def: to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor)
strong.kjv: attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 προσ-καρτερέω, -ῶ (< καρτερός, strong, stedfast), [in LXX: Nu 13:21 (חזק hith.), To 5:8 א, Da Th Su 6*;]
to attend constantly, continue stedfastly, adhere to, wait on: c. dat. pers., Mk 3:9, Ac 8:13 10:7; c. dat. rei, Ac 1:14 2:42 6:4, Ro 12:12, Col 4:2; seq. ἐν, Ac 2:46; εἰς, Ro 13:6.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed compound of G4314 (πρός) and G2776 (κεφαλή);
strong.def: something for the head, i.e. a cushion

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προσ-κεφάλαιον, -ου, τό, [in LXX: Ez 13:18, 20 (כֶּסֶת), I Es 3:8*;]
a pillow, cushion: Mk 4:38.†

strong.def: to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** προσ-κλίνω, [in LXX: II Mac 14:24*;]
1. to make to lean against.
2. to make the scale incline one way or another; hence, metaph., of persons, to incline (sc. ἑαυτόν) towards: pass., Ac 5:36.†

strong.def: to roll towards, i.e. block against

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * προσ-κυλίω,
to roll up, roll to: c. acc. et dat., Mt 27:60; acc. seq. ἐπί, Mk 15:46.†

strong.def: to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 προσ-λαμβάνω, [in LXX: Ps 117 (18):16 (משׁה hi.), Ps 72 (73):24 (לקח), etc.;]
1. to take in addition.
2. to take to oneself, take, receive; in NT always mid., -ομαι;
(a). of things: of food, c. acc., Ac 27:33; c. gen. part., Ac 27:36;
(b). of persons: c. acc., Mt 16:22, Mk 8:32 (v. Swete, in l.), Ac 17:5 18:26 28:2, Ro 14:1, 3 15:7, Phm 17.†

strong.def: to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in
strong.kjv: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 προσ-μένω, [in LXX: Jg 3:25 A (חוּל hi.), To 2:2 א, Wi 3:9, III Mac 7:17*;]
1. to wait longer, continue, remain still: Ac 18:18; seq. ἐν, I Ti 1:3.
2. C. dat., to remain with: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:32. Metaph., to remain attached to, cleave unto, abide in: τ. κυρίῳ, Ac 11:23 (R, txt.; ἐν τ. κ., R, mg., v. supr.); τ. χάριτι τ. θεοῦ, Ac 13:43; τ. δεήσεσιν, I Ti 5:5.†

strong.derivation: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of the same as G3730 (ὁρμή) (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull);
strong.def: to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προσ-ορμίζω (< ὅρμος, an anchorage),
to bring a ship to anchor at; usually in mid., to come to anchor near, and so pass. in late writers (Ael., Dio Cass.): Mk 6:53.†

strong.def: to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as G4313 (προπορεύομαι))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προσ-πορεύομαι, [in LXX for קרב, נגשׁ, etc.;]
to come near, approach: c. dat. pers., Mk 10:35.†

strong.derivation: from G4314 (πρός) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 προσ-τρέχω, [in LXX for רוּץ;]
to run to: Mk 9:15 10:17, Ac 8:30.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * πρύμνα, -ης, ἡ,
prop. fem. of adj. πρύμνος, -η, -ον, (sc. ναῦς), the hindmost part of a ship, the stern: Mk 4:38, Ac 27:29; opp. to πρῷρα, Ac 27:41.†

strong.def: at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 πρωί (Rec. πρωΐ), adv. (< πρό), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר, בַּבֹּקֶר;]
in the morning, early: Mt 16:3 (R, txt.) 21:18, Mk 1:35 11:20 13:35 15:1 16:[9], Jo 18:28 20:1; λίαν π., Mk 16:2; ἅμα π., Mt 20:1; ἀπὸ π. (cf. ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν, Ex 18:13), Ac 28:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πτύω, [in LXX: Nu 12:14 (ירק), Si 28:12*;]
to spit: Mk 7:33 8:23, Jo 9:6 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐμ-πτύω).†

strong.def: a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 πτῶμα, -τος, τό (< πίπτω), [in LXX: Jg 14:8 (מַפֶּלֶת), Jb 16:15 (14) (פֶּרֶץ), Is 51:19 (שֹׁד), Jth 8:19, Wi 4:18, al.;]
1. a fall, metaph., a misfortune, calamity (Trag., Plat., Polyb., al.; LXX).
2. That which has fallen;
(a). of buildings, a ruin (Polyb.);
(b). of living creatures, in cl. (poët. only) usually c. gen., νεκρῶν, etc., but also absol., as in late writers and NT, a fallen body, a carcase, corpse: Mt 14:12 24:28, Mk 15:45; π. αὐτοῦ, Mk 6:29; αὐτῶν, Re 11:8, 9 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 472 f.).†

strong.derivation: from a primary (the fist as a weapon);
strong.def: the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πυγμή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX: Ex 21:18, Is 58:4 (אֶגְרוֹף)*;]
the fist: πυγμῇ νίψασθαι τ. χεῖρας (T, πυκνά; Vg., Goth., Copt., crebro), to wash the hands with the fist (diligently, R, txt.; up to the elbow, R, mg.; the exact meaning is doubtful; v. Swete, in l.): Mk 7:3.†

strong.def: to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * πυρέσσω (< πῦρ),
to be ill of a fever: Mt 8:14, Mk 1:3.†

strong.def: to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πωρόω, -ῶ (< πῶρος, 1. a stone. 2. a callus), [in LXX: Jb 17:7 B (כּהה), Pr 10:20 A*;]
to petrify, harden, form a callus. Metaph., π. τ. καρδίαν, Jo 12:40. Pass., Ro 11:7; τ. νοήματα, II Co 3:14; ἡ καρδία, Mk 6:52 8:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 * πώρωσις, -εως, ἡ (< πωρόω),
a covering with a callus, a hardening: metaph., Mk 3:6, Ro 11:25, Eph 4:18.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (H07227 with pronominal suffix);
strong.def: my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 *† ῥαββεί (Rec. -βί, v. WH, App., 155) (Heb. and Aram. רַבִּי, my master; v. Dalman, Words, 327, 331 ff.),
a title of respectful address to Jewish teachers, Rabbi: Mt 23:7, 8; of John, Jo 3:26; of Christ, Mt 26:25, 49, Mk 9:5 11:21 14:45, Jo 1:30, 50 3:2 4:31 6:25 9:2 11:8; κύριε ῥ., Mk 10:51 (WH, mg., v.s. ῥαββουνεί).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) *† ῥαββουνεί (Rec. -βονί, v.s. ῥαββεί) (Aram. רַבּוֺנִי, later, רִבּוֺנִי, my master; on the Greek vocalization and the relation of the word to ῥαββεί, v. Dalman, Words, 324, 340; Gr., 140n; DB, iv, 190);
Rabboni: Mk 10:51 (WH, mg., κύριε ῥαββεί), Jo 20:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ῥάκος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Is 64:6 (5) (בֶּגֶד), Je 45 (38):11 (סְחָבָה), Es 4:17 * ;]
1. a ragged garment (Hom.).
2. a rag, remnant, piece of cloth: Mt 9:16, Mk 2:21.†

strong.kjv: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ῥοῦφος, -ου, ὁ
(Lat.), Rufus: Mk 15:21, Ro 16:13.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee or (H07662 with pronominal suffix);
strong.def: thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.c., WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי),
sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34 (Ps 21 (22):2, Heb. עֲוַבְתָּנִי).†

strong.derivation: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from H07965);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σαλώμη, -ης, ἡ (< Heb. שָׁלוֹם),
Salome: Mk 15:40 16:1.†

strong.def: of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σανδάλιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: Jos 9:5, Is 20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, q.v.), Jth 10:4 16:9 * ;]
a sandal: Mk 6:9, Ac 12:8.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 σβέννυμι [in LXX chiefly for כּבה ;]
of fire or things on fire, to quench: c. acc, Mt 12:20, Eph 6:16, He 11:34; pass., Mt 25:8, Mk 9:[44, 46], 48, Metaph. (cf. Ca 8:7, IV Mac 16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, I Th 5:19.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 σέβω [in LXX (chiefly for יָרֵא, Jos 4:24, al.) and NT always mid., σέβομαι, exc. IV Mac 5:24 ;]
to worship: c. acc. pers., Mt 15:9, Mk 7:7, Ac 18:13 19:27; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, Ac 16:14 18:7; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, Ac 13:43, 50 17:4, 17 (cf. προσήλυτος).†

strong.derivation: feminine of a compound of G4642 (σκληρός) and G2588 (καρδία);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ (< σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: De 10:16, Je 4:4 (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Si 16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, ib. 3:26, 27) * ;]
hardness of heart: Mt 19:8, Mk 10:5 16:[14].†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 † σκοτίζω (< σκότος), [in LXX for חשׁךְ ;]
to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, Mt 24:29, Mk 13:24, Lk 23:45 (Rec., WH, mg.), Re 8:12. Metaph., of the mind, Ro 1:21 11:10 (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;]
a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaph., of fut. punishment, Mk 9:48 (LXX, Is 66:24; cf. Si 7:17, Jth 16:17).†

strong.def: to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σμυρνίζω (< σμύρνα),
1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79).
2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Mk 15:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) σπάω [in LXX chiefly for שׁלף, ;]
in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157),
to draw: μάχαιραν, Mk 14:47, Ac 16:27,†

strong.derivation: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of G138 (αἱρέομαι) in the sense of its cognate G1507 (εἱλίσσω);
strong.def: a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ** σπείρα, -ης (on this form of gen., v. M, Pr., 38, 48; Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, 12; Deiss., BS, 186), [in LXX: Jth 14:11, II Mac 8:23 12:20, 22 * ;]
1. (= Lat. spira) anything or rolled up, a coil.
2. As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort (v. Swete, Mk., 375; Westc., Jo., 251 f.): Mt 27:27, Mk 15:16, Jo 18:3, 12, Ac 10:1 21:31 27:1.†

strong.def: a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σπεκουλάτωρ, -ορος (Rec. -ωρος), ὁ (Lat. speculator),
1. prop., a spy or scout.
2. An executioner: Mk 6:27 (v. Swete, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * σπόγγος, -ου, ὁ
a sponge: Mt 27:48, Mk 15:36, Jo 19:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 * σφυρίς (T, Rec. σπυρίς, v. WH, App., 148; Bl., § 6, 7), -ίδος, ἡ,
a flexible mat-basket for carrying provisions: Mt 15:37 16:10, Mk 8:8, 20 Ac 9:25 (v.s. κόφινος).†

strong.def: to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 στενάζω [in LXX for אנח ni., אנק, etc. ;]
to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): Mk 7:34, II Co 5:2, 4, He 13:17, Ja 5:9 (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, Ro 8:23 (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω).†

strong.derivation: from an apparently primary (to twine or wreathe);
strong.def: a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, G1238 (διάδημα)), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 στέφανος, -ου, ὁ (< στέφω, to encircle), [in LXX chiefly for עֲטָרָה ;]
1. that which surrounds or encompasses (as a wall, a crowd: Hom., al.).
2. a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, q.v.; cf. Deiss., LAE, 372 ff.; on its use in LXX for the golden crown of royalty (prop., διάδημα, q.v., cf. Hort and Mayor on Ja 1:12): Mt 27:29, Mk 15:17, Jo 19:2, 5, I Co 9:25, Re 4:4, 10 6:2 9:7 12:1 14:14. Metaph.: Phl 4:1, Re 3:11; τ. δικαιοσύνης (cf. Deiss., LAE, 312), II Ti 4:8; τ. δόξης, I Pe 5:4; καυχήσεως, I Th 2:19 (v. M, Th., in l.); τ. ζωῆς (gen. appos.), Ja 1:12, Re 2:10.†

strong.derivation: from the perfect tense of G2476 (ἵστημι);
strong.def: to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 † στήκω late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (v. B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii), [in LXX: Ex 14:13 A, Jg 16:26 B, III Ki 8:11 B * ;]
= ἵστημι, to stand: Mk 3:31 11:25, Jo 1:26, Re 12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaph., to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Ga 5:1 (but v. Field, Notes, 189 f.), II Th 2:15; seq. ἐν, Jo 8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), I Co 16:13, Phl 1:27 4:1; c. dat., Ro 14:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 στίλβω [in LXX: Na 3:3 (לַהַב), etc. ;]
to shine, glisten: Mk 9:3.†

strong.def: a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 στοιβάς, v.s. στιβάς.

strong.def: to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † στυγνάζω (< στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Is 5:17, Wi 17:5, Da LXX 2:12*), [in LXX: Ez 27:35 28:19 32:10 (שָׁמֵם)* ;]
to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Mk 10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Mt 16:3 (|[WH]|, R, mg., om.).†

strong.def: to seat oneself in company with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-κάθημαι (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Ps 100 (101):6 (ישׁב) * ;]
to sit together or with: c. dat., Ac 26:30; seq. μετά, c. gen., Mk 14:54.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2201 (ζεῦγος);
strong.def: to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-ζεύγνυμι (Rec. συζ-), [in LXX: Ez 1:11, 23 (חבר) * ;]
to yoke to­gether: metaph., of union in wedlock, Mt 19:6, Mk 10:9.†

strong.def: to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-λυπέω (Rec. συλλ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Ps 68 (69):20, Is 51:19 (נוּד) * ;]
to make to grieve with (Arist.). Pass., to be moved to grief by sympathy: seq. ἐπί, c. dat., Mk 3:5.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4825 (σύμβουλος);
strong.def: advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 **† συμβούλιον, -ου, τό (< σύμβουλος), [in LXX: IV Mac 17:17 א * ;]
a word of the Græco-Roman period (of. Lat. consilium, and v. Deiss., BS, 238) = cl. συμβουλία (Arist., Xen.),
1. counsel: σ. λαμβάνειν, Mt 12:14 22:15 27:1, 7 28:12; διδόναι, Mk 3:6 (ποιεῖν, Rec.); ποιεῖν, Mk 15:1 (ἑτοιμάζειν, WH, mg.).
2. By meton., a council (IV Mac, l.c.א; συνέδριον, AR): Ac 25:12 (v. MM, xxiv).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4844 (συμπίνω);
strong.def: a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-ανα-βαίνω [in LXX for עלה ;]
to go up with: c. dat. pers., seq. εἰς, c. acc. loc., Mk 15:41, Ac 13:31.†

strong.def: to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** συν-απο-θνήσκω [in LXX: Si 19:10 * ;]
to die with or together: Mk 14:31, II Co 7:3 (v. Meyer, in l.), II Ti 2:11.†

strong.def: to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** συνεργέω, -ῶ [in LXX: I Es 7:2, I Mac 12:1 * ;]
1. prop., to work together (with): absol., Mk 16:[20], I Co 16:16, II Co 6:1; c. dat., Ja 2:22; dat. commod., Ro 8:28, T, R, txt. (but v. infr.).
2. In Hellenistic writers (M, Pr., 65), trans., to cause to work together (cf. ICC, in l.): c. acc. rei, Ro 8:28 [WH] R, mg. (but v. supr.).†

strong.def: to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-θλίβω [in LXX: Ec 12:6 א A (רצץ), Si 34 (31):14, I Mac 15:14 A * ;]
to press together, press on all sides: Mk 5:24, 31.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of G4932 (συντέμνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-τόμως, adv. (< συντέμνω) [in LXX: Pr 13:23 (בְּלֹאמׅשְׁפָּט) 23:28, III Mac 5:25 * ;]
concisely, briefly: Ac 24:4 (for a similar ex., v. MM, xxiv).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 συν-τρέχω [in LXX: Ps 49 (50):18 (עִם רָצָה), II Mac 2, Jdt 4 * ;]
to run together or with: seq. ἐκεῖ, Mk 6:33; πρόσ, c. acc., Ac 3:11; metaph., I Pe 4:4.†

strong.derivation: feminine of a compound of G4948 (Σύρος) and the same as G5403 (Φοινίκη);
strong.def: a Syro-phœnician woman, i.e. a female native of Phœnicia in Syria

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) Συροφοινίκισσα (Rec. -φοίνισσα), -ης, ἡ
a Syropænician woman: Mk 7:26, WH, txt., RV (cf. ἡ Φοινίκη Συρία, Diod., 19, 93).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);
strong.def: a sign in common, i.e. preconcerted signal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † σύσ-σημον (T, συν-), -ου, τό (< σῆμα), [in LXX: Jg 20:38, 40 (מַשְׂאֵת), Is 5:26 49:22 62:10 (נֵס) * ;]
a fixed sign or signal: Mk 14:44. (Strab., Plut., al.; condemned by Atticists, v. Rutherford, NPhr., 492 f.) †

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G4714 (στάσις);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) *† στασιαστής (< στασιάζω, to stir up sedition, Jth 7:15, II Mac 4:30 14:6 *)
= Att.. στασιώτης,
a rebel, revolutionist, one who stirs up sedition: Mk 15:7 (FlJ, al.).†

strong.def: to impale in company with (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 * συν-σταυρόω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ,
to crucify together with: pass., c. dat., Jo 19:32; id. seq. σύν, Mt 27:44, Mk 15:32. Metaph., of the mystical death of the Christian with Christ: Ro 6:6, Ga 2:20 (Eccl.).†

strong.def: a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 * σχίσμα, -τος, τό (< σχίζω),
a rent (Arist., al.): Mt 9:16, Mk 2:21. Metaph., a dissension, division: Jo 7:43 9:16 10:19, I Co 1:10 11:18 12:25.†

strong.def: the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ταλειθά (Rec. ταλιθά), (Aram. טְלִיתָא, v. Dalman, Gr., 150),
talitha, i.e. maiden: Mk 5:41.†

strong.def: an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for חָרָשׁ ;]
an artificer in wood, stone or metal, but esp. a carpenter (v. MM, xxiv): Mt 13:55, Mk 6:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 τέρας, -ατος, τό [in LXX chiefly for מוֹפֵת ;]
a wonder, marvel: in NT always pl., τ. κ. σημεῖα, Mt 24:24, al. (v.s. σημεῖον)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 τέταρτος, -η, -ον [in LXX chiefly for רְבִיעִי ;]
fourth: Mt 14:25, Mk 6:48, Ac 10:30, Re 4:7 6:7, 8 8:12 16:8 21:19.†

strong.derivation: from the multiplicative adverb of G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G5507 (χίλιοι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 τετρακισ-χίλιοι, -αι, -α
four thousand: Mt 15:38 16:10, Mk 8:9, 20, Ac 21:38.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of a derivative of G5056 (τέλος) and G827 (αὐγή);
strong.def: in a far-shining manner, i.e. plainly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τηλαυγῶς adv. (< τῆλε, afar, + αὐγή, radiance), poët. and in late prose,
at a distance clearly: Mk 8:25 (WH, mg., δηλαυγῶς).†

strong.def: perhaps akin to G2334 (θεωρέω)); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from G5442 (φυλάσσω), which is properly to prevent escaping; and from G2892 (κουστωδία), which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), i.e. to note (a prophecy; figuratively, to fulfil a command); by implication, to detain (in custody; figuratively, to maintain); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried)
strong.kjv: hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
70 τηρέω, -ῶ [in LXX for שָׁמַר, נָצַר, etc. ;]
1. to watch over, guard, keep, preserve: Mt 27:36, Ac 16:23, al.; ἑαυτόν, II Co 11:9, I Ti 5:22, Ja 1:27, Ju 21; seq. εἰς, Jo 12:7, Ac 25:21, I Pe 1:4, II Pe 2:4, 9 3:7, Ju 6; ἐν, Jo 17:11, 12, Ju 21; ἐκ, Jo 17:15, Re 3:10; τ. πίστιν, II Ti 4:7, Re 14:12; τ. ἑνότητα τ. πνεύματος, Eph 4:3.
2. to watch, give heed to, observe: τ. σάββατον, Jo 9:16; τ. ἐντολήν (-άς), Mt 19:17, Jo 14:15 15:10, I Ti 6:14, I Jo 2:3, 4 3:22, 24 5:3, Re 12:17 14:12; τ. λόγον (-ους), Jo 8:51, 52, 55 14:23, 24 15:20 17:6, I Jo 2:5, Re 3:8, 10 22:7, 9; τ. νόμον, Ac 15:5, Ja 2:10; τ. παράδοσιν, Mk 7:9; τ. ἔργα, Re 2:26; τ. γεγραμμένα, Re 1:3 (cf. δια-, παρα-, συν-τηρέω)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Τιμαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. טִימַי (?), v. Zorell, s.v.),
Timæus: Mk 10:46.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 0 (KJV) τουτέστι = τοῦτ ̓ ἔστι

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 τριακόσιοι, -αι, -α
three hundred: Mk 14:5, Jo 12:5.†

strong.def: to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** τρίζω [in Aq.: Am 2:13; Sm.: Is 38:14 * ;]
1. prop., of sounds by animals, to cry, chirp, etc.
2. Of other sounds, e.g., trans., τ. ὀδόντας, to gnash or grind the teeth: Mk 9:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 τρόμος, -ου, ὁ (< τρέμω), [in LXX for רִעָדָה, רַעַד, פַּחַד, etc. ;]
trembling, quaking, esp. from fear: Mk 16:8; φόβος κ. τ. (as in Ge 9:2, Ex 15:16, De 2:25, Is 19:16, al.), I Co 2:3, II Co 7:15, Eph 6:5, Phl 2:12.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 τρύβλιον (Rec. τρυβλίον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for קְעָרָה ;]
a bowl, dish: Mt 26:23, Mk 14:20 (Hippocr., Aristoph., Plut., al.).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of (to wear away;
strong.def: akin to the base of G5134 (τραῦμα), G5147 (τρίβος) and G5176 (τρώγω)); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † τρυμαλιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< τρύω, to wear away), [in LXX: Je 13:4 (נָקִיק), etc. ;]
= τρύμη, a hole: τ. ῥαφίδος, eye of a needle, Mk 10:25.†

strong.def: healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ὑγιής, -ές, acc., ὑγιῆ (Attic usually -ιᾶ), [in LXX for חַי, etc. ;]
sound, whole, healthy: Mt 12:13 15:31, Jo 5:[4], 6, 9, 11, 14, 15 7:23, Ac 4:10; seq. ἀπό, Mk 5:34; of words, opinions, etc. (as in cl.), metaph., λόγος, Tit 2:8.†

strong.def: to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 (KJV) ὑμνέω, -ῶ (< ὕμνος) [in LXX for הָלַל pi., שִׁיר, יָדָה hi., etc. ;]
1. trans., c. acc pers. (in cl. also c. acc. rei), to sing to, laud, sing to the praise of: Ac 16:25, He 2:12.
2. Intrans., to sing: in LXX and NT, of singing hymns and praises to God (Ps 64 (65):13, al.), Mt 26:30, Mk 14:26 (v. Swete, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὑπερηφανία, -ας, ἡ (< ὑπερήφανος, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;]
haughtiness, arrogance, disdain: Mk 7:22 (Plat., Xen.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑπερ-περισσῶς comp adv.,
beyond measure, exceedingly: Mk 7:37.†

strong.def: to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὑπο-δέω [in LXX: II Ch 28:15, Ez 16:10 (נָעַל) * ;]
to bind under, esp. of foot gear. Most freq. in mid, and pass. c. acc;
(a). of the foot, ὑποδησάμενοι τ. πόδας, your feet shod: Eph 6:15;
(b). of that which is put on, σανδάλια: Mk 6:9, Ac 12:8.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G3025 (ληνός);
strong.def: vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὑπολήνιον, -ου, τό (< ὑπό, ληνός), [in LXX: Jl 3 (4):13, Ha 2:17(16), Za 14:10, Is 16:10 (יֶקֶב) * ;]
a vessel or trough beneath a winepress to receive the juice (RV, a pit for the winepress) Mk 12:1 (v. Swete, in l, and cf. ληνός).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† ὑστέρησις, -εως, ἡ (< ὑστερέω), [in Aq.: Jb 30:3 * ;]
need, want: opp. to τὸ περισσεῦον, Mk 12:44; καθ’ ὑ., Phl 4:11 (eccl.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
49 φανερόω, -ώ [in LXX: Je 40 (33):6 (גּלה pi.) * ;]
to make visible, clear, manifest or known: c. acc rei, Jo 2:11 17:6, Ro 1:19, I Co 4:5, II Co 2:14 11:6, Col 4:4, Tit 1:3; pass., Mk 4:22, Jo 3:21 9:3, Ro 3:21 16:26, II Co 4:10, 11, Eph 5:13, Col 1:26, II Ti 1:10, He 9:8, I Jo 3:2 4:9, Re 3:18 15:4; c. acc pers., of Christ, Jo 7:4 21:1; pass., II Co 3:3 5:10, 11, I Jo 2:19; of Christ, Mk 16:12, 14, Jo 1:31 21:14, Col 3:4, I Ti 3:16, He 9:26, I Pe 1:20 5:4, I Jo 1:2 (ἡ ζωή; v. Westc., in l.) 2:28 3:2, 5, 8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** φανερῶς adv. (< φανερός), [in LXX: II Mac 3:28 * ;]
(a). manifestly, openly: Mk 1:45; opp. to ἐν κρυπτῷ„ Jo 7:10;
(b). clearly: Ac 10:3 (II Mac 3:28).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φάντασμα, -τος, τό (< φαντάζω), [in LXX: Jb 20:8 A (חִזָּיוֹן), Is 28:7 A, Wi 17:15 * ;]
= φάσμα, an appearance, apparition (Æsch., al.): Mt 14:26, Mk 6:49 (v. DCG, i, 111b).†

strong.derivation: probably akin to the base of G5351 (φθείρω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ** φθόνος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Wi 2:24 6:23, I Mac 8:16, III Mac 6:7 * ;]
envy: Ro 1:29, Ga 5:21, I Ti 6:4, Tit 3:3, I Pe 2:1; διὰ φθόνον, Mt 27:18, Mk 15:10, Phl 1:15; πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τ. πνεῦμα (on the meaning, v. R, txt., mg. 1, 2; Hort, Ja., 93 f.), Ja 4:5.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum;
strong.def: to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† φραγελλόω, -ῶ (< φραγέλλιον, q.v.),
to scourge: c. acc., Mt 27:26, Mk 15:15 (eccl.).†

strong.def: to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience)
strong.kjv: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
26 φρονέω, -ῶ (< φρήν), [in LXX: De 32:29, Za 9:2 (חָכָם), Ps 93 (94):8 (שָׂכַל hi.), Is 44:18 (בִּין) ib. 28, Es 8:13, Wi 1:1 14:30, I Mac 10:20, II Mac 9:12; 14:8, 26 * ;]
1. to have understanding (Hom., al.).
2. to think, to be minded in a certain way: ὡς νήπιος, I Co 13:11; c. acc. (usually neut., adj., or pron., as freq. in cl.), ὃ δεῖ, Ro 12:3; ἃ, Ac 28:22; τοῦτο, Phl 3:15; τι ἑτέρως, ib.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο, Ga 5:10; τ. αὐτὸ φ. (Deiss., BS, 256), to be of the same mind, II Co 13:11, Phl 2:2 4:2; id. seq. εἰς (ἐν) ἀλλήλους(οις), Ro 12:16 15:5; τ. ἓν φ., Phl 2:2 (Lft., in l.); seq. ὑπέρ, Phl 1:7.
3. to have in mind, be mindful of, think of (Hdt., Xen., al.; Es, 1Mac, ll. c.): τὰ τ. θεοῦ, opp. to τ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Mt 16:23, Mk 8:33; τὰ τ. σαρκός, opp. to τ. τ. πνεύρατος, Ro 8:5; τ. ἐπίγεια, Phl 3:19; τὰ ἄνω, opp. to τ. ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, Col 3:2; τοῦτο φρονεῖτε (RV, have this mind in you), Phl 2:5; ὑψηλά, Ro 12:16; φ. ἡμέραν (to observe a day), Ro 14:6; seq. ὑπέρ, Phl 4:10 (cf. κατα-, παρα-, περι-, ὑπερ-φρσνέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 φύλλον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for עָלֶה ;]
a leaf: Mt 21:19 24:32, Mk 11:13 13:28, Re 22:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χαλκίον, -ου, τό (< χαλκός), [in LXX: Jb 41:22(23) (סִיר), etc. ;]
a brazen (copper) vessel: Mk 7:4.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from G5465 (χαλάω) through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose);
strong.def: copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 χαλκός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;]
copper: I Co 13:1, Re 18:12; by meton., of copper coin, Mt 10:9, Mk 6:8 12:41.†

strong.derivation: from a form of the same as G5490 (χάσμα);
strong.def: a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 χεῖλος, -ους, τό, gen. pl., -εων (v. Bl., § 8, 4; Thackeray, Gr., I, 151), [in LXX chiefly for שָׂפָה ;]
a lip (as in Heb., of the lip as the organ of speech): Mt 15:8, Mk 7:6, Ro 3:13, I Co 14:21, He 13:15, I Pe 3:10 (LXX). Metaph., of things, an edge, brink, etc. (Hom., Hdt., al.): of the sea­shore, He 11:12.†

strong.def: akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 χειμών, -ῶνος, ὁ [in LXX for גֶּשֶׁם, סְתָיו ;]
1. winter: Jo 10:22, II Ti 4:21; gen., χειμῶνος, in winter, Mt 24:20, Mk 13:18.
2. Prop., a winter storm, hence, generally, a storm, tempest: Mt 16:3 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Ac 27:20.†

strong.derivation: from G5495 (χείρ) and a derivative of G4160 (ποιέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 χειρο-ποίητος, -ον (< χείρ, ποιέω), [in LXX (of idols) for אֱלִיל ;]
made by hand (i.e. of human handiwork): of temples, Mk 14:58, Ac 7:48 17:24, He 9:11, 24; of circumcision, Eph 2:11.†

strong.def: the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
21 χιλίαρχος (in Hdt., al., -ης), -ου, ὁ (< χίλιοι, ἄρχω) [in LXX chiefly for אֶלֶף שַׂר ;]
a chiliarch, the commander of a thousand, esp. a Roman military tribune, the commander of a cohort: Jo 18:12, Ac 21:31-33, 37 22:24-29 23:10, 15, 17-19, 22 24:7, 22 25:23; more generally, of officers of similar rank, Mk 6:21, Re 6:15 19:18 (v., DB, i, 352b; DCG, i, 271a, 307a).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 χλωρός, -ά, -όν (< χλόη), [in LXX for יֶרֶק, etc. ;]
(a). pale green: χόρτος, Mk 6:39, Re 8:7; πᾶν χ., Re 9:4;
(b). pale: ἵππος, Re 6:8.†

strong.def: a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) χοῦς, -οός acc., οῦν, ὁ, (contr. from χόος), [in LXX chiefly for עָפָר ;]
1. earth, soil.
2. In later writers (Plut., LXX), = κονιορτός, dust: Mk 6:11, Re 18:19.†

strong.def: to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 χωρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ge 13:6 (נשׂא), III Ki 7:26, 38 (כּוּל hi.), II Ch 4:5 (חזק hi.), Wi 7:23, 24, al. ;]
I. Intrans.,
1. to make room, give way, retire, pass: seq. εἰς, Mt 15:17; metaph. (EV, come), εἰς μετάνοιαν, II Pe 3:9.
2. to go forward, advance, progress (Plat., Polyb., al.) ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ. ἐν ὑμῖν, Jo 8:37 (R, txt., hath not free course; R, mg., hath no place, for wh. cf. Field, Notes, 94 f.).
II. Trans., to have space for holding, to hold: Mk 2:2 (cf. Ge, l.c.), Jo 21:25; of measures (III Ki, II Ch, ll. c.), Jo 2:6. Metaph., of having or making room in mind or heart: Mt 19:11, 12 (EV, receive), II Co 7:2 (R, txt., open your hearts; mg., make room) (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ὑπο-χωρέω).†

strong.def: to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 χωρίζω [in LXX: II Ch 12:8, al. (בּדל ni., etc.), Wi 1:3, II Mac 5:21, al. ;]
1. to separate, divide, put asunder: c. acc. rei, opp. to συζεύγνυμι Mt 19:6, Mk 10:9; c. acc. pers., seq. ἀπό (Wi 1:3), Ro 8:35, 39; pf. pass ptcp., He 7:26.
2. In late writers, mid. and 1 aor pass., to separate oneself, depart: Phm 15; seq. ἀπό Ac 1:4, ἐκ, Ac 18:1-2; of divorce (polyb., al.), I Co 7:10, 11, 15 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-χωρίζω).†

strong.def: a spot or plot of ground
strong.kjv: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 χωρίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: I Ch 27:27 (כֶּרֶם), II Mac 11:5 12:7, 21, IV Mac 15:20 * ;]
1. a place, region.
2. an estate, property, piece of land: Mt 26:36, Mk 14:32, Jo 4:5, Ac 1:18, 19 4:34 5:3, 8 28:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ψευδό-χριστος, -ου ὁ
a false Christ or Messiah, "a pretender to the Messianic office" (Swete, Mk., 309; cf. also Tr., Syn., § xxx): Mt 24:24, Mk 13:22 (cf. ἀντίχριστος).†

strong.derivation: diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5567 (ψάλλω) (meaning a crumb);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 (KJV) *† ψιχίον, -ου, τό
dimin. of ψίξ,
a crumb: Mt 15:27, Mk 7:28.†

strong.def: a pang or throe, especially of childbirth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὠδίν (late form of ὠδίς), -ῖνος, ἡ [in LXX forחֶבֶל (and wrongly forחֶבֶל, cf. Ac, l.c.), חִיל, etc. ;]
a birth pang, travail pain: I Th 5:3; metaph., of extreme suffering, Mt 24:8, Mk 13:8; ὠδῖνες θανάτου (Ps 17 (18):4 הֶבְלֵימָוֶת), Ac 2:24.†

strong.def: oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 † ὡσαννά (T, ὠσ-) (Heb נָא and הוֹשֵׁעַ; v. Dalman, Words, 220 IL; Gr., 249),
hosanna: Mt 21:9, Mk 11:9-10, Jo 12:13; τ. υἱῷ Δανείδ, Mt 21:9, 15.†

strong.def: the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first:

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
Α, α, ἄλφα (q.v.), τό, indecl.,
alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, αʹ = 1, α͵ = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses:
1. ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) negative, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος.
2. ἀ-, ἁ- copulative, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός.
3. An intensive force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but v. Boisacq, s.v.).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀβαδδών (Heb. אֲבַדֹּון, destruction; LXX, ἀπώλεια, only in Wisdom Lit., of the place of the ruined dead: Jb 26:6, 28:22, 31:12, Ps 88:12, Pr 15:11*), indecl.;
in NT, Abaddon, the angel of the Abyss: Re 9:11.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G922 (βάρος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀβαρής, -ές (< βαρός),
without weight; metaph. (MM, VGT, s.v.) not burdensome: II Co 11:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἀβιούδ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אֲבִיָּהוּד),
Abiud, Abihud: Mt 1:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἄγαβος, -ου, ὁ
Agabus: Ac 11:28, 21:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀγαθοεργέω, -ῶ,
to do good, show kindness: 1 Ti 6:18 (Cremer, 8).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀγαθοποιία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀγαθοποιός),
well-doing: I Pe 4:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀγαθοποιός, -όν = cl. ἀγαθουργός, [in LXX, of a woman who deals pleasantly in order to corrupt, Si 42:14*;]
doing well, acting rightly (Plut.): I Pe 2:14 (Cremer, 8; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ἀγαθωσύνη (on the termination, v.s. ἁγιότης, and cf. WH, App., 152; MM, VGT, s.v.), -ης, ἡ (< ἀγαθός), [in LXX for טוֹבָה, טוֹב, טוּב, only in Heb. bks. ;]
goodness (representing "the kindlier, as δικαιοσύνη, the sterner element in the ideal character," AR, Eph., 5:9; on its relation to χρηστότης, v. Tr., Syn., §lxiii): Ro 15:14, Ga 5:22, II Th 1:11.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1062 (γάμος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** ἄ-γαμος, -ον [in LXX: IV Mac 16:9 * ;]
unmarried: I Co 7:8, 32; fem. (= cl. ἄνανδρος), I Co 7:11, 34.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀγανάκτησις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀγανακτέω), [in LXX: Es 18:3 א1*;]
indignation: II Co 7:11 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἅγαρ (Rec. Ἄ-), ἡ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀγάρα, -ης, Heb. הָגָר),
Hagar (Ge 16): Ga 4:24, 25.†

strong.def: compare the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη)); a receptacle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀγγεῖον, -ου, τό (< ἄγγος), [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי;]
a vessel (v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 25:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀγγελία, -ας, ἡ (< ἄγγελος), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁמוּעָה;]
a message: I Jo 1:5, 3:11 (Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἄγε, prop. imperat. of ἄγω,
come! used as adv. and addressed, like φέρε, to one or more persons: Ja 4:13, 5:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1075 (γενεαλογέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀγενεαλόγητος, -ον (< γενεαλογέω),
without genealogy, i.e. without recorded pedigree (cf. Ne 7:64): He 7:3 (Cremer, 152; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1085 (γένος);
strong.def: properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀγενής, -ές (< γένος),
1. unborn (Plat.);
2. of no family, ignoble, base (opp. to ἀγαθός, Soph., Fr., 105): opp. to εὐγενής, I Co 1:28 (for exx. from π., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 † ἁγιασμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἁγιάζω), [in LXX: Ez 45:4 (מִקְדָּשׁ), Si 7:31, etc.;]
as an active verbal noun in -μός, it signifies properly the process τὸ ἁγιάζειν, rather than the resultant state, ἁγιωσύνη, hence,
1. consecration;
2. sanctification: so strictly in Ro 6:19, 22 (but v. Meyer), I Co 1:30, I Th 4:3, 7, II Th 2:13, He 12:14, I Pe 1:2. Elsewhere it perhaps (Ellic.; but v. Milligan, Th., 48) inclines to the resultant state: I Th 4:4, I Ti 2:15 (Cremer, 55, 602).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
233 ἅγιος, -α, ον (< τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate), [in LXX chiefly for קֹ֫דֶשׁ;]
primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration.
1. Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory: Lk 1:49, Jo 17:11, Re 4:8. Hence
(a). of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: Mt 24:15, He 9:1;
(b). of persons employed by him, as angels: I Th 3:13; prophets, Lk 1:70; apostles, Eph 3:5.
2. Applied to persons as separated to God's service:
(a). of Christ, Mk 1:24, Jo 6:69, Ac 4:30;
(b). of Christians, Ac 9:13, Ro 1:7, He 6:10, Re 5:8.
3. In the moral sense of sharing God's purity: Mk 6:20, Jo 17:11, Ac 3:14, Re 3:7.
4. Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings: I Co 7:14, Eph 1:4.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἁγιότης, -ητος, ἡ (< ἅγιος), [in LXX: II Mac 15:2*;]
sanctity, holiness, regarded, properly, as an abstract quality (v. next word, and cf. Lft. Notes, 49; MM, VGT, s.v.): II Co 1:12, He 12:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἁγιωσύνη (cf. ἀγαθωσύνη), -ης, ἡ (< ἅγιος), [in LXX: Ps 29 (30):4 96 (97):12 (קֹדֶשׁ), 95 (96):6 (עֹז), 144 (145):5 (הוֹד), II Mac 3:12*;]
holiness, the state in man resulting from ἁγιασμός, q.v.: Ro 1:4, II Co 7:1, I Th 3:13 (Cremer, 52; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄγκιστρον, -ου, τό (< ἄγκος, a bend), [in LXX חַכָּה, etc.;]
a fish-hook: Mt 17:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** ἄγκυρα, -ας, ἡ (< ἄγκος, a bend), [in Sm.: Je 52:18*;]
an anchor: Ac 27:29, 30 40; fig. (MM, VGT, s.v.), He 6:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἁγνεία (WH, ἁγνία), [in LXX for טָהֳרָה, נָזִיר, נֶזֶר, etc.;]
purity: I Ti 4:12, 5:2 (Cremer, 58. For exx. of ceremonial use in π., v. MM, Exp., iv).†

strong.def: to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἁγνίζω (> ἁγνός), [in LXX always ceremonially, chiefly for קדשׁ;]
to purify, cleanse from defilement;
(a). ceremonially: Jo 11:55, Ac 21:24, 26 24:18;
(b). morally: Ja 4:8, I Pe 1:22, I Jo 3:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἁγνισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (> ἁγνίζω), [in LXX: Nu 6:5 (נֵזֶר) 8:7 19:17 (חַטּאת), etc.;]
purification: in ceremonial sense, Ac 21:26(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀγνόημα, -τός, τό (< ἀγνοέω), [in LXX: Ge 43:12 (מִשְׁגֶּה), To 3:3, Jth 5:20, Si 23:2 51:19, I Mac 13:39*;]
a sin of ignorance (so in π.; v. MM, VGT, s.v.): He 9:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἄγνοια, -ας, ἡ (< ἀγνοέω), [in LXX chiefly for אָשָׁם, שְׁגָגָה;]
ignorance : Ac 3:17 17:30, Eph 4:18 (with sense of wilful blindness; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), I Pe 1:14.†

strong.def: properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἁγνός, -ή, -όν (< ἅγος, v.s. ἅγιος), [in LXX chiefly for טָהוֹר (Pss, and Pr. only), also II Mac 13:8, IV Mac 18:7, al.;]
1. free from ceremonial defilement , in a condition prepared for worship (for exx. of pagan usage, V. MM, VGT, s.v.).
2. holy, sacred, venerable (II Mac 13:8).
3. As in OT (cl.), pure, chaste, undefiled, guiltless;
(a). of persons: II Co 7:11 11:12, I Ti 5:22, Tit 2:5, I Jo 3:3;
(b). of things: Phl 4:8, Ja 3:17, I Pe 3:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἁγνότης, -τητος, ἡ (< ἁγνός),
purity, chastity (cf. ἁγιότης): II Co 6:6 11:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἁγνῶς (< ἁγνός), adv.,
purely, with pure motives: Phl 1:17.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1108 (γνῶσις);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀγνωσία, -ας, ἡ (< γινώσκω), [in LXX: Jb 35:16 (בְּלִי־דַּעַת), Wi 13:1, III Mac 5:27*;]
ignorance (opp. to γνῶσις): I Co 15:34, I Pe 2:15 (v. Hort in l.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1110 (γνωστός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἄγνωστος, -ον (< γινώσκω), [in LXX: Wi 11:18 18:3, II Mac 1:19 2:7 (Cremer, 157)*;]
unknown: Ac 17:23 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀγοραῖος, -ον (< ἀγορά),
1. frequenting the ἀγορά, a lounger in the ἀγορά (Xen., al.): Ac 17:5.
2. In late writers (Strab., al.), proper to the ἀγορά: ἀγοραῖοι (sc. ἥμεραι) ἀγονται (cf. Lat. conventus agere), court-days are kept, Ac 19:38 (for exx. of both usages, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1121 (γράμμα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀγράμματος, ὂν (< γράφω),
without learning (γράμματα), un-lettered (in π. freq. in formula used by one who signs for an illiterate; MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 4:13 (but cf. Thayer, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀγρι-έλαιος, -ον
1. of the wild olive (Anth.).
2. As subst., the wild olive: Ro 11:17, 24 (CGT, in l.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 Ἀγρίππας, -α (Bl., §7, 2), ὁ,
Agrippa (II): Ac 25:13, 22, 23, 24, 26 26:1, 2, 19, 27, 28, 32. (For Agrippa I, v.s. Ἡρῴδης, 3.) †

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀγρυπνία, -ας, ἡ (v. supr.), [in LXX: Si9, II Mac 2:26*;]
sleeplessness, watching: II Co 6:5 11:27. (Plat., Hdt.; for exx. in π., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: a bringing up, i.e. mode of living

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἄγω), [in LXX: Es 2:20 10:3, II Mac 4:16 6:8 11:24, III Mac 4:10*;]
1. a carrying away.
2. a leading, guiding; metaph., training; hence, from the expression ἀ. τοῦ βίου, absol., conduct, way of life: II Ti 3:10 (Cremer, 61; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀγών, -ῶνος, ὁ (< ἄγω), [in LXX: Is 7:13 (לאה), Es 4:17, Wi 4:2 10:12, II Mac6, IV Mac5*;]
1. a gathering, esp. for games.
2. a place of assembly.
3. a contest, struggle, trial; metaph. (MM, VGT, s.v.),
(a). of the Christian life as a contest and struggle: Phl 1:30, I Th 2:2, I Ti 6:12, II Ti 4:7 He 12:1;
(b). solicitude, anxiety: Col 2:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀδάπανος, -ον (< δαπάνη),
without expense, free of charge: I Co 9:18.†

strong.def: brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† ἀδελφότης, -ητος, ἡ (< ἀδελφός), [in LXX: I Mac 12:10, 17, IV Mac5*;]
1. abstract, brotherhood, brotherly affection (LXX).
2. Concrete, the brotherhood, the Christian community: I Pe 2:17 5:9 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀδηλότης, -ητος, ἡ (< ἄδηλος),
uncertainty: I Ti 6:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀδήλως (< ἄδηλος),
adv. uncertainly: of direction, I Co 9:26.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1252 (διακρίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀ-διά-κριτος, -ον (< διακρίνω), [in LXX: Pr 25:1*;]
1. not to be parted, mixed, undistinguishable (cf. Pr 25:1, and v. Lft., Ignat. Eph., §3).
2. without uncertainty (Hort, in l., but v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Ja 3:17.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G1223 (διά) and G3007 (λείπω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀδιάλειπτος, -ον (< διαλείπω),
unremitting, incessant: Ro 9:2, II Ti 1:3. (For exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.)†

strong.def: uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 **† ἀδιαλείπτως (v. supr.), adv., [in LXX: I Mac 12:11, II Mac4, III Mac 6:33*;]
unremittingly, incessantly: Ro 1:9, I Th 1:3 2:13 5:17.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1311 (διαφθείρω);

strong.kjv: evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀδίκημα, -τος, τό (< ἀδικέω), [in LXX for עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, etc.;]
a wrong, injury, misdeed (MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 18:14 24:20, Re 18:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀδίκως, adv. (< ἄδικος), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc.;]
unjustly, undeservedly: I Pe 2:19.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1384 (δόκιμος);
strong.def: unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἀ-δόκιμος, -ον, [in LXX: Pr 25:4, Is 1:22 (סִיג)*;]
1. of things (prop. of metals: LXX, Pr 25:4, Is 1:22), not standing the test, rejected: γῆ, He 6:8.
2. Of persons, rejected after testing, reprobate: Ro 1:28, I Co 9:27, II Co 13:5-7, II Ti 3:8, Tit 1:16 (Cremer, 212).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἄδολος, -ον,
1. guileless (Pind., Thuc).
2. Of liquids (Æsch., Eur., and late prose writers), genuine, pure (in π. and in MGr. of wine, also of corn: MM, VGT, s.v.; Milligan, NTD, 77): of milk, metaph., I Pe 2:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἁδραμυντηνός (T, Rec. Ἀδραμυττηνός), -ή,-όν,
of Adramyttium, a seaport of Mysia: Ac 27:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἁδρίας (T, Rec. Ἀδρίας), -ου, ὁ,
the Adriatic sea, in later Greek usage extended to take in all the waters between Greece and Italy: Ac 27:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
