classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἰερεμίας (T, Rec. Ἱερ-; v. WH, § 408), -ου, ὁ (Heb. יִרְמְיָה, יִרְמְיָהוּ),
Jeremiah the prophet: Mt 2:17 16:14 27:9 (a ref. to Za 11:13).†

strong.derivation: from G2413 (ἱερός) and the same as G4241 (πρέπω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἱεροπρεπής, -ές (< ἱερός, πρέπει), [in LXX: IV Mac 9:25 11:20*;]
suited to a sacred character, reverend (RV, reverent): Tit 2:3 (cf. Tr., Syn., § xcii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἱερο-συλέω, -ῶ (< ἱερόσυλος, q.v.), [in LXX: II Mac 9:2*;]
to rob a temple (commit sacrilege, R, mg.): Ro 2:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἱερόσυλος, -ον (< ἱερόν, συλάω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:42 (cf. -λημα, II Mac 4:39; -λία, 13:6)*;]
robbing temples: Ac 19:37.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2411 (ἱερόν) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);
strong.def: to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἱερουργέω, -ῶ (< ἱερουργός, a sacrificing priest) [in LXX: IV Mac 7:3 R (cf. -γία, IV Mac 3:30 א R)*;]
to perform sacred rites; c. acc., to minister in priestly service (minister in sacrifice, R, mg.), τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, Ro 15:16.†

strong.def: sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἱερωσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< ἱερός), [in LXX: I Ch 29:22 (כּהן), I Es 5:38, Si 45:24, I Mac 2:54 3:49 7:9, 21, IV Mac 5:35 7:6*;]
priesthood: He 7:11, 12, 24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰεφθάε (FlJ, -θάς, -οῦ), ὁ (Heb. יִפְתָּח),
Jephthah: He 11:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἰεχονίας, -ον, ὁ (Heb. יְהוֹיָכִין, Jehoiakin),
Jechoniah: Mt 1:11, 12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἱκανότης, -ητος, ἡ (< ἱκανός),
sufficiency, ability (Plat.): II Co 3:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἱκανόω, -ῶ (< ἱκανός), [in LXX chiefly for רַב;]
to make sufficient, render fit: c. dupl. acc., II Co 3:6; c. acc. pers. seq. εἰς, Col 1:12.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the base of G2425 (ἱκανός) (through the idea of approaching for a favor);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἱκετήριος, -α, -ον (< ἱκέτης, a suppliant), [in LXX: Jb 40:22(27), II Mac 9:18*;]
of a suppliant; as subst., ἡ ἱ. (sc. ῥάβδος),
1. in cl., an olive-branch, carried by a suppliant.
2. In late Gk. = ἱκεσία, supplication: pl., δεήσεις κ. ἱ., He 5:7.

strong.def: image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Ἰκόνιον, -ου, τό,
Iconium, a city of the province of Galatia: Ac 13:51 14:1, 19, 21 16:2, II Ti 3:11.†

strong.def: propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἱλαρός, -ά, -όν (< ἵλαος = ἵλεως, q.v.), [in LXX: Pr 19:12 (רָצוֹן) 22:8, Es 5:1, Jb 33:26, Si 13:26 26:4, III Mac 6:35*;]
cheerful, joyous: II Co 9:7 (Pr 22:8(9)(LXX)).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἱλαρότης, -ητος, ἡ (< ἱλαρός), [in LXX: Pr 18:22 (רָצוֹן)*;]
cheerfulness: Ro 12:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἱλασμός, -οῦ (< ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: Le 25:9, Nu 5:8 (כִּפֻּרִים), Ps 129(130):4, Da TH 9:9 (סְלִיחָה), Am 8:14 (אַשְׁמָה), Ez 44:27 (חַטָּאת), I Ch 28:20, Si 18:20 A, II Mac 3:33*;]
1. an appeasing (Plut.).
2. a means of appeasing, propitiation (Philo; Nu 5:8, Ez 44:27): I Jo 2:2 4:10.
3. In LXX also forgiveness (Ps 129(130):4, Da TH 9:9).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G2433 (ἱλάσκομαι);
strong.def: an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἱλαστήριος, -α, -ον (< ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: IV Mac 17:22; neut., Ex 25:16(17) ff. 31:7 35:12 38:5 (37:6) ff., Le 16:2, 13 ff. Nu 7:89 (כַּפֹּרֶת), Ez 43:14, 17, 20 (עֲזָרָה) Am 9:1 (on the original here, v. Deiss., BS, 127)*;]
propitiatory (μνῆμα, FlJ, Ant., xvi, 7, 1; θάνατος, II Mac, l.c.): of Christ, Ro 3:25; as subst., το ἱ. (sc. ἐπίθεμα, Ex 25:16, 17, where the word first occurs in LXX and where ἱ. ἐ. = כַּפֹּרֶת (q.v. in BDB, s.v.), elsewhere rendered simply τὸ ἱ; cf. Deiss., 124 ff.; Westc., He., in l.), He 9:5.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from the alternate form of G138 (αἱρέομαι);
strong.def: cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἵλεως, -ων (Att. for ἵλαος), [in LXX for חָלִיל, I Ki 14:45, II Ki 20:20, al.; ἵ. εἶναι, סלח, III Ki 8:30 ff., Je 38(31):34, al.;]
propitious, merciful: τ. ἀδικίαις, He 8:12 (Je 38(31):34; cf. III Ki 8:30 ff.); ἵ. σοι (sc. ἔστω ὁ θεός), Mt 16:22 (cf. I Ki 14:45).†

strong.derivation: neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation;
strong.def: (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰλλυρικόν, -οῦ, τό,
Illyricum, a region bordering on the Adriatic Sea: Ro 15:19.†

strong.def: of uncertain affinity); to long for

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἱμείρω, [in LXX: Jb 3:21 B3R (ABא, ὁμ-);] I Th 2:8(Rec.), v.s. ὁμείρομαί.

strong.def: Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 Ἰόππη (FlJ, id., and also Ἰόπη), -ης, ἡ, (Heb. יָפוֹ),
Joppa: Ac 9 10 11.†

strong.def: rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἰός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Ez 24:6, 11, 12 (חֶלְאָה), Ps 139 (140):3 (חֵמָה), al.;]
1. an arrow.
2. rust (Ez 24:6): Ja 5:3 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).
3. poison: fig., Ro 3:13 (Ps 139 (140):3), Ja 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † Ἰουδαΐζω (< Ἰουδαῖος), [in LXX: Es 8:17 (יהד hith.)*;]
to conform to Jewish practice, to Judaize: Ga 2:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † Ἰουδαϊκός, ή, -όν, [in LXX: II Mac 8:11 V, 13:21*;]
Jewish: Tit 1:14.†

strong.def: Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† Ἰουδαϊκῶς adv.;
in Jewish fashion: Ga 2:14.†

strong.def: "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † Ἰουδαϊσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< Ἰουδαΐζω), [in LXX: II Mac 2:21 8:1 14:38, IV Mac 4:26*;]
Judaism, the observance of Jewish rites: Ga 1:13, 14.†

strong.derivation: feminine of the same as G2457 (Ἰούλιος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰουλία, -ας, ἡ,
Julia: Ro 16:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἰούλιος, -ου, ὁ,
Julius: Ac 27:1, 3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰουνίας, -α, ὁ (or Ἰουνία, -ας, ἡ, Junia; AV, H, mg.
Junias: Ro 16:7.†

strong.def: Justus, the name of three Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἰοῦστος, -ου, ὁ,
Justus, the surname of,
1. Joseph Barsabbas: Ac 1:23.
2. Titus, of Corinth: Ac 18:7.
3. Jesus, a Christian of Rome: Col 4:11.†

strong.def: an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἱππεύς, -έως (on acc. pl., -εῖς, ν. Bl., § 8, 2; Thack., Gr., 148),ὁ (< ἵππος), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָשׁ;]
a horseman: Ac 23:23, 32.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G2462 (ἵππος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἱππικός, -ή, -όν (< ἵππος), [in LXX: I Mac 15:33, III Mac 1:1*;]
of a horse or of horsemen, equestrian; as subst., τὸ ἱ. (sc. στράτευμα), cavalry: He 9:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 ἵππος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for סוּס, sometimes for פָּרָשׁ, רֶכֶב;]
a horse: Ja 3:3, Re 6:2 ff. Re 9:7 ff. Re 14:20 18:13 19:11 ff.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from G2046 (ἐρέω) (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἶρις, -ιδος, ἡ, [in LXX: Ex 30:24 (קִדָּה)*, (קֶשֶׁת, Ge 9:13, Ez 1:28, is rendered by τόξον);]
1. Iris, the messenger of the gods.
2. a rainbow or halo: Re 4:3 10:1.
3. The plant Iris (cf. Ex 30:24).†

strong.def: Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰσσαχάρ (Rec. Ἰσαχ-, Ἰσασχ- (Elz.), T, -άχαρ), ὁ indecl. (FlJ, Ἰσάχαρις, Ἰσάσχ-) (Heb. יִשְׁשָׂכָר, Ge 30:18),
Issachar: Re 7:7.†

strong.derivation: assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of G1492 (εἴδω);

strong.def: likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication, equity

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἰσότης, -ητος, ἡ (< ἴσος), [in LXX: Jb 36:30, Za 4:7*;]
1. equality: II Co 8:13, 14.
2. equity, fairness: τὸ δίκαιον κ. τὴν ἰ., Col 4:1 (for distinction bet. τὸ δ. and ἡ ἰ., v. ICC, in l).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἰσότιμος, -ον, (< ἴσος, τιμή),
equally privileged, held in equal honour: πίστις, II Pe 1:1 (R, mg., equally precious, but v Field, Notes, 240; Mayor, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἰσόψυχος -ον (< ἴσος, ψυχή), [in LXX: Ps 54(55):13 (כְּעֶרְכִּי)*;]
1. of equal spirit (Æsch., Agam., 1470).
2. like-minded: Phl 2:20.†

strong.def: an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 Ἰσραηλείτης (Rec. -λίτης),ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Nu 25:8 (יִשְׂרָאֵל), III Ki 20 (21):1 (יִזְרְעֵאלִי; Luc. Ἰεζραηλίτης), etc.;]
an Israelite, the name expressive of theocratic privilege (v.s. Ἑβραῖος): Ro 9:4 11:1, II Co 11:22; ἀληθῶς Ἰ., Jo 1:48; ἄνδρες Ἰ., Ac 2:22 3:12 5:35 13:16 21:28.†

strong.def: to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἱστορέω, -ῶ (< ἵστωρ, one learned or skilled in) [in LXX: I Es 1:33, 42*;]
1. c. acc. rei, to inquire into, learn by inquiry.
2. C. acc. pers., to inquire of or about.
3. to narrate, record.
4. In late writers, to visit, become acquainted with: Ga 1:18 (v. Ellic., in l., and cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Ἰταλία, -ας, ἡ,
Italy: ἡ Ἰ. (v. Bl., § 46, 11), Ac 18:2 27:1, 6, He 13:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰταλικός, -ή, -όν (< Ἰταλία),
Italian: σπεῖρα Ἰ., Ac 10:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἴχνος, -εος (-ους), τό, [in LXX for כַּף, etc.;]
a track, footstep: metaph. (as freq. in cl.), στοιχεῖν τοῖς ἴ., Ro 4:12; περιπατεῖν τοῖς ἴ., II Co 12:18; ἐπακολουθεῖν τοῖς ἴ., I Pe 2:21 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἰωάθαμ (WH, -θάμ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. יוֹתָם),
Jotham, King of Judah: Mt 1:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰώβ, ὁ (Heb. אִיּוֹב),
Job: Ja 5:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰωήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. יוֹאֵל),
Joel: Ac 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἰωράμ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. יְחוֹרָם),
Joram, Jehoram: Mt 1:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἰωσαφάτ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. יְהוֹשָׁפָט),
Jehoshaphat: Mt 1:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἰωσείας (-σίας, Rec.), -ου, ὁ (Heb. יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ),
Josiah: Mt 1:10, 11.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet);
strong.def: "iota", the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put (figuratively) for a very small part of anything

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἰῶτα, τό,
iota (Heb. י, i.e. the smallest letter): Mt 5:18.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and the neuter plural of G3739 (ὅς);
strong.def: according to which things, i.e. just as

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 καθά adv. (for καθ’ ἅ), [in LXX: Ge 7:9 19:8, al. (כַּאֲשֶׁר, כְּ), Is 58:11, Wi 3:10, al. ;]
just as, according as: Mt 27:10(LXX), Lk 1:2, D (cf. Bl., § 78, 1; Phil. Gosp., 8 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 καθ-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (< καθαιρέω), [in LXX: Ex 23:24 (הָרֵס), I Mac 3:43*;]
a pulling down, destruction: fig., κ. ὀχυρωμάτων, II Co 10:4; opp. to οἰκοδομή, II Co 10:8 13:10.†

strong.def: to cleanse, i.e. (specially) to prune; figuratively, to expiate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καθαίρω (< καθαρός), [in LXX: Is 28:27 (דּוּשׁ ho.), II Ki 4:6, Je 51:39 א* ;]
to cleanse: of pruning, Jo 15:2 (cf. καθαρίζω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 καθάπερ (for καθ’ ἅπερ = καθά) adv., [in LXX for כַּאֲשֶׁר, Ge 12:4, Ex 7:6, al.;]
just as, even as: Ro 3:4 4:6 9:13 10:15 11:8 12:4, I Co 10:10 12:12, II Co 1:14 3:13, 18 8:11, I Th 2:11 3:6, 12 4:6, He 4:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** καθ-άπτω, [in Sm.: Ca 1:6*;]
1. to fasten on, put upon, c. acc.
2. Act. for mid. (cf. Bl., § 53, 3), to lay hold of, attack: c. gen., χειρός, Ac 28:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καθαρότης, -ητος, ἡ (< καθαρός), [in LXX: Ex 24:10 (טֹהַר), Wi 7:24*;]
purity, cleanness: c. gen., He 9:13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * καθηγητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< καθηγέομαι, to go before, guide),
1. prop., a guide.
2. a master, teacher (MGr. professor): Mt 23:16.†

strong.def: to reach to, i.e. (neuter of present active participle, figuratively as adjective) becoming

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 καθ-ήκω, [in LXX: impers., Le 5:10, Ez 21:27 (32), al. (מִשְׁפָּט); τὰ κ., Ex 5:13, al. (דָּבָר), etc.;]
1. to come down, come to.
2. to be fit, proper: impers., c. acc. et inf., Ac 22:22 (on the tense, v. Bl., § 63, 4); τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα, Ro 1:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† καθημερινός, -ή, -όν (< καθ’ ἡμέραν), [in LXX: Jth 12:15*;]
daily (MGr. καθημερνός): Ac 6:1.†

strong.def: according to which thing, i.e. precisely as, in proportion as

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 καθό (= καθ’ ὅ), adv., [in LXX: Le 9:5, 15 (אֲשֶׁר), I Es 1:50, Si 16:20, Ba 1:6, II Mac 4:16*;]
as, according as: Ro 8:26, II Co 8:12, I Pe 4:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καθόλου (= καθ’ ὅλου and so in cl. bef. Arist.), adv., [in LXX: Ex 22:11(10), Am 3:3, 4; Ez 13:3, 22 17:14 (τὸ κ, μή = לְבִּלְתִּי), Da LXX TH 3:50*;]
on the whole, in general: μή κ., not at all, Ac 4:18.†

strong.def: to behold fully, i.e. (figuratively) distinctly apprehend

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καθ-οράω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Nu 24:2 (ראה), Jb 10:4 39:26, III Mac 3:11*;]
1. to look down.
2. to discern clearly: Ro 1:20.†

strong.def: Cain, (i.e. Cajin), the son of Adam

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Καίν (Τ, Κάϊν), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Κάϊς, -ιος), (Heb. קַיִן; Ge 4:1),
Cain: He 11:4, I Jo 3:12, Ju 11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 καινότης, -ητος, ἡ (< καινός), [in LXX: III Ki 8:53, Ez 47:12*;]
1. novelty (Thuc., Isocr., LS, s.v.).
2. freshness, newness: ἐν κ. ζωῆς (v. Lft., Notes, 296), Ro 6:4; ἐν κ. πνεύματος, Ro 7:6.†

strong.def: and indeed, i.e. nevertheless or notwithstanding

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 καίπερ, concessive particle, [in LXX: Pr 6:8, Wi 11:9, Jh 1:13, II-IV Mac11*;]
although: c. ptcp., Phl 3:4, He 5:8 7:5 12:17, II Pe 1:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** καίτοι (= καί τοι, and so also written in cl.), concessive particle, [in LXX: IV Mac 2:6*;]
and yet, although: Ac 14:17; c. ptcp., He 4:3.†

strong.def: and yet indeed, i.e. although really

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 * καίτοιγε, strengthened form of καίτοι, q.v. (and v.s. γε): Jo 4:2.†

strong.def: badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively) malignity, or (passively) trouble

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 κακία, -ας, ἡ (< κακός), [in LXX chiefly for רָאָה;]
1. badness in quality (opp. to ἀρετή, excellence).
2. wickedness, depravity, malignity: Ac 8:22, Ro 1:29, I Co 5:8 14:20, Eph 4:31, Col 3:8, Tit 3:3, Ja 1:21, I Pe 2:1, 16.
3. In late Gk., evil, trouble, affliction (Am 3:6, I Ki 6:9, Ec 7:15, Si 19:6, al.): Mt 6:34 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2556 (κακός) and G2239 (ἦθος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** κακοήθεια (WH, -θία), -ας, ἡ (< κακός, ἦθος), [in LXX: Es 8:13, III Mac 3:22 7:3 A, IV Mac 1:4 3:4*;]
malignity, malevolence: Ro 1:29 (Cremer, 329).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2256 (ἡμιώριον) and G3806 (πάθος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κακοπάθεια (WH, -θία), -ας, ἡ (< κακοπαθής, suffering), [in LXX: Ma 1:13 (תְּלָאָה), II Mac 2:26, 27, IV Mac 9:8*;]
distress, affliction: Ja 5:10.†

strong.kjv: be afflicted, endure afflictions (hardness), suffer trouble

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κακοπαθέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Jon.4.10 (עמל)*;]
to suffer evil, endure affliction: II Ti 2:9 4:5, Ja 5:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κακοποιός, -όν (< κακόν, ποιέω), [in LXX: Pr 12:4 (בּוּשׁ hi.) Pr 24:19 (רעע hi.)*;]
doing evil; as susbt., an evil-doer: I Pe 2:12, 14 4:15.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G2556 (κακός) and G2192 (ἔχω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † κακουχέω, -ῶ (< κακόν, ἔχω), [in LXX: III Ki 2:26 11:39 (ענה pi., hith.)*;]
to ill-treat, hurt, torment: pass. ptcp., He 11:37 13:3.†

strong.kjv: make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 κακόω, -ῶ (< κακός), [in LXX chiefly for רעע hi., ענה pi.;]
1. to ill-treat, afflict, distress: c. acc. pers., Ac 7:6, 19 12:1 18:10, I Pe 3:13.
2. (not in cl.), to embitter (Ps 105 (106):32): Ac 14:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κάκωσις, -εως, ἡ (κακόω), [in LXX (for עֳנִי, רָעָה, etc.): Ex 3:7, Je 2:28, Wi 3:2, al.;]
ill-treatment: Ac 7:34(LXX).†

strong.def: a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καλάμη, -ης, ἡ (cf. κάλαμος), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, Ex 5:12, Is 5:24, al.;]
a stalk of corn, stubble: I Co 3:12.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G2566 (καλλίον) and G1636 (ἐλαία);
strong.def: a cultivated olive tree, i.e. a domesticated or improved one

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * καλλιέλαιος, ου, ἡ,
the garden olive (opp. to ἀγριέλ-): Ro 11:24.†

strong.derivation: neuter of the (irregular) comparative of G2570 (καλός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) καλλίων, -ον,
compar. of καλός, v.s. καλῶς.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† καλο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ,
a teacher of that which is good: Tit 2:3.†

strong.def: Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) Καλοὶ Λιμένες,
Fair Havens, a harbour in Crete: Ac 27:8.†

strong.def: to do well, i.e. live virtuously

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † καλο-ποιέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Le 5:4 F (καλῶς π., B)*;]
to do well, act honourably: II Th 3:13 (cf. Ga 6:9 τὸ καλὸν π.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κάλυμμα, -τος, τό (< καλύπτω), [in LXX: Nu 3:25 4:8 ff. (מִכְסֶה), Ex 34:33 ff. (מַסְוֶה), etc.;]
a covering, veil: II Co 3:13-16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κάμινος, -ου, ἡ, [in LXX: Ge 19:28, Ex 19:18, Is 48:10, al. (כִּבְשָׁן, כּוּר), Da LXX TH 3:6 ff. (אַתּוּן);]
a furnace: Mt 13:42, 50, Re 1:15 9:2.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and the base of G3466 (μυστήριον);
strong.def: to shut down, i.e. close the eyes

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 καμμύω (syncopated form of καταμύω, used by Ep. and κοινή writers; Rutherford, NPhr., 426 f.), [in LXX: Is 6:10 (שׁעע hi.) 29:10 33:15 (עצם), La 3:44 AR*;]
to shut the eyes: τ. ὀφθαλμούς, Mt 13:15, Ac 28:27 (Is 6:10).†

strong.def: properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to tire (figuratively, faint, sicken)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κάμνω, [in LXX: Jb 10:1 (קוּט ni.) 17:2, Wi 4:16 15:9, IV Mac 3:8 7:13*;]
1. to work; hence, from the effect of continued work,
2. to be weary: He 12:3.
3. to be sick: Ja 5:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κάμπτω, [in LXX chiefly for כּרע, IV Ki 1:13, II Ch 29:29, Is 45:24(23), al.;]
to bend, bow: c. acc. rei, γόνυ, τὰ γ.; c. dat. pers., τῇ Βάαλ, Ro 11:4(LXX); πρὸς τ. πατέρα, Eph 3:14; by meton., πᾶν γόνυ for πᾶς, Ro 14:11(LXX), Phl 2:10 (cf. ἀνα-, συν-κάμπτω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Κανά (Rec. -νᾶ), ἡ, indecl.,
Cana, of Galilee: Jo 2:1, 11 4:46 21:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κανδάκη, -ης, ἡ,
Candace: Ac 8:27.†

strong.def: a rule ("canon"), i.e. (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κανών, -όνος, ὁ (cf. κάννα, and Heb. קָנֶה, a reed), [in LXX: Mi 7:4, Jth 13:6, IV Mac 7:21 (and in Aq., Ps 18 (19):5, Jb 38:5)*;]
1. a rod or bar (Jth 13:6).
2. a measuring rule; hence, metaph,
3. a rule or standard: Ga 6:16.
4. a limit (RV, province): II Co 10:13, 15, 16. (For the history of the word and esp. its later meanings, v. Westc., Canon, App. A; cf. also MM, Exp., xv; Cremer, 744.)†

strong.def: to retail, i.e. (by implication) to adulterate (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * καπηλεύω (< κάπηλος, a huckster, cf. Is 1:22(LXX), Si 26:29),
to make a trade of (RV, mg., make merchandise of), or perhaps (cf. Is 1:22(LXX)) to corrupt (RV, txt.): II Co 2:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 καπνός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX for עָשָׁן;]
smoke: Re 8:4 9:2, 3, 17, 18 14:11 15:8 18:9, 18 19:3; ἀτμὶς καπνοῦ, Ac 2:19(LXX).†

strong.def: Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Καππαδοκία, -ας, ἡ,
Cappadocia, a province of Asia Minor: Ac 2:9, I Pe 1:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† καρδιο-γνώστης, -ου, ὁ (< καρδία, γνώστης),
knower of hearts: Ac 1:24 15:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κάρπος, -ου, ὁ
Carpus: II Ti 4:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καρπο-φόρος, -ον (< καρπύς, φέρω), [in LXX: Je 2:21 (זֶרַע), Ps 106 (107):34 148:9 (פְּרִי)*;]
fruitful: Ac 14:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καρτερέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Jb 2:9 (חזק hi.), Is 42:14 (פּעה), Si 2:2 12:15, II, IV Mac7*;]
to be steadfast, patient: He 11:27 (cf. προσ-καρτερέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-βάλλω, [in LXX chiefly for נפל hi.;]
1. to cast down, prostrate: metaph., pass., II Co 4:9.
2. to put down, lay down: metaph., mid., c. acc., θεμέλιον, He 6:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατα-βαρέω, -ῶ,
to weigh down: metaph., c. acc. pers., II Co 12:16.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and G1018 (βραβεύω) (in its original sense);
strong.def: to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κατα-βραβεύω (< βραβεύς, an umpire, cf. βραβεῖον),
to give judgment against, condemn (v. Field, Notes, 196; Abbott, Essays, 104 f.): Col 2:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † καταγγελεύς, -έως, ὁ,
a proclaimer, herald (in Inscr., κ. ἀγώνων, Deiss., LAE, 97): c. gen. obj., Ac 17:18.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);
strong.kjv: declare, preach, shew, speak of, teach

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 κατ-αγγέλλω, [in LXX: Pr 17:5 A, II Mac 8:36 9:17*;]
1. to proclaim, declare: c. acc. rei, Ac 3:24 16:21 17:23; τ. ἀνάστασιν, Ac 4:2; τ. λόγον τοῦ Θ., τ. Κ., Ac 13:5 15:36; ὁδὸν σωτηρίας, Ac 16:17; φῶς, Ac 26:23; τ. μυστήριον τοῦ Θ., I Co 2:1; τ. εὐαγγέλιον, 9:14; τ. θάνατον τοῦ Κ., 11:26; pass., ἄφεσις, Ac 13:38; ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θ., Ac 17:13; ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν, Ro 1:8; c. acc. pers., of Christ, ὅν, Ac 17:3, Col 1:28; τ. Χριστόν, Phl 1:17; pass., Phl 1:18.
2. to denounce (Xen., al.); (for comparison with ἀγγέλλω, ἀναγ-, ἀπαγ-, v. Westc. on I Jo 1:5; and cf. προ-καταγγέλλω).†

strong.def: to note against, i.e. find fault with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κατα-γινώσκω (v.s. γινώσκω), [in LXX: De 25:1 (רשׁע hi.), Pr 28:11 (חקר), Si 14:2 19:5*;]
to blame, condemn: c. gen. pers., I Jo 3:20, 21; pass., κατεγνωσμένος ἦν (RV, he stood condemned, v. Ellie., in l.; but cf. Field, Notes, 188): Ga 2:11.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G4486 (ῥήγνυμι);
strong.def: to rend in pieces, i.e. crack apart

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κατ-άγνυμι, [in LXX for נחת pi., etc.;]
to break: c. acc. rei, Mt 12:20(LXX), Jo 19:31-33.†

strong.def: to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to overcome

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατ-αγωνίζομαι, depon., "perfective" compound (M, Pr., 116);
1. to struggle against.
2. to conquer, overcome: He 11:33.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κατά-δηλος, -ον (δὴλος),
quite manifest, evident: He 7:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-δουλόω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for עבד;]
to enslave: II Co 11:20, Ga 2:4.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G1413 (δυνάστης);
strong.def: to exercise dominion against, i.e. oppress

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-δυναστεύω, [in LXX for ינה, עשׁק, etc.;]
to exercise power over, oppress: c. acc. pers. (Xen.; LXX, Mi 2:2, Wi 2:10, al.); c. gen. pers., Ja 2:6 (ὑμᾶς, T); pass., Ac 10:38 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κατα-καλύπτω, [in LXX chiefly for כּסה pi.;]
to cover up; mid., to cover or veil oneself: I Co 11:6; τ. κεφαλήν, I Co 11:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † κατα-καυχάομαι, -ῶμαι, [in LXX: Za 10:12 (הלךְ hith.), Je 27 (50):11 (עלז), Je 27 (50):38 (הלל)*;]
1. to boast against, exult over: c. gen., Ro 11:18, Ja 2:13; seq. κατά, c. gen., Ja 3:14 (T, om. κατά).
2. seq. ἐν, to glory in (Za 10:12, Je 27:38).†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of a compound of G2819 (κλῆρος) and G1325 (δίδωμι);
strong.def: to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) † κατα-κληρονομέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for נחל, ירשׁ, etc.;]
1. to distribute by lot or as an inheritance (Nu 34:18, Jos 14:1, al.): Ac 13:19.
2. to receive by inheritance (De 1:38, al.).†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G2830 (κλύδων);
strong.def: to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-κλύζω, [in LXX for שׁטף, Ps 77 (78):20, al.;]
to inundate, deluge: pass., II Pe 3:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† κατά-κριμα, -τος, τό (< κατακρίνω),
penalty (RV, condemnation; but cf. Deiss., BS, 264 f.; MM, Exp., xv): Ro 5:16, 18 8:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† κατά-κρισις, -εως, ἡ (< κατακρίνω),
condemnation: II Co 3:9 7:3 (cf. Deiss., LAE, 91 f.).†

strong.def: to be a traducer, i.e. to slander

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 κατα-λαλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for דּבר ni., pi.;]
to speak evil of, rail at: in cl., c. acc.; in LXX,
(a). c. gen.,
(b). seq. κατά, c. gen.; in NT, c. gen. (M, Pr., 65): Ja 4:11, I Pe 2:12; pass., I Pe 3:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† κατα-λαλιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< κατάλαλος), [in LXX: Wi 1:11*;]
evil-speaking, railing: pl., II Co 12:20, I Pe 2:1.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G2980 (λαλέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατά-λαλος, -ου, ὁ,
a railer, defamer: Ro 1:30.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original meaning);
strong.def: to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-λέγω, [in LXX: De 19:16 (ענה), II Mac 7:30 R*;]
1. to lay down; mid. (in Hom.), to lie down.
2. to narrate (LXX, De 19:16, II Mac 7:30).
3. to choose out, hence, to enrol (as of soldiers, Hdt., Thuc., a1., v. LS, s.v.): of widows, pass., I Ti 5:9 (cf. Ellic.; CGT, in l.).†

strong.def: a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κατά-λειμμα, -τος, τό (< καταλείπω), [in LXX far שָׁאַר (Is 10:22 14:22), שְׁאֵרִית, etc.;]
a remnant: Ro 9:27, Rec. (for ὑπόλειμμα, q.v.).†

strong.def: exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to (the divine) favor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κατ-αλλαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< καταλλάσσω), [in LXX: Is 9:5(4), II Mac 5:20*;]
1. exchange.
2. reconciliation: Ro 5:11; κ. κόσμου, Ro 11:15; διακονία τῆς κ., II Co 5:18; λόγος τῆς κ., II Co 5:19.†

strong.def: to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 κατ-αλλάσσω (Att. -ττω; cf. ἀλλάσσω), [in LXX: Je 31 (48):39 (חתת), II Mac 1:5 7:33 8:29*;]
prop., to change, exchange (esp. of money); hence, of persons, to change from emnity to friendship, to reconcile (for exx. in cl., v. Thayer, LS): of the reconciliation of man to God (Lft., Notes, 288; ICC on Ro 5:10; DCG, ii, 474, 797), II Co 5:18, 19; pass., Ro 5:10, II Co 5:20; of a woman returning to her husband, I Co 7:11 (cf. ἀπο-καταλλάσσω).†

strong.def: left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατά-λοιπος, -ον, [in LXX for שְׁאָר, שְׁאֵרִית, יֶרֶר, etc.;]
left remaining: ἱο κ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Ac 15:17(LXX).†

strong.def: to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-μανθάνω, [in LXX: Ge 34:1 (ראה), Jb 35:4(5) (שׁוּר), Si 9:5, 8, al.;]
to learn thoroughly, observe well, consider carefully (on distinction bet. κ. and μανθάνω, cf. M, Pr., 117): Mt 6:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-μένω, [in LXX for ישׁב (Nu 20:1, al.), etc.;]
to remain permanently, abide: Ac 1:13, I Co 16:6, WH (παραμ-, T, RV).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κατ-ανά-θεμα,
Rec. for κατάθεμα, q.v.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατα-θεματίζω,
to curse vehemently: Mt 26:74 (cf. ἀναθεμ-).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατ-αν-αλίσκω, [in LXX chiefly for אכל;]
1. to use up, spend.
2. to consume: of fire, ptcp., He 12:29(LXX).†

strong.def: to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * κατα-ναρκάω, -ῶ (< ναρκάω, to grow numb, in LXX, in causal sense, for יקע, Ge 32:25(26); without Heb. equiv., Ge 32:32(33), Jb 33:19, Da LXX 11:6*);
1. to cause to grow numb.
2. Intrans., to grow numb; hence metaph., to be inactive, be burdensome to c. gen., II Co 11:9 12:13, 14; pass., to be quite numb (Hippocr.).†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί);
strong.def: to meet against, i.e. arrive at (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 † κατ-αντάω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Ki 3:29 (חוּל), II Mac 4:21, 24, 44 6:14*;]
to come to, arrive at: seq. εἰς, c. acc. loc., Ac 16:1 18:19, 24 21:7 25:13 (v. M, Pr., 132) 27:12 28:13; seq. ἀντικρύ, c. gen., Ac 20:15. Metaph., seq. εἰς, c. acc. pers., I Co 10:11 14:36; id. c. acc. rei, to attain to: Ac 26:7, Eph 4:13, Phl 3:11.†

strong.def: a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with G3506 (νεύω) or even with G3571 (νύξ))) stupor (lethargy)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κατά-νυξις, -εως, ἡ (< κατανύσσω, q.v.), [in LXX: Ps 59 (60):3 (תַּרְעֵלָה), Is 29:10 (תַּרְדֵּמָה)*;]
1. a pricking.
2. (Perhaps through resembl. of κατανύσσω to -νυστάζω), torpor of mind, stupefaction: Ro 11:8(LXX) (v. ICC, in l.; Field, Notes, 157).†

strong.def: to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κατα-νύσσω, [in LXX: Ge 34:7 (עצב hith.), Le 10:3, Ps 4:4, Ps 29:12, al. (דּמם), Da LXX TH Su 10 (רדם ni.), Si 12:12 14:1, al.;]
1. to strike or prick violently.
2. to stun.
3. Of strong emotion, pass., to be smitten: τὴν καρδίαν, Ac 2:37 (v.s. κατάνυξις).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 κατά-παυσις, -εως, ἡ (< καταπαύω), [in LXX chiefly for מְנוּחָה, Ps 94 (95):11, Is 66:1, al.; ἡμέρα τῆς κ., II Mac 15:1;]
1. in cl., a putting to rest, causing to cease.
2. In LXX and NT, rest, repose: Ac 7:49(LXX), He 3:11, 18 4:1, 3, 5, 10, 11.†

strong.def: to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κατα-παύω, [in LXX for נוּחַ, שׁבת, etc.;]
1. trans.,
(a). to cause to cease, restrain: Ac 14:18;
(b). to cause to rest: He 4:8.
2. Intrans., to rest: seq. ἀτό, He 4:4(LXX), 10.†

strong.def: to drink down, i.e. gulp entire (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 κατα-πίνω, [in LXX chiefly for בּלע;]
1. to drink down, swallow: Mt 23:24, Re 12:16.
2. to devour: I Pe 5:8. Metaph., to swallow up, consume: pass., I Co 15:54(LXX), II Co 2:7 5:4, He 11:29.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G4192 (πόνος);
strong.def: to labor down, i.e. wear with toil (figuratively, harass)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** κατα-πονέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Mac 8:2 (A), III Mac 2:2, 13*;]
to wear down, oppress, treat hardly: pass., Ac 7:24, II Pe 2:7.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of the same as G4195 (Πόντος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-πονίζω, [in LXX for טבע pu., Ex 15:4 A, בּלע pi., שׁטף, Ps 54 (55):9 68 (69):2, al.;]
to throw into the sea, sink or drown therein: Mt 14:30; pass., 18:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 κατ-άρα, -ας, -ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for קְלָלָה;]
a curse: Ga 3:10, 13, He 6:8, II Pe 2:14; opp. to εὐλογία, Ja 3:10; concrete, of Christ, Ga 3:13 (v. Lft. in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατ-αριθμέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Ch 31:19 (יחשׂ hith.), al.;]
to number or count among: seq. ἐν, Ac 1:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατ-άρτισις, -εως, ἡ (< καταρτίζω),
a strengthening, making fit: in ethical sense, II Co 13:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† καταρτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in Sm.: Is 38:12*;]
= κατάρτισις (but v. ICC, Eph 4:12): Eph 4:12.†

strong.def: to sway downward, i.e. make a signal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** κατα-σείω, [in LXX: Da TH Bel 14 AR, I Mac 6:38*;]
1. to shake down.
2. Of the hand, to shake or wave as a signal: τ. χεῖρα, Ac 19:33; τ. χειρί, Ac 13:16; id. c. dat. pers., Ac 21:40; seq. inf., Ac 12:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-σκάπτω, [in LXX for נתץ, הרס, etc.;]
to dig down: Ro 11:3(LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G4639 (σκιά);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κατα-σκιάζω,
to overshadow: c. acc., He 9:5.†

strong.def: to be a sentinel, i.e. to inspect insidiously

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-σκοπέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Ki 10:3, I Ch 19:3 (רגל pi.), I Mac 5:38 (A)*;]
to view closely, inspect, spy out: c. acc., Ga 2:4.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) (intensive) and G4649 (σκοπός) (in the sense of a watcher);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατά-σκοπος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for רגל pi.;]
a spy: He 11:31.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G2596 (κατά) and G4679 (σοφίζω);
strong.def: to be crafty against, i.e. circumvent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κατα-σοφίζομαι, [in LXX: Ex 1:10 (חכם hith.), Jth 5:11 10:19*;]
to deal craftily with, outwit: Ac 7:19(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** κατα-στέλλω, [in LXX: II Mac 4:31, III Mac 6:1*;]
1. to let down, lower.
2. to keep down, restrain: c. acc., Ac 19:35, 36.†

strong.def: properly, a position or condition, i.e. (subjectively) demeanor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† κατά-στημα, -τος, τό (καθίστημι), [in LXX: III Mac 5:45 (-εμα, A)*;]
1. condition, of health, etc.
2. demeanour: Tit 2:3 (for exx. v. Field, Notes, 220).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< καταστέλλω), [in LXX: Is 61:3 (מַעֲטֶה)*;]
1. a letting down, checking.
2. steadiness, quietness in demeanour.
3. LXX and NT (cf. Plut., ii, 65 D; -ίζω = vestire), a garment, dress, attire: I Ti 2:9 (but v. Ellic., in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατα-στρηνιάω, -ῶ,
to wax wanton against: c. gen., I Ti 5:11.

strong.def: an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. demolition; figuratively, apostasy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ (< καταστρέφω), [in LXX: Jb 21:17, Pr 1:27 (אֵיד), al.;]
1. overthrow: II Pe 2:6 (WH, om.).
2. Metaph., subversion, upsetting (cf. καθαίρεσις, II Co 13:10): II Ti 2:14.†

strong.def: to strew down, i.e. (by implication) to prostrate (slay)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-στρώννυμι, [in LXX: Nu 14:16 (שׁחט), Jb 12:23 (שׁטח), Jth4, II Mac4*;]
1. to strew or spread over.
2. to lay low, overthrow: I Co 10:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-σφραγίζω, [in LXX: Jb 9:7 37:7 (חתם), Wi 2:5*;]
to seal up, secure with a seal: Re 5:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † κατά-σχεσις, -εως, ἡ (< κατέχω), [in LXX nearly always for אֲחֻזָּה;]
1. a holding back.
2. LXX and NT, a holding fast, possession: Ac 7:5, 45.†

strong.def: to place down, i.e. deposit (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-τίθημι, [in LXX: I Ch 21:27 שׁוּב hi.), Ps 40 (41):8 (יצק), I Mac 10:23, al.;]
to lay down, deposit, lay by: Mk 15:46, T; mid., to lay up for oneself: χάριν (Hdt., al., v. LS, s.v.), c. dat. pers., Ac 24:27 25:9.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and (to cut);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† κατα-τομή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in Sm.: Je 48 (31):37 (κατατέμνω is used in LXX of forbidden mutilations: Le 21:5, al.);]
1. incision.
2. excision, concision, mutilation: in sarcasm, by paronomasia, in contrast to (true) περιτομή (Phl 3:3), of Judaizing Christians, Phl 3:2 (v. Lft., in l.; Cremer, 883).†

strong.def: to run down, i.e. hasten from a tower

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-τρέχω, [in LXX: Le 26:37, Jg 1:6 (רדף), al.;]
to run down: seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Ac 21:32.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to bear down, i.e. (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a vote

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κατα-φέρω, [in LXX for ירד hi., etc.;]
to bring down: αἰτιώματα, Ac 25:7; ψῆφον, to cast a ballot, Ac 26:10; pass., to be borne down: ὕπνῳ, ἀπὸ τ. ὕ., Ac 20:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-φεύγω, [in LXX for נוּס, etc.;]
to flee for refuge: seq. εἰς, Ac 14:6; metaph., c. inf., He 6:18.†

strong.def: to spoil entirely, i.e. (literally) to destroy; or (figuratively) to deprave;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-φθείρω, [in LXX chiefly for שׁחת hi., Ge 6:12, al.;]
1. to destroy entirely.
2. In moral sense (as LXX), to deprave, corrupt: pass. pf. ptcp., seq. τ. νοῦν, II Ti 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κατα-φρονητής, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX for בֹּגֵד, בֹּגְדוֹת, Hb 1:5 2:5, Ze 3:4*;]
a despiser: Ac 13:41.†

strong.def: subterranean, i.e. infernal (belonging to the world of departed spirits)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κατα-χθόνιος, -ον (< χθών, the earth),
subterranean, under the earth (in cl., of the infernal gods): of the departed in Hades, opp. to ἐπουράνιος, ἐπίγειος, Phl 2:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** κατα-χράομαι, -ῶμαι, [in LXX: Ep. Je 28, III Mac 4:5 5:22*;]
to make full use of, use to the uttermost, use up: I Co 7:31; c. dat., I Co 9:18 (for other senses, v. LS, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατείδωλος, -ον (< εἴδωλον),
full of idols: Ac 17:16.†

strong.kjv: before (the presence of), in the sight of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † κατενώπιον adv. (= Hom., κατένωπα), [in LXX: Ps 43 (44):15, al.;]
over against, before: c. gen., τ. δόξης, Ju 24; metaph. (cf. κατέναντι, and v. Lft., Col 1:22), τ. θεοῦ, Eph 1:4, Col 1:22.†

strong.def: to work fully, i.e. accomplish; by implication, to finish, fashion

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
22 κατ-εργάζομαι (emphatic form of ἐργάζομαι), [in LXX for פּעל, etc. (9 exx., each for a different Heb. word);]
to effect by labour, achieve, work out, bring about: c. acc., Ro 4:15 5:3 7:8, 15, 17, 18, 20, II Co 7:10, Eph 6:13, Ja 1:3; pass., II Co 12:12; c. acc. rei et dat. pers., Ro 7:13, II Co 4:17 7:11 9:11; id. seq. διά, c. gen. pers., Ro 15:18; τ. σωτηρίαν, Phl 2:12; c. acc. pers. seq. εἰς, II Co 5:5 (RV, wrought); of evil deeds, Ro 1:27 2:9, I Co 5:3, I Pe 4:3.†

strong.def: to stand over against, i.e. rush upon (assault)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατ-εφ-ίστημι,
to rise up against: Ac 18:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * κατηγορία, -ας, ἡ (< κατήγορος),
an accusation, charge: c. gen. pers., Jo 18:29; seq. κατά, c. id., I Ti 5:19; c. gen. rei, Tit 1:6.†

strong.def: against one in the assembly, i.e. a complainant at law; specially, Satan

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κατήγορος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Pr 18:17 (ריב), II Mac 4:5*;]
an accuser: Ac 23:30, 35 24:8 (WH, R, txt. om.) Ac 25:16, 18.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and perhaps a derivative of the base of G5316 (φαίνω) (meaning downcast in look);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κατήφεια, -ας, ἡ (< κατηφής, downcast, Wi 17:4*),
dejection: Ja 4:9.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G2447 (ἰός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† κατ-ιόω, -ῶ (intensive of ἰόω; < ἰός), [in LXX: Si 12:11*;]
to rust over; pass., become rusted over: Ja 5:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † κατ-οικητήριον, -ου, τό (< κατοικέω), [in LXX for מוֹשָׁב, מָעוֹן, etc.;]
a habitation, dwelling-place: Eph 2:22, Re 18:2.†

strong.def: residence (properly, the condition; but by implication, the abode itself)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κατ-οικία, -ας, ἡ (< κατοικέω), [in LXX chiefly for מוֹשָׁב, Ex 35:3, al.;]
1. a dwelling: Ac 17:26.
2. a settlement (Polyb.).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι) (compare G2072 (ἔσοπτρον));
strong.def: to mirror oneself, i.e. to see reflected (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κατοπτρίζω (< κάτοπτρον, a mirror),
to show as in a mirror. Mid., to see oneself mirrored (v. MM, Exp., xv); c. acc. rei (R, txt., but v. mg.), to reflect as a mirror: II Co 3:18 (cf. Abbott, Essays, 94).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός) (compare G1357 (διόρθωσις));
strong.def: something made fully upright, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (specially, good public administration)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 κατόρθωμα, -τος, τό, Rec. for διόρθωμα (q.v.), Ac 24:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατώτερος, -έρα, -ερον (< κάτω), [in LXX for תַּחְתּוֹן, תַּחְתִּי;]
lower; τὰ. κ. τῆς γῆς (v. AR, Eph 4:9; for rendering this lower earth, v. ICC, Eph 4:9), the lower parts of the earth (cf. Ps 138 (139):15; cf. also MGr., ἡ κάτου γῆ, the underworld, Thumb, MGV, 334): Eph 4:9.†

strong.def: properly, a burn (concretely), but used (abstractly) of a glow

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 καῦμα, -τος, τό (< καίω), [in LXX for חֹם, חֹרֶב, etc.;]
heat: Re 7:16 16:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 καῦσις, -εως, ἡ (< καίω), [in LXX for בּער pi., etc.;]
burning: He 6:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† καυσόω, -ῶ (< καῦσος, burning heat, fever),
1. to burn with fever (Galen., al.).
2. In NT, to burn with great heat: II Pe 3:10, 12 (V. Mayor, in l.).†

strong.def: to brand ("cauterize"), i.e. (by implication) to render unsensitive (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† καυστηριάζω (Rec. καυτηρ-, and so usually in Gk. writers, v. Soph., Lex., s.v.),
to mark by branding, brand (AV, scar, but v. CGT, in l.): metaph., pass. pf. ptcp., I Ti 4:2 (cf. καυτήριον, IV Mac 15:22*).†

strong.derivation: from some (obsolete) base akin to that of (to boast) and G2172 (εὔχομαι);
strong.def: to vaunt (in a good or a bad sense)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
37 καυχάομαι, -ῶμαι, [in LXX for הלל hith., etc.;]
to boast or glory (in LXX, of joyous exultation, and so in the NT quotations, infr.; cf. DB, ii, 790b; Hort on Ja 1:9): absol., I Co 1:31(LXX) I Co 4:7 13:3, II Co 10:13, 17(LXX) 11:16, 18 12:1, 6, Eph 2:9, Ja 4:16; c. acc. rei, II Co 9:2 11:30; seq. ἐν (LXX), Ro 2:23 5:3, I Co 3:21, II Co 5:12 10:15 11:12 12:5, 9, Ga 6:13, 14, Ja 1:9; ἐν (τ.) θεῷ, Ro 2:17 5:11; ἐν κυρίῳ, I Co 1:31(LXX), II Co 10:17(LXX); ἐν Χ. Ἰησοῦ, Phl 3:3; seq. ἐπί c. dat., Ro 5:2; περί, c. gen., II Co 10:8; εἰς, II Co 10:16; ὑπέρ, c. gen. pers., II Co 7:14 12:5; ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, I Co 1:29 (cf. ἐν, κατα-καυχάομαι).†

strong.def: a boast (properly, the object; by implication, the act) in a good or a bad sense

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 καύχημα, -τος, τό (< καυχάομαι), [in LXX chiefly for תְּהִלָּה, תִּפְאֶרֶה;]
1. a boast (Pind.): II Co 5:12 9:3 (Thayer, s.v.; e. contra, 2, Ellic., Lft., on Ga 6:4; Lft., Notes, 204, 277).
2. ground or matter of glorying: Ro 4:2, I Co 5:6 9:15, 16, II Co 1:14, Ga 6:4, Phl 1:26 2:16, He 3:6 (cf. καύχησις).†

strong.def: boasting (properly, the act; by implication, the object), in a good or a bad sense
strong.kjv: boasting, whereof I may glory, glorying, rejoicing

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 † καύχησις, -εως, ἡ (< καυχάομαι), [in LXX for תִּפְאֶרֶה (I Ch 29:13, Ez 16:12, al);]
a boasting, glorying: Ro 3:27, II Co 11:10, 17, Ja 4:16; seq. ὑπέρ, II Co 7:4 8:24; ἐτί, c. gen., II Co 7:14; ἔχω τὴν κ. ἐν Χρ. Ἰησ., Ro 15:17; στέφανος καυχήσεως (Ez 16:12, al.), I Th 2:19; of the cause of glorying, a boast ( = καύχημα), II Co 1:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Κενχρεαί (Rec. Κεγχ-; v. WH, App., 150), -ῶν, αἱ,
Cenchreæ, a port of Corinth: Ac 18:18, Ro 16:1.†

strong.def: Cedron (i.e. Kidron), a brook near Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κεδρών (v.s. κέδρος), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, gen. -ῶνος; Heb. קִדְרוֹן), [in LXX: II Ki 15:23, IV Ki 23:6, al.;]
Cedron (OT, Kidron): χείμαρρος τοῦ Κ., Jo 18:1 (L, Tr., mg., R, txt.; cf. Bl., § 10, 5; Lft., Essays, 172 ff).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κειρία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Pr 7:16 (מַרְבַּדִּים)*;]
1. a bed-cord (Aristoph., AV., 816;Pr 7:16.).
2. In pl., swathings (cf. Field, Notes, 96 f.): Jo 11:44.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κείρω, [in LXX chiefly for גּזז, Is 53:7, al.;]
to cut short the hair, shear: a sheep, Ac 8:32 (Is 53:7). Mid., to have one's hair cut off, be shorn: absol., I Co 11:6; τ. κεφαλήν, Ac 18:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κέλευσμα, -τος, τό, (< κελεύω), [in LXX: Pr 24:62 (30:27)*;]
a call, summons, shout of command: I Th 4:16 (v. M, Th., in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† κενοδοξία, -ας, ἡ (< κενόδοξος), [in LXX: Wi 14:14, II Mac 2:15 8:19*;]
1. foolish fancy, vain opinion, error (LXX, Wi 14:14, II Mac 2:15 8:19).
2. vainglory, groundless conceit: Phl 2:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κενόδοξος, -ον (< κενός, δόξα),
vain-glorious: Ga 5:26.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G2756 (κενός) and G5456 (φωνή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† κενοφωνία, -ας, ἡ (< κενός, φωνέω), [cf. κενολογέω (צפף), Is 8:19*;]
empty talk, babbling: pl., I Ti 6:20, II Ti 2:16.†

strong.def: to make empty, i.e. (figuratively) to abase, neutralize, falsify
strong.kjv: make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 κενόω, -ῶ (< κενός, q.v.), [in LXX: Je 14:2 15:9 (אמל pu.)*;]
to empty. Metaph., to empty, make empty, vain or of no effect: καύχημα, I Co 9:15; ἑαυτόν, of Christ, Phl 2:7 (v Lft.; ICC, in l, and esp. Gifford, Incarn., 54 ff.); pass., πίστις, Ro 4:14; ὁ σταυρός, I Co 1:17; καύχημα, II Co 9:3.†

strong.def: a point ("centre"), i.e. a sting (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κέντρον, -ου, τό (< κεντέω, to prick), [in LXX: Pr 26:3 (מֶתֶג), Ho 13:14 (קֹטֶב), 5:12, Si 38:25, IV Mac 14:19*;]
1. a sting (IV Mac 14:19): Re 9:10. Metaph. (as Ho 13:14): τ. θανάτου, I Co 15:55(LXX), 56.
2. a goad: pl., Ac 26:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κενῶς, adv., [in LXX: Is 49:4 (לְרִיק)*;]
in vain, to no purpose: Ja 4:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κεραμεύς, -εως, ὁ (< κεράννυμι), [in LXX for יצר, Ps 2:9, Je 18:2, al.;]
a potter: Ro 9:21; ὁ ἀγρὸς τοῦ κ., Mt 27:7, 10(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κεραμικός, -ή, -όν (< κέραμος), [in LXX: Da LXX 2:41 (פֶּחָר)*;]
1. (cl.) of a potter (e.g. γῆ).
2. In LXX and NT, = cl., κεραμεοῦς (Plut., κεράμειος, Polyb., -μαῖος, etc), earthen: Re 2:27.†

strong.derivation: prolonged form of a more primary (which is used in certain tenses);
strong.def: to mingle, i.e. (by implication) to pour out (for drinking)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κεράννυμι, [in LXX for מסךְ, Is 5:22, al.;]
to mix, mingle, chiefly of the diluting of wine: Re 18:6; by oxymoron, κεκεράσμενος ἄκρατος, Re 14:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** κέρδος, -εος (-ους), τό, [in Aq.: Ez 27:24; Sm.: Ps 29 (30):10, al.;]
gain: Phl 1:21 3:7, Tit 1:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κέρμα, -τος, τό (< κείρω),
1. a slice, hence,
2. a small coin: pl., Jo 2:15.†

strong.def: a handler of coins, i.e. money-broker

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κερματιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (κερματίζω, to cut small, coin into small money),
a money changer: Jo 2:14.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G2776 (κεφαλή);
strong.def: a principal thing, i.e. main point; specially, an amount (of money)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κεφάλαιος, -α, -ον (< κεφαλή), [in LXX (-αιον, τό) for רֹאשׁ, Nu 4:2, al.;]
of the head; metaph., principal, chief; mostly as subst., κεφάλαιον, τό;
1. the chief point: He 8:1.
2. the sum total, amount: Ac 22:28 (other meaning, LS, s.v.).†

strong.def: properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κεφαλίς, -ίδος, ἡ (dimin. of κεφαλή), [in LXX for מְגִלָּה, וָו, etc.;]
1. a little head.
2. an extremity, capital (of a column).
3. (As in Ez 2:9, Ps 39 (40):8, II Es 6:2) a roll: κ. βιβλίου, He 10:7(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κηπ-ουρός, -οῦ, ὁ (< κῆπος + οὖρος, a watcher),
a gardener: Jo 20:15.†

strong.def: a herald, i.e. of divine truth (especially of the gospel)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κῆρυξ (κήρ-, T), -υκος, ὁ, [in LXX: Da LXX TH 3:4 (כָּרוֹז), Ge 41:43, Si 20:15, IV Mac 6:4*;]
a herald: I Ti 2:7, II Ti 1:11, II Pe 2:5.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G5490 (χάσμα);
strong.def: a huge fish (as gaping for prey)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κῆτος, -εος (-ους), τό, [in LXX: Jh 2:1, 11 (דָּג), Ge 1:21 (תַּנִּין), etc.;]
a huge fish, sea-monster: Mt 12:40(LXX).†

strong.def: the Rock; Cephas (i.e. Kepha), a surname of Peter

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 Κηφᾶς, -ᾶ (v. Bl., § 10, 3), ὁ (Aram. כֵּיפָא),
Cephas, i.e. Peter: Jo 1:43, I Co 1:12 3:22 9:5 15:5, Ga 1:18 2:9, 11, 14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κιθάρα, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for כִּנּוֹר, freq. in Pss (32 (33):2, al.); and in (Da 3:5, al.) for קִיתָרֹס, itself a transliteration of κίθαρις, the Homeric form of κ. (cf. CB, Dn., lviii);]
a lyre, harp: I Co 14:7, Re 5:8 14:2 15:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κιθαρίζω, [in LXX: Is 23:16 (נגן pi.)*;]
to play upon the lyre or harp: I Co 14:7, Re 14:2.†

strong.derivation: from G2788 (κιθάρα) and a derivative of the same as G5603 (ᾠδή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * κιθαρ-ωδός, -οῦ, ὁ (< κιθάρα, ἀοιδός, a singer)
one who plays and sings to the lyre, a harper: Re 14:2 18:22.†

strong.def: Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 Κιλικία, -ας, ἡ,
Cilicia, a province of Asia Minor: Ac 6:9 15:23, 41 21:39 22:3 23:34 27:5, Ga 1:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κιννάμωμον (Rec. κινάμ-), -υο, τό (from the Phœnician, v. LS, s.v., and cf. Heb. קִנָּמוֹן)
cinnamon: Re 18:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 κίνδυνος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Ps 114 (116):3 (מֵצַר), Si 3:26, al.;]
danger, peril: Ro 8:35; pl., II Co 11:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Κείς (Rec. Κίς), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. קִישׁ),
Kish: Ac 13:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) Καῦδα (TR, mg., Κλαῦδα; Rec. Κλαύδη), ἡ,
Cauda, Clauda, an island near Crete: Ac 27:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κλαυδία, -ας, ἡ,
Claudia: II Ti 4:21.†

strong.def: Claudius, the name of two Romans

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Κλαύδιος, -ου, ὁ,
Claudius;
1. the Emperor: Ac 11:28 18:2.
2. A military tribune, C. Lysias: Ac 23:26.†

strong.def: stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the act)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κλέμμα, -τος, τό (< κλέπτω), [in LXX: Ge 31:39, Ex 22:3, 4 (2, 3) (גָּנַב, גְּנֵבָה)*;]
1. a thing stolen (Arist., LXX).
2. = κλοπή, theft (Plato, al.): pl., Re 9:21.†

strong.derivation: from a shorter form of G2564 (καλέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κλέος, -ους, τό, [in LXX: Jb 28:22 (שֵׁמַע) Jb 30:8*;]
1. a rumour, report.
2. good report, fame, glory: I Pe 2:20.†

strong.def: a limb or shoot (as if broken off)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 κλῆμα, -τος, τό (< κλάω), [in LXX chiefly for זְמוֹרָה, דָּלִית, Ez 15:2 17:6, 7, al.;]
a vine-twig, vine-branch: Jo 15:2, 4-6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κλήμης, -εντος, ὁ,
Clement: Phl 4:3.†

strong.def: to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a privilege)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κληρόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: I Ki 14:41 (לכד ni.), Es 4:11 A (קרא ni.), Is 17:11*;]
1. to cast lots.
2. to choose by lot.
3. to assign by lot, assign a portion: pass., ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἐκληρώθημεν, Eph 1:11 (on the various interpretations, v. ICC; AR; Ellic., in l.).†

strong.derivation: from a shorter form of G2564 (καλέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 κλῆσις, -εως, ἡ (καλέω), [in LXX: Je 38 (31):6 (קרא), Jth 12:10 A, III Mac 5:14*;]
a calling, call; in NT, always of the Divine call to salvation: Ro 11:29, I Co 1:26 7:20, Eph 1:18 4:1, 4, Phl 3:14, II Th 1:11, II Ti 1:9, He 3:1, II Pe 1:10 (Cremer, 332).†

strong.def: invited, i.e. appointed, or (specially), a saint

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 κλητός, -ή, -όν (< καλέω), [in LXX for קרא, מִקְרָא, Ex 12:16, al.;]
called, invited (as to a banquet, Æsch., I Ki 1:41, III Mac 5:14); in NT, always of the Divine call;
(a). to some office: κ. ἀπόστολος, Ro 1:1, I Co 1:1;
(b). to salvation: Ro 8:28, I Co 1:24, Ju 1; κ. καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ κ. πιστοί, Re 17:14; in gosp. (not in pl., v.s. καλέω) disting. fr.ἐκλεκτός, Mt 20:16 (WH, txt., R, omit), 22:14; κ. Ἰησοῦ Χρ., Ro 1:6; κ. ἅγιοι, saints by calling, Ro 1:7, I Co 1:2.†

strong.def: a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of country

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κλίμα, -τος, τό (< κλίνω), [in LXX: Jg 20:2 A (פִּנָּה)*;]
1. an inclination, slope, esp. the slope from the equator to the pole (Arist).
2. a region (Polyb., al.): pl., Ro 15:23, II Co 11:10, Ga 1:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † κλυδωνίζομαι (< κλύδων), [in LXX: Is 57:20 (גּרשׁ)*;]
to be tossed by waves; metaph., to be tossed like waves (cf. FlJ, Ant., ix, 11, 3): Eph 4:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κλωπᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram.; on the original, v. Lft., Gal., 267 f.),
Clopas: Jo 19:25.†

strong.def: to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κνήθω (late form of κνάω),
1. to scratch.
2. to tickle; pass., to itch: II Ti 4:3.†

strong.def: Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κνίδος, -ου, ἡ,
Cnidus, a city (and peninsula) on S.W. coast of Asia Minor: Ac 27:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** κοίμησις, -εως, ἡ, [in LXX: Si 46:19 48:13*;]
a reclining, resting: Jo 11:13.†

strong.def: to share with others (objectively or subjectively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 κοινωνέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Ch 20:35, Jb 34:8, Ec 9:4 (חבר), Pr 1:11, Wi 6:23, Si 13:1, al.;]
to have a share of, go shares in (something) with (some one), take part in: c. gen. rei (as usually in cl., so Pr 1:11), He 2:14; c. dat. rei, Ro 12:13 15:27, I Ti 5:22, I Pe 4:13, II Jo 11; c. dat. pers., seq. εἰς, Phl 4:15; ἐν, Ga 6:6 (cf. συν-κοινωνέω).†

strong.def: partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 κοινωνία, -ας, ἡ (< κοινωνός), [in LXX: Le 6:2 (5:21) (יָד תְּשׂוּמֶת), Wi 8:18, III Mac 4:6*;]
1. fellowship, communion: Ac 2:42, II Co 6:14, Phl 1:5; τ. υἱοῦ, I Co 1:9; τ. αἵματος, σώματος Χρ., I Co 10:16; παθημάτων αὐτσῦ, Phl 3:10; τ. πνεύματος, II Co 13:13, Phl 2:1; δεξιὰς κοινωνίας, Ga 2:9; τ. πίστεώς σου, Phm 6; seq. μετὰ: τ. πατρός, I Jo 1:3, 6; ἡμῶν, ἀλλήλων, ib. 3, 7.
2. contribution (as outcome of fellowship): Ro 15:26, II Co 8:4 9:13, He 13:6 (cf. Art. Communion, DB, i, 460 ff.; MM, Exp., xv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κοινωνικός, -ή, -όν (< κοινωνία),
1. sociable.
2. ready to communicate or impart (R, mg., ready to sympathize, v. Field, Notes, 213 f.): I Ti 6:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κοιτών, -ῶνος, ὁ (< κοίτη = Att.., δωμότιον, v. Kennedy, Sources, 40), [in LXX chiefly for חֶדֶר, II Ki 4:7, Jl 2:16, I Es 3:3, al.;]
a bed-chamber; ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κ., a chamberlain: Ac 12:20.†

strong.derivation: from G2848 (κόκκος) (from the kernel-shape of the insect);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 † κόκκινος, -η, -ον (< κόκκος, as used of the "berry" of the ilex coccifera, v. DB, iv, 416), [in LXX for תּוֹלֵעָה, תּוֹלָע, שָׁנִי, Ex 25:4, Ge 38:28, Is 1:18, al.;]
scarlet: Mt 27:28, He 9:19, Re 17:3; neut., without substantive, of clothing, Re 17:4 18:12, 16,†

strong.def: properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κολάζω (< κόλος, docked), [in LXX: Da 6:12 (13) (no Heb.), I Es 8:24, Wi 3:4 (and freq.), I Mac 7:7, al.;]
1. to curtail, dock, prune.
2. to check, restrain.
3. to chastise, correct, punish: pass., II Pe 2:9; mid., cause to be punished (III Mac 7:3): Ac 4:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κολακία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (< κολακεύω, to flatter),
flattery: I Th 2:5 (v. Lft., Notes, 23).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κόλασις, -εως, ἡ, (< κολάζω), [in LXX: Ez 14:3-7 18:30 44:12, (מִכְשׁוֹל) 43:11, λαμβάνειν τὴν κ. (כּלם ni.); Wi 11:13 16:2, 24 19:4, Je 18:20, II-IV Mac5*;]
correction, penalty, punishment: Mt 25:46, I Jo 4:18.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a cake;
strong.def: prob akin to the base of G2853 (κολλάω)); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κολλούριον (TTr., κολλύ-, the more usual form), -ου, τό (dimin. of κολλύρα = κόλλιξ, a coarse bread roll), [in LXX: III Ki 12:24hil B*;]
1. a small bread roll (LXX, III Ki 12:24hil).
2. (Usually in pl., LS, s.v.) an eye salve shaped like a roll: Re 3:18.†

strong.def: Colossæ, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κολοσσαί (so in cl.; -ασσαί, Rec., LTr.), -ῶν, αἰ,
Colossæ, a city on the Lycus in Phrygia: Col 1:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** κολυμβάω, -ῶ, [in Al.: Is 25:11*;]
to dive, plunge into the sea: Ac 27:43 (cf. ἐκ-κολνμβάω).†

strong.def: a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κολυμβήθρα, -ας, ἡ (< κολυμβάω), [in LXX for בְּרֵכָה, IV Ki 18:27, al.;]
a swimming pool, pool: Jo 5:2, [4], 7 9:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κολωνία, (Rec. -ώνια), -ας, ἡ (< Lat. colonia),
a colony: Ac 16:12 (v. Lft., Phi., 50 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * κομάω, -ῶ (< κόμη),
to wear long hair: I Co 11:14, 15.†

strong.derivation: apparently from the same as G2865 (κομίζω);
strong.def: the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from G2359 (θρίξ); which properly denotes merely the scalp)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κόμη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX: Nu 6:5, Ez 44:20 (פֶּרַע), al.;]
the hair: I Co 11:15.†

strong.derivation: neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of 2865 (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. nice);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κομψός, -ή, -όν (< κομέω, to take care of),
well-dressed, elegant, fine; compar. neut., κομψότερον ἔχειν (cf. κόμψως ἔχειν, Epict., and colloq. Eng., "to be doing finely"): Jo 4:52.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κονιάω, -ῶ (< κονία, dust, lime), [in LXX: De 27:2, 4 (שִׂיד), Pr 21:9*;]
to plaster or whiten over: of tombs, Mt 23:27; fig., of a hypocrite, Ac 23:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κοπετός, -οῦ, ὁ (< κόπτω, mid.), [in LXX chiefly for מִסְפֵּד;]
= cl. κομμός, a beating of the head and breast, lamentation: seq. ἐπί c. dat. pers., Ac 8:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κοπή, -ῆς, ἡ (< κόπτω), [in LXX: Ge 14:17, Jos 10:20 (נכה hi., מַכָּה), De 28:25 (נגף), Jth 15:7*;]
1. in cl., a stroke, a pounding (as in a mortar).
2. In LXX, a smiting in battle: He 7:1(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κορέ indecl. (in FlJ, -έου), ὁ (Heb. קֶרַח),
Korah: Ju 11.†

strong.def: to cram, i.e. glut or sate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** κορέννυμι (< κόρος, surfeit), [in Sm.: Ps 21 (22):27, Al, 102 (103):5*;]
to satisfy: pass., τροφῆς, Ac 27:38; metaph., of spiritual things, I Co 4:8.†

strong.def: a Corinthian, i.e. inhabitant of Corinth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κορίνθιος, -α, -ον,
Corinthian; as subst., ὁ Κ., a Corinthian: Ac 18:8, 27 (WH, txt., R, omit), II Co 6:11; 1Co, 2Co, tit.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Κόρινθος, -ου, ἡ,
Corinth: Ac 18:1, 27 19:1, I Co 1:2, II Co 1:1, 23, II Ti 4:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 Κορνήλιος, -ου, ὁ (Lat.),
Cornelius: Ac 10:1 ff.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * κοσμικός, -ή, -όν (κόσμος),
1. pertaining to the world or universe.
2. of this world, earthly. He 9:1.
3. In ethical sense, worldly: ἐπιθυμίαι, Tit 2:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κόσμιος, -ον (in cl. -α, -ον), (< κόσμος), [in LXX: Ec 12:9 (תּקן)*;]
orderly, decent, modest: I Ti 2:9 (WH, mg., -ίως, q.v.) 3:2.†

strong.def: a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κοσμοκράτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (< κόσμος, κρατέω),
1. in Orphic hymns, al. (v. AR, Eph 6:12), a ruler of the whole world (and so in Rabbinic writings: קוֺזמוֺקְרָטוֺר).
2. a ruler of this world (in contrast to παντοκράτωρ): οἱ κ. τ. σκότους τούτου, the rulers of this dark world, Eph 6:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κούαρτος, -ου, ὁ (Lat.)
Quartus: Ro 16:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† κουστωδία, -ας, ἡ, (Lat. custodia),
a guard: Mt 27:65, 66 28:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κουφίζω (< κοῦφος, light), [in LXX: Ex 18:22, Jh 1:5, al. (קלל hi.), Es 5:1, al.;]
1. intrans., to be light (poetic chiefly).
2. to lighten, make light: c. acc., Ac 27:38.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κραταιός, -ά, -όν (< κράτος), (in cl. poët. form of κρατερός), [in LXX chiefly for חָזָק and cognates;]
strong, mighty: I Pe 5:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κρέας, -έως, pl., κρέα, [in LXX for בָּשָׂר (freq.);]
flesh, meat: Ro 14:21, I Co 8:13.†

strong.derivation: neuter of an alternate form of G2909 (κρείττων);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 κρείσσων (Epic and old Att.) and κρείττων (later Att.), prop. comparat. of κρατύς, strong, but in sense often (as in cl., v. LS, s.v.) as comparat. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
better;
(a). as to advantage or usefulness: I Co 11:17, He 11:40 12:24; πολλῷ μᾶλλον κ., Phl 1:23; κρεῖσσον ποιεῖν, I Co 7:38; ἐστιν, seq. inf., I Co 7:9, II Pe 2:21;
(b). as to excellence: He 1:4 6:9 7:7, 19, 22 8:6 9:23 10:34 11:16, 35; κ. ἐστι, seq. inf., I Pe 3:17.†

strong.derivation: comparative of a derivative of G2904 (κράτος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 κρείσσων (Epic and old Att.) and κρείττων (later Att.), prop. comparat. of κρατύς, strong, but in sense often (as in cl., v. LS, s.v.) as comparat. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
better;
(a). as to advantage or usefulness: I Co 11:17, He 11:40 12:24; πολλῷ μᾶλλον κ., Phl 1:23; κρεῖσσον ποιεῖν, I Co 7:38; ἐστιν, seq. inf., I Co 7:9, II Pe 2:21;
