to travel on foot or by land: Ac 20:13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3982 (πείθω) and G757 (ἄρχω);
strong.def: to be persuaded by a ruler, i.e. (genitive case) to submit to authority; by analogy, to conform to advice

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πειθαρχέω, -ῶ (< πείθομαι, ἀρχή), [in LXX: Da LXX 7:27 (שְׁמַע), Si 30:38 (33:28), I Es 8:94*;]
to obey one in authority, be obedient: Tit 3:1; c. dat., Ac 27:21; θεῷ, Ac 5:29, 32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πειθός (πιθός, WH), -ή, -όν (< πείθω), = cl. πιθανός,
persuasive: I Co 2:4 (not found elsewhere).†

strong.derivation: from the base of G4008 (πέραν) (through the idea of piercing);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πεῖρα, -ας, ἡ (< πειράω), [in LXX: De 28:56 (π. λαμβάνειν, נסה pi.) 33:8 (מַסָּה), Wi 18:20, 25, II Mac 8:9, IV Mac 8:1*;]
a trial, experiment; π. λαμβάνειν, to make trial, have experience of: He 11:29, 36 (for exx., v. Field, Notes, 232 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πειράω, more commonly as depon., πειράομαι, [in LXX for נסה;]
to try, attempt: Ac 26:21.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G3982 (πείθω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πεισμονή, -ῆς, ἡ (< πείθω),
persuasion: Ga 5:8.†

strong.def: deep or open sea, i.e. the main

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πέλαγος, -ους, τό, [in LXX: II Mac 5:21, IV Mac 7:1*;]
the deep sea, the deep, the sea: Ac 27:5; τὸ π. τῆς θαλάσσης, Mt 18:6.

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G4141 (πλήσσω) (meaning an axe);
strong.def: to chop off (the head), i.e. truncate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πελεκίζω (< πέλεκυς, a battle-axe),
to out off with an axe, esp. to behead: c. acc., Re 20:4 (Polyb., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πέμπτος, -η, -ον, [in LXX for חֲמִישִׁי and cognate forms;]
fifth: Re 6:9 9:1 16:10 21:20.†

strong.derivation: from a primary (to toil for daily subsistence);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πένης, -ητος, ὁ (< πένομαι, to work for one's daily bread), [in LXX for אֶבְיוֹן, עָנִי, דַּל, etc.;]
one who works for his living, a labourer, a poor man: II Co 9:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πενθερός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for חָם, Ge 38:13, al.; also for חֹתֵן, Jg 1:16 A;]
a father-in-law: Jo 18:13.†

strong.derivation: strengthened from the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πένθος, -ους, τό, [in LXX chiefly for אֵבֶל;]
mourning: Ja 4:9, Re 18:7, 8 21:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πεντάκις, adv.,
five times: II Co 11:24.†

strong.derivation: feminine of the ordinal of G4004 (πεντήκοντα);
strong.def: fiftieth (G2250 (ἡμέρα) being implied) from Passover, i.e. the festival of "Pentecost"

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πεντηκοστός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX for חֲמִשִּׁים, Le 25:10, 11, IV Ki 15:23, 27; I Mac4, II Mac 14:4; ἡ π., To 2:1, II Mac 12:32*;]
fiftieth. As subst., ἡ π.;
(a). (sc. μερίς), at Athens, a tax of two per cent.;
(b). (sc. ἡμέρα, i.e. the fiftieth day after the Passover), Pentecost, the second of the three great Jewish feasts (To 2:1, II Mac 12:32; ἑορτὴ ἑβδομάδων, De 16:10, al.): Ac 2:1 20:16, I Co 16:8.†

strong.derivation: from the perfect of the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 † πεποίθησις, -εως, ἡ (< πείθω), [in LXX: IV Ki 18:19 (בִּטָּחוֹן)*;]
confidence: II Co 1:15 3:4 10:2, Eph 3:12; seq. εἰς, II Co 8:22; ἐν, Phl 3:4 (the word is condemned by the Atticists, v. Rutherford, NPhr., 355).†

strong.def: fortified; Pergamus, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Πέργαμος, -ου, ἡ (so Xen., Paus., al., but -ον, τό in Strabo, Polyb., and most writers, also in Inscr.; in NT the termination is uncertain),
Pergamum, a city of Mysia: Re 1:11 2:12.†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G4010 (Πέργαμος);
strong.def: a tower; Perga, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Πέργη, -ης, ἡ,
Perga, a city of Pamphylia: Ac 13:13, 14 14:25.†

strong.derivation: from G4012 (περί) and G138 (αἱρέομαι) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to remove all around, i.e. unveil, cast off (anchor); figuratively, to expiate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 περι-αιρέω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for סוּר hi.;]
to take away that which surrounds, take away, take off (τείχη, Hdt., Thuc.; χιτῶνα, Plat.; δακτύλιον, Ge 41:42, cf. σφρηγῖδα, Hdt., ii, 151): τ. κάλυμμα, pass., II Co 3:16; as nautical term (RV, cast off), ἀγκύρας, Ac 27:40; absol., to cast loose: Ac 28:13. Metaph., to take away entirely: ἐλπίς, pass., Ac 27:20; ἁμαρτίας, He 10:11.†

strong.def: to flash all around, i.e. envelop in light

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† περι-αστράπτω, [in LXX: IV Mac 4:10*;]
to flash around: c. acc., Ac 9:3; seq. περί Ac 22:6 (Eccl. and Byzant.).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4016 (περιβάλλω);
strong.def: something thrown around one, i.e. a mantle, veil

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 περι-βόλαιον, -ου, τό (< περιβάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for לְבוּשׁ, כְּסוּת and cognate forms;]
that which is thrown around, a covering, in NT,
(a). a mantle (Ps 101 (102):27, Is 59:17, al.): He 1:12(LXX);
(b). a veil: I Co 11:15 (but v. ICC, in l.).†

strong.def: to bind around one, i.e. enwrap

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 περι-δέω, [in LXX: Jb 12:18 (אסר)*;]
to tie round, bind round: c. acc. et dat., pass., Jo 11:44.†

strong.def: to work all around, i.e. bustle about (meddle)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** περι-εργάζομαι, [in LXX: Wi 8:5 א1, Si 3:23*;]
1. to waste one's labour about a thing.
2. to be a busybody: II Th 3:11 (cf. Plat., Apol., 19 B).†

strong.def: working all around, i.e. officious (meddlesome, neuter plural magic)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * περίεργος, -ον,
I. of persons;
1. over careful.
2. curious, meddling, a busybody: I Ti 5:13.
II. Of things;
1. over-wrought.
2. superfluous.
3. curious, uncanny; τὰ π., curious arts, magic: Ac 19:19 (v. Deiss., BS, 3235.).†

strong.derivation: from G4012 (περί) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to come all around, i.e. stroll, vacillate, veer
strong.kjv: fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 περι-έρχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for סבב;]
to go about (as an itinerant): Ac 19:13 28:13 (περιελόντες, WH, R, mg.), He 11:37; τ. οἰκίας, from house to house: I Ti 5:13.†

strong.def: a putting all around, i.e. decorating oneself with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† περί-θεσις, -εως, ἡ (< περιτίθημι), [in Sm.: Ps 31 (32):9*;]
a putting around, putting on: I Pe 3:3.†

strong.def: to stand all around, i.e. (near) to be a bystander, or (aloof) to keep away from

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 περι-ίστημι (Rec. ΐστημι), [in LXX: Jos 6:3 (סבב), II Ki 13:31 (נצב ni.), I Ki 4:16, Ep. Je 37, Jth 5:22, II Mac 14:9*;]
1. to place around.
2. to stand around: Jo 11:42; c. acc. pers., Ac 25:7. Mid. (in late writers), to turn oneself about to avoid, to shun: c. acc. rei, II Ti 2:16, Tit 3:9.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4012 (περί) and G2508 (καθαίρω);
strong.def: something cleaned off all around, i.e. refuse (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † περι-κάθαρμα, -τος, τό (< περικαθαίρω, to purify on all sides or completely, De 18:10, Jos 5:4, IV Mac 1:29*), [in LXX: Pr 21:18 (כֹּפֶר)*;]
1. a victim, expiation (Pr 21:18).
2. refuse, rubbish: pl., I Co 4:13 (v. ICC, in l.).†

strong.derivation: feminine of a compound of G4012 (περί) and G2776 (κεφαλή);
strong.def: encirclement of the head, i.e. a helmet

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † περι-κεφαλαία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX for כּוֹבַע, קוֹבַע;]
a helmet: fig., I Th 5:8; c. gen. explic., π. τ. σωτηρίου, Eph 6:17 (cf. Is 59:17).†

strong.def: strong all around, i.e. a master (manager)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† περι-κρατής, -ές, [in LXX: Da TH Sus 39 A*;]
having full command of: Ac 27:16.†

strong.def: to leave all around, i.e. (passively) survive

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 περι-λείπομαι, depon. mid. and pass., [in LXX: II Ch 34:21 A (שׁאר ni.), II Mac 1:31 8:14, IV Mac 12:6 13:18*;]
to be left remaining, remain over, survive: I Th 4:15, 17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 περι-μένω, [in LXX: Ge 49:18 (קוה pi.), Wi 8:12*;]
to wait for: c. acc.., Ac 1:4.†

strong.def: all around, i.e. (as an adjective) circumjacent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πέριξ, adv., [in Al.: Le 13:33*;]
round about: αἱ π. πολεῖς, Ac 5:16.†

strong.derivation: from the present participle feminine of a compound of 4012 and G1510 (εἰμί);
strong.def: being beyond usual, i.e. special (one's own)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † περιούσιος, -ον (< περίειμι, to be over and above), [in LXX: Ex 19:5 23:22, De 7:6 14:2 26:18 (סְגֻלָּה, עַם ם׳)*;]
one's own, of one's own possession: λαὸς π. (cf. LXX, Ex 19:5 23:22, De 7:6 14:2 26:18), Tit 2:14.†

strong.def: a being held around, i.e. (concretely) a passage (of Scripture, as circumscribed)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 περι-οχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< περιέχω), [in LXX for מְצוּדָה, מָצוֹר, etc.;]
1. compass, circumference.
2. a portion circumscribed, a section: Ac 8:32.†

strong.derivation: from G4012 (περί) and the base of G4008 (πέραν);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† περι-πείρω,
to put on a spit, hence, to pierce: metaph., ἑαυτὸν . . . ὀδύναις, I Ti 6:10.†

strong.def: acquisition (the act or the thing); by extension, preservation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 † περι-ποίησις, -εως, ἡ (< περιποιέω), [in LXX: II Ch 4:13 (12) (מִחְיָה), Ma 3:17 (סְגֻלָּה), Hg 2:10 (9)*;]
1. preservation: He 10:39 (II Ch 4:13).
2. acquisition, obtaining: I Th 5:9, II Th 2:14 (and so perh. Eph 1:14, v. infr.).
3. a possession: Eph 1:14 (but v. supr., and cf. ICC, in l.), I Pe 2:9(LXX).†

strong.def: to tear all around, i.e. completely away

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** περι-ρήγνυμι (Rec. -ρρ-, v. supr.), [in LXX: II Mac 4:38*;]
to break or tear off all around: freq. of garments, τ. ἱμάτια, Ac 16:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † περισσεία, -ας, ἡ (< περισσεύω), [in LXX: Ec12 (יִתְרוֹן and cogn. forms, 1:3, al.)*;]
1. abundance, superfluity: Ro 5:17, II Co 8:2 10:15, Ja 1:21 (so also Inscr., v. LAE, 80).
2.
(a). superiority (Ec, v. supr.);
(b). profit (ib.).†

strong.kjv: more abundant(-ly), X the more earnest, (more) exceedingly, more frequent, much more, the rather

strong.def: circumcision (the rite, the condition or the people, literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
36 † περι-τομή, -ῆς, ἡ (< περιτέμνω), [in LXX: Ge 17:13, Ex 4:25, 26 (מוּל ni., מוּלָה), Je 11:16*;]
circumcision;
(a). of the rite itself: Jo 7:22, 23, Ac 7:8, Ro 4:11, Ga 5:11, Phl 3:5;
(b). of the state of circumcision: Ro 2:25-28 3:1, I Co 7:19, Ga 5:6 6:15, Col 3:11; ἐν π. ὤν, Ro 4:10;
(c). by meton., ἡ π. = οἱ περιτμηθέντες, the circumcised: Ro 3:30 4:9, 12 15:8, Ga 2:7-9, Eph 2:11; οἱ ἐκ τῆς π., of Jews, Ro 4:12; of Jewish Christians, Ac 11:2, Ga 2:12, Tit 1:10; οἱ ἐκ π. πιστοί, Ac 10:45; οἱ ὄντες ἐκ π., Col 4:11. Metaph., Ro 2:29, Col 2:11, Phl 3:3.†

strong.derivation: from G4012 (περί) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);
strong.def: to turn around, i.e. (mentally) to craze

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** περι-τρέπω, [in LXX: Wi 5:23*;]
to turn about, turn: c. acc. et, dat., Ac 26:24 (cf. FlJ, Ant., ix, 4, 4).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** περι-φρονέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: IV Mac 6:9 14:1*;]
1. to examine on all sides, consider carefully (Aristoph.).
2. = ὑπερφρονέω, to have thouphts beyond, to despise (Thuc., Plut., al.; IV Mac 6:9 14:1): Tit 2:15.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G4012 (περί) and (to rub);
strong.def: something brushed all around, i.e. off-scrapings (figuratively, scum)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† περί-ψημα, -τος, τό (< περιψράω, to wipe off all round), [in LXX: To 5:18*;]
that which is wiped off, offscouring: metaph. (assoc. with περικάθαρμα, q.v.), I Co 4:13 (and so prob., To 5:18, as EV; but v. Thayer, s.v., for the meaning expiation, ransom, in To; and cf. LS, s.v. κάθαρμα; Lft., Notes, 200 f., and on Ign., Eph., 8).†

strong.def: perhaps by reduplication of the base of G4008 (πέραν)); to boast

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† περπερεύομαι (< περπερος, vainglorious),
to boast or vaunt oneself: I Co 13:4 (elsewh. only in Antonin.; v. Abbott, Essays, 87).†

strong.def: a Persian woman; Persis, a Christian female

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Περσίς, -ίδος, ἡ,
Persis: Ro 16:12.†

strong.def: the by-gone, i.e. (as noun) last year

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† πέρυσι, adv. (< πέρας),
last year, a year ago: ἀπὸ π. (as in π. v. Deiss., BS, 221; LAE, 70), II Co 8:10 9:2.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of a primary verb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πέτομαι, [in LXX chiefly for עוּף;]
to fly: Re 4:7 8:13 12:14 14:6 19:17 (Rec. πετάομαι, q.v.).†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which in its simpler form occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses);
strong.def: to fix ("peg"), i.e. (specially) to set up (a tent)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πήγνυμι, [in LXX chiefly for נטה, also for תּקע, etc.;]
to make fast, to fix; of tents, to pitch: He 8:2 (cf. προσ-πήγνυμι).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a (presumed) derivative of (the blade of an oar;
strong.def: from the same as G3976 (πέδη)); a "pedal", i.e. helm

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * πηδάλιον, -ου, τό (< πηδός, the blade of an oar),
a rudder: Ja 3:4; pl., Ac 27:40.†

strong.derivation: a quantitative form (the feminine) of the base of G4225 (πού);
strong.def: how much (as an indefinite), i.e. in size or (figuratively) dignity

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πηλίκος, -η, -ον, [in LXX: Za 2:2 (6) (כַּמָּה), IV Mac 15:22*;]
interrog., how large, how great? (prop., of magnitude, as πόσος of quantity): in exclamations, = ἡλίκος (v. Bl., § 51, 4), Ga 6:11; of personal greatness, He 7:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 πηλός, οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for חֹמֶר, טִיט;]
1. clay, as used by a potter: Ro 9:21 (cf. Is 29:16, al.).
2. = βόρβορος, wet clay, mud: Jo 9:6, 11, 14, 15.†

strong.def: to squeeze, i.e. seize (gently by the hand (press), or officially (arrest), or in hunting (capture))
strong.kjv: apprehend, catch, lay hand on, take

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 πιάζω (cf. MGr. πιάνω; v. Kennedy, Sources, 155), Doric and late Att. for πιέζω in its later senses; [in LXX: Ca 2:15 (אחז), Si 23:21*;]
1. to lay hold of: Ac 3:7 (Theocr.).
2. to take, capture, apprehend: Jo 7:30, 32, 44 8:20 10:39 11:57 21:3, 10, Ac 12:4, II Co 11:32, Re 19:20 (v. MM, xx).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of a derivative of G3982 (πείθω) and G3056 (λόγος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πιθανολογία, -ας, ἡ (< πιθανός, persuasive, plausible), in cl. (Plat),
the use of probable arguments, as opp. to demonstration (ἀπόδειξις); hence, persuasive speech: Col 2:4 (v. ICC, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πικραίνω (< πικρός), [in LXX for מרר, קצף, etc.;]
to make bitter: Re 10:9; pass., Re 8:11 10:10; metaph., to embitter (LXX): pass., seq. πρός, Col 3:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πικρία, -ας, ἡ (< πικρός), [in LXX chiefly for מַר, מָרָה and cognate forms;]
bitterness;
(a). of taste (Arist., Je 15:17, al.);
(b). metaph., of temper, character, etc.: Ro 3:14(LXX), Eph 4:31; ῥίζα πικρίας, He 12:15; χολὴ π., a malignant disposition, Ac 8:23.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from G4078 (πήγνυμι) (through the idea of piercing);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πικρός, -ά, -όν (poët. in cl.), [in LXX chiefly for מַר;]
1. sharp, pointed.
2. sharp to the senses; of taste, bitter: opp. to γλυκύ, Ja 3:11; metaph., harsh, bitter: Ja 3:14.

strong.derivation: a reduplicated and prolonged form of a primary ; which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses);
strong.def: to fire, i.e. burn (figuratively and passively, become inflamed with fever)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πίμπρημι (in cl. prose, rare in the simple form), [in LXX: Nu 5:21, 22, 27 (צָבֶה)*;]
1. to blow, burn.
2. Later, to cause to swell; mid., of parts of the body, to become swollen (LXX): Ac 28:6 (cf. ἐμπίπρημι).†

strong.def: perhaps akin to the alternate of G4095 (πίνω) through the idea of repletion); plumpness, i.e. (by implication) richness (oiliness)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πιότης, -ητος, ἡ (< πίων, fat), [in LXX chiefly for דֶּשֶׁן;]
fatness: Ro 11:17.†

strong.def: Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Πισιδία, -ας, ἡ,
Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor: Ac 14:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πιστόω, -ῶ (< πιστός), [in LXX chiefly for אמן ni.;]
to make trustworthy (Thuc., III Ki 1:36), hence, to establish (I Ch 17:14). Pass. and mid., to be assured of: c. acc. rei, II Ti 3:14.†

strong.def: objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 πλάνη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX: Pr 14:8 (מִרְמָה), Wi 1:12, al;]
a wandering. Metaph., a going astray, an error (in NT always with respect to morals or religion): Mt 27:64, Ro 1:27, Eph 4:14, I Th 2:3, II Th 2:11, Ja 5:20, II Pe 2:18 3:17, I Jo 4:6, Ju 11.†

strong.def: a rover ("planet"), i.e. (figuratively) an erratic teacher

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πλανήτης, -ου, ὁ (< πλανάω), [in LXX: Ho 9:17 (נדד)*;]
= πλάνης, a wanderer: ἀστέρες π. (cl. planets), wandering stars, Ju 13 (WH, mg., -τες).†

strong.def: roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πλάνος, -ον, [in LXX: Jb 19:4 (מְשׁוּגָה), Je 23:32*;]
1. wandering.
2. leading astray, deceiving: πνεύματα π., I Ti 4:1. As subst., ὁ π., a deceiver, impostor: Mt 27:63, II Co 6:8, II Jo 1:7.†

strong.def: a moulding-board, i.e. flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πλάξ, -ακός, ἡ, [in LXX for לוּחַ;]
anything flat and broad.
1. a plain (poët.).
2. In late writers (Luc., al.), a flat stone, a tablet: II Co 3:3, He 9:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πλάσμα, -τος, τό (< πλάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for יֵצֶר;]
that which is moulded or formed : Ro 9:20(LXX).†

strong.def: to mould, i.e. shape or fabricate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πλάσσω, [in LXX chiefly for יצר;]
to form, mould: Ro 9:20(LXX), I Ti 2:13.†

strong.def: moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πλαστός, -ή, -όν (< πλάσσω),
1. formed, moulded (Hes., Plat., al.).
2. Metaph., made up, fabricated, feigned (Hdt., Xen., al.): II Pe 2:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πλάτος, -ους, τό, [in LXX chiefly for רֹחַב;]
breadth: Eph 3:18, Re 21:16; τ. π. τῆς γῆς (Hb 1:6, מֶרְחָב), Re 20:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πλατύνω (< πλατύς), [in LXX chiefly for רחב hi.;]
to make broad, enlarge, extend: c. acc. rei, Mt 23:5. Metaph. (cf. Ps 118 (119):32, al.), pass., ἡ καρδία, II Co 6:11; ὑμεῖς, II Co 6:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πλέγμα, -τος, τό (< πλέκω), [in Aq., Th.: Is 28:5*;]
what is woven or twisted (as basket-work, nets, etc.); a braiding (sc. τριχῶν, cf. I Pe 3:3): pl., I Ti 2:9.†

strong.def: to do, make or be more, i.e. increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound
strong.kjv: abound, abundant, make to increase, have over

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 πλεονάζω (< πλέον), [in LXX for עדף, רבה, etc.;]
I. Intrans.
1. Of persons;
(a). to abound in (Arist.);
(b). to superabound: II Co 8:15(LXX).
2. Of things, to abound, superabound: Ro 5:20 6:1, II Co 4:15, Phl 4:17, II Th 1:3, II Pe 1:8.
II. Trans. (Nu 26:54, Ps 70 (71):21; not cl, v. Lft., Notes, 48 f.), to make to abound: I Th 3:12 (cf. ὑπερ-πλεονάζω).†

strong.def: to be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach
strong.kjv: get an advantage, defraud, make a gain

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πλεονεκτέω, -ῶ (< πλεονέκτης, q.v.), [in LXX: Hb 2:9, Ez 22:27 (בּצע), Jg 4:11 B*;]
1. intrans., to have more, to have an advantage (cl., c. gen. pers.).
2. Trans., in late writers (v. M, Pr., 65), to overreach, defraud: c. acc. pers., II Co 7:2 12:17, 18; ἐν τ. πράγματι, I Th 4:6 (v. M, Th., in l.); pass., II Co 2:11 (as also in cl.; v. LS, s.v.).†

strong.def: holding (desiring) more, i.e. eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** πλεονέκτης, -ου, ὁ (< πλέον, ἔχω), [in LXX: Si 14:9*;] = ὁ θέλων πλέον ἔχειν (v. MM, xx),
one desirous of having more, covetous: I Co 5:10, 11 6:10, Eph 5:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πλευρά, -ᾶς, ἡ, [in LXX (freq. pl. as in Hom.) chiefly for צֵלָע;]
the side: Mt 27:49 ([[WH]] R, mg.), Jo 19:34 20:20, 25, 27, Ac 12:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 πληθύνω (causal of πληθύω, to be full, < πληθύς, Ion. for πλῆθος), [in LXX chiefly for רבה hi.;]
1. trans., to increase, multiply: II Co 9:10, He 6:14(LXX); pass., to be increased, to multiply: Mt 24:12, Ac 6:7 7:17 9:31 12:24; c. dat. pers. (Da LXX TH 3:31 (98) al.), I Pe 1:2, II Pe 1:2, Ju 2.
2. Intrans., to be increased, to multiply: Ac 6:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πλήκτης, -ου, ὁ (< πλήσσω), [in Sm.: Ps 34 (35):15*;]
a striker, brawler: I Ti 3:3, Tit 1:7 (Arist., Plut., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† πληροφορία, -ας, ἡ (< πληροφορέω),
full assurance, confidence: I Th 1:5; τ. συνέσεως, Col 2:2; τ. ἐλπίδος, He 6:11; πίστεως, He 10:22 (cf. Lft. on Col 2:2; M, Th., 9).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G4130 (πλήθω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πλησμονή, -ῆς, ἡ (< πίμπλημι), [in LXX chiefly for שׂבע and cognate forms;]
a filling up, satiety: πρὸς π. σαρκός (RV, against the indulgence of the flesh; but ICC, in l., for the full satisfaction of the flesh, op. cit., 276 ff.), Col 2:23.†

strong.derivation: apparently another form of G4111 (πλάσσω) (through the idea of flattening out);
strong.def: to pound, i.e. (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πλήσσω, [in LXX chiefly for נכה hi., ho.;]
to strike, smite: pass., Re 8:12 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐπι-πλήσσω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** πλόος, πλούς gen., -όου, -οῦ (and in late writers also πλοός, like νοός from νοῦς), ὁ (< πλέω), [in LXX: Wi 14:1*;]
a voyage: Ac 21:7 27:9, 10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * πλουσίως, adv.,
richly, abundantly: Col 3:16, I Ti 6:17, Tit 3:6, II Pe 1:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πλουτίζω (< πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עשׁר hi.;]
to make rich, enrich: c. acc. pers., pass., II Co 9:11. Metaph., of spiritual riches, c. acc. pers., II Co 6:10; seq. ἐν, pass., I Co 1:5.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of an obsolete (to "flow");

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πλύνω. [in LXX chiefly for כּבס pi.;]
to wash (inanimate objects, esp. clothing): τ. δίκτυα, Lk 5:2. Fig., τ. στολάς, Re 7:14 22:14 (cf. Ps 50 (51):4, 9 and v.s. ἀπο-πλύνω).†

strong.def: non-carnal, i.e. (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (dæmoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 * πνευματικός, -ή, -όν (< πνεῦμα),
1. of or caused by the wind, air or breath (Arist., al.).
2. spiritual (opp. to σωματικός, Plut.);
(a). of created beings: τὰ π. (RV, the spiritual hosts), Eph 6:12; of that which is related to the human spirit, opp. to ψυχικός, I Co 15:44, 46;
(b). of that which belongs to or is actuated by the Divine Spirit;
α. of persons: I Co 2:15 3:1 14:37, Ga 6:1; οἶκος π., fig., I Pe 2:5;
β. of things: Ro 1:11 7:14, I Co 2:13 10:3, 4 12:1 14:1, Eph 1:3 5:19, Col 1:9 3:16, I Pe 2:5; opp. to τ. σαρκικά, Ro 15:27, I Co 9:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† πνευματικῶς, adv. (< πνεῦμα),
spiritually;
(a). by the aid of the Holy Spirit: I Co 2:13(WH, mg.), 14;
(b). in a spiritual sense: Re 11:8.†

strong.def: throttled, i.e. (neuter concretely) an animal choked to death (not bled)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * πνικτός, -ή, -όν (< πνίγω),
strangled: Ac 15:20, 29 21:25 (cf. Le 17:13, 14).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πνοή, -ῆς, ἡ (< πνέω), [in LXX chiefly for נְשָׁמָה;]
1. a blowing, blast, wind: Ac 2:2.
2. a breathing, breath: Ac 17:25 (Ge 2:7, al.).†

strong.derivation: from G4228 (πούς) and another element of uncertain affinity;
strong.def: a dress (G2066 (ἐσθής) implied) reaching the ankles

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ποδήρης, -ες (< πούς), [in LXX: Ex 25:6 (7) 35:9 (חֹשֶׁן), 28:4 29:5 (מְעִיל), 28:27 (31) (אֵפוֹד), Ez 9:2, 3, 11 (בַּד), Za 3:5 (4) (מַחֲלָצוֹת), Wi 18:24, Si 27:8 45:8*;]
reaching to the feet: of a garment (sc. χιτών, cf. Ex 25:6 (7) 28:4, 27 (31) 29:5 35:9, Ez 9:2, 3, 11; Xen., al.), Re 1:13 (for -η, LT7 read -ην; v. M, Pr., 49).†

strong.def: a product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ποίημα, -τος, τό (< ποιέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַעֲשֶׂה (freq. in Ec);]
that which is made or done, a work: Ro 1:20, Eph 2:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ποίησις, -εως, ἡ (ποιέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַעֲשֶׂה and cognate forms;]
1. a making (Hdt., Thuc., al.).
2. a doing (Si 19:18 51:19): Ja 1:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** ποιητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< ποιέω), [in LXX: I Mac 2:67*;]
1. in cl., a maker, author.
2. Esp., a poet: Ac 17:28.
3. Later, a doer: τ. νόμου, Ro 2:13, Ja 4:11 (I Mac 2:67); ἔργου, Ja 1:25; λόγου, Ja 1:22, 23.†

strong.def: to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 πολεμέω, -ῶ (< πόλεμος), [in LXX chiefly for לחם ni.;]
to make war, fight: Re 12:7b 19:11; seq. μετά (II Ki 21:15 and v. M, Pr., 106, 247), Re 2:16 12:7a 13:4 17:14; hyperb., of private quarrels, Ja 4:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† πολιτάρχης, -ου, ὁ, = πολίαρχος (Pind., Eur.),
the ruler of a city, a politarch: Ac 17:6, 8 (v. MM, xx).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πολιτεία, -ας, ἡ (< πολιτεύω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:11 6:23 8:17 13:14, III Mac 3:21, 23, IV Mac 3:20 8:7 17:9*;]
1. citizenship: Ac 22:28 (III Mac 3:21, 23, Hdt., Xen., a1.).
2. government, administration (Aristoph., Dem., al.).
3. a commonwealth: Eph 2:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πολίτευμα, -τος, τό (< πολιτεύω), [in LXX: II Mac 12:7*;]
1. an act of administration.
2. a form of government.
3. = πολιτεία,
(a). citizenship: Phl 3:20 (R, txt.);
(b). community, commonwealth: Phl 3:20 (R, mg.; for exx. v. MM, xx).†

strong.derivation: middle voice of a derivative of G4177 (πολίτης);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πολιτεύω, more freq. as depon., -ομαι, and so in LXX and NT (< πολίτης), [in LXX: Es 8:13, II Mac 6:1 11:25, III Mac 3:4, IV Mac4*;]
to be a citizen, live as a citizen: metaph., of conduct as based on heavenly citizenship, Ac 23:1, Phl 1:27.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3056 (λόγος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πολυλογία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Pr 10:19 (דְּבָרִים רֹב)*;]
much speaking, loquacity: Mt 6:7.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3313 (μέρος);
strong.def: in many portions, i.e. variously as to time and agency (piecemeal)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πολυμερῶς, adv. (< πολύς, μέρος),
in many parts or portions: He 1:1 (Plut., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πολυ-ποίκιλος, -ον,
1. much variegated, of greatly differing colours (Eur.).
2. manifold: Eph 3:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πολύσπλαγχνος, -ον (< πολύς, σπλάγχνον),
very pitiful: Ja 5:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * πολύτιμος, -ον (< πολύς, τιμή),
1. much revered (Menand.).
2. very costly, very precious: Mt 13:46 26:7 (βαρύτιμος, WH), Jo 12:3; comparat., I Pe 1:7.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G5158 (τρόπος);
strong.def: in many ways, i.e. variously as to method or form

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πολυτρόπως, adv. (< πολύτροπος, 1. much turning. 2. manifold), [in LXX: IV Mac 3:21 A*;]
in many ways or manners: He 1:1 (Philo).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πόμα, -τος, τό (< πίνω), late form of Att. πῶμα, [in LXX: Ps 101 (102):9 (שִׁקּוּי), al.4*;]
drink: I Co 10:4, He 9:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πόνος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for עָמָל, etc.;]
1. labour, toil: Col 4:13.
2. The consequence of toil, distress, suffering, pain (Xen., al., LXX): Re 16:10, 11 21:4.†

strong.def: a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ποντικός, -ή, -όν,
Pontic, of Pontus: Ac 18:2.

strong.def: a sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Πόντος, -ου, ὁ,
Pontus, a region of Asia Minor, bordering on the πόντος Εὔξεινος: Ac 2:9, I Pe 1:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Πόπλιος, -ου, ὁ
(Latin), Publius: Ac 28:7, 8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** πορθέω collat. form (in cl. chiefly poët.) of πέρθω, [in LXX: IV Mac 4:23 11:4*;]
to destroy, ravage: Ac 9:21, Ga 1:13, 23.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of (a way, i.e. means);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† πορισμός, -ου, ὁ (< πορίζω, to procure), [in LXX: Wi 13:19 14:2*;]
1. a providing.
2. a means of gain: I Ti 6:5, 6 (Polyb., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πόρκιος, -ου, ὁ,
Porcius, prænomen of Porcius Festus (v.s. Φῆστος): Ac 24:27.†

strong.def: to act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 πορνεύω, [in LXX for זנה;]
1. to prostitute the body for hire.
2. to commit fornication: Mk 10:19 (WH, mg), I Co 6:18 10:8, Re 2:14, 20. Metaph. (as in LXX: I Ch 5:25, Je 3:6, Ho 9:1, al.), of idolatry (but v. Swete, Ap., 180 f.), Re 17:2 18:3, 9 (cf. ἐκ-πορνεύω).†

strong.def: akin to the base of G4097 (πιπράσκω)); a (male) prostitute (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ** πόρνος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Si 23:16-18*;]
1. a male prostitute (Xen., al.).
2. a fornicator: I Co 5:9-11 6:9, Eph 5:5, I Ti 1:10, He 12:15 13:4, Re 21:8 22:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πορφύρεος, -α, -ον, contr., -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν (< πορφύρα), [in LXX for אַרְגָּמָן;]
purple: Jo 19:2, 5; as subst., πορφυροῦν (sc. ἱμάτιον), Re 17:4 18:6.†

strong.derivation: feminine of a compound of G4209 (πορφύρα) and G4453 (πωλέω);
strong.def: a female trader in purple cloth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πορφυρόπωλις, -ιδος, ἡ,
a seller of purple fabrics: Ac 16:14.†

strong.def: a drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a draught

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πόσις, -εως, ἡ (< πίνω), [in LXX: Da, LXX TH 1:10 (מִשְׁתֶּה)*;]
1. prop., drinking: Ro 14:17, Col 2:16 (v. Lft.; ICC, in l.).
2. = πόμα, drink: Jo 6:55 (cf. βρῶσις).†

strong.derivation: from G4215 (ποταμός) and a derivative of G5409 (φορέω);
strong.def: river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ποταμο-φόρητος, -ον,
carried away by a stream: Re 12:15 (for two exx. in π., v. MM, xxi).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a comparative of the base of G4226 (ποῦ);
strong.def: interrogative as adverb, which (of two), i.e. is it this or that

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πότερος, -α, -ον,
which of two. Neut., adverbially, πότερον, whether: Jo 7:17.†

strong.def: little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e. Puteoli), a place in Italy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ποτίολοι, -ων, οἱ,
Puteoli (mod. Pozzuoli), a city on the Bay of Naples: Ac 28:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πότος, -ου, ὁ (< πίνω), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁתֶּה;]
a drinking bout, carousal: I Pe 4:3.†

strong.derivation: genitive case of an indefinite pronoun (some) otherwise obsolete (compare G4214 (πόσος));
strong.def: as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
52 πού, enclitic particle,
1. anywhere, somewhere: He 2:6 4:4.
2. in some degree, perhaps, about: Ac 27:29 (T, μήπου), Ro 4:19; δή που (T, δήπου), surely: He 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πούδης (in π., gen. -εντος, v. Zorell, s.v.), ὁ (Latin),
Pudens: II Ti 4:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πραγματία (Rec. -εία, as in cl.), -ας, ἡ (< πραγματεύομαι), [in LXX for חֵשֶׁל, etc.;]
1. careful application, hard work.
2. business, occupation: pl., II Ti 2:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 9 πρᾳότης, πραότης, v.s. πραΰτης.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πραΰς, -εῖα, -ΰ, and πρᾷος (or πρᾶος, v. Bl., § 3, 3), -α, -ον (v. LS, Thayer, s.v.), [in LXX (always -ΰς, exc. II Mac 15:12, -ᾷος, v. Thackeray, Gr., 180 f.) for עָנָו, עָנָיו, עָנִי;]
gentle, meek: Mt 5:5 11:29 21:5(LXX), I Pe 3:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 πραΰτης (Rec. -ότης, exc. Ja 1:21 3:13, I Pe 3:15, where πρᾳύτης), -ητος, ἡ, late form of πραότης, [in LXX: Ps 44 (45):4 89 (90):10 131 (132):1 (עַנְוָה, עֻנּוֹת, Es 5:1, Si6*;]
gentleness, meekness: I Co 4:21, II Co 10:1, Ga 5:23 6:1, Eph 4:2, Col 3:12 (v. Lft., in l.), II Ti 2:25, Tit 3:2, Ja 1:21 3:13, I Pe 3:15.†

strong.def: to tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 πρέπω, [in LXX: Ps 92 (93):5 (נאה pi.), etc.;]
1. to be clearly seen.
2. to resemble.
3. to be fitting or becoming, to suit: c. dat., He 7:26, I Ti 2:10, Tit 2:1; impers., c. dat., Eph 5:3; id. seq. inf., He 2:10; πρέπον ἐστίν, c. dat. pers. et inf., Mt 3:15; c. acc. et inf., I Co 11:13 (v. Bl., § 72, 5).†

strong.def: to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * πρεσβεύω (< πρέσβυς),
1. to be the elder, to take precedence.
2. to be an ambassador (v.s. πρεσβύτης): II Co 5:20, Eph 6:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πρεσβῦτις, -ιδος, ἡ, fem, of πρεσβύτης, [in LXX: IV Mac 16:14*;]
an aged woman: Tit 2:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πρηνής, -ές (in Att. also πρανής), [in LXX: Wi 4:19, III Mac 5:43, 50 6:23*;]
headlong, prone: Ac 1:18.†

strong.derivation: a strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πρίζω = πρίω, [in LXX: Am 1:3, Da TH Su 59*;]
to saw, saw asunder (= π. δίχα, Thuc., iv, 100): pass, He 11:37 (cf. δια-πρίω).†

strong.def: feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Πρίσκα, -ας, ἡ (Lat.), and Πρίσκιλλα, -ης, ἡ,
Prisca: Ro 16:3, I Co 16:19, II Ti 4:19; Priscilla: Ac 18:2, 18, 26; the wife of Aquila, v.s. Ἀκύλας.†

strong.def: Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 3 Πρίσκιλλα, v.s. Πρίσκα.

strong.def: to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προ-αιρέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: for חשׁק, etc.;]
to bring forth or forward. Most freq. in mid., to take by choice, prefer, propose: II Co 9:7.†

strong.derivation: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G156 (αἰτία);
strong.def: to accuse already, i.e. previously charge

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προ-αιτιάομαι, -ῶμαι,
to accuse or charge beforehand: Ro 3:9 (not elsewhere).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προ-ακούω,
to hear beforehand: Col 1:5 (v. Lft., in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† προ-αμαρτάνω,
to sin before: II Co 12:21 13:2.†

strong.def: relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προβατικός, -ή, -όν (< πρόβατον), [in LXX (π. πύλη): Ne 3:1, 32 12:39 (צֹאן)*;]
of sheep: ἡ π. (sc. πύλη, v. supr.), the sheep-gate, Jo 5:2.†

strong.derivation: from G4253 (πρό) and a reduplicated form of G971 (βιάζω);
strong.def: to force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προ-βιβάζω, causal of προβαίνω, [in LXX: Ex 35:34 (ירה hi.), De 6:7 (שׁנן pi.)*;]
to lead forward, lead on; metaph., to induce, incite, urge: Mt 14:8.†

strong.def: to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † προ-βλέπω, [in LXX: Ps 36 (37):13 (ראה)*;]
to foresee: mid., He 11:40 (v. Bl., § 24, 55, 1).†

strong.def: to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προ-γίνομαι, [in LXX: Wi 19:13 אA, II Mac 14:3 15:8*;]
to happen before: pf. pass. ptcp., Ro 3:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** προ-γινώσκω, [in LXX: Wi 6:13 8:8 18:6*;]
to know beforehand, foreknow: II Pe 3:17; c. acc. pers., Ac 26:5; of the Divine foreknowledge, Ro 8:29 11:2, I Pe 1:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† πρό-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ (< προγινώσκω), [in LXX: Jth 9:6 11:19*;]
foreknowledge: Ac 2:23, I Pe 1:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πρό-γονος, -ον (< προγίνομαι), [in LXX: Es 4:17, Si 8:4, al.;]
1. born before.
2. As subst., in pl., οἱ π., ancestors, forefathers: II Ti 1:3; of living parents (so Plat.), I Ti 5:4.†

strong.def: to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe
strong.kjv: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 προ-γράφω, [in LXX: Da LXX 3:3 cod., I Mac 10:36*;]
1. to write before: Ro 15:4, Eph 3:3, Ju 4.
2. to write in public, placard, proclaim (Dem., Plut., al.): Ga 3:1 (Lft., in l.).
3. = ζωγραφέω, to pourtray, depict: Ga 3:1 (Syr. Pesh., Chrys.; Field, Notes, 189; CGT, in l.).†

strong.def: plain before all men, i.e. obvious

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** πρό-δηλος, -ον, [in LXX: Jth 8:29, II Mac 3:17 14:39*;]
1. evident beforehand.
2. clearly evident: I Ti 5:24, 25, He 7:14.†

strong.def: to give before the other party has given

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προ-δίδωμι, [in LXX: Ez 16:34 A (נתן), IV Mac 4:1, al.;]
1. to give before, give first: Ro 11:35 (Jb 41:2 (11) LXX, al.).
2. to betray (IV Mac 4:1).†

strong.def: a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πρό-δρομος, -ον (< προτρέχω), [in LXX: Nu 13:21 (20), Is 28:4 (בּכר), Wi 12:8*;]
running forward, going in advance. As subst., ὁ π., an advance guard, forerunner: He 6:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) προ-εῖδον, aor. without pres. in use (v.s. προοράω), [in LXX: Ge 37:18 (ראה), Ps 138 (139):3 (סכן hi.)*;]
to foresee: Ac 2:31 (προϊδών; WH, προιδών), Ga 3:8.†

strong.def: to hope in advance of other confirmation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προ-ελπίζω,
to hope before: seq. ἐν, Eph 1:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† προ-ενάρχομαι,
to begin before: II Co 8:6; c. acc., τὸ θέλειν, II Co 8:10 (not elsewhere).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G1861 (ἐπαγγέλλω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† προ-επ-αγγέλλω,
to announce before. Mid., to promise before: c. acc. rei, Ro 1:2, II Co 9:5 (Dio. Cass.).†

strong.def: to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 προ-ετοιμάζω, [in LXX: Is 28:24 B, Wi 9:8*;]
to prepare before: c. acc. rei, Ro 9:23 (οἷς for ἅ by attraction), Eph 2:10.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2097 (εὐαγγελίζω);
strong.def: to announce glad news in advance

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προ-ευαγγελίζομαι,
to announce glad tidings beforehand: Ga 3:8.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2192 (ἔχω);
strong.def: to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προ-έχω, [in LXX: Jb 27:6 A (חזק hi.)*;]
1. Trans., to hold before; mid., to hold something before oneself (Hdt.), hence, metaph., to excuse oneself: Ro 3:9, R, mg. (but v. Field, Notes, 152 f.; Lft., Notes, 266 f.; ICC and Vau., in l.).
2. Intrans.
(a). to project;
(b). in running, to have the start, hence, metaph., to excel: pass., Ro 3:9, R, txt. (v. reff. supr.).†

strong.def: to lead the way for others, i.e. show deference

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προ-ηγέομαι, [in LXX: De 20:9 (בְּרוֹשׁ), Pr 17:14 (לִפְנֵי), II Mac 4:40, al.;]
1. to go before as leader (in cl., c. gen., dat.): Ro 12:10 (Chrys., Vg., al.; v. ICC, in l.).
2. In a sense not elsewhere found, ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι = ἀ. ἡγούμενοι ὑπερέχοντας: Ro 12:10 (ICC, cf. I Th 5:13, Phl 2:3 and EV "preferring").†

strong.derivation: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
strong.def: fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with G2250 (ἡμέρα) implied) a designated day

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προ-θέσμιος, -α, -ον, [in Sm.: Jb 28:3, Da 9:26*;]
appointed beforehand. In Attic law, as subst. (so always in cl.), ἡ π. (sc. ἡμέρα), a day appointed beforehand, a previously appointed time: Ga 4:2.†

strong.kjv: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** προθυμία, -ας, ἡ (< πρόθυμος), [in LXX: Si 45:23*;]
eagerness, willingness, readiness: Ac 17:11, II Co 8:11, 12, 19 9:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προθύμως, [in LXX: II Ch 29:34 (לֵבָב יִשְׁרֵי), To 7:8, al.;]
eagerly, readily, with a ready mind: I Pe 5:2.†

strong.def: to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 προ-ΐστημι, [in LXX: II Ki 13:17, Pr 23:5 26:17, Is 43:24, Am 6:10 (no proper Heb. equiv.), Da LXX Bel 7, I Mac 5:19, IV Mac 11:27*;]
1. trans. in fut., 1 aor., and mid. 1 aor., to put before, set over (Plat., al.).
2. Intrans., in pf., plpf., 2 aor. and mid. pres. and impf.;
(a). to preside, rule, govern: Ro 12:8, I Ti 5:17; c. gen., I Th 5:12, I Ti 3:4, 5, 12;
(b). to direct, maintain: c. gen. rei, καλῶν ἔργων, Tit 3:8, 14 (on R, mg., profess honest occupations, v. CGT, in l.; Field, Notes, 223 f.).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2564 (καλέω);
strong.def: to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προ-καλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Mac 8:11 A*;]
to call forth. Most freq. in mid.,
(a). to challenge; hence, to provoke: Ga 5:26;
(b). to invite (II Mac 8:11).†

strong.def: to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† προ-κατ-αγγέλλω,
to announce beforehand: c. acc. et inf., Ac 3:18; seq. περί, Ac 7:52.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προ-κατ-αρτίζω,
to make ready beforehand: II Co 9:5.†

strong.def: to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πρό-κειμαι, [in LXX: Ex 39:18 (36), Nu 4:7 (פָּנִים), etc.;] used as pass. of προτίθημι;
1. to be set before one, to be set forth: He 6:18 12:1, 2, Ju 7.
2. to present oneself, be present: II Co 8:12 (v. Mey., in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προ-κηρύσσω,
1. to proclaim by herald.
2. Of one who acts as a herald, to proclaim: Ac 13:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 **† προ-κοπή, -ῆς, ἡ (< προκόπτω), [in LXX: Si 51:17, II Mac 8:8*;]
progress (prop., on a journey, then generally): Phl 1:12, 25, I Ti 4:15 (condemned by Atticists, v. Rutherford, NPhr., 158).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G2919 (κρίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πρό-κριμα, -τος, τό (< cl. προκρίνειν, 1. to prefer. 2. to judge beforehand),
pre-judging, prejudice: I Ti 5:21 (v. Cremer, 378).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προ-κυρόω, -ῶ,
to establish or confirm beforehand: Ga 3:17.†

strong.def: to be a witness in advance i.e. predict

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προ-μαρτύρομαι,
to protest beforehand (cf. μαρτύρομαι, and V. Hort, in l.): I Pe 1:11 (elsewhere only in Theod. Met., xiv/AD.).†

strong.def: to consider in advance, i.e. look out for beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 προ-νοέω, -ῶ, and depon. -έομαι, οῦμαι, [in LXX: Da LXX 11:37 (בִּין), Wi 6:7, al.;]
1. to foresee.
2. to provide (RV, take thought for): c. acc. rei, καλά, Ro 12:17 (-ούμενοι), II Co 8:21 (-οῦμεν).
3. to provide for (seq. περί, Wi 6:7): c. gen. pers., I Ti 5:8 (-εῖ, WH, mg., -εῖται).†

strong.def: forethought, i.e. provident care or supply

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πρόνοια, -ας, ἡ (< πρόνοος, careful), [in LXX: Da LXX 6:18 (19) Wi 14:3 17:2, II-IV Mac6*;]
foresight, forethought: Ac 24:3; π. ποιεῖσθαι, c. gen. (Dem., 546, 6), make provision for, show care for: Ro 13:14.†

strong.def: to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 προ-οράω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Ps 15 (16):8) (שׁוה pi.), I Es 5:63 A*;]
to see before (as to place or time): c. acc., Ac 21:29. Mid., c. acc., seq. ἐνώπιόν μου, Ac 2:25(LXX).†

strong.def: to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively) predetermine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 *† προ-ορίζω,
to predetermine, foreordain: c. acc., Ro 8:30; id. et inf., Ac 4:28; id. seq. εἰς, I Co 2:7, Eph 1:5; c. dupl. acc., Ro 8:26; pass., Eph 1:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προ-πάσχω,
to suffer before: I Th 2:2.†

strong.def: to send forward, i.e. escort or aid in travel
strong.kjv: accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ** προ-πέμπω, [in LXX: I Es 4:47, Jth 10:15, Wi 19:2, I Mac 12:4, II Mac 6:23*;]
1. to send before, send forth.
2. to set forward on a journey, escort: c. acc. pers., I Co 16:11, Tit 3:13, III Jo 6; seq. εἰς, Ac 20:38; οὗ, I Co 16:6; ἕως, Ac 21:5; pass., Ac 15:3, Ro 15:24, II Co 1:16.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G4098 (πίπτω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 προπετής, -ές (< προπίπτω), [in LXX: Pr 10:14 (אֱוִיל) 13:3 (פֹּשׂק) Si 9:18*;]
falling forwards, headlong. Metaph., precipitate, rash, reckless: of persons, II Ti 3:4; of things, Ac 19:36.†

strong.derivation: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά) (mean to harangue);
strong.def: to address, i.e. salute by name

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προσ-αγορεύω, [in LXX: De 23:6 (7) (דָּרַשׁ), II Es 10:11, B:1 (ידה hith.), Wi 14:22, I Mac 14:40, II Mac 1:36 4:7 10:9 14:37*;]
to address, greet, salute; hence, to call by name, address, style: c. dupl. acc., pass., He 5:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * προσ-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ, (< προσάγω),
1. a bringing to.
2. approach, access (v. Lft., Notes, 284; MM, xxi): Ro 5:2, Eph 2:18 3:12 (but v. Ellic., Eph., 59 f., where the transitive sense "introduction" is advocated).†

strong.def: to fill up further, i.e. furnish fully

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** προσ-αναπληρόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Wi 19:4*;]
to fill up by adding to, to supply fully: II Co 9:12 11:9.†

strong.def: to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * προσ-ανα-τίθημι,
to lay on or offer besides; mid.,
(a). to lay on oneself in addition, undertake besides;
(b). c. gen. pers., of giving or obtaining information, to consult, communicate: Ga 1:16 2:6 (Lft., in l.; cf. ἀνα-τίθημι).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προσ-απειλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Si 13:3 א*;]
to threaten further: Ac 4:21.†

strong.def: to require additionally, i.e. want further

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προσ-δέομαι, [in LXX: Pr 12:9 חָסֵר, Si6*;]
to want further, need in addition: Ac 17:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προσ-εάω, -ῶ,
to permit further: Ac 27:7.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4314 (πρός) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος);
strong.def: to sit near, i.e. attend as a servant

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προσεδρεύω (< πρόσεδρος, sitting near), [in LXX: I Mac 11:40*;]
1. to sit near.
2. to attend regularly: c. dat., I Co 9:13, Rec. (v.s. παρεδρεύω).†

strong.derivation: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of G2247 (ἧλος);
strong.def: to peg to, i.e. spike fast

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προσ-ηλόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: III Mac 4:9*;]
to nail to: c. acc. et dat., fig., Col 2:14.†

strong.def: an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † προσήλυτος, -ον (< προσελαύνω), [in LXX for גֵּר;]
1. one who has arrived, a stranger.
2. Of converts to Judaism, a proselyte (v. DB, s.v.): Mt 23:15, Ac 2:10 6:5 13:43.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προσ-καρτέρησις, -εως, ἡ (< προσκαρτερέω),
stedfastness, perseverance: Eph 6:18.†

strong.def: to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to associate with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προσ-κληρόω, -ῶ,
to allot to, assign to by lot; pass. (but perh. as mid., EV, consorted with, so Syr.): Ac 17:4 (for exx., v, Cremer, 749).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4314 (πρός) and G2827 (κλίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πρόσ-κλισις, -εως, ἡ (< προσκλίνω),
inclination partiality: I Ti 5:21.†

strong.def: a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 † πρόσ-κομμα, -τος, τό (< προσκόπτω), [in LXX: Ex 23:33 34:12 (מוֹקֵשׁ), Is 8:14 (נֶגֶף), Jth 8:22, Si 17:25, al.;]
(a). a stumble, stumbling: λίθος προσκόμματος (= אֶבֶן נֶגֶף, Is 8:14), fig., Ro 9:32, 33, I Pe 2:8(LXX);
(b). = προσκοπή, an occasion of stumbling, a stumbling-block: metaph., Ro 14:13, 20, I Co 8:9 (Plut.).†

strong.def: a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προσκοπή, -ῆς, ἡ (< προσκόπτω), [in Gr. Ven.: Pr 16:18 (כִּשָּׁלוֹן)*;]
an occasion of stumbling, offence: II Co 6:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προσ-κυνητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< προσκυνέω),
a worshipper: Jo 4:23.†

strong.def: to talk to, i.e. converse with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 προσ-λαλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Ex 4:16 AB2 (דּבר pi.), Wi 13:17*;]
to speak to: Ac 28:20; c. dat. pers., Ac 13:43.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πρόσ-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις, as in Att.), -εως, ἡ (< προσλαμβάνω),
1. an assumption (Plat.).
2. a receiving (cf. προσλαμβάνω): Ro 11:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προσ-οφείλω,
to owe besides: Phm 19 (v. Field, Notes, 225).†

strong.derivation: from G4314 (πρός) and a form of (to be vexed with something irksome);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † προσ-οχθίζω, [in LXX: Le 26:15, al. (גּעל); Le 18:25, al. (קוֹא), Ps 94 (95):10, Ez 36:31 (קוּט), Si 6:25, al. (other writers use ὀχθέω, rarely -ίζω);]
to be angry with: c. dat., He 3:10(LXX), 17.†

strong.derivation: from G4314 (πρός) and the same as G3983 (πεινάω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πρόσπεινος, -ον (< πεῖωα, hunger),
hungry: Ac 10:10.†

strong.def: to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προσ-πήγνυμι,
to fasten to: absol., to crucify, Ac 2:23.†

strong.derivation: feminine of a derivative of G4291 (προΐστημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προστάτις, -ιδος, ἡ (fem. of προστάτης),
a patroness, protectress: Ro 16:2.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4314 (πρός) and G5315 (φάγω);
strong.def: something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. a relish (specially, fish; compare G3795 (ὀψάριον))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προσφάγιον, -ου, τό (< φαγεῖν),
Hellenistic for ὄψον (v.s. ὀψάριον), a relish or dainty (esp. cooked fish), to be eaten with bread: Jo 21:5 (have ye taken any fish, Field, Notes, 109; Abbott, Essays, 105; cf. M, Pr., 170n; MM, Exp., xxi).†

strong.derivation: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G4969 (σφάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πρόσφατος, -ον (on the derivation, v. Boisacq, s.v. and cf. -ως), [in LXX: Nu 6:3 (לַח), De 32:17, Ec 1:9 (חָדָשׁ), Ps 80 (81):9 (זוּר), Si 9:10*;]
1. originally, freshly slain.
2. Generally (from Æsch. on), new, fresh, recent: ὁδός, He 10:20 (v. MM, Exp., xxi; Rutherford, NPhr., 471 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προσφάτως, adv. (v.s. πρόσφατος), [in LXX: De 24:5 (חָדָשׁ), Jth 4:3, 5, Ez 11:3, II Mac 14:36*;]
recently: Ac 18:2 (v. MM, Exp., xxi).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G4314 (πρός) and G5368 (φιλέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προσφιλής, -ές (< φιλέω), [in LXX: Es 5:1, Si 4:7 20:13*;]
(a). of persons, in both act. and pass. sense (LXX, Es 5:1, Si 4:7 20:13);
(b). of things, pleasing, agreeable (EV, lovely): Phl 4:8.†

strong.def: presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 προσ-φορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< προσφέρω), [in LXX: III Ki 7:48 (פָּנִים) Ps 39 (40):6 (מִנְחָה), I Es 5:52, Si 14:11, al.;]
1. a bringing to, offering (Plat., al.).
2. (Less freq. in cl.), a present, an offering; in NT, of sacrificial offerings: Ac 21:26 24:17, Eph 5:2, He 10:5, 8, 14; περί ἁμαρτίας, He 10:18; c. gen. obj., Ro 15:16, He 10:10.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G4314 (πρός) and (to pour);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πρόσ-χυσις, -εως, ἡ,
a pouring or sprinkling upon: He 11:28.†

strong.def: to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προσωπολημπτέω (Rec. -ληπτ-), -ῶ (< -λήμπτης, q.v.),
to have respect of persons: Ja 2:9.†

strong.def: an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† προσωπο-λήμπτης (Rec. -λήπτης, v. Bl., § 6, 8), -ου, ὁ (< πρόσωπον λαμβάνειν, v.s. πρόσωπον),
a respecter of persons: Ac 10:34 (on this group of cognate forms, v. Mayor, ja., 78 f.; and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 44).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† προσωπολημψία (Rec. -ληψία), -ας, ἡ (< προσωπολήμπτης),
respect of persons: Ro 2:11, Eph 6:9, Col 3:25, Ja 2:1 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προ-τάσσω, [in LXX: II Mac 8:36 R (Α, προστ-)*;]
1. to place in front.
2. to arrange beforehand: Ac 17:26, Rec. (for προστ., Edd.).†

strong.def: to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for scourging)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προ-τείνω, [in LXX: II Mac7, III Mac 2:1*;]
to stretch out, stretch forth: of preparations for scourging (v. Field, Notes, 136 f.), Ac 22:25.†

strong.derivation: neuter of G4387 (πρότερος) as adverb (with or without the article);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 A. Compar., πρότερος, -α, -ον, [in LXX for לִפָנִים, רִאשׁוֹן, etc.;]
before, of time, place, rank, etc.; in NT always of Time, before, former: Eph 4:22. Adverbially, πρότερον, before, aforetime, formerly: Jo 7:50, II Co 1:15, He 4:6; opp. to ἔπειτα, He 7:27; τὸ π., Jo 6:62 9:8, Ga 4:13, I Ti 1:13; αἱ π. ἡμέραι, He 10:32; αἱ π. ἐπιθυμίαι, I Pe 1:14.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G5087 (τίθημι);
strong.def: to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 προ-τίθημι, [in LXX: Ex 40:4, 23, Le 24:8 (ערךְ) Ps 53 (54):3 (שׂוּם), etc.;]
1. to set before, set forth publicly; so also in mid.: c. acc. pers., Ro 3:25 (for a suggested alt. rend., v. MM, xxii).
2. Mid., to set before oneself, propose, purpose: c. inf., Ro 1:13; c. acc. rei, Eph 1:9.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);
strong.def: to turn forward for oneself, i.e. encourage

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** προ-τρέπω, [in LXX: Wi 14:18, II Mac 11:7, IV Mac 12:7 15:12 16:13*;]
to urge forwards, exhort, persuade. Mid., in same sense (as also in cl.): Ac 18:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 † προφητεία, -ας, ἡ (< προψητεύω), [in LXX for נְבוּאָה, חָזוֹן;]
the gift (and its exercise) of interpreting the Divine will and purpose, prophecy, prophesying: of OT prophecy, Mt 13:14, II Pe 1:20, 21; of NT prophecy, Ro 12:6, I Co 12:10 13:2 14:6, 22, I Ti 4:14, Re 11:6 22:19; pl., I Co 13:8, I Th 5:20, I Ti 1:18; οἱ λόγοι τῆς π., Re 1:3 22:7, 10, 18; τ. πνεῦμα τῆς π., Re 19:10 (Luc., FlJ, LXX, π.; v. Deiss., BS, 235 f.; MM, xxii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† προφητικός, -ά, -όν (< προφήτης),
of prophecy, prophetic: Ro 16:26, II Pe 1:19.†

strong.def: to get an earlier start of, i.e. anticipate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 προ-φθάνω, [in LXX chiefly for קדם pi.;]
c. ptcp. (as in cl., but more freq. the simple φθάνω, q.v.), to anticipate: Mt 17:25.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G5495 (χείρ);
strong.def: to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 προ-χειρίζω (< πρόχειρος, at hand), [in LXX: Ex 4:13 (שׁלח), Jos 3:12 (לקח), Da LXX 3:22, II Mac 3:7 8:9 14:12 A*;]
1. to put into the hand, deliver up: pass., Ac 3:20.
2. More freq. as depon., -ομαι, to take into one's hand; hence, metaph., to propose, determine, choose: c. inf., Ac 22:14; c. acc. pers., Ac 26:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * προ-χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ (v. χειροτονέω),
to choose or appoint beforehand: Ac 10:41 (Plat., al.).†

strong.def: before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πρόχορος, -ου, ὁ,
Prochorus: Ac 6:5.

strong.derivation: feminine of a derivative of G4404 (πρωΐ) as noun;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 2 πρωία, v.s. πρώιος.

strong.def: dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 πρώϊμος, v.s. πρόϊμος.

strong.def: pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † πρωινός (Rec. -ϊνος, v. WH, App., ή, -όν (< πρωί), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר;] = cl. πρώιος,
at early morn, early: ἀστήρ, Re 2:28 22:16.†

strong.derivation: feminine of a presumed derivative of G4253 (πρό) as noun;
strong.def: the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * πρῷρα (Rec. incorrectly πρώρα, v. Bl., § 3, 3; LS, s.v.), -ης (for Att. -ας, v. Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, l 2), ἡ,
the forward part of a ship, the prow: Ac 27:30; opp. to πρύμνα, Ac 27:41.†

strong.def: to be first (in rank or influence)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πρωτεύω (< πρῶτος), [in LXX: Es 5:11, II Mac 6:18 13:15*;]
to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place: Col 1:18.†

strong.def: one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain (champion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πρωτοστάτης, -ου, ὁ (< πρῶτος, ἵστημι), [in LXX: Jb 15:24 AB*;]
prop., of soldiers, one who stands first, one in the front rank (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaph., a leader: Ac 24:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † πρωτοτόκια, -ων, τά (< πρωτότοκος), [in LXX (with v.l. -εῖα, -εία): Ge 25:31 ff. 27:36, De 21:17, I Ch 5:1 (בְּכוֹרָה)*;]
the rights of the first-born, birthright (= cl. ἡ πρεσβεία): He 12:16.†

strong.def: to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πταίω, [in LXX chiefly for נגף ni.;]
1. trans., to cause to stumble (I Ki 4:3, cf. Deiss., BS, 681).
2. Intrans., to stumble. Metaph., in moral sense, Ro 11:11, Ja 2:10 3:2, II Pe 1:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πτέρνα, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for עָקֵב;]
the heel: fig., ἐπαίρειν τὴν π. ἐπί, Jo 13:18(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πτηνός, -ή, -όν (< πέτομαι), [in Aq.: Jb 5:7*;]
winged; as subst., τὰ π., birds: I Co 15:39.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πτόησις, -εως, ἡ (< πτοέω), [in LXX: Pr 3:25 (פַּחַד), Sir 50:4 א1, I Mac 3:25 R*;]
a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. acc.) or of any terror (v. ICC, in l.): I Pe 3:6.†

strong.derivation: from (Ptolemy, after whom it was named);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πτολεμαΐς, -ΐδος, ἡ,
Ptolemais, a maritime city of Phœnicea: Ac 21:7.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G4429 (πτύω) (and thus akin to G4422 (πτοέω));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πτύρομαι, depon.,
to be startled, frightened: Phl 1:28. (The active πτύρω is also found in some late writers.)†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πτύσμα, -τος, τό, (< πτύω),
spittle: Jo 9:6 (Hipp., Polyb., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πτωχεία, -ας, ἡ (< πτωχεύω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי;]
beggary, destitution: II Co 8:2, 9, Re 2:9.†

strong.def: to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πτωχεύω (< πτωχός), [in LXX: Jg 6:6, Ps 78 (79):8 (דּלל); Jg 14:15 A, Pr 23:21 (ירשׁ); Ps 33 (34):10 (רוּשׁ), To 4:21*;]
1. to be a beggar, to beg (so chiefly in cl.).
2. to be poor as a beggar, to be destitute, poor: opp. to πλούσιος ὤν, II Co 8:9.†

strong.derivation: from (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located);
strong.def: a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πύθων, -ωνος, ὁ,
1. in cl., Python, a serpent slain by Apollo, who is hence surnamed the Pythian.
2. In Plut. (ii, 414 E), a name given to ventriloquist soothsayers (ἐγγαστρίμυθοι; cf. Le 19:31 20:6, 27, I Ki 28:7), and perhaps in this sense πνεῦμα πύθωνα, a python-spirit: Ac 16:16.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the same as G4435 (πυγμή);
strong.def: to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πυκτεύω (< πύκτης, a pugilist),
to box: I Co 9:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** πυρά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< πῦρ), [in LXX: Jth 7:5, Wi 17:6, al.;]
a fire: Ac 28:2, 3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πύρινος, -η, -ον, [in LXX: Ez 28:14, 16 (אֵשׁ), Si 48:9*;]
fiery: Re 9:17.†

strong.def: to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust)
strong.kjv: burn, fiery, be on fire, try

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 πυρόω, -ῶ (< πῦρ), [in LXX chiefly for צרף;]
to set on fire, burn up. In NT always pass.,
1. to be set on fire, to burn: Eph 6:16, II Pe 3:12; ptcp., glowing, Re 1:15. Metaph., of grief or indignation, II Co 11:29; of lust, I Co 7:9.
2. Of metals (cf. Jb 22:25, Ps 11 (12):7, Za 13:9), to be refined or purified by fire: Re 3:18 (and so in RV, Re 1:15, but v. supr.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † πυρράζω (< πυρρός), [in LXX, πυρρίζω: Le 13:19, 42 ff. 14:37 (אֲדַמְדָּם)*;]
to be fiery red: Mt 16:|[2, 3]|.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πυρρός, -ά, -όν (< πῦρ), [in LXX for אֱדֹם;]
fiery red: Re 6:4 12:3.†

strong.def: ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πύρωσις, -εως, ἡ (< πυρόω), [in LXX: Pr 27:21 (כּוּר), Am 4:9 (שִׁדָּפוֹן)*;]
1. a burning: Re 18:9, 18.
2. a refining or trial by fire: metaph., I Pe 4:12.†

strong.derivation: adverb from the base of G4225 (πού);
strong.def: an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ῥαάβ (and Ραχάβ, Mt 1:5; Ραχάβη, -ης, in FlJ), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. רָחָב),
Rahab (LXX, Jos 2:1, al.): He 11:31, Ja 2:25.†

strong.def: to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ῥαβδίζω (< ῥάβδος), [in LXX: Jg 6:11 Ru 2:17 (חבט) * ;]
to beat with a rod: Ac 16:22, II Co 11:25.†

strong.def: a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ῥαβδοῦχος, -ου, ό (< ῥάβδος, ἔχω),
one who carries a rod or staff of office;
(a). an umpire or judge (Plat.);
(b). in late writers, a Roman lictor: Ac 16:35, 38.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of (easy, i.e. reckless) and G2041 (ἔργον);
strong.def: easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥᾳδιούργημα, -τος, τό (< ῥᾳδιουργέω, to act recklessly or wrongly)
1. a reckless act.
2. crime, villany: Ac 18:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥᾳδιουργία, -ας, ἡ (v.s. ῥᾳδιούργημα),
1. ease in doing, facility (Xen.).
