2. easiness, laziness (Xen.).
3. recklessness, wickedness (of lewdness, Xen.; fraud, Plut.; in π., of theft, MM, xxii): Ac 13:10.†

strong.def: O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥακά (T, ῥαχά),
usually taken to represent the Aram. רֵיקָא, a shortened form of רֵיקָן, "empty," as vocalized in the Galilæan dialect; an expression of contempt, raca: Mt 5:22 (cf. DB, iv, 191 f.; and for other explanations, v. Zorell, s.v.).†

strong.def: Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥαμά (Rec. -ᾶ), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. רָמָה),
Ramah: Mt 2:18 (LXX).†

strong.def: to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ῥαντίζω [in LXX: Le 6:27 (20), IV Ki 9:33 (נזה), Ps 50 (51):7 (חטא pi.) * ;] (-ρραίνω, Rec., v. WH, App., 139 f.), [in LXX for נָזָה hi. ;]
= cl., ῥαίνω,
to sprinkle, besprinkle: c. acc., He 9:13, 19; id. et dat., ib. 21; pass., Re 19:13, WH; of cleansing by sprinkling, He 10:22 (v. M, Gr., ii, 100); mid., Mk 7:4 (WH, txt., R, mg.).†
περι-ραίνω
to sprinkle around: Re 19:13 T (ῤεραντισμένον, WH; ῤε-, R, txt.; βεβαμμένον, Rec., R, mg.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ῥαντισμός, -ῦο, ὁ (< ῥαντίζω), [in LXX for נִדָּה ;]
sprinkling: of the ceremonial sprinkling of blood for purification, He 12:24, I Pe 1:2 (v. Hort, Pe., 23 ff.).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of a primary (to let fall, "rap");
strong.kjv: smite (with the palm of the hand)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ῥαπίζω (< ῥαπίς, a rod), [in LXX: Jg 16:25, Ho 11:4, I Es 4:31 * ;]
1. prop., to strike with a rod.
2. In late writers, to strike (the face) with the palm of the hand: Mt 26:67; c. acc. pers., seq. εἰς τ. σιαγόνα, Mt 5:39 (cf. Field, Notes, 40, 105).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 Ῥαχάβ, v.s. Ραάβ.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥαχήλ, ἡ indecl. (Heb. רָחֵל),
Rachel: Mt 2:18 (LXX).†

strong.def: Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥεβέκκα, -ας (v. Bl., § 7, 2), ἡ, (Heb. רִבְקָה),
Rebecca: Ro 9:10.†

strong.def: a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ῥέδη (v. WH, App., 151), -ης, ἡ (a Gallic word),
a chariot: Re 18:13.†

strong.derivation: by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (H03594);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 Ῥεμφάν, Ῥεφάς, v.s. Ῥομφά.

strong.def: for some tenses of which a prolonged form is used to flow ("run"; as water)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
22 ῥέω [in LXX chiefly for זוּב ;]
to flow: Jo 7:38 (cf. παραρρέω).†

strong.derivation: perhaps akin (or identical) with G4482 (ῥέω) (through the idea of pouring forth);
strong.def: to utter, i.e. speak or say

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2335 λέγω, [in LXX very freq., chiefly for אמר; λέγει for נְאֻם, Ge 22:16, al.;]
1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Ac 13:15 24:10; seq. orat. dir., Mt 9:34, Mk 3:11, Jo 1:29, al.; seq. ὅτι recit., Mk 3:21, Lk 1:24, Jo 6:14, al.; acc. et. inf., Lk 11:18, Jo 12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Mt 11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Mt 25:9, Mk 3:33, 7:28, Lk 24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Mt 3:9, Lk 3:8, al.; of writing, II Co 8:8, Phl 4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, Ro 4:3, Ja 2:23, al.; c. acc. rei, Lk 8:8 9:33, Jo 5:34, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369 f.), Mt 27:11, Mk 15:2, Lk 23:3, Jo 18:37; c. dat. pers., seq. orat. dir., Mt 8:20, Mk 2:17, al. mult.; id. seq. ὅτι, Mt 3:9, al.; c. prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., Mk 4:41, Jo 11:56, He 9:5, al.; to mean (cl.), Mk 14:71, Jo 6:71, I Co 10:29, al.; to call, name, Mk 10:18; pass., Mt 9:9, Mk 15:7, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥήγιον, -ου, τό
Rhegium, a town in Sicily: Ac 28:13.†

strong.def: a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥήτωρ, -ορος, ὁ
a public speaker, an orator: Ac 24:1.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of G4483 (ῥέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ῥητῶς adv. (< ῥητός, stated, specified),
in stated terms, expressly: I Ti 4:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ῥιζόω, -ῶ (< ῥίζα), [in LXX: Is 40:24, Je 12:2 (שׁרשׁ), Si 3:28 24:12 * ;]
to cause to take root. Metaph., to plant, fix firmly, establish: pass. (EV, rooted), ἐν ἀγάπῃ, Eph 3:18 (17) ; ἐν Χριστῷ, Col 2:7 (cf. ἐκ ριζόω).†

strong.def: a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥιπή, ῆς, ἡ (< ῥίπτω),
poët. in cl., any rapid movement such as the throw or flight of a javelin, the rush of wind or flame, the flapping of wings, the twinkling of lights; ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ, the twinkling of an eye: I Co 15:52 (L, mg., ῥοπή, q.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G4496 (ῥίπτω) (meaning a fan or bellows);
strong.def: to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ῥιπίζω (< ῥιπίς, a fan) [in LXX: Da LXX 2:35 (נְשָׂא) * ;]
primarily, to fan a fire, hence generally, to make a breeze (Plut., al.). In pass. (cf. Philo, de incer. mund., 24), to be tossed or blown by the wind: of waves, ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ, blown and raised with the wind (Hort, in l.), Ja 1:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ῥιπτέω, v.s. ῥίπτω.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ῥοβοάμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. רְחַבְעָם),
Rehoboam: Mt 1:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥόδη, -ης, ἡ
Rhoda: Ac 12:13.†

strong.def: Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥόδος, -ου, ὁ
the island of Rhodes: Ac 21:1.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of (a whir);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥοιζηδόν adv. (< ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow),
with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): II Pe 3:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥουβήν, ὁ indecl., (Heb. רְאוּבֵן),
Reuben: Re 7:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥούθ, ἡ indecl. (Heb. רוּת),
Ruth: Mt 1:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥυπαρία, -ας, ἡ (ῥυπαρός)
filthiness: metaph., of moral defile­ment, Ja 1:21.†

strong.def: dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ῥυπαρός, -ά, -όν (< ῥύπος), [in LXX: Za 3:4, 5, (3, 4) (צוֹא)* ;]
filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.c.), Ja 2:2; metaph., of moral defilement, Re 22:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Is 4:4 (צֹאָה), Jb 14:4 (טָמֵא), etc. ;]
dirt, filth: I Pe 3:21.†

strong.def: to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥυπόω, -ῶ (< ῥύπος),
to make filthy: Re 22:11 Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).†

strong.def: a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ῥυτίς, -ίδος, ἡ
a wrinkle: Eph 5:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 Ῥωμαῖος, -α, -ον
Roman: Jo 11:48, Ac 2:10 (RV, from Rome), Ac 16:21, 37, 38 22:25-27, 29 23:27 25:16 28:17.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a presumed derivative of G4516 (Ῥώμη);
strong.def: Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ῥωμαϊστί adv.,
in Latin: Jo 19:20.†

strong.def: strength; Roma, the capital of Italy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 Ῥώμη, -ης, ἡ
Rome: Ac 18:2 19:21 23:11 28:14, 16, Ro 1:7, 15, II Ti 1:17.†

strong.def: probably akin to G4506 (ῥύομαι)); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ῥώννυμι [in LXX: II Mac 9:20 11:21, 28, 33; III Mac6 * ;]
to strengthen; most freq. in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): Ac 15:29 23:30 Rec., R, mg.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (H06635 in feminine plural);
strong.def: armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † σαβαώθ indecl., [in LXX for צְבָאוֺת, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase יהוה צי is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; v. DB, iii, 137 f.) ;]
Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (v. DB, l.c.): Ro 9:29 (LXX), Ja 5:4.†

strong.def: a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, Ex 16:30, al.),
a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaph., as in Mishna (Zorell, s.v.), He 4:9.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶם ;]
a drag-net, seine: Mt 13:47.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, v. supr., s.v. Σαδδουκαῖος)
Sadoc, Zadok: Mt 1:14.†

strong.def: to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σαίνω
1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn.
2. Metaph., of persons, c. acc., to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., I Th 3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, v. ICC, and M, Th., in l.).†

strong.derivation: probably from G4535 (σάλος) (from the surge on the shore);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σαλαμίς, -ῖνος, ἡ
Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: Ac 13:5.†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G4531 (σαλεύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σαλείμ, τό indecl.,
Salim: Jo 3:23 (v. Westc., in l.; DB, iii, 354).†

strong.def: Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σαλήμ, ἡ (Heb. שָׁלֵם Ge 14:18),
Salem: He 7:1, 2 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן),
Salmon: Mt 1:4, 5, Lk 3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†

strong.derivation: perhaps of similar origin to G4529 (Σαλαμίς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ
Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Ac 27:7.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from G4535 (σάλος) (through the idea of quavering or reverberation);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;]
a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: I Co 14:8, He 12:19, Re 1:10 4:1 8:2, 6, 13 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Mt 24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, I Th 4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., I Co 15:52.†

strong.def: to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 σαλπίζω [in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;]
to sound a trumpet: Re 8:6 ff. 9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaph., Mt 6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: I Co 15:52.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σαλπιστής (so Inscr. and late writers for Att. σαλπιγκτής), -οῦ, ὁ,
a trumpeter: Re 18:22.†

strong.def: a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, v. supr.), -ιδος, ἡ
1. in FlJ (B.J., I, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria.
2. a Samaritan woman: Jo 4:9.†

strong.def: Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σαμοθρᾴκη (-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ
Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: Ac 16:11.†

strong.def: Samus, an island of the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σάμος, -ου, ἡ
Samos, an island in the Ægean: Ac 20:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל),
Samuel (I Ki 1:20, al.): Ac 3:24 13:20, He 11:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן),
Samson (Jg 13 ff.): He 11:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σανίς, -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX: Ca 8:9, Ez 27:5 (לוּחַ) * ;]
a board, plank: Ac 27:44

strong.def: Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 Σαούλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל)
Saul;
(a). the King of Israel: Ac 13:21;
(b). the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): Ac 9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σαπφείρα, -ης (v. B1., § 3, 4), ἡ (< Aram. שַׁפִּירָא)
Sapphira: Ac 5:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for סַפִּיר ;]
sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): Re 21:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ
1. a plaited rope (Æsch.).
2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: II Co 11:33.†

strong.def: Sardis, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Σάρδεις, -εων, αἱ
Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: Re 1:11 3:1, 4.†

strong.def: sardine (G3037 (λίθος) being implied), i.e. a gem, so called

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † σάρδινος, -ου, ὁ
= σάρδιον (q.v.), Re 4:3, Rec.†

strong.derivation: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base;
strong.def: sardian (3037 being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σάρδιον, -ον, τό [in LXX for אֹדֶם, Ex 28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;]
the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Re 4:3 21:20.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G4556 (σάρδιος) and (the nail of a finger;
strong.def: hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ (< σάρδιον, ὄνυξ),
sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Re 21:20.†

strong.def: pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 * σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (< σάρξ) (v.l. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7)
= Lat. carnalis, i.e.
(a). associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Ro 15:27, I Co 9:11;
(b). in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, I Pe., 133): I Co 3:3, II Co 1:12 10:4, I Pe 2:11.†

strong.def: similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 σάρκινος, -η, -ον (< σάρξ), [in LXX: II Ch 32:8, Ez 11:19 36:26 (בָּשָׂר), Es 4:17, Pr 24:23 (29:27) * ;]
= Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; v. Tr., Syn., § lxxii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., v. MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Ro 7:14, I Co 3:1, II Co 3:3, He 7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except II Co, l.c., but the evidence is decisive against it.)†

strong.def: Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Σάρρα, -ας, ἡ (Heb. שָׂרָה, Ge 17:15),
Sarah: Ro 4:19 9:9, He 11:11, I Pe 3:6.†

strong.def: Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σάρων, -ωνος (acc -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן),
the plain of Sharon: Ac 9:35.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin, the same as G4549 (Σαούλ);
strong.def: Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, q.v.),
Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: Ac 7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8, 11, 22, 24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1, 2, 7, 9.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from a derivative of G4576 (σέβομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** σεβάζομαι (< σέβας, reverential awe), [in Aq.: Ho 10:5 * ;]
1. to fear (Hom).
2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: Ro 1:25

strong.def: something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** σέβασμα, -τος, τό (< σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wi 14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;]
an object of worship: Ac 17:23, II Th 2:4.†

strong.def: venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * σεβαστός, -ή, -όν (σεβάζομαι)
1. reverend, august.
2. In late writers, with reference to the Roman Imperial name;
(a). ὁ Σ., Augustus, i.e. the Roman Emperor: Ac 25:21, 25;
(b). Augustan: σπείρα σ., Ac 27:1 (See further, Deiss., BS, 218.) †

strong.derivation: probably from G4951 (σύρω) through its congener (to fasten;
strong.def: akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι)); a chain (as binding or drawing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX: Jg 16:13, 14, 19 (מַחְלָפוֺת), Pr 5:22 (חֶבֶל) * ;]
1.
(a). a cord;
(b). a chain (cf. Pr., l.c.): σειραὶ ζόφου, II Pe 2:4, Rec., R, mg. (v.s. σειρός).
2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. c.).†

strong.def: to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 σείω [in LXX chiefly for רעשׁ ;]
to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, He 12:26 (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Mt 27:51 (LXX); συκῆ, Re 6:13. Metaph., to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Mt 21:10 28:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σέκουνδος (Rec. Σεκοῦνδος), -ου, ὁ
(Lat.), Secundus: Ac 20:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σελευκία (Rec. -εύκεια),
Seleucia, a city of Syria: Ac 13:4.†

strong.derivation: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of G4582 (σελήνη);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† σεληνιάζω (< σελήνη), act, in Manetho (Carm., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι,
to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): Mt 4:24 17:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;]
fine wheaten flour: Re 18:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 σεμνός, -ή, -όν (< σέβομαι), [in LXX: Pr 6:8 8:6 15:26(נָגִיד,נֹעַם), II Mac 6:11, 6:28 8:15, IV Mac 5:36 7:15 17:5 * ;]
1. reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings.
2. grave, serious; of persons: I Ti 3:8, 11, Tit 2:2; of things: Phl 4:8 (v. Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (< σεμνός), [in LXX: II Mac 3:12 * ;]
gravity: I Ti 2:2 3:4 (Vg. castitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, s.v.), Tit 2:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σέργιος, -ου, ὁ
Sergius, surnamed Paulus: Ac 13:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 σημαίνω (< σῆμα, a sign), [in LXX for רוּעַ hi., תָּקַע, etc. ;]
to give a sign, signify, indicate: c. acc. rei, Ac 25:27, Re 1:1 (cf. MM, xxii); c. acc. et inf., Ac 11:28; seq. quæst. indir., Jo 12:33 18:32 21:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σημειόω, -ῶ (< σημεῖον), [in LXX: Ps 4:6 (נשׂא)* ;]
to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: II Th 3:14 (freq. in π.; v. ICC, M, Th., in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σήπω [in LXX; Ps 37 (38):5 (מקק ni.), Jb 33:21 (כּלה) 40:7, Si 14:19, al. ;]
to make corrupt: 2 pf. act, with mid, sense (v. M, Pr., 154), σέσηπεν, has perished, become corrupted, Ja 5:2.†

strong.derivation: from (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured;
strong.def: hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; v. Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν (< οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk),
silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Re 18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†

strong.derivation: from G4597 (σής) and a derivative of G977 (βιβρώσκω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † σητό-βρωτος, -ον (< σής, βιβρώσκω), [in LXX: Jb 13:28 (אֲכָלוֺ עָשׁ) * ;]
moth-eaten: Ja 5:2.†

strong.def: probably akin to the base of G2476 (ἵστημι)); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σθενόω, -ῶ (< σθένος, strength),
to strengthen: c. acc., I Pe 5:10 (Hesych.).†

strong.derivation: apparently from (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** σιγή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Wi 18:14, III Mac 3:23 * ;]
silence: Ac 21:40, Re 8:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 σιδήρεος, -α, -ον (-οῦς, -ᾶ -οῦν) (< σίδηρος), [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]
of iron: Ac 12:10, Re 2:27 9:9 12:5 19:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σίδηρος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]
iron: Re 18:12.†

strong.def: a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σικάριος, -ου, ὁ (Lat.; < sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii),
a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): Ac 21:38.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 Σίλας, -α (acc to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; v. Dalman, Gr., 1575),
Silas (called also Σιλουανός, q.v.): Ac 15:22, 27, 32, 34, 40 16:19, 25, 29 17:4, 10, 14, 15 18:5 †

strong.def: a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σιμικίνθιον (also written σημι-), -ου, τό (Lat. semicinctium),
a work­man's apron: Ac 19:12.†

strong.def: Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Σινά (-ᾶ, Rec.), (Heb. סִינַי),
indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό
Sinai (Ex 19:11, al.): Ac 7:30, 38, Ga 4:24, 25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† σιτιστός, -ή, -όν (< σιτίζω, to fatten) [in Sm.: Ps 21 (22):13, Je 46 (26):21 * ;]
= σιτευτός, fattened; as subst., pl., τὰ σ., fatlings: Mt 22:4.†

strong.def: Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 Σιών (Heb. צִיּוֹן),
indecl.,
in NT anarth., but in LXX when used of the city of Jerusalem, ἡ Σ.
Zion;
1. the mountain: in typical sense, of the Church, He 12:22; of heaven, Re 14:1.
2. The city, i.e. Jerusalem; in poetical sense;
(a). of the inhabitants: θυγάτηρ Σ, Mt 21:5, Jo 12:15 (LXX);
(b). in wider sense, of Israel: Ro 11:26;
(c). fig.: τίθήμι ἐν Σ λίθον, Ro 9:33, I Pe 2:6 (LXX).†

strong.def: a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** σκάφη, -ης, ἡ (< σκάπτω), [in LXX: Da LXX Bel 32, TH ib. 33 * ;]
anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: Ac 27:16, 30, 32.†

strong.def: through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 σκέλος, -ους, τό [in LXX for רֶגֶל, etc. ;]
the leg from the hip downwards: Jo 19:31-33 †

strong.def: perhaps akin to the base of G4649 (σκοπός) through the idea of noticeableness); clothing

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σκέπασμα, -τος, τό (< σκεπάζω, to cover),
a covering, esp. clothing: I Ti 6:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σκευᾶς, -ᾶ
Sceva: Ac 19:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: III Mac 5:45 R * ;]
equipment, tackle: Ac 27:19.†

strong.def: the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σκηνοπηγία, -ας, ἡ (< σκηνή, πήγνυηι), [in LXX for סֻכּוֺת, De 16:16 31:10, Za 14:16, 18, 19; I Es 5:51, I Mac 10:21, II Mac 1:9, 18 * ;]
prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, Le 23:34, al.; v. Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: Jo 7:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σκηνοποιός, -όν (< σκηνή, ποιέω),
making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: Ac 18:3.†

strong.def: a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** σκῆνος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Wi 9:15 * ;]
= σκηνή,
a tent, tabernacle (C.I., 3071). Metaph., of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: II Co 5:1, 4.†

strong.def: to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 σκηνόω, -ῶ (< σκηνή), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכֵן ;]
to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, v. MM, Exp., xxii): seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Re 7:15; seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., Jo 1:14; id. c. dat. loc., Re 12:12 13:6; seq. μετά, c. gen. pers., Re 21:3 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).†

strong.def: an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 σκήνωμα, -τος, τό (< σκηνόω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל ;]
a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling (Ps 131 (132):5, al.), Ac 7:46. Metaph., of the body: II Pe 1:13, 14.†

strong.def: dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 σκληρός, -ά, -όν (< σκέλλω, to dry), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה ;]
hard to the touch, rough, harsh, (opp. to μαλακός); metaph., in various uses;
(a). of men, hard, stern, severe: Mt 25:24;
(b). of things, hard, rough, violent: σκληρόν σοι (ἐστι), Ac 26:14; λόγος, Jo 6:60; ἄνεμος, Ja 3:4; σκληρὰ λαλεῖν, Ju 15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ (< σκληρός), [in LXX: De 9:27 (קְשִׁי), etc. ;]
hardness; metaph., of stubbornness: Ro 2:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † σκληρο-τράχηλος, -ον (σκληρός, τράχηλος), [in LXX: Ex 33:3, 5 (עֹרֶף ־קָשֶׁה), etc. ;]
stiff-necked: metaph., Ac 7:51.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 σκληρύνω (< σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קשׁה hi., also for חזק ;]
to harden. Metaph., to harden, make stubborn: c. acc. pers., Ro 9:18; τ. καρδίας (Ps 94 (95):8), He 3:8, 15 4:7. Pass., to become hardened: Ac 19:9, He 3:13.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from the base of G4628 (σκέλος) and G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);
strong.def: withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ [in LXX: Nu 33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Ho 2:6 (8) (סִיר), Ez 28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Si 43:19 * ;]
anything pointed, esp.
1. in cl., a stake
2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. c.): σ. τῇ σαρκί, II Co 12:7 (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).†

strong.def: perhaps akin to G4626 (σκάπτω) through the idea of concealment; compare G4629 (σκέπασμα)); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for צֹפֶה ;]
1. a watcher, watchman (Ez 3:17, al.).
2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wi 5:12, 21, al.). Metaph., of an aim or object: Phl 3:14.†

strong.def: to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 σκοτόω, -ῶ (< σκότος), [in LXX for חשׁךְ, קדר, שׁחר ;]
to darken: Re 9:2 16:10. Metaph., of the mind : pass., Eph 4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1519 (εἰς) and G2965 (κύων) and G906 (βάλλω);
strong.def: what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† σκύβαλον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Si 27:4 * ;]
refuse, esp. dung (v. MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Phl 3:8.†

strong.def: a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ
Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Col 3:11.†

strong.derivation: from G4663 (σκώληξ) and a derivative of G977 (βιβρώσκω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον (< σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω),
eaten of worms: Ac 12:23 (cf. II Mac 9:9, and v. MM, xxiii) †

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σμαράγδινος (< σμάραγδος, q.v.),
1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11).
2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Re 4:3 (for the construction, v. Swete, in l.; Zorell, s.v.).†

strong.def: the emerald or green gem so called

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ (and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Ex 28:9 (שֹׁהַם) 36:17 (39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Ez 28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;]
emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, s.v.; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Re 21:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σμύρνα (in some MSS, ζμ-; v. Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מוֹר מֹר ;]
myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Mt 2:11, Jo 19:39.†

strong.def: Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Re 1:11 2:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σμυρναῖος, -α, -ον
of Smyrna: Re 2:8, Rec.†

strong.def: to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σοφίζω (< σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חכם ;]
to make wise, instruct: c. acc. pers., II Ti 3:15 (cf. Ps 18 (19):8 (Ps 118 (119):98). As depon., -ομαι;
(a). intrans., to become wise (III Ki 4:27 ( 5:11)), Ec 2:15, and freq. in Si 7:5, al.);
(b). trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., II Pe 1:16 (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σπανία, -ας, ἡ (= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (I Mac 8:3) or Σ. as here),
Spain: Ro 15:24, 28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † σπαταλάω, -ῶ (< σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Si 27:13 *), [in LXX: Ez 16:49 (שׁקט hi.), Si 21:15 * ;]
to live riotously: I Ti 5:6, Ja 5:5 (Polyb.).†

strong.def: to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) σπένδω [in LXX chiefly for נסך hi. ;]
to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., fig., σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): Phl 2:17 (v. Lft., in l.), II Ti 4:6 (for exx. from π., v. Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).†

strong.def: a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σπερμολόγος, -ον (< σπέρμα, λέγω)
a seed picker;
(a). prop., of birds (Arist., Aristoph, al.);
(b). in Attic slang, of an idler who lives on scraps picked up in the agora; hence, as subst., ὁ σ., an idle babbler: Ac 17:18.†

strong.def: a ledge or reef of rock in the sea

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ (on the gender in Ju, l.c., v. Mayor, Ju., 41),
1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaph., of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but v. infr.).
2. In late writers = σπίλος (q.v.), a spot, stain; metaph., Ju, l.c., R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but v. supr.).†

strong.def: to stain or soil (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† σπιλόω [in LXX: Wi 15:4 * ;]
to stain, spot, defile: c. acc., Ja 3:6, Ju 23.†

strong.def: a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ
1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.).
2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaph.,
(a). of moral blemish: Eph 5:27
(b). of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l.): II Pe 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< σπείρω), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:29 (זרע), I Mac 10:30 * ;]
1. a sowing.
2. seedtime.
3. seed sown (of human offspring, Soph., Tr., 316, 420): I Pe 1:23
(cf. σπέρμα, and v. Milligan, NTD, 105 f.).†

strong.def: to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest
strong.kjv: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 σπουδάζω (< σπουδή), [in LXX chiefly for בּהלni.;]
to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: c. inf. (v. M, Pr., 205 f.), Ga 2:10, Eph 4:3, I Th 2:17, II Ti 2:15 4:9, 21, Tit 3:12, He 4:11, II Pe 1:10 3:14; c. acc. et inf. (on this construction v. Mayor in l.; MM, xxiii), II Pe 1:15 (for other constructions v. LS, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον (< σπουδή), [in LXX: Ez 41:25 * ;]
in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: seq. ἐν, II Co 8:22; compar., -οτεροσς ib. 17 (here in superl. sense, v. Bl., § 44, 3) 22.†

strong.def: more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise

strong.derivation: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as stationary);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 στάμνος, -ου (ὁ and), ἡ [in LXX: Ex 16:33 (צִנְצֶנֶת), III Ki 12:24 14:3 (בַּקְבֻּק), Da LXX Bel 32 * ;]
prop., an earthen jar for racking off wine, hence, generally, a jar: He 9:4.†

strong.def: a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 στατήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ [in Aq., Sm., for שֶׁקֶל ;]
a stater;
(a). a weight;
(b). a coin (used by late writers of the Greek τετράδραχμον): Mt 17:27 26:16, WH, mg.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Στάχυς, -υος, ὁ
Stachys: Ro 16:9 (v. Lft., Phl., 174; MM, xxiii).†

strong.def: to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** στέγω (cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Si 8:17 * ;]
1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.).
2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Si, l.c., Polyb., al.): I Co 13:7, R, mg.
3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., v., Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): I Co 9:12 13:7, I Th 3:1, 5.†

strong.derivation: probably strengthened from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι);
strong.def: properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 στέλλω [in LXX (mid.): Ma 2:5 (חתת ni.), Pr 31:24 (26), Wi 7:14 14:1, II Mac 5:1, III Mac 1:19 4:11 * ;]
1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wi, II Mac, ll. c.).
2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: II Co 8:20; seq. ἀπό, II Th 3:6
(cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * στέμμα, -τος, τό (< στέφω, to put around, enwreath)
a wreath, garland: as used in sacrifices, Ac 14:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 στεναγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< στενάζω), [in LXX for אֲנָחָה, אֲנָקָה, נְאָקָה, etc. ;]
a groaning: Ac 7:34 (LXX κραυγή), Ro 8:26.†

strong.def: to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ (< στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: Jos 17:15 (אוּץ), Jg 16:16 (אלץ pi.), Is 28:19 (20) (קצר) Is 49:19 (צרר), IV Mac 11:11 * ;]
1. to be straitened (cf. Is 49:19); metaph., to be anxious (Hipp., al.).
2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., II Co 4:8 6:12.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4728 (στενός) and G5561 (χώρα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (v. supr.) [in LXX for צוּקָה, etc. ;]
narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaph. (Xen., Polyb., De 28:53, Wi 5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Ro 2:9 8:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), II Co 6:4 12:10.†

strong.def: stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 στερεός, -ά, -όν [in LXX: Nu 8:4 (מִקְשָׁה); σ. πέτρα, Is 5:28 (צַר), etc. ;]
hard, firm, solid: τροψή, He 5:12, 14; θεμέλιος, fig., II Ti 2:19. Metaph.,
(a). in bad sense, hard, cruel (Hom., al.);
(b). in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει, I Pe 5:9.†

strong.def: to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 στερεόω, -ῶ (< στερεός), [in LXX: Is 42:5 (רקע), Je 5:3 (חזק pi.), etc. ;]
(a). to make firm or solid;
(b). to strengthen, make strong; c. acc. pers., Ac 3:16; τ. βάσεις, pass., ib. 7. Metaph. (cf. Je, l.c.): τ. πίστει, pass., Ac 16:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 στερέωμα, -τος, τό (< στερεόω), [in LXX: Ge 1:6 ff., Ps 18 (19):1 150:1, Ez 1:22-26 10:1 13:5, Da LXX, TH 3:(56), 12:3 (רָקִיעַ), De 33:26 (שׁחק), Ps 17 (18):2 70 (71):3 (סֶלַע), Es 9:29, I Es 8:78 (82), Si 43:1, 8, I Mac 9:14 * ;]
a solid body;
(a). a support, foundation (Arist., al.); metaph., strength (Ps 17 70, I Mac, ll. c.); steadfastness, firmness: τ. πίστεως, Col 2:5;
(b). the dome of heaven (believed to be a solid canopy), the firmament (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Στεφανᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ
Stephanas: I Co 1:16 16:15, 17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 Στέφανος, -ου, ὁ
Stephen: Ac 6:5, 8, 9 7:59 8:2 11:19 22:20.†

strong.def: to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 στεφανόω, -ῶ (< στέφανος), [in LXX for עטר ;]
c. acc. pers.,
to crown: of a victor, II Ti 2:5. Metaph., δόξῃ κ. τιμῇ, He 2:7, 9 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Is 3:1 * ;]
1. a setting firmly, supporting.
2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: II Pe 3:17.†

strong.def: a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 στίγμα, -τος, τό (< στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Ca 1:11 (נְקֻדָּה) * ;]
a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Ga 6:17 (v. Lft., in l.; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX: Ez 40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;]
a portico: Jo 5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jo 10:23, Ac 3:11 5:12 †

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4748 (στοιχέω);
strong.def: something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Wi 7:17 19:18, IV Mac 12:13 * ;]
prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence,
1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.).
2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.).
3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) He 5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Ga 4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, ib. 3, Col 2:8, 20 (but v. infr.).
4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. c.): II Pe 3:10, 12.
5. The heavenly bodies (Diog. Laert.).
6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. c., v. ICC on Col 2:8; Enc. Bibl., s.v. " Elements ").†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of (to range in regular line);
strong.def: to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 στοιχέω, -ῶ (< στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ec 11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;]
to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaph., in late writers, to walk by rule: Ac 21:24; c. dat., to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Ro 4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Ga 5:25 6:16, Phl 3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * στόμαχος, -ου, ὁ (< στόμα),
prop., a mouth, an opening;
(a). in early Gk. writers, the throat;
(b). of the opening of the stomach (Arist.);
(c). in later writers (Plut., al.), the stomach: I Ti 5:23.†

strong.def: military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 στρατεία (on the orthogr., v. Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ (< στρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]
an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaph., II Co 10:4 (-τιά, T), I Ti 1:18.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense);
strong.def: to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† στρατολογέω, -ῶ (< στρατός, λέγω),
to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: II Ti 2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).†

strong.def: to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 στρεβλόω, -ῶ (< στρέφω), [in LXX: II Ki 22:27 (פּתל hithp.), III Mac 4:14, IV Mac 9:17 12:4, 11 15:14 * ;]
to twist, torture. Metaph. (cf. II Ki, l.c.), to twist or pervert language: II Pe 3:16.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G4764 (στρῆνος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** στρηνιάω, -ῶ (< στρῆνος, q.v.), [in Sm.: Is 61:6 (אכל) * ;]
a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Re 18:7, 9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 στρῆνος, -ους, τό (cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;]
insolent luxury, wantonness: Re 18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, v. Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary (to hate);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * στυγητός, -όν (< στυγέω, to hate),
hated, hateful: Tit 3:3.†

strong.def: properly akin to the base of G2476 (ἵστημι)); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 στύλος (T, στῦλος, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for עַמּוּד, also for קֶרֶשׁ, etc. ;]
a pillar, regarded especially as a support: σ. πυρός, Re 10:1; σ. ἐν τ. ναῷ, fig., Re 3:12, Metaph., Ga 2:9; τ. ἀληθείας, I Ti 3:15.†

strong.def: a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) Στωικός (Rec. -ϊκός, T, Στοϊκός), -ή, -όν,
Stoic: Ac 17:18.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G1097 (γινώσκω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ (< συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), [in LXX: Si prol.14 (B1א1 om.) 313, Mac 14:20* ;]
1. confession.
2. fellow feeling; hence, concession, allowance: I Co 7:6 (v. ICC, in l.).
3. pardon.†

strong.def: to suffer hardship in company with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† συν-κακοπαθέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ,
to bear evil treatment along with, take one's share of ill-treatment: II Ti 2:3; c. dat. commod., τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, ib. 1:18.†

strong.def: to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-κακουχέομαι (Rec. συγκ-), -οῦμαι, pass.
to endure adversity with: c. dat. pers., He 11:25. Not elsewhere.†

strong.def: to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-κάμπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Ps 68:10, 23(מעדhi.), etc. ;]
to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, fig., Ro 11:10 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-κατα-βαίνω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Ps 48 (49):17 (ירד), Wi 10:13, Da LXX TH 3:49 * ;]
to go down with: Ac 25:5. In late writers also metaph. (Wis, l.c.), to condescend, on wh. v. Rutherford, NPhr., 485 f.†

strong.def: a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-κατά-θεσις (Rec συγκ-), -εως, ἡ (< συνκατατίθημι)
concord, agreement: II Co 6:16 (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G5585 (ψηφίζω);
strong.def: to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-κατα-ψηφίζω (Rec. συγκ-),
1. to condemn with or together (Plut., Themist., 21).
2. to vote one a place among: pass., Ac 1:26. Not elsewhere .†

strong.def: to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-κεράννυμι (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Da LXX 2:43 (עֲרַב ithpa.), II Mac 15:39 * ;]
to mix or blend together, compound: c. acc., I Co 12:24; ptcp. pf. pass., He 4:2, T, WH, mg., R, mg.; id., of persons, c. dat. instr., to be united with, agree with, ib., WH, txt., R, txt. (v. Westc., in l.).†

strong.def: to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-κινέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ,
to move together. Metaph., to excite, stir up: τ. λαόν, Ac 6:12 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†

strong.def: a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† συν-κληρο-νόμος (Rec. συγκ-), -ου, ὁ
a co-inheritor, fellow-heir: Ro 8:17, Eph 3:6; c. gen. rei, He 11:9, I Pe 3:7 (for exx., v. Deiss., LAE, 88 f.).†

strong.def: to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in
strong.kjv: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * συν-κοινωνέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ,
to have fellowship with or in (in cl., c. gen. rei, dat. pers.): c. dat. rei, Eph 5:11, Re 18:4; id. c. gen. pers., Phl 4:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† συν-κοινωνός (Rec. συγκ-), όν,
partaking jointly of: c. gen. rei, Ro 11:17, I Co 9:23; id. c. gen. pers., Phl 1:7; seq. ἐν, Re 1:9.†

strong.def: to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-κομίζω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Jb 5:26 (עלה) * ;]
1. to bring together, collect (Hdt., Xen., al.).
2. to take up a body for burial (Soph., Aj., 1048): Ac 8:2 (v. Field, Notes, 116).†

strong.def: to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 συν-κρίνω (Rec. συγκ-) [in LXX chiefly for פּתר ;]
1. to compound, combine: I Co 2:13, R, mg.1 (Lft., Notes, 180 f.).
2. In Arist. and later writers (Wi 7:29, al.) = παραβάλλω, to compare: I Co, l.c., R, txt. (Field, Notes, 168), II Co 10:12
3. In LXX, of dreams, to interpret (Ge 40:8, I Co, l.c., R, mg.2 (but v. reff. supr.).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and (to pour) or its alternate;
strong.def: to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind)
strong.kjv: confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 συν-χέω (Rec. συγ-), [in LXX for בּלל, רגז, etc. ;]
to pour together, commingle, confuse; metaph., confound, throw into confusion, stir up trouble: Ac 21:27 (cf. συν-χύννω).†

strong.def: to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† συν-χράομαι (Rec. συγ-), -ῶμαι, [in Al.: I Ki 30:19 * ;]
to use together with. Metaph., c. dat. pers., to associate with: Jo 4:9 (Polyb., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σύγχυσις, -εως, ἡ (< συγχέω), [in LXX: Ge 11:9 (בָּבֶל), I Ki 5:6, 12 (11) 14:20 (מְהוּמָה) * ;]
confusion: of a popular uproar, Ac 19:29.†

strong.def: to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * συν-ζάω (Rec. συζ-),
to live with: opp. to συναποθανεῖν, II Co 7:3; of life in union with Christ, here and hereafter, Ro 6:8, II Ti 2:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-ζητητής (Rec. συζ-), -οῦ, ἁ (< συνζητέω),
a disputer, disputant: I Co 1:20.†

strong.def: co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** σύν-ζυγος (Rec. ουζ-), or as WH, mg., Σύνζυγος, -ον (< συνζεύγνυμι), [in Aq., Ez 23:21 * ;]
a yoke fellow. Prob., as proper name, Σ. γνήσιε, genuinely Synzygus, S. properly so-called, Phl 4:3 (v. ICC, Lft., in l.; MM, xxiii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† συν-ζωο-ποιέω (Rec. συζ-), ῶ-,
to make alive or quicken together with; metaph., of the spiritual life: τ. Χριστῷ, Eph 2:5; σὺν τ. Χ., Col 2:13.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G4813 (συλάω) and (the reduplicated form of) G71 (ἄγω);
strong.def: to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συλαγωγέω, -ῶ (< σύλη, booty + ἄγω),
to carry off as spoil, lead captive (θυγατέρα, Heliod., Aeth., 10, 35): metaph., Col 2:8.†

strong.def: probably akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι); compare G4661 (σκῦλον)); to despoil

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συλάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ep. Je 1:18 * ;]
c. acc. pers., to strip, plunder, spoil: II Co 11:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συμ-βουλεύω [in LXX chiefly for יעץ ;]
1. to advise, counsel: c. dat. pers., Jo 18:14; id. seq. inf., Re 3:18.
2. Mid., to take counsel, consult: seq. ἵνα, Mt 26:4 ("reciprocal middle," v. M, Pr., 157); c. inf., Ac 9:23.†

strong.def: causative (by reduplication) of the base of G939 (βάσις)); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach
strong.kjv: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 συν-βιβάζω (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: Ex 4:12, 15, Le 10:11, Jg 13:8, Ps 31 (32):8 (ירה hi.); Ex 18:16, De 4:9, Is 40:13 (ידע hi.), ib. 14 (בּין hi.), Da TH 9:22 (שׂכל hi.) * ;]
1. to join or knit together, unite: Eph 4:16, Col 2:2 (but v. infr.), ib. 19.
2. to compare, consider, conclude (Plat.): Ac 16:10.
3. to deduce, prove, demonstrate (Arist.): Ac 9:22.
4. As in LXX ("translation Greek," = ἐμβιβάζω, metaph.), to teach, instruct: I Co 2:16, Ac 19:33, R, mg. (also in Vg., Col 2:2, instructi, but v. supr.).†

strong.def: to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σύμβουλος, -ου, ὁ (< σύν, βουλή), [in LXX forיוֺעֵץand cogn. forms ;]
a counsellor, adviser: Ro 11:34 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3129 (μανθάνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-μαθητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ
a fellow-disciple: Jo 11:16 (on the use of συν- in such compounds as this, v. Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).†

strong.def: to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * συν-μαρτυρέω (Rec. συμμ-), -ῶ,
to bear witness with: Ro 2:15; c. dat., Ro 8:16; seq. ὅτι, Ro 9:1.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and G3307 (μερίζω);
strong.def: to share jointly, i.e. participate in

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † συν-μερίζω (Rec. συμμ-), [in LXX: Pr 29:24 א2 (חלק) * ;]
to distri­bute in shares. Mid., to have a share in: I Co 9:13 (Diod., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * συν-μέτοχος (Rec. συμμ-), -ον,
partaking together with; as subst., ὁ σ., a joint partaker (c. dat. pers. et gen. rei, FlJ, BJ, i, 24, 6): c. gen. rei, Eph 3:6; c. gen. pers., ib. 5:7 (Arist.).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3401 (μιμέομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-μιμητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ
a fellow-imitator: c. gen. obj., Phl 3:17 (v. ICC, in l.). Not elsewhere.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† σύμ-μορφος, -ον (< σύν, μορφή),
1. absol., similar (Luc.).
2. con­formed to: c. dat., Phl 3:21; c. gen., Ro 8:29 (v. B1., § 36, 11; 37, 6).†

strong.def: to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) συμ-μορφόω, -ῶ
Rec. for -ίζω (q.v.), Phl 3:10.†

strong.def: to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate
strong.kjv: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** συν-παθέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: IV Mac 5:25 AR 13:23 * ;]
to have a fellow feeling for or with, sympathize with or in: c. dat. rei, He 4:15; dat. pers., ib. 10:34 (Arist., Plut., al.).†

strong.def: having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συμπαθής, -ές (< σύν, πάσχω) [in LXX: Jb 29:25 A (אֹבֵל), IV Mac 5:25א, 13:23 15:4 * ;]
1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: I Pe 3:8.
2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.c.; Dion. H.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-παρα-καλέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ,
to call upon or exhort together (Plat.). Pass., to be strengthened or comforted with and among: Ro 1:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 συν-παρα-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Ge 19:17 (ספה ni.), Jb 1:4 (שׁלח), III Mac 1:1 * ;]
to take along with: as a companion, c. acc., Ac 12:25 15:37, 38 (on the tenses, v. M, Pr., 130), Ga 2:1.†

strong.def: to be at hand together, i.e. now present

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-πάρειμι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX: To 12:12 ΑΒ, Pr 8:27 (?), Wi 9:10 * ;]
to be present together or with: c. dat. pers., Ac 25:24.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and G3958 (πάσχω) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** συν-πάσχω (Rec. συμπ-), [in Al.: I Ki 22:8 * ;]
1. to suffer together or with: Ro 8:17, I Co 12:26.
2. to sympathize with (Plat., Arist.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * συν-πέμπω (Rec. συμπ-)
to send together with: c. acc. et dat., II Co 8:22; id. seq. μετά, c. gen., ib. 18.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G4012 (περί) and G2983 (λαμβάνω);
strong.def: to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-περι-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-),
1. to enclose (Ez 5:3 (צוּר) *).
2. to embrace: c. acc. pers., Ac 20:10.†

strong.def: to partake a beverage in company

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συμπόσιον, -ου, τό (< συμπίνω), [in LXX: Es 7:7 (מִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן) 4:17, I Mac 16:16, II Mac 2:27, III Mac 4:16 5:36 6:33; σ. οἴνου, Sir 34 (31):31 35 (32):5, 49:1 * ;]
1. a drinking party
2. By meton., of the party itself, the guests (Plut); pl., σ. σ. (colloq.; v. M, Pr., 97), in parties or companies: Mk 6:39.†

strong.def: a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-πολίτης (Rec. σνμπ-), -ου, ὁ
a fellow-citizen: pl., σ. τ. ἁγίων, opp. to ξένοι κ. πάροικοι, Eph 2:19 (Eur.; C.I., 6446; condemned by Atticists; v. Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-πρεσβύτερος (Rec. συμπ-), -ου, ὁ
a fellow-elder: I Pe 5:1 (Eccl.).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage
strong.kjv: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 συμ-φέρω [in LXX: Je 33 (26):14 (טוֹב), Pr 19:10 (נָאוֶה), Si 30:19, al. ;]
1. trans. to bring together: c. acc. rei, Ac 19:19.
2. Intrans., and mostly impers., συμφέρει, it is expedient, profitable or an advantage: I Co 6:12 10:23, II Co 8:10; c. inf. (M, Pr., 210), Mt 19:10, Jo 18:14; c. dat., seq. ἵνα (Bl., § 69, 5), Mt 5:29, 30 18:6, Jo 11:50 16:7. Ptcp., ςυμφέρων, profitable: I Co 12:7; pl., Ac 20:20; (οὐ σ. sc. ἐστιν; = οὐ συμφέρει; cf. Thuc., iii, 44, 2), II Co 12:1; as subst., τὸ σ., profit, He 12:10.†

strong.def: to say jointly, i.e. assent to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σύν-φημι (Rec. συμ-),
to consent, confess: c. dat., seq. ὅτι, Ro 7:16.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G5443 (φυλή);
strong.def: a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συμ-φυλέτης, -ου, ὁ (< σύν, φυλή; cf. σύμφυλος, Aq.: Za 13:7; and v. Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.)
a fellow-tribesman, fellow-countryman: I Th 2:14 (v. M, Th., in l., and Intr. liii). Not found elsewhere.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω);
strong.def: grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σύμ-φυτος, -ον (< συμφύω, to make to grow together) [in LXX: Za 11:2 (בּצר), Es 7:7, 8א2, Am 9:13, III Mac 3:22 * ;]
1. congenital, innate (Plat., al.; III Mac, l.c.).
2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ (v. Field, Notes, 155 f.), Ro 6:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συμ-φώνησις, -εως, ἡ (< συμφωνέω),
concord, agreement: seq. πρός, c. acc. pers., II Co 6:15.†

strong.def: sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σύμφωνος, -ον (< σύν, φωνή), [in LXX: Ec 7:15 (14) (לְעֻמַּת), IV Mac 7:7 14:7 * ;]
agreeing in sound. Metaph., harmonious, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου (for exx. from π., v. Deiss., BS, 255), by agreement, I Co 7:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συμ-ψηφίζω [in LXX: Je 29 (49):20 A * ;]
to reckon together, count up: Ac 19:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σύν-ψυχος (Rec. συμ-), -ον (< ψυχή),
of one mind: Phl 2:2.†

strong.def: to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-αγωνίζομαι
to strive together with, to help (prop., of sharing in a contest): c. dat. pers. et rei, Ro 15:30.†

strong.def: to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * συν-αθλέω, -ῶ
= συναγωνίζομαι: c. dat. commod., Phl 1:27; c. dat. pers., seq. ἐν, Phl 4:3.†

strong.def: to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 συν-αίρω [in LXX: Ex 23:5 (עזב) * ;]
to take up together: σ. λόγον (of which there are several exx. in π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 118 f.; MM, i, xxiv; M, Pr., 160), to settle accounts, Mt 18:23, 24; seq. μετά, C. gen. pers., Mt 25:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† συν-αιχμάλωτος, -ου, ὁ
a fellow prisoner (prop., of a captive in war, v. Lft., Col., 234): Ro 16:7, Col 4:10, Phm 23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συν-αλίζω [in Al.: Ps 140 (141):4 * ;]
to assemble with: Ac 1:4 (EV, mg., eating with, but on this rendering and on the force of the pres. ptcp. here, v. Field, Notes, 110).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G303 (ἀνά) and G3396 (μίγνυμι);
strong.def: to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * συν-ανα-μίγνυμι (acc to Bl., 8, -μείγνυμι), [in LXX: Ho 7:8 A (בּלל hithpo.), Ez 20:18 A * ;]
to mix up together; pass., reflex, and metaph., to associate with (Plut., Ath., al.): I Co 5:9, 11, II Th 3:14 (v. M, Th., 117).†

strong.def: to recruit oneself in company with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-ανα-παύομαι [in LXX: Is 11:6 (רבץ) * ;]
c. dat. pers., to lie down to rest with, sleep with. Metaph., to be refreshed in spirit with: Ro 15:32 (L, om.).†

strong.def: to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 συν-απ-άγω [in LXX: Ex 14:6 (לקח) * ;]
to lead away with or together (Ex, l.c.). Pass., metaph. (as συμπεριφέρομαι, v. LS, s.v.), to be carried away with: c. dat., Ga 2:13, II Pe 3:17; of accommodating one­self to (EV, condescend to) things or persons (on the meaning, v. ICC, in l.; Field, Notes, 163), Ro 12:16.†

strong.def: to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-απ-όλλυμι [in LXX chiefly forספה;]
to destroy with or together. Pass., to perish together (with): c. dat. pers., He 11:31.†

strong.def: to despatch (on an errand) in company with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-απο-στέλλω [in LXX: Ex 33:2, 12 (שׁלח), I Es 5:2 * ;]
to send along with: c. acc., II Co 12:18 (cf. MM, xxiv).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of G719 (ἁρμός) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense of laying);
strong.def: to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† συν-αρμολογέω, -ῶ (< ἁρμός, λέγω), = cl. συναρμόζω,
to fit or frame together: of the parts of a building, Eph 2:21; of the members of the body, Eph 4:16 (Eccl.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συν-αυξάνω [in LXX: II Mac 4:4, IV Mac 13:27 * ;]
to cause to increase or grow together. Pass., to grow together: Mt 13:30 (Xen., al.).†

strong.def: a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 σύν-δεσμος, -ου, ὁ (< συνδέω), [in LXX for קשׁר, קטר, etc. ;]
that which binds together, a bond: of the ligaments of the body, Col 2:19. Metaph., σ. ἀδικίας, Ac 8:23; τ. τελειότητος, Col 3:14; τ. εἰρήνης, Eph 4:3 (v. Lft., Col., ll. c.).†

strong.def: to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-δέω [in LXX for שׁבץ, etc. ;]
(a). to bind together;
(b). to bind together with: pass., He 13:3.†

strong.def: to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-δοξάζω
1. to join in approving (Arist.).
2. In NT only, to glorify together: pass., Ro 8:17.†

strong.def: a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 σύν-δουλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Es 4:7, 9, 17, 23 5:3, 6 6:6, 13 (כְּנָת) * ;]
a fellow-servant: Mt 18:28-33 24:49; of servants of the same divine Lord, Col 1:7 4:7, Re 6:11; so of angels, Re 19:10 22:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συνδρομή, -ῆς, ἡ (< συντρέχω), [in LXX: Jth 10:18, III Mac 3:8 * ;]
a concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering: Ac 21:30 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†

strong.def: to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 συν-εγείρω [in LXX: Ex 23:5 B2 (עזב), Is 14:9 (עוּר pil.), IV Mac 2:14 * ;]
to raise together: metaph., of the Christian's mystical resur­rection with Christ, Eph 2:6; pass., Col 2:12 3:1.†

strong.derivation: from a prolonged form of G4894 (συνείδω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
30 συν-είδησις, -εως, ἡ (< συνεῖδον), [in LXX: Ec 10:20 (מַדָּע), Wi 17:11, Si 42:18 א * ;]
1. consciousness: c. gen. obj., He 10:2, I Pe 2:19.
2. In ethical sense, innate discernment, self-judging consciousness, conscience (Stoics and late writers): Ro 2:15 9:1, I Co 10:29, II Co 1:12 4:2 5:11, I Ti 4:2, He 9:14; σ. ἀγαθή, Ac 23:1, I Ti 1:5, 19, I Pe 3:16, 21; ἀσθενής, I Co 8:7, 10; ἀσθενοῦσα, ib. 12; ἀπρόσκοπος, Ac 24:16; καθαρά, I Ti 3:9, II Ti 1:3; καλή, He 13:18; πονηρά, He 10:22; ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ σ., Tit 1:15; διὰ τὴν σ., Ro 13:5, I Co 10:25, 27, 28; κατὰ σ., He 9:9; ὑπὸ (τῆς) σ., Jo 8:[9] (Rec.), I Co 10:29 (cf. Cremer, 233 ff.; ICC on Ro 2:15; DB, i, 468 ff.).†

strong.def: to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of
strong.kjv: consider, know, be privy, be ware of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** συν-εῖδον irreg. aor. of συνοράω (v.s. εἶδον), [in LXX: I Mac 4:21א, II Mac 2:24 4:4, 41 R 5:17 7:4, 20 8:8, III Mac 2:8 A * ;]
1. to see together or at the same time (Arist., Xen.).
2. to see in one view, hence, of mental vision, to comprehend, understand (LXX, Polyb., Plut., al.) : Ac 12:12 14:6 (on the related σύνοιδα, v. s.v.).†

strong.kjv: go in with, go with into

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-εισ-έρχομαι [in LXX: Jb 22:4 (עִם בּוֹא), etc. ;]
to enter together: c. dat. pers., seq. εἰς, c. acc. loc., Jo 6:22 18:15.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G1553 (ἐκδημέω);
strong.def: a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† συν-έκδημος, -ου, ὁ (< ἔκδημος, abroad),
a fellow-traveller: Ac 19:29, II Co 8:19.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G1586 (ἐκλέγομαι);
strong.def: chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-εκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν
chosen together with, co-elect: ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτή (on the meaning, v. ICC, in l.), I Pe 5:13.†

strong.def: to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ** συν-ελαύνω [in LXX: II Mac 4:26, 42 5:5 * ;]
to drive together, force together: εἰς εἰρήνην, Ac 7:26, Rec. (WH, RV, συνήλλασσεν).†

strong.def: to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-επι-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ
to join in attesting, bear witness together with: He 2:4 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and a primary (to follow);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συν-έπομαι [in LXX: II Mac 15:2, III Mac 5:48 R 6:21 * ;]
to follow with, accompany: c. dat. pers., Ac 20:4.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);
strong.kjv: companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
