classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 ** συνεργός, -όν [in LXX: II Mac 8:7 14:5 * ;]
a fellow-worker: c. gen. pers., Ro 16:3, 9, 21, Phl 2:25 4:3, I Th 3:2, Rec., Phm 1, 24; θεοῦ (cf. Lft., Notes, 41, 188), I Co 3:9 (pl.), I Th 3:2 [WH] R, mg. (R, txt., διάκονον τοῦ θ.; on the original reading, v. ICC, in l.); τ. χαρᾶς ὑηῶν, II Co 1:24; τ. ἀληθείᾳ, III Jo 8; seq. εἰς, II Co 8:23, Col 4:11.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a presumed compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast);
strong.def: to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * συν-ευωχέω, -ῶ
to entertain together. Pass., to fare sumptuously or feast together or with: Ju 12; c. dat. pers., II Pe 2:13 (Arist., Luc., al.).†

strong.def: to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-εφ-ίστημι
to place over. Pass.,
1. to stand over (Thuc.).
2. to rise together: seq. κατά, c. gen. pers. (against), Ac 16:22.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);
strong.def: to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-ήδομαι
to rejoice together; c. dat., to rejoice with or in: τ. νόμῳ τ. θεοῦ, Ro 7:22 (v. Lft., Notes, 304).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G2239 (ἦθος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** συνήθεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἦθος), [in LXX: IV Mac 2:12 6:13 13:22, 27 * ;]
1. intimacy.
2. habit, custom: Jo 18:39, I Co 11:16; c. gen. obj. (cf. Æschin., 23, 37, and v. MM, xxiv), habitual use, force of habit with respect to, I Co 8:7.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G2244 (ἡλικία);
strong.def: a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-ηλικιώτης (< ἡλικία), = συνῆλιζ (Æsch.),
one of the same age, an equal in age: Ga 1:14.†

strong.def: to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * συν-θάπτω
to bury together with: in symbolical sense, of baptism, αὐτῷ (with Christ), Ro 6:4, Col 2:12.†

strong.def: to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-θρύπτω
to break in pieces, crush: metaph., τ. καρδίαν, Ac 21:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † συν-οδεύω [in LXX: Za 8:21 א1 (הלך), To 5:16א, Wi 6:23 * ;]
to journey with: c. dat. pers., Ac 9:7 (Plut., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-οικέω, -ῶ [in LXX for בּעל etc. ;]
to dwell together: of man and wife (Hdt., al.), c. dat. pers., I Pe 3:7,†

strong.def: to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συν-οικοδομέω, -ῶ [in LXX: I Es 5:68 * ;]
1. to build together or with (c. dat. pers., I Es, l.c.).
2. Of various materials, to build up together (Thuc., al.): metaph., of Christians, Eph 2:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-ομιλέω, -ῶ
to converse with (absol., FlJ, BJ, v, 13, 1; seq. μετά, Cebes, 13): c. dat. pers., Ac 10:27.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of G3725 (ὅριον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-ομορέω, -ῶ
to border on: c. dat., Ac 18:7 (Byz.).†

strong.def: to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 συν-τάσσω [in LXX chiefly for צוה pi. ;]
to prescribe, ordain, arrange: c. dat. pers, Mt 21:6 26:19 27:10 (LXX).†

strong.def: entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 συντέλεια, -ας, ἡ (< συντελέω), [in LXX chiefly for כָּלָה and (in Da) for קֵץ ;]
1. in cl., a joint payment or contribution for public service; hence, generally, joint action (Plat.).
2. In late writers (Polyb., al.), consummation, completion: σ. τ. αἰῶνος, -ων (cf. Da LXX TH 12:13, al.), Mt 13:39, 40, 49 24:3 28:20, He 9:26.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);
strong.def: to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 συν-τέμνω [in LXX chiefly for חרץ ;]
1. to cut in pieces.
2. to cut down, cut short: metaph., λόγον, Ro 9:28 (LXX) (Hdt., Plat., Eur., al.).†

strong.def: concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σύν-τριμμα, -τος, τό (< συντρίβω), [in LXX (Le 21:19, al.) chiefly for שֶׁבֶר; also for שֹׁד (Is 59:7), etc. ;]
a fracture (Arist.; Le, l.c., al.). Metaph., calamity, destruction (Isa, l.c., Wi 3:3, al.): Ro 3:16 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and G5162 (τροφός) (in a passive sense);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σύν-τροφος, -ου, ὁ (< συντρέφομαι, to be brought up together) [in LXX: III Ki 12:24, I Mac 1:6 R, II Mac 9:29 * ;]
1. prop., one nourished or brought up with, a foster-brother: Ac 13:1 EV.
2. In Hellenistic usage, as a court term, an intimate friend of a king (v. Deiss., BS, 305, 310 f.): Ac 13:1 (cf. also MM, xxiv).†

strong.def: an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Συντύχη (T, -τυχή), -ης, ἡ
Syntyche: Phl 4:2.†

strong.def: to act hypocritically in concert with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-υπο-κρίνομαι
to play a part with, dissemble with: c. dat., Ga 2:13 (Polyb.).†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);
strong.def: to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. assist

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-υπουργέω, -ῶ
to help together, join in serving: c. dat. instr., II Co 1:11.†

strong.def: to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-ωδίνω
to be in travail together (Arist.): metaph. (Eur.), Ro 8:22.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3660 (ὀμνύω);
strong.def: a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** συνωμοσία, -ας, ή (συνόμνυμι, to conspire), [in Sm.: Ez 22:25 * ;]
a conspiracy: Ac 23:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Συράκουσαι, -ῶν, αἱ
Syracuse: Ac 28:12.†

strong.def: a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σύρτις (L, σῦρτις), -εως, acc. -ιν, ἡ,
Syrtis, the name of two large sand-banks on the Libyan coast: Ac 27:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 σύρω [in LXX: IV Ki 17:13 (סחב), IV Mac 6:1, al. ;]
to draw, drag: c. acc. rei, Jo 21:8, Re 12:4; c. acc. pers., of taking to trial or punish­ment, Ac 8:3; ἔξω τ. πόλεως, Ac 14:19; ἐπὶ τ. πολιτάρχας (cf. IV Mac, l.c.), Ac 17:6 (cf. κατα-σύρω).†

strong.def: of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σύν-σωμος (Rec. συσσ-), -ον (< σῶμα),
of the same body: Eph 3:6 (Eccl.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συ-στατικός (Tr. συν-), -ή, -όν (< συνίστημι),
1. for putting together, constructive.
2. for bringing together, introductory, commendatory: ἐπιστολή (Arist., Diog. L., al.; and v. MM, xxiv), II Co 3:1.†

strong.def: to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συν-στέλλω (Rec. συσ-), [in LXX: Jg 8:28 11:33 (כּנע ni.), Si 4:31, al. ;]
1. to draw together, contract, shorten: of time, I Co 7:29.
2. to wrap up: of enshrouding a body for burial (Eur.), c. acc., Ac 5:6.†

strong.def: to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * συν-στενάζω (Rec. συσ-),
to groan together or with: Ro 8:22 (c. dat. pers., Eur., Ion., 935).†

strong.def: to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† συν-στοιχέω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ,
to stand in the same rank or line (Polyb). Metaph., to correspond to: Ga 4:25 (v. Lft., in l.).†

strong.def: a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * συν-στρατιώτης (Rec. συσ-), -ου, ὁ
a fellow-soldier (Plat., Xen., al.). Metaph., of fellowship in Christian service: Phl 2:25, Phm 2 .†

strong.def: to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συ-στρέφω [in LXX chiefly for קשׁר ;]
1. to twist together: c. acc. rei, Ac 28:3.
2. Pass., of persons, to gather themselves together: Mt 17:22 (WH, R, mg.).†

strong.def: a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συ-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ (< συστρέφω), [in LXX: Ho 4:19 13:12 (צרר); σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Am 7:10 (קשׁר), etc. ;]
1. a twisting together (Plat.).
2. a concourse, a riotous gathering (Polyb.): Ac 19:40; σ. ποιεῖσθαι (Am, l.c.), to make a compact (RV, banded themselves together): Ac 23:12.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G4976 (σχῆμα);
strong.def: to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively)
strong.kjv: conform to, fashion self according to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * συν-σχηματιζω (Rec. συσ-), (< σχῆμα),
to conform to (Arist.). Pass., to be conformed to, conform oneself to: Ro 12:2, I Pe 1:14.†

strong.def: Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Συχάρ (Ε, Σιχάρ), indecl., ἡ,
Sychar, a town of Samaria: Jo 4:5.†

strong.def: Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Συχέμ indecl. (Heb. שְׁכֶם),
Shechem;
1. the son of Hamor (Ge 33:19): Ac 7:16 b, Rec.
2. A city of Samaria (AV, Sychem; in LXX also sometimes Σίκιμα, -ων, as in FlJ): Ac 7:16 a,b.†

strong.def: butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 σφαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< σφάζω), [in LXX for טֶבַח, הֲרֵגָה, etc. ;]
slaughter: Ac 8:32 (LXX); πρόβατα σφαγῆς, Ro 8:36 (LXX); ἡμέρα σφαγῆς, Ja 5:5.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G4967 (σφαγή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σφάγιον, -ου, τό (< σφαγή), [in LXX: Am 5:25 (זֶבַח), Ez 21:10, 15, 28 (טֶבַח), Le 22:23 (נְדָבָה) * ;]
a victim for slaughter: Ac 7:42 (LXX).†

strong.def: to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 σφάζω [in LXX chiefly for שׁחט ;]
to slay, slaughter (esp. of victims for sacrifice): ἀρνίον, Re 5:6, 12 13:8; of persons, I Jo 3:12, Re 5:9 6:4, 9 18:24; ἐσφαγμένη εἰς θάνατον (RV, smitten unto death), Re 13:3 (cf. κατα-σφάζω).†

strong.derivation: adverb from the same as G4970 (σφόδρα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σφοδρῶς adv.,
exceedingly: Ac 27:18.†

strong.def: to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest
strong.kjv: (set a, set to) seal up, stop

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 σφραγίζω [in LXX chiefly for חתם (De 32:34, al.), also for סתם (Da TH 8:26) ;]
to seal,
(a). for security: Mt 27:66, Re 20:3; τ. καρπὸν τοῦτον, fig. (cf. Deiss., BS, 238 f.; MM, xxiv; DB, iv, 427a), Ro 15:28;
(b). for concealment, hence, metaph., to hide (Da TH 9:24, Jo 14:17): Re 10:4 22:10;
(c). for distinction, Re 7:3-8; metaph., Eph 1:13 4:30; mid., II Co 1:22;
(d). for authentication (Es 8:8): Jo 3:33 6:27 (cf. κατα-σφραγίζω).†

strong.def: a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 σφραγίς, -ῖδος, ἡ [in LXX: Ex 28:11, al. (חֹתָם) 35:22 (חָח), Si 17:22, al. ;]
1. a seal, signet: Re 7:2.
2. The impression of a seal or signet, a seal (on its various purposes, v.s. σφραγίζω): on a book or roll, Re 5:1, 2, 5, 9 6:1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12 8:1; metaph., Ro 4:11, I Co 9:2, II Ti 2:19, Re 9:4.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as (a ball, "sphere";
strong.def: compare the feminine , a hammer); the ankle (as globular)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σφυδρόν, -οῦ, τό
= σφυρόν,
the ankle: Ac 3:7 (v. Bl., § 6, 8).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 (ἔχω) as adverb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** σχέδον adv. (< ἔχω), [in LXX: II Mac 5:2, III Mac 5:14, 45 * ;]
1. of place, near.
2. Of degree, almost, nearly: Ac 13:44 19:26, He 9:22.†

strong.def: a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σχῆμα, -τος, τό (< ἔχω), [in LXX: Is 3:17 (פֹּת) * ;]
figure, fashion: I Co 7:31, Phl 2:8.†

strong.def: of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σχοινίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of σχοῖνος, a rush), [in LXX chiefly for חֶבֶל;]
a rope (prop., one made of rushes): Jo 2:15, Ac 27:32.†

strong.def: to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σχολάζω (< σχολή), [in LXX: Ex 5:8, 17, Ps 45 (46):10 (רפה ni., hi.) * ;]
to be at leisure, hence, to have time or opportunity for, to devote oneself to, be occupied in: I Co 7:5; of things, to be unoccupied, empty (Plut., Eur., al.): οἶκος, Mt 12:44, Lk 11:25 (T [WH], R, om.).†

strong.derivation: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 (ἔχω);
strong.def: properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 σχολή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Ge 33:14 (κατὰ σ., לְאִטִּי), Pr 28:19, Si 38:24 * ;]
1. leisure.
2. Later (from Plato on),
(a). that for which leisure is employed, a disputation, lecture;
(b). the place where lectures are delivered, a school: Ac 19:9 (for the later sense of employment, v. MM, xxiv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * σωματικῶς adv.,
bodily, corporeally: Col 2:9 (v. ICC, Lft., in l.).†

strong.derivation: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and G3962 (πατήρ);
strong.def: of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σώπατρος, -ου, ὁ
Sopater: Ac 20:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 σωρεύω [in LXX: Pr 25:22 (חתה), Jth 15:11 * ;]
(a). to heap on: c. acc. seq. ἐπί c. acc., Ro 12:20 (LXX) (Arist., al.);
(b). to heap with: c. acc. et dat., metaph., ἁμαρτίαις, II Ti 3:6 (overwhelmed with, Field, Notes, 217) (Polyb.).†

strong.derivation: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and that of G4599 (σθενόω);
strong.def: of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Σωσθένης, -ου, ὁ
Sosthenes;
(a). a Jewish ruler: Ac 18:7;
(b). a Christian: I Co 1:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Σωσίπατρος, -ου, ὁ
Sosipater: Ro 16:21.†

strong.def: to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** σωφρονίζω [in Aq.: Is 38:16 * ;]
to make σώφρων, recall one to his senses, control (RV, train): c. acc. pers., Tit 2:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† σωφρονισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< σωφρονίζω),
(a). an admonishing (FlJ, Plut., al.);
(b). self-control, self-discipline: II Ti 1:7 (on the reflexive meaning here, v. Ellic., in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** σωφρόνως adv., [in LXX: Wi 9:11 * ;]
with sound mind, prudently, soberly: Tit 2:12.†

strong.def: soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** σωφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Es 3:13, Wi 8:7, II Mac 4:37, IV Mac 6 * ;]
(a). soundness of mind, good sense, sanity (opp. to μανία, Xen.): Ac 26:25;
(b). self-control, sobriety: I Ti 2:9 (v. Tr., Syn., § xx), ib. 15.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and that of G5424 (φρήν);
strong.def: safe (sound) in mind, i.e. self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** σώφρων, -ον [in LXX: IV Mac 9 * ;]
(a). of sound mind, sane, sensible;
(b). self-controlled, sober-minded: I Ti 3:2, Tit 1:8 2:2, 5 (Arist.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) *† ταβέρνη
(Lat. taberna), v.s. Τρεῖς Ταβέρναι.

strong.def: the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ταβειθά (Rec. Ταβιθά), ἡ (Aram. טַבְיְתָא or טְבִיתָא),
Tabitha: Ac 9:36, 40 (cf. Δορκάς).†

strong.def: something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τάγμα, -τος, τό (< τάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for דֶּגֶל, also for חַיָּה, רַגְלִי ;]
that which has been arranged or placed in order; esp. as military term, a company, troop, division, rank: metaph., I Co 15:23 (v. ICC, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τακτός, -ή, -όν (< τάσσω), [in LXX: Jb 12:5 (שַׁאֲנָן) * ;]
ordered, fixed, stated: ἡμέρα, Ac 12:21,†

strong.def: to be wretched, i.e. realize one's own misery

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ταλαιπωρέω, -ῶ (< ταλαίπωρος), [in LXX Chiefly for שָׁדַד pu. ;]
1. to do hard labour, suffer hardship or distress: Ja 4:9.
2. In cl. occasionally trans., to weary, distress (so Ps 16 (17):9, Is 33:1).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ταλαιπωρία, -ας, ἡ (< ταλαίπωρος) [in LXX chiefly for שֹׁד ;]
1. hard work (Hippocr.).
2. hardship, suffering, distress: Ro 3:16 (LXX) pl., Ja 5:1 (v. B1., § 32, 6; WM, 220; Swete, Mk., 153).
(Hdt., Thuc., al.; and cf. MM, xxiv.)†

strong.derivation: from the base of G5007 (τάλαντον) and a derivative of the base of G3984 (πεῖρα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ταλαίπωρος, -ον [in LXX: Ps 136 (137):8 (שָׁדַד), Is 33:1 (ποιεῖν τ., שָׁדַד), To 13:10, Wi 3:11, al. ;]
distressed, miserable, wretched: Ro 7:24, Re 3:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ταλαντιαῖος, -α, -ον (< τάλαντον),
(a). worth a talent;
(b). of a talent's weight: Re 16:21.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of (to bear;
strong.def: equivalent to G5342 (φέρω)); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent"

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 τάλαντον, -ου, τό [in LXX for כִּכָּר ;]
1. a balance (Hom.).
2. that which is weighed, a talent;
(a). a talent in weight (in Horn. always of gold);
(b). a sum of money, whether gold or silver, equivalent to a talent in weight (v. DB, iii, 418 ff.): Mt 18:24 25:15ff.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5011 (ταπεινός) and the base of G5424 (φρήν);
strong.kjv: humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 *† ταπεινοφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< ταπεινόφρων)
lowliness of mind, humility: Ac 20:19, Eph 4:2, Phl 2:3, Col 3:12, I Pe 5:5; of a false humility, Col 2:18, 23 (rare outside of NT, but found in bad sense in FlJ, BJ, iv, 9, 2; also in Epictet., v. Tr., Syn., § xlii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 τάραχος, -ου, ὁ (< ταράσσω), [in LXX for מְהוּמָה, etc. ;]
later form of ταραχή (Xen., al.; v. Thackeray, Gr., 159): Ac 12:18 19:23.†

strong.def: a Tarsean, i.e. native of Tarsus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ταρσεύς, -έως, ὁ (< Ταρσός),
of Tarsus: Ac 9:11 21:39.†

strong.derivation: perhaps the same as (a flat basket);
strong.def: Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ταρσός, -οῦ
Tarsus, a city of Cilicia: Ac 9:30 11:25 22:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ταρταρόω, -ῶ (< Τάρταρος, a Greek name for the underworld, esp. the abode of the damned),
to cast into hell: II Pe 2:4 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ταῦρος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹר ;]
a bull: Mt 22:4, Ac 14:13, He 9:13 10:4.†

strong.derivation: neuter plural of G3588 (ὁ) and G846 (αὐτός) as adverb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ταφή, -ῆς, ἡ (< θάπτω), [in LXX chiefly for קֶבֶר and cognate forms ;]
burial: Mt 27:7 (Hdt., al.; for other meanings, v. LS, s.v., Deiss., BS, 355 f., MM xxiv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 τάφος, -ου, ὁ (< θάπτω), [in LXX chiefly for קֶבֶר ;]
1. a burial (Hom., al.).
2. a grave, tomb (Hes., Hdt., al.): Mt 23:27, 29 27:61, 64, 66 28:1, Ro 3:13 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: as if neuter plural of G5036 (ταχύς) (adverbially);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** τάχα (< ταχύς), adv., [in LXX: Wi 13:6 14:19 * ;]
(a). (chiefly poët.), quickly, presently;
(b). perhaps: Ro 5:7, Phm 15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ταχινός, -ή, -όν [in LXX: Pr 1:16, Hb 1:6, Is 59:7 (מָהַר), Wi 13:2, Si 11:22 18:26 * ;]
poët. and late for ταχύς, swift: of swift approach, II Pe 1:14 2:1.†

strong.derivation: neuter singular of the comparative of G5036 (ταχύς) (as adverb);
strong.def: more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament

a little child: as a term of endearment, in voc. pl., Jo 13:33, Ga 4:19, I Jo 2:1, 12, 28 3:7, 18 4:4 5:21.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5043 (τέκνον) and the base of G1096 (γίνομαι);
strong.def: to be a child-bearer, i.e. parent (mother)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† τεκνογονέω, -ῶ
to beget or bear children: I Ti 5:14 (Anthol.).†

strong.def: childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * τεκνογονία, -ας, ἡ,
child-bearing: I Ti 2:15 (Arist.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5043 (τέκνον) and G5142 (τρέφω);
strong.def: to be a childrearer, i.e. fulfil the duties of a female parent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:

to rear young (of bees, Arist.),
to bring up children: I Ti 5:10.†

strong.def: complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with G3588 (ὁ)) completeness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 τέλειος, -α, -ον (< τέλος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלֵם, תָּמִים and cogn. forms ;] (There is probably no reference in St. Paul's usage to the use of this term in the ancient mysteries; cf. ICC on Col 1:28; but v. also Lft., in l, and Notes, 173 f.) †
having reached its end, finished, mature, complete, perfect;
1. of persons, primarily of physical development,
(a). full-grown, mature: He 5:14; ethically: Phl 3:15; opp. to νήπιος (-άζειν), I Co 2:6 14:20, Eph 4:13; τ. καὶ πεπληροφορημένοι, Col 4:12; τ. ἐν Χριστῷ, Col 1:28;
(b). complete, perfect (expressing the simple idea of complete goodness, without reference either to maturity or to the philosophical idea of a τέλος; v. Hort on Ja 1:4): Mt 5:48 19:21, Ja 1:4 3:2; of God, Mt 5:48.
2. Of things, complete, perfect: Ro 12:2; ἔργον, Ja 1:4; νόμος, ib. 25; δώρημα, ib. 17; ἀγάπη, I Jo 4:18; τὸ τ., I Co 13:10; compar., τελειοτέρα (σκηνή), He 9:11.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 τελειότης, -ητος, ἡ (< τέλειος), [in LXX: Jg 9:16, 19 (תָּמִים), Pr 11:3 (תֻּמָּה), Wi 6:15 12:17, Je 2:2 * ;]

1. a finishing.

classic.entry:

art, craft, trade: Ac 17:29 18:3, Re 18:22 (WH, R, mg., om.).†

2. esteem, honour: Ro 12:10 13:7, I Co 12:23, I Ti 5:17 6:1, He 5:4, I Pe 2:7 (R, txt., preciousness, cf. Hort, in l), 3:7; τ. διδόναι, I Co 12:24; ἔχειν, Jo 4:44, He 3:3; τ. καὶ δόξα (δ. κ. τ.), Ro 2:7, 10, I Ti 1:17, He 2:7 (LXX), 9, I Pe 1:7, II Pe 1:17, Re 4:9, 11 5:12, 13 7:12 21:26; τ. καὶ κράτος, I Ti 6:16; εἰς τ., Ro 9:21, II Ti 2:20, 21; ἐν τ., Col 2:23; I Th 4:4; by meton., of marks of honour, Ac 28:10.†

wherefore then, so therefore: I Th 4:8, He 12:1 (Hdt., Plat., al.).†

classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † τροπο-φορέω, -ῶ [in LXX: De 1:31 B.l (נָשָׂא) * ;]
1. to bear another's manners (R, txt., suffered he their manners): c. acc pers., Ac 13:18 (Rec., WH, R, txt.; ἐτροφο-, T, R, mg.).
2. = τροφοφορέω (q.v.), (v. Kühner3, I, 276): Ac, l.c.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Τρόφιμος, -ου, ὁ
Trophimus: Ac 20:4 21:29, II Ti 4:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τροφός, -οῦ, ἡ (< τρέφω), [in LXX: Ge 35:8, IV Ki 11:2, II Ch 22:11 Is 49:23 (מֵינֶקֶת) * ;]
a nurse: I Th 2:7.†

strong.def: a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τροχιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< τροχός), [in LXX: Pr 2:15 4:11, 26, 27 5:6, 21 (מַעְגָּל), Ez 27:19 A* ;]
the track of a wheel, hence, a track, path: fig., He 12:13 (LXX) †

strong.def: a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τροχός, -οῦ, τό (< τρέχω), [in LXX chiefly for אוֹפָן ;]
a wheel: Ja 3:6 (v. Mayor, Hort, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Τρύφαινα, -ης, ἡ
Tryphæna: Ro 16:12 (v. Lft., Phl., 175 f.; MM, xxv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τρυφάω, -ῶ (< τρυφή), [in LXX: Ne 9:25 (עָדַן hithp.), Is 66:11 (עָנַג hithp.), Si 14:4 * ;]
to live daintily, luxuriously, to fare sumptuously: Ja 5:5 (cf. ἐν-τρυφάω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Τρυφῶσα, -ης, ἡ, ς, ἡ
Tryphosa: Ro 16:12 (v. Lft., Phl., 175 f.).†

strong.def: the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Τρῳάς (Rec. Τρω-), -άδος, ἡ
Troas, a city near the Hellespont: Ac 16:8, 11 20:5, 6, II Co 2:12, II Ti 4:13.†

strong.derivation: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of G5134 (τραῦμα) and G5147 (τρίβος) through the idea of corrosion or wear;
strong.def: or perhaps rather of a base of G5167 (τρυγών) and G5149 (τρίζω) through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 * τρώγω
1. prop., of animals, to gnaw, munch, crunch (Hom., al.).
2. Of men, to eat raw food, as vegetables, nuts, etc. (Hdt., al.).
3. In late vernacular, simply to eat (= ἐσθίω): Mt 24:38, Jo 6:54, 56, 57, 58 13:18 (LXX ἐσθίων) (v. Kennedy, Sources, 82, 155; MM, xxv).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G5180 (τύπτω) (meaning a drum, "tympanum");
strong.def: to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 τυμπανίζω (< τύμπανον, a kettle-drum), [in LXX: I Ki 21:13 (14) (תָּוָה pi?) * ;]
1. to beat a drum.
2. to torture by beating, beat to death (cf. Westc. on He, l.c.): pass., He 11:35.†

strong.def: a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning)
strong.kjv: en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 (KJV) τύπος, -ου, ὁ (< τύπτω), [in LXX: Ex 25:39 (40) (תַּבְנִית), Am 5:26 (צֶלֶם), III Mac 3:30, IV Mac 6:19 * ;]
1. the mark of a blow: τῶν ἥλων, Jo 20:25.
2. An impression, impress, the stamp made by a die; hence, a figure, image: Ac 7:43 (LXX).
3. form (Plat.): Ro 6:17; the sense or substance of a letter (III Mac, l.c.), Ac 23:25.
4. an example, pattern: Ac 7:44, He 8:6 (LXX); in ethical sense, Phl 3:17, I Th 1:7, II Th 3:9, I Ti 4:12, Tit 2:7, I Pe 5:3; in doctrinal sense, type (v. ICC, in l.), Ro 5:14.†

strong.derivation: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of G2962 (κύριος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Τύραννος, -ου, ὀ
Tyrannus: Ac 19:9.†

strong.def: a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Τύριος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ
a Tyrian: Ac 12:20.†

strong.def: to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 τυφλόω, -ῶ (< τυφλός), [in LXX: Is 42:19 (עִוֵּר), To 7:7 א, Wi 2:21 א * ;]
to blind, make blind: metaph., Jo 12:40 (LXX, καμμύω), II Co 4:4, I Jo 2:11.†

strong.def: to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit
strong.kjv: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * τυφόω, -ῶ (< τῦφος, smoke; metaph., conceit),
prop., to wrap in smoke; used only metaph., to puff up, becloud with pride: pass., I Ti 3:6 6:4, II Ti 3:4 (Dem., Arist., al.).†

strong.def: to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * τύφω (< τῦφος, smoke
to raise a smoke; pass., to smoke: Mt 12:20 (LXX, καπνιζόμενον).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† τυφωνικός, -ή, -όν (< τῦφων, a hurricane, typhoon)
tempestuous: Ac 27:14.†

strong.def: fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Τύχικος, (T, Rec., Τυχικός), -ου, ὁ
Tychicus: Ac 20:4, Eph 6:21, Col 4:7, II Ti 4:12, Tit 3:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὑακίνθινος, -η, -ον (< ὑάκινθος), [in LXX for תַּחַשׁ, תְּכֵלֶת ;]
of hyacinth, hyacinthine (v.s. ὑάκινθος), "doubtless meant to describe the blue smoke of a sulphurous flame" (Swete): Re 9:17 (Hom., Eur., al.).†

strong.def: the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὑακίνθος, -ου, ό [in LXX chiefly for תְּכֵלֶת ;]
hyacinth;
(a). in cl., a flower, prob. the dark blue iris;
(b). in late writers, a precious stone of the same colour, perhaps the sapphire: Re 21:20 (Phil., FlJ, al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ὑάλινος, -η, -ον (< ὕαλος),
of glass, glassy Re 4:6 15:2.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from the same as G5205 (ὑετός) (as being transparent like rain);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὕαλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Jb 28:17 (זְכוּכִית) * ;]
1. (Hdt.) a clear transparent stone.
2. (from Plat. on) glass: Re 21:18, 21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὕβρις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;]
1. wantonness, insolence.
2. = ὕβρισμα, an act of wanton violence, an outrage, injury: II Co 12:10; metaph., of a loss by sea (Pind.), Ac 27:10, 21 (v. MM, xxv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὑβριστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< ὑβρίζω), [in LXX chiefly for גֵּאֶה ;]
a violent, insolent man: Ro 1:20, I Ti 1:13 (EV, injurious).†

strong.def: a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὑδρία, -ας, ἠ (< ὕδωρ), [in LXX for כַּד ;]
1. prop., a water-pot or jar: Jo 2:6, 7 4:28.
2. More freq. in Attic = ἄγγος, a pot, urn or jar of any kind, as for holding wine, coins, etc. (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 23; MM, xxv).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5204 (ὕδωρ) and a derivative of G4095 (πίνω);
strong.def: to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὑδροποτίω, -ῶ (< ὕδωρ, πίνω), [in LXX: Da LXX 1:12 שָׁתָה מַיִם) * ;]
to drink water, opp. to οἴνῳ χρῆσθαι: I Ti 5:23 (Hdt., i, 71; Plat., Rep., 561 c, al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 (KJV) ὑετός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ὕω, to rain), [in LXX chiefly for מָטָר,גֶּשֶׁם ;]
rain: Ac 14:17 28:2, He 6:7, Ja 5:18, Re 11:6; ὄψιμος (q.v.), sc. ὑ., Ja 5:7.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G5207 (υἱός) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
strong.def: the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 *† υἱοθεσία, -ας, ἡ (cf. the cl. phrases, υἱὸν τίθεσθαι, θετὸς υἱός), freq. in Inscr. (v. Deiss., BS, 239), adoption of a son (or daughter); metaph., of God's relation established
(a). with Israel: Ro 9:4;
(b). with Christ­ians: Ro 8:15, Ga 4:5, Eph 1:5; of its consummation, Ro 8:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὕλη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Jb 19:29 (†) 38:40 (סֻכָּה), Ps 68 (69):2 Blא(יָוֵן), Is 10:17 (שָׁמִיר), Wi 11:17 15:13, Si 28:10, II Mac 2:24, IV Mac 1:29 * ;]
1. wood, forest, woodland (Thuc., Xen., al.).
2. wood, timber, fuel (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.): Ja 3:5 (v. Hort, Ja., 70, 104 f.).
3. = Lat. materia, esp. in Philosophy, matter (Arist. and later writers; Wi, ll. c.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ὑμέναιος, -ου, ὁ
Hymenæus: I Ti 1:20, II Ti 2:17.†

strong.derivation: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of (to celebrate;
strong.def: probably akin to G103 (ᾄδω); compare H05667); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὕμνος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for תְּהִלָּה, נְגִינָה, שִׁיר, etc. ;]
a hymn;
(a). in cl. a festal song in praise of gods or heroes;
(b). in LXX and NT a song of praise addressed to God: Eph 5:19, Col 3:16.†

strong.def: attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 † ὑπακοή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ὑπακούω), [in LXX: II Ki 22:36 (עֲנָוָה); in Aq.: ib. 23:23 * ;]
obedience (opp. to παρακοή);
1. in general, absol., εἰς ὑ., Ro 6:16; c. gen. subjc., II Co 7:15 10:6, Phm 21; c. gen. obj., Ro 1:5 (Lft, Notes, 246) 16:26, I Pe 1:22; τ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 10:5.
2. Of obedience to God's commands: absol., I Pe 1:2; opp. to ἁμαρτία, Ro 6:16; τέκνα ὑπακοῆς, I Pe 1:14; c. gen. subj., Ro 15:18 16:19.
3. Of Christ's obedience: absol., He 5:8; c. gen. subj., Ro 5:19.
(The word is not found except in LXX, NT and eccl.).†

strong.def: in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὕπανδρος, -ον [in LXX: Nu 5:20, 29 (אִישׁ תַּחַת), Pr 6:24, 29, Si 9:9 41:21 * ;]
under or subject to a man, married: γυνή, Ro 7:2 (Polyb., Diod., al.).†

strong.def: an encounter or concurrence (with G1519 (εἰς) for infinitive, in order to fall in with)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 † ὑπ-άντησις, -εως, ἡ (< ὑπαντάω), [in LXX: Jg 11:34, εἰς ὑ. (לִקְרָאת), etc. ;]
a going to meet: εἰς ὑ. (v. M, Pr., 14 n), Mt 8:34 25:1, Jo 12:13.†

strong.def: existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὕπαρξις, -εως, ἡ (< ὑπάρχω), [in LXX for רְכוּשׁ, הוֹן, etc. ;]
1. subsistence, existence (Arist., al.).
2. In late writers, = τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, substance, property: He 10:34; pl., Ac 2:45.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὑπ-είκω [in LXX: IV Mac 6:35 * ;]
1. o retire, withdraw.
2. to yield, submit: metaph., He 13:17.†

strong.def: under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὑπ-εναντίος, -α, -ον [in LXX for אָיַב, צַר, etc. ;]
set over against, opposite. Metaph. (Plat., Arist., al.), opposed to, contrary to: c. dat. pers., Col 2:14; absol., as subst., ὁ ὑ., He 10:27 (cf. Is 26:11).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G142 (αἴρω);
strong.def: to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty
strong.kjv: exalt self, be exalted above measure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὑπερ-αίρω [in LXX: II Ch 32:23 (נָשָׂא ni.), etc. ;]
to lift or raise over. Mid., to uplift oneself: II Co 12:7; seq. ἐπί, c. acc, pers., II Th 2:4 (cf. II Mac 5:23).†

strong.derivation: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the base of G188 (ἀκμήν);
strong.def: beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑπέρακμος, -ον
past the bloom of youth: I Co 7:36 (Eustath.).†

strong.def: above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὑπερ-άνω compound adv., [in LXX for עַל, מֵעָל, etc. ;]
above: as prep. c. gen., Eph 1:21 4:10, He 9:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὑπερ-αυξάνω
to increase beyond measure: II Th 1:3 (v. Lft., Notes, 98).†

strong.derivation: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the base of G939 (βάσις);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ὑπερ-βαίνω [in LXX for עָבַר, etc. ;]
1. trans., to step over, trans­gress (R, overreach: I Th 4:6).
2. Intrans., to transgress: metaph., I Th 4:6 (R, txt.; v. M, Th., in l.).†

strong.derivation: adverb from present participle active of G5235 (ὑπερβάλλω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὑπερβαλλόντως [in LXX: Jb 15:11 א B (†) * ;]
above measure: II Co 11:23.†

strong.def: to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ὑπερ-βάλλω [in LXX: Jb 15:11 A (†), Si 5:7 25:11, al. ;]
1. trans., to throw over or beyond.
2. Intrans., to run beyond. In both senses, metaph., to exceed, surpass, transcend: II Co 3:10 9:14, Eph 1:19 2:7; c. gen. obj., Eph 3:19.†

strong.def: a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with G1519 (εἰς) or G2596 (κατά)) pre- eminently
strong.kjv: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ** ὑπερ-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ὑπερβάλλω), [in LXX: καθ’ ὑ., IV Mac 3:18 * ;]
a throwing beyond. Metaph., excess, superiority, excellence: II Co 4:7 12:7; καθ’ ὑπερβολήν, beyond measure, exceedingly, Ro 7:13, I Co 12:31, II Co 1:8, Ga 1:13; κ. ὑ. εἰς ὑ. , beyond all measure, II Co 4:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ὑπερ-εῖδον, aor. [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;]
to overlook: c. acc rei, Ac 17:30

strong.derivation: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the neuter plural of G1565 (ἐκεῖνος);
strong.def: above those parts, i.e. still farther

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑπερ-έκεινα
comp. adv. (v. Bl., 28, 2; M, Pr., 99),
beyond: as prep. c. gen., τὰ ὑ. ὑμῶν, II Co 10:16 (Byz. and eccl.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑπερ-εκ-τείνω
to stretch out overmuch: metaph., ἑαυτούς, II Co 10:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑπερ-εν-τυγχάνω
to intercede or make petition for (v. Deiss., BS, 121 f.): seq. ὑπέρ, Ro 8:26.†

strong.def: to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ὑπερ-έχω [in LXX: Ge 25:23 (אָמַץ), Ex 26:13 (עֲדַף), Si 36:7, al. ;]
1. trans., to hold over or above.
2. Intrans. (when a noun follows, the case is governed by the prep.; v. Bl., § 34, 1; 36, 8), to rise above, overtop; metaph.,
(a). to be superior in rank, etc.: Ro 13:1, I Pe 2:13 (cf. Wi 6:6);
(b). to be superior, excel, surpass: c. gen. (cl.; v. supr.), Phl 2:3; c. acc (cl.; v. supr.), Phl 4:7; as subst., τ. ὑπερέχον, the excel­lency, the surpassing worth, Phl 3:8.†

strong.def: to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ὑπερ-νικάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Da TH 6:3; in Sm.: Ps 42 (43):1 * ;]
to be more than conqueror: Ro 8:37 (eccl.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὑπέρ-ογκος, -ον [in LXX: De 30:11 (נִפְלֵאת), etc. ;]
of excessive weight or size; metaph., excessive, immoderate, in late writers, of arrogant speech (v. Mayor on Ju, l.c.): n. pl., II Pe 2:18, Ju 16.†

strong.def: prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὑπεροχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ὑπερέχω) [in LXX: Je 52:22 (קוֹמָה), II Mac 3:11, al. ;]
a projection, eminence, as the peak of a mountain. Metaph. (Arist.), excellence, pre-eminence: λόγου ἢ σοφίας, I Co 2:1; οἱ ἐν ὑ. (for a parallel to this phrase, v. Deiss., BS, 255, and cf. II Mac, l.c.), I Ti 2:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ὑπερ-περισσεύω
to abound more exceedingly: Ro 5:21. Mid., in same sense (RV, overflow): c. dat. rei, II Co 7:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑπερ-πλεονάζω
to abound exceedingly: I Ti 1:14 (Ps Sol 5:19; Herm., Mand., v, 2, 5).†

strong.def: to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὑπερ-υψόω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ps 36 (37):35 (עָרִיץ) Ps 96 (97):9 (עָלָה ni.), Da TH 4:34 11:12 (רוּם), ib. LXX TH 3:52ff.* ;]
1. to exalt beyond measure, exalt to the highest place: Phl 2:9.
2. to extol (Da, ll. c.).†

strong.def: to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὑπερ-φρονέω, -ῶ [in LXX: IV Mac 13:1 14:11 16:2 * ;]
1. to be overproud, high-minded (Æsch.): μὴ ὑ. παρ’ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν (on the paranom., v. Vau., in l.), Ro 12:3.
2. to overlook, think slightly of (Thuc., Plat.).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G5228 (ὑπέρ);
strong.def: a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὑπερῷον, -ου, τό (neut. of ὑπερῷος, above, < ὑπέρ) [in LXX for עֲלִיָּה and cogn. forms ;]
1. in cl., the upper story or upper rooms where the women resided (Hom., a1.).
2. In LXX and NT, an upper chamber, roof-chamber, built on the flat roof of the house (v. DB, iii, 674a): Ac 1:13 9:37, 39 20:8 (cf. IV Ki 23:22).†

strong.def: to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ὑπ-έχω [in LXX: Ps 88 (89):50 (נָשָׂא), La 5:7 (סָבַל), Wi 12:21, II Mac 4:48 * ;]
to hold or put under. Metaph., to undergo, suffer: δίκην, Ju 7 (Soph., Eur., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὑπήκοος, -ον (< ὑπακούω), [in LXX: Jo 17:13 (לָמַם) Pr 21:28 (שׁוֺמֵעַ), etc. ;]
giving ear, obedient, subject: Phl 2:8; c. dat. pers., Ac 7:39; εἰς πάντα, II Co 2:9.†

strong.def: to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ὑπηρετέω, -ῶ (< ὑπηρέτης) [in LXX: Wi 16:21, 24, 25 19:6, Si 39:4 * ;]
prop., to serve as rower on a ship (Diod., al.). In cl. always metaph., to minister to, serve: c. dat. pers., Ac 13:36 20:34 24:23.†

strong.def: to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ** ὑπο-βάλλω [in LXX: Da TH 3:9 A, I Es 2:18 * ;]
to throw or put under. Metaph.,
(a). to subject, submit;
(b). to suggest, whisper, prompt;
(c). to suborn (v. Field, Notes, 113), instigate: c. acc pers., Ac 6:11.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G1125 (γράφω);
strong.def: an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ὑπογραμμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ὑπογράφω, (a) to write under; (b) to trace letters for copying), [in LXX: II Mac 2:28 * ;]
1. a writing-copy, hence,
2. an example: I Pe 2:11 (Philo).†

strong.def: an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ὑπό-δειγμα, -τος, τό (< ὑποδείκνυμι), [in LXX: Ez 42:15, Si 44:16, II Mac 6:28, 31, IV Mac 17:23 * ;]
used by later writers (Xen. onwards) for παράδειγμα (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 62),
(a). a figure, copy: He 8:5 9:23;
(b). an example for imitation, Jo 13:15, Ja 5:10; for warning, He 4:11, II Pe 2:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὑπόδικος, -ον
brought to trial, answerable to: c. dat. pers., τ. θεῷ, Ro 3:19 (v. MM, xxv).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G2218 (ζυγός);
strong.def: an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὑπο-ζύγιος, -α, -ον [in LXX for חֲמוֹר ;]
under the yoke; as subst., τὸ ζ. (Hdt., al.), a beast of burden; colloq., an ass (v. Deiss., BS, 160 f.), and so always in LXX and NT: Mt 21:5 (LXX), II Pe 2:16.†

strong.def: to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὑπο-ζώννυμι [in LXX: II Mac 3:19 * ;]
to undergird (Hdt., al.; ὑπὸ τ. μάστους, II Mac, l.c.); of a ship, to undergird or frap: Ac 27:17 (v. DB, ext. 367a).†

strong.def: to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ὑπο-λείπω [in LXX chiefly (pass.) for יָתַר ni., שָׁאַר ni. ;]
to leave remaining (Hom., Thuc., al.): pass., of survivors, Ro 11:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑπο-λιμπάνω
collat. form of ὑπολείπω,
to leave behind

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὑπό-μνησις, -εως, ἡ (ὑπομιμνήσκω) [in LXX: Ps 70 (71):6 א (תְּהִלָּה), Wi 16:11, II Mac 6:17 * ;]
a reminding, reminder: ἐν ὑ., II Pe 1:13 3:1; c. gen., II Ti 1:5.†

strong.def: to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ὑπο-νοέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Da TH 7:25 (סְבַר), To 8:16, Jth 14:14, Si 23:21 * ;]
to suspect, conjecture: Ac 25:18; c. acc et inf., Ac 13:25 27:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ὑπόνοια, -ας, ἡ (< ὑπονοέω), [in LXX: Da LXX 4:16, 32 5:6 (רַעְיוֹן), Sir 3:34* ;]
a suspicion: I Ti 6:4.†

strong.def: to sail under the lee of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) *† ὑπο-πλέω
to sail under, i.e. under the lee of: c. acc, Ac 27:4, 7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὑπο-πνέω
1. to blow underneath (Arist.).
2. to blow gently: Ac 27:13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G2476 (ἵστημι);
strong.def: a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 (KJV) ὑπό-στασις, -εως, ἡ (< ὑφίστημι, to set under, stand under, support) [in LXX for מַצָּב (I Ki 13:23 14:4 B), תִּקְוָה (Ru 1:12, Ez 19:5), etc., also in Wi 16:21 ;]
1. a support, base or foundation (in various senses).
2. substance (Arist., al.; opp. to φαντασία, ἔμφασις): He 1:3
3. steadiness, firmness (Polyb., al.), hence, assurance, confidence: II Co 9:4 11:17, He 3:14 11:1 (here perhaps title-deed, as that which gives reality or guarantee; v. MM, xxv).†

strong.def: to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 (KJV) ὑπο-στέλλω [in LXX: De 1:17 (גּוּר), Jb 13:8 (נָשָׂא פָּנִים), Hb 2:4 (עָפַל pu.), Hg 1:10 (כָּלָא), Ex 23:21, Wi 6:7, III Mac 5:20 * ;]
1. to draw in, let down (ἱστίον, οὐράν, etc.).
2. to draw back, withdraw: ἑαυτόν, Ga 2:12 (Polyb., al.; v. Lft., in l.). Mid., to shrink or draw back: He 10:38 (LXX); seq. τοῦ, c. inf., Ac 20:27; οὐδέν, ib. 20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) *† ὑπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ὑποστέλλω),
1. a letting down, lowering (Plut.).
2. a shrinking back (Hesych.): οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς (on the gen., v. Bl., § 35, 2), He 10:39.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** ὑπο-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Wi 18:16 A * ;]
subjection: II Co 9:13, Ga 2:5. I Ti 2:11 3:4.†

strong.def: to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) ὑπο-τίθημι [in LXX for שׂוּם, etc. ;]
to place under, lay down. Metaph., τ. τράχηλον ὑποθεῖναι, to risk one's life (v. Deiss., LAE, 119 f.): Ro 16:4; mid., to suggest: I Ti 4:6.†

strong.derivation: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);
strong.def: to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὑπο-τρέχω
to run in under; of navigators, to run in the lee of : c. acc. (v. M, Pr., 65), Ac 27:16.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of G5179 (τύπος);
strong.def: typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ὑπο-τύπωσις, -εως, ἡ (< ὑποτυπόω, to delineate),
an outline, sketch. Metaph., a pattern, example: I Ti 1:16, II Ti 1:13.†

strong.def: to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 (KJV) ὑπο-φέρω [in LXX for נָשָׂא, etc. ;]
to bear by being under. Metaph., to endure: c. acc rei, I Co 10:13, II Ti 3:11, I Pe 2:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὗς, ὑός, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX for חֲזִיר ;]
swine: fem. (sow), II Pe 2:22,†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ὕσσωπος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for אֵזוֹב ;]
hyssop, of which a bunch was used in ritual sprinklings: He 9:19; of a branch or rod (?) of hyssop, Jo 19:29 (but v. Field, Notes, 106 ff., for suggestion to substitute ὑσσῷ here).†

strong.derivation: comparative from G5259 (ὑπό) (in the sense of behind);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ὕστερος, -α, -ον [in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms ;]
latter, later: ἐν ὑ. καιροῖς, I Ti 4:1 (on the reading ὁ ὕ., WH, for ὁ πρῶτος, v. WH, App., in l.). Neut., τὸ ὕ., used adverbially instead of ὑστέρως, afterwards, later: Mt 4:2 21:29, 32, 37 25:11 26:60, Mk 16:14, Lk 20:32, Jo 13:36, He 12:11; c. gen., Mt 22:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὑφαντός, -ή, -όν (< ὑφαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב ;]
woven: Jo 19:23.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5308 (ὑψηλός) and G5424 (φρήν);
strong.def: to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὑψηλο- φρονέω, -ῶ = μεγαλοφρονεῖν (Xen., Plat., al.),
to be high-minded: I Ti 6:17 (WH, mg., ὑψηλὰ, φρονεῖν).†

strong.def: an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὕψωμα, -τος, τό [in LXX: Jb 24:24 (†), Jth 10:8 13:4 15:9 * ;]
(a). height: Ro 8:39;
(b). that which is lifted up, a barrier: II Co 10:5.†

strong.def: exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † φανέρωσις, -εως, ἡ (< φανερόω), [in LXX as v.l. for δήλωσις אוּרִים), Le 8:8, Cod. Ven. (Thayer, s.v.) * ;]
manifestation: I Co 12:7, II Co 4:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φανός, -οῦ, ὁ (< φαίνω),
a torch or lantern (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 131 f.): Jo 18:3.†

strong.def: to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φαντάζω (< φαίνω) [in LXX: Wi 6:16, Si 31 (34):5* ;]
to make visible. In cl. used in pass. only, = φαίνομαι, to become visible, appear: ptcp., He 12:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φαντασία, -ας, ἡ (< φαντάζω), [in LXX: Za 10:1 (חָזִיז), חֲזִיז), Hb 2:18, 19 3:10, Wi 18:17 * ;]
1. as philos. term,
(a). imagination;
(b). = φάντασμα (Plat., Arist.).
2. In later writers (Polyb., al.), show, display: Ac 25:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Φαραώ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה),
Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: Ac 7:13, 21, Ro 9:17, He 11:24; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, Ac 7:10.†

strong.def: medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φαρμακία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (< φαρμακεύω, to administer drugs) [in LXX: Ex 7:11, 22 8:7, 18 (3, 14) (לָט, חַרְטֹם), Is 47:9, 12 (כֶּשֶׁף) Wi 12:4 18:13 * ;]
poët. and late prose form of φαρμακεία,
1. generally, the use of medicine, drugs or spells (Xen.).
2. (a) poisoning (Plut., Polyb.);
(b). sorcery, witchcraft: Ga 5:20 (v. Lft., in l.), Re 9:21 (WH, txt., φαρμάκων) 18:23 (cf. LXX, ll. c.).†

strong.def: a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) * φαρμακεύς, -έως, ὁ (< φάρμακον)
a sorcerer: Re 21:8, Rec.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φαρμακός, -ή, -όν [in LXX for מְכַשֵׁף, etc. ;]
devoted to magical arts. As subst., ὁ φ. = φαρμακεύς, a magician, sorcerer: Re 21:8 22:15.†

strong.derivation: from G5346 (φημί) (not the same as "phase", which is from G5316 (φαίνω));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 φάσις, -εως, ἡ (< φαίνω), [in LXX: II Es 4:17, Da TH Su :55, IV Mac 15:25 א1* ;]
information, esp. against fraud or other crime: Ac 21:31.†

strong.derivation: prolongation from the same as G5346 (φημί);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 φάσκω [in LXX: Ge 26:20 (אמר), Da LXX Bel :8, II Mac 14:27, 14:32, III Mac 3:7 * ;]
to affirm, assert: c. acc. et inf., Ac 24:9 25:19; c. inf. et nom., Ro 1:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 φαῦλος, -η, -ον [in LXX: Pr 22:8 (עַוְלָה) 29:9 (אֳבִיל), etc. ;]
slight, worthless, of no account, both of persons and things in various shades of meaning (v. LS, s.v.), in NT, as freq. in cl., always with distinct moral reference (v. Ellic., Past. Epp., 203; Hort, Ja., 85; Tr., Syn., lxxxiv), worthless, bad: Jo 3:20, Tit 2:8, Ja 3:16; opp. to ἀγαθός (q.v.), Jo 5:29, Ro 9:11, II Co 5:10.†

strong.def: to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 φείδομαι [in LXX for חמל, חוּס, חשׂךְ, etc. ;]
to spare: II Co 13:2; c. gen. pers., Ac 20:29, Ro 8:32 11:21, I Co 7:28, II Co 1:23, II Pe 2:4, 5; c. inf., to forbear, II Co 12:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† φειδομένως
adv. from ptcp. (v. Bl., § 25, 1),
sparingly: II Co 9:6 (Plut.).†

strong.derivation: by transposition for a derivative probably of G5316 (φαίνω) (as showing outside the other garments);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φελόνης (Rec. φαιλ-), -ου, ὁ
by metath. for παινόλης (also φενόλης, φαινόλιον; Lat. pænula)
a cloak (v. DCG, i, 338; on the idea that the meaning here is book-cover, v. CGT, in l.; Milligan, NTD, 20; Field, Notes, 217 f., where the view that the φ. here is an eccl. vestment is discussed): II Ti 4:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 φῆλιξ (L, Φή-), -ικος, ὁ
Felix, procurator of Judæa: Ac 23:24, 26 24:3, 22, 24, 25, 27 25:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 φῆστος, -ου, ὁ
(Porcius), Festus, procurator of Judæa: Ac 24:27 25:1ff. Ac 26:24, 25, 32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 φθαρτός, -ή, -όν (φθείρω) [in LXX: Le 22:25 (מִשְׁחָת), Is 54:17 Aא3, Wi 9:15 14:8, II Mac 7:16 * ;]
perishable, corruptible: ἄνθρωπος, Ro 1:23 (opp. to ἄφθαρτος θεός); στέφανος, I Co 9:25 (opp. to ἄφθαρτος); σπσρά, I Pe 1:23 (opp. to ἄφθ.); neut., τὸ φ. τοῦτο, I Co 15:53, 54; pl., I Pe 1:18.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to G5338 (φέγγος) and thus to G5346 (φημί);
strong.def: to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 φθέγγομαι [in LXX for ענה, נבע hi., etc. ;]
of men or animals, to utter a sound or voice: absol., Ac 4:18; seq. ἐν φωνῇ, II Pe 2:16; c. acc., ὑπέρογκα, ib. 18.†

strong.derivation: probably strengthened from (to pine or waste);
strong.def: properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 φθείρω [in LXX chiefly for שׁחת hi., pi., also for חבל, etc. ;]
to destroy, corrupt, spoil (on the varied usage and distinctive meaning of the word, v. Mayor on II Pe, App., 175 ff.): c. acc., I Co 3:17 15:23, II Co 7:2; seq. ἀπό, II Co 11:3; ἐν, II Pe 2:12, Ju 10, Re 19:2; κατά, Eph 4:22 (cf. δια-, κατα-φθείρω).†

strong.def: akin to the base of G5351 (φθείρω)) and G3703 (ὀπώρα) (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φθιν-οπωρινός, -ή, -όν (< φθινόπωρον, late autumn),
autumnal: δένδρα φ., autumn trees (said to be without fruit therefore at a time when fruit might be expected; v. Mayor's elaborate note, Ep. Ju., 55-59, and reff. there): Ju 12.†

strong.def: utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φθόγγος, -ου, ὁ (< φθέγγομαι), [in LXX: Ps 18 (19):4 (קַו), Wi 19:18 * ;]
a sound: Ro 10:18 (LXX) I Co 14:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φθονέω, -ῶ (< φθόνος), [in LXX: To 4:7, 16 AB * ;]
to envy: c. dat. (L, txt., Tr., mg., WH, mg., acc.), as in cl., Ga 5:26.†

strong.def: decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 φθορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< φθείρω) [in LXX for שַׁחַת, חֶבֶל, etc. ;]
destruction, corruption, decay (v. Mayor on II Pe, App.,175 ff.): Ro 8:21, I Co 15:42, Col 2:22, II Pe 2:12; opp. to ζωὴ αἰώνιος, Ga 6:8; by meton., of that which is subject to corruption, I Co 15:50; of moral decay, II Pe 1:4 2:12, 19 (cf. Wi 14:12).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 φιάλη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for מִזְרָק ;]
a shallow bowl (= Lat. patera), used for pouring libations, etc.: Re 5:8 15:7 16:1-17 17:1 21:9.†

strong.def: fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φιλ-άγαθος, -ον [in LXX: Wi 7:22 * ;]
loving that which is good, loving goodness: Tit 1:8 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†

strong.derivation: from (the same as G5361 (φιλάδελφος)), a king of Pergamos;
strong.def: Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Φιλαδελφία (Rec. -έλφεια), -ας, ἡ
Philadelphia, a city of Lydia: Re 1:11 3:7.†

strong.kjv: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 φιλαδελφία, -ας, ἡ (< φιλάδελφος), [in LXX: IV Mac 13:23, 26 14:1 * ;]
the love of brothers, brotherly love: of Christians' mutual love as brethren (v.s. ἀδελφός), Ro 12:10, I Th 4:9, He 13:1, I Pe 1:22, II Pe 1:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φιλ-άδελφος, -ον [in LXX: II Mac 15:14, IV Mac 13:21 15:10 * ;]
loving one's brother, loving like a brother (Soph., Xen., al.): of Christians' love for one another (EV, loving as brethren), I Pe 3:8.†

strong.def: fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φίλανδρος, -ον
1. loving men (Æsch.).
2. Of a wife, loving her husband (freq. in epitaphs, v. LS, s.v., Deiss., BS, 255): Tit 2:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** φιλανθρωπία, -ας, ἡ (< φιλάνθρωπος, humane), [in LXX: Es 8:13, II Mac 6:22 14:9, III Mac 3:15, 18 * ;]
humanity, kindness (v. Field, Notes, 147 f.): Ac 28:2, Tit 3:4 (cf. also DCG, ii, 356 ff.).†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G444 (ἄνθρωπος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φιλανθρώπως adv., [in LXX: II Mac 9:27, III Mac 3:20 * ;]
humanely, kindly: Ac 27:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φιλαργυρία, -ας, ἡ (< φιλάργυρος), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:26 2:15 א1 * ;]
love of money, avarice: I Ti 6:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φίλ-αυτος, -ον
loving oneself (Arist.); in bad sense (ib.), selfish: II Ti 3:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φιλήδονος, -ον (φίλος, ἡδονή),
loving pleasure: II Ti 3:4 (Polyb., Plut. al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φιλήμων, -ονος, ὁ
Philemon: Phm 1.†

strong.def: amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φίλητός (T, Φιλητός), -ου, ὁ
Philetus: II Ti 2:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φιλία, -ας, ἡ (< φίλος), [in LXX chiefly for אַהֲבָה ;]
friendship: c. gen. obj., Ja 4:4.†

strong.def: a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φιλιππήσιος, -ου, ὁ (for other forms in use, v. Lft., in l.)
a Philippian: Phl 4:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 φίλιπποι, -ων, οἱ (on the pl., v. WM, § 27, 3)
Philippi: Ac 16:12 20:6, Phl 1:1, I Th 2:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φιλό-θεος, -ον
loving God (Arist.): II Ti 3:4.†

strong.def: fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φιλόλογος, -ου, ὁ
Philologus: Ro 16:15.†

strong.def: probably akin to G3534 (νῖκος)); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φιλό-νεικος, -ον (< νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: Ez 3:7 (מֵצַח־חָזָק)* ;]
fond of strife, contentious: I Co 11:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * φιλο-ξενία, -ας, ἡ (< φιλόξενος),
love of strangers, hospitality: Ro 12:13, He 13:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * φιλό-ξενος, -ον
loving strangers, hospitable: I Ti 3:2, Tit 1:8, I Pe 4:9.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G4413 (πρῶτος);
strong.def: to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φιλοπρωτεύω (< φιλόπρωτος, Plut., al.)
to strive to be first: III Jo 9 (eccl.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** Φιλο-σοφία, -ας, ἡ (< φιλόσοφος), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:1 5:10, 22 7:9, 21 * ;]
the love and pursuit of wisdom; hence, philosophy, investi­gation of truth and nature: of the so-called philosophy of false teachers, Col 2:8 (v. Lft., ICC, in l.).†

strong.def: fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher"

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φιλό-σοφος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Da LXX 1:20 (אַשָּׁף), IV Mac 1:1 5:35 7:7 * ;]
a philosopher: Ac 17:18.†

strong.derivation: from G5384 (φίλος) and (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children);
strong.def: fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φιλόστοργος, -ον (< στοργή, family affection), [in LXX: IV Mac 15:13 * ;]
tenderly loving, affectionate (Xen., Plut., al.): of Christians, Ro 12:10.†

strong.def: fond of one's children, i.e. maternal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φιλότεκνος, -ον (< φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: IV Mac 15:4-6 * ;]
loving one's children (Hdt., Arist., Plut., al.): of women, joined with φίλανδρος, q.v., Tit 2:4.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G5092 (τιμή);
strong.def: to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** φιλοτιμέομαι, -οῦμαι (< φίλος, τιμή), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:35 A ;]
to love or seek after honour, hence, to be ambitious, emulous (Plat., Plut., al.): c. inf., Ro 15:20, II Co 5:9, I Th 4:11.†

strong.def: with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φιλοφρόνως (< φιλόφρων) adv., [in LXX: II Mac 3:9, IV Mac 8:5 * ;]
kindly, with friendliness: Ac 28:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) * φιλόφρων, -ον (< φίλος, φρήν),
friendly, kind. I Pe 3:8, Rec.†

strong.derivation: active participle of the base of G5395 (φλόξ);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φλέγων, -οντος, ὁ
Phlegon: Ro 16:14.†

strong.def: to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φλογίζω (< φλόξ), [in LXX: Ex 9:24 (לקח hith.), Nu 21:14 (†), Ps 96 (97):3 (להט pi.), Da TH 3:27(94) (חֲרַךְ ithp.), Si 3:30, I Mac 3:5 * ;]
to set on fire, burn, burn up: fig., Ja 3:6 (on the meaning of the sentence, v. Hort, in l.).†

strong.def: to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φλυαρέω, -ῶ (< φλύαρος),
to talk nonsense: c. acc. pers., ἡμᾶς (EV, prating against us), III Jo 10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φλύαρος, -ον (< φλύω, to babble), [in LXX: IV Mac 5:10 * ;]
babbling, garrulous: I Ti 5:13 (EV, tattlers; of things, φιλοσοφία, IV Mac, l.c.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 φοβερός, -ά, -όν (< φοβέω), [in LXX chiefly for נוֺרָא, also for דְּחַל, אָיֹם ;]
fearful, whether act, or pass.;
1. act., = δεινός, causing fear, terrible (LXX): He 10:27, 31 12:21
2. Pass., = δειλός, feeling fear, timid (cl. in both senses).†

strong.def: probably akin to the base of G5457 (φῶς)); Phœbe, a Christian woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φοίβη, -ης, ἡ
Phœbe, a deaconess of Cenchræa: Ro 16:1.†

strong.def: palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 φοινίκη, -ης, ἡ
Phœnicia: Ac 11:19 15:3 21:2 (v. DB, iii, 856b, 857an).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φοῖνιξ (on the accent, v. Bl., § 4, 2; WM, § 6, lc), -ικος, ὁ, [in LXX for תָּמָר,תֹּמֶר,תִּמֹּרָה;]
the date-palm, palm: τὰ βαΐα τῶν φ., Jo 12:13; of palm branches, φοίνικες (as Arist., II Mac 10:7, al.), Re 7:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Φοῖνιξ, -ικος, ο, ἡ
(a). a Phœnician (also with fem., Φοίνισσα, Hom., al.);
(b). Phœnix, a city of Crete: Ac 27:12.†

strong.def: a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which G443 (ἀνθρωποκτόνος) does not necessarily imply; while G4607 (σικάριος) is a special term for a public bandit)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 * φονεύς, -έως, ὁ (φόνος) [in LXX: Wi 12:5 * ;]
a murderer: Mt 22:7 Ac 7:52 28:4, I Pe 4:15, Re 21:8 22:15; ἀνὴρ φ., Ac 3:14.†

strong.def: to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 φορέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Pr 16:23 (יָסַף hi.), Si 11:5, al. ;]
frequent. of φέρω, denoting repeated or habitual action (cf. Tr., Syn., § lviii), most commonly used of clothing, weapons, etc., to bear constantly, wear: Mt 11:8, Jo 19:5, Ro 13:4, I Co 15:49, Ja 2:3.†

strong.def: a forum or market-place; only in comparative with G675 (Ἄππιος); a station on the Appian road

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φόρον, -ου, τό
(Lat. forum): Ἀππίου Φ., v.s. Ἄππιος.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φορτούνατος (Rec. Φουρ-, v. Mayser, 116 f.), -ου, ὁ
(Lat.) Fortunatus: I Co 16:17 (v. Lft., Cl. Ro., 1Co., 59).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative from the base of G5417 (φραγελλόω);
strong.def: a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φραγέλλιον, -ου, τό
(Lat. flagellum), a scourge: Jo 2:15.†
